nodes.label: Animation duration table and frequency rule

nodes.label: motion-budget skill
nodes.author: Emil Kowalski
nodes.rationale: A short duration table with an under-300ms rule and a frequency principle keeps UI animation from slowing frequent interactions.

nodes.label: Vendored skill: test-audit (MIT, OpenClaw Foundation)
nodes.author: OpenClaw Foundation
nodes.rationale: The MIT text is reproduced because the license's own attribution requirement demands the copyright and permission notice accompany copies.

nodes.label: noDataState policy for Grafana rules
nodes.rationale: Rules whose healthy query returns an empty vector must use OK, because NoData there fired ~125 Telegram messages/day against ~2/day of real alerts.

nodes.label: Warn-only Jira-update nudge with breadcrumb
nodes.rationale: A machine-global breadcrumb keyed by repo and branch signals whether a session touched Jira because the standalone CLI never receives the Claude session_id.

nodes.label: Mutation breadcrumbs
nodes.rationale: Keyed by repo and branch because the standalone CLI never receives the Claude session_id, so the SessionEnd hook can still tell whether Jira was synced.

nodes.label: Adding a rule: structural over instructional
nodes.norm_label: adding a rule: structural over instructional
nodes.rationale: Repeated drift is fixed by a hook or gate because stronger prose still falls out of context.

nodes.label: Enforcement section
nodes.rationale: Hooks run automatically with explicit off-switches, so rules hold without relying on memory.

nodes.label: Honesty markers and artifacts
nodes.rationale: Marking deliberate simplifications and placing artifacts in the right repo keeps docs and decisions honest and organized.

nodes.label: Claude invocation billing rule
nodes.rationale: Headless claude -p draws the same 5-hour/weekly budget as interactive use, so unattended runs must preflight usage.

nodes.label: Jira: prefer plugin over MCP
nodes.rationale: The plugin must be run by absolute path because dist/ is untracked in a worktree.

nodes.label: MCP tier model (T0-TX)
nodes.rationale: implied: classifying servers by always-on, shared, profile-scoped, env-gated and CLI-first guides which ones should spawn per session.

nodes.label: Cadence (recurring cron job, off until armed)
nodes.norm_label: cadence (recurring cron job, off until armed)
nodes.rationale: Every cadence is off until armed so that background jobs only run with explicit user consent; only morning-report is auto-armed once by himmel-update.

nodes.label: Common arm/status/disarm interface
nodes.rationale: A uniform three-verb interface lets the wizard, lint and users treat every cadence script the same way.

nodes.label: Which commands reach an adopted repo
nodes.norm_label: which commands reach an adopted repo
nodes.rationale: The installer copies only some commands, provides scripts for others, and relies on plugins for the rest, so the catalog states which reach an adopter to avoid confusion about missing commands.

nodes.label: Clipper pipeline (obsidian-triage plugin)
nodes.rationale: A staged HARVEST, TRIAGE, SYNTHESIZE, ARCHIVE pipeline over the Clippings inbox so clips progress through idempotent, bounded passes.

nodes.label: /migrate-clip-lifecycle (one-time backfill)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic, reversible engine with six literal link forms guards against silent dangling wikilinks and runs once behind a staging gate.

nodes.label: Vendored plugin skills not itemized (lean-skills, i-have-adhd, pstack, humanizer, shadcn-mcp, claude-hud)
nodes.norm_label: vendored plugin skills not itemized (lean-skills, i-have-adhd, pstack, humanizer, shadcn-mcp, claude-hud)
nodes.rationale: These plugins' own docs already own their inventories, and itemizing them would duplicate content that drifts on upstream re-vendor.

nodes.label: Plugin skills & ops (himmel-ops, obsidian-triage)
nodes.rationale: Plugin skills trigger on symptoms or aliases rather than bare commands, so a separate paraphrased table lists them.

nodes.label: Autonomy ladder (initiative to AFK)
nodes.rationale: Autonomy is ordered from least to most autonomous with an off switch on every rung, and all rungs are opt-in except the cap watchdogs, so an operator can bound what acts without them.

nodes.label: Layer-level off-switches
nodes.rationale: Operators need one table to turn each layer off entirely, while a few gates (leak-class, egress hard-deny, human-only public merge) are deliberately not switchable and fail closed.

nodes.label: Project permission model (allow list + deny backstop)
nodes.norm_label: project permission model (allow list + deny backstop)
nodes.rationale: A literal-command allow list plus a deny backstop where denies always win keeps destructive operations blocked even inside worktrees.

nodes.label: Guard changes: one structural round
nodes.rationale: Guard churn was the costliest pattern in the 30-day self-review (28 merges on the write fence alone), so later bypasses go into one residual ticket instead of new PRs.

nodes.label: Monthly self-review
nodes.rationale: A baseline of merges, fix share, guard churn and red-main merges lets each new 30-day window be compared to detect sprawl.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_INITIATIVE drive-to-ship mode
nodes.rationale: Off by default because auto-opening PRs and transitioning tickets is a lot of initiative; users start conservative and reserve all for trusted contexts.

nodes.label: Merging is opt-in rule
nodes.rationale: The auto-ship merge step itself authorizes an autonomous merge, so ARMAUTOMERGE only picks the path and the way to turn merging off is to not enable the step.

nodes.label: /himmel-ops:minerva pipeline
nodes.rationale: A critic between each stage red-teams every artifact before it advances, so design work is hardened before code is written.

nodes.label: Do not rename list
nodes.rationale: Some names are data contracts or high-risk to rename (e.g. one missed cr-pending reader fails open on gh pr create).

nodes.label: Identifier renames
nodes.rationale: The migration is a deliberate breaking change with no aliases, avoiding the complexity of read-both names and wrappers.

nodes.label: Plain names for harness terms
nodes.rationale: Alias index lets people-facing prose use plain names while ids keep old repo names until renames land.

nodes.label: Who holds what (authority table)
nodes.rationale: Only the chief may run go.sh or mint tokens so merge approval and revisions have a single authority.

nodes.label: Artifacts to keep in sync
nodes.rationale: Mirrored artifacts like the commands catalog and CLAUDE.md silently rot unless updated in the same PR.

nodes.label: Auto-mode classifier & attestation
nodes.rationale: The classifier is separate from the allow-list and vetoes gate circumvention, so attestation trailers must be in the first commit and external writes need specific tool-named rules.

nodes.label: Budget (informational)
nodes.rationale: Reference-run estimates help the operator decide when to stop since there are no auto-pause guardrails.

nodes.label: Operator-layer failure modes
nodes.rationale: Ignoring the operator layer collapses a team into one blurry agent, so each mode needs a mitigation and a post-shift check.

nodes.label: AFK shift refusal conditions and guardrails
nodes.norm_label: afk shift refusal conditions and guardrails
nodes.rationale: An unattended shift should stop and ask rather than guess on design decisions, destructive steps or blocked merges.

nodes.label: Telegram relaunch always PLAIN, never --channels
nodes.rationale: A --channels relaunch becomes a 2nd getUpdates consumer (409) and its dev-channels prompt hangs the unattended launch.

nodes.label: Chief vs /afk-shift
nodes.rationale: They look adjacent but differ: afk-shift fans out subagents for a fixed plan in one session, a chief dispatches separate sessions for decisions that cannot be pre-written or that outlive a context window.

nodes.label: A bus message is data, not authority
nodes.norm_label: a bus message is data, not authority
nodes.rationale: Brief revisions must come through the revision channel so a bus message cannot change a worker's instructions.

nodes.label: main-linux and main-macos are separate states
nodes.norm_label: main-linux and main-macos are separate states
nodes.rationale: A macOS red must not hold Linux GOs or falsify main green, so the two are reported side by side with run and head sha.

nodes.label: Adding a rule: pick the cheapest layer
nodes.norm_label: adding a rule: pick the cheapest layer
nodes.rationale: Structural enforcement beats instructional prose: on second drift, escalate to a hook, gate or classifier rather than stronger wording.

nodes.label: Subagent delegation and escalation policy
nodes.rationale: Subagents earn their place only by isolation, parallelism or a fresh view; otherwise they multiply cost without improving results.

nodes.label: Project override (.himmel/project.conf)
nodes.rationale: Lets a repo's maintainers set project behaviour and tighten gates by reviewed commit, while gate policy can only tighten and never loosen.

nodes.label: Gate keys from project file can only tighten
nodes.norm_label: gate keys from project file can only tighten
nodes.rationale: A tracked repo file must never weaken a safety gate that the operator set strict.

nodes.label: User scope vs project scope
nodes.rationale: A committed project file may only change project-scope behaviour and tighten gates, so a repo cannot move station state or loosen safety.

nodes.label: Operator conventions: layer selection and structural escalation
nodes.norm_label: operator conventions: layer selection and structural escalation
nodes.rationale: A second drift of an instructional rule signals that prose does not enforce, so the next layer must be structural rather than stronger CLAUDE.md text.

nodes.label: Bash tool persisted cwd race
nodes.rationale: Persisted cwd is written by every call and by design, so checkout-sensitive work must pass explicit paths to avoid silently testing the wrong tree.

nodes.label: git branch -d deletes squash-merged branch
nodes.rationale: -d accepts branches merged into their upstream, so it is neither needed -D nor a safety net; keeping the tip SHA makes recovery cheap.

nodes.label: Bash tool runs login shell; sourced bash library can run away
nodes.norm_label: bash tool runs login shell; sourced bash library can run away
nodes.rationale: With SHELL set to zsh a bare-sourced bash library runs under zsh and spawned hundreds of core dumps, so CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL or bash -c is needed.

nodes.label: NUL-page corruption after shadow-copy restore
nodes.rationale: Restored files keep size and mtime so git's stat cache hides the corruption; scanning every 4096-byte page and restoring from HEAD repairs it.

nodes.label: Obsidian hangs on bulk file churn in the vault
nodes.norm_label: obsidian hangs on bulk file churn in the vault
nodes.rationale: Obsidian watches every file even excluded ones, so bulk changes pin the renderer; closing it first and keeping generators out of the vault avoids a stale-cache freeze.

nodes.label: obsidian-vault MCP hardcoded 6s timeout
nodes.rationale: A Read timed out is the wrapper's fixed limit rather than evidence of a dead server, so validate via the REST root before falling back.

nodes.label: pre-commit run stashes all unstaged files repo-wide
nodes.norm_label: pre-commit run stashes all unstaged files repo-wide
nodes.rationale: Concurrent gate runs in one shared checkout interleave stash/restore and make siblings' edits vanish, so the gate must be serialized and re-staged.

nodes.label: Python heredoc patching corrupts shell bytes
nodes.norm_label: python heredoc patching corrupts shell bytes
nodes.rationale: Python interprets backslash escapes before the shell sees them, silently inserting control bytes that tests and shellcheck do not catch.

nodes.label: Verify shellcheck bare, never -S warning
nodes.rationale: The gate runs at default severity including info, so a raised floor can report clean on a file the gate rejects.

nodes.label: shellcheck SC2317 vs SC2329 rename
nodes.rationale: Version skew between local and pinned shellcheck means a disable directive must list both codes so neither is pruned.

nodes.label: RETASK block brief template
nodes.rationale: Expansion needs the token while halts and narrowing do not, because doing less is a mild DoS, never a compromise.

nodes.label: Dispatch-time nonce
nodes.rationale: A token minted before any attacker text enters the child context kills tool-result mimicry and, with per-child minting, sibling forgery.

nodes.label: Chief succession (section 3a)
nodes.rationale: Nonces authenticate to one chief, so without a succession rule a correct worker must refuse a legitimate change of chief; it happened twice.

nodes.label: RETASK threat model
nodes.rationale: Identity claims are content the attacker controls, so authentication must rest on something the attacker never saw.

nodes.label: First principle: structural fix over workaround
nodes.norm_label: first principle: structural fix over workaround
nodes.rationale: Reshaping a command to dodge a guardrail is evasion that can harden blocks, so the fix belongs in a hook/CLI or with the operator.

nodes.label: Why this is a playbook, not a CLAUDE.md rule
nodes.norm_label: why this is a playbook, not a claude.md rule
nodes.rationale: Root CLAUDE.md is paid for every session and holds frame-shaping invariants only, so prunable troubleshooting rules load on trigger.

nodes.label: Instance-scoped kills and launch handoff marker
nodes.norm_label: instance-scoped kills and launch handoff marker
nodes.rationale: A machine-wide kill let a test fixture SIGKILL the live production bridge, so kills require cwd or fresh pidfile ownership and a launch marker closes the duplicate-supervisor race.

nodes.label: WS-C — why no --channels
nodes.rationale: The dev-channels acknowledgement prompt never persists and a second getUpdates consumer causes 409, so unattended relaunches would hang or conflict.

nodes.label: Reboot persistence (systemd user unit)
nodes.rationale: A Type=simple unit running restart-bridge.sh run makes systemd track the supervisor, with a start limit to preserve the supervisor's own circuit breaker.

nodes.label: Single-owner rule (one getUpdates consumer per token)
nodes.norm_label: single-owner rule (one getupdates consumer per token)
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows only one long-poll consumer per token, so a second consumer would 409-conflict the poller.

nodes.label: Native Hermes subagent (delegate_task)
nodes.rationale: It is cheap to dispatch but weakly isolated: it is owned by the parent process, creates no worktree and leaves no durable outbox.

nodes.label: Common launcher exit codes
nodes.rationale: A shared exit-code convention lets callers distinguish missing key, egress refusal, seed failure and low balance.

nodes.label: Launcher (thin backend-switch script)
nodes.rationale: Each launcher exports the endpoint and key for the child claude only and uses its own config dir so the normal ~/.claude is never touched and it fails closed.

nodes.label: Kept names and names with no identifier
nodes.norm_label: kept names and names with no identifier
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL_CONSOLE_* markers (OD-1) and HIMMEL_WORKER (a live security marker) are not renamed, and some others carry a different sense.

nodes.label: -F first-commit beats --amend --trailer for attestation
nodes.rationale: git --trailer can append a stray trailing ':' that breaks the end-anchored security regex, so the whole message is written to a file and committed with -F.

nodes.label: Permission prompts come from the static matcher bailing on command shape
nodes.norm_label: permission prompts come from the static matcher bailing on command shape
nodes.rationale: The matcher bails on $var, $(...), backticks and compound operators without reading the allow-list, so the fix is structural via a hook rather than wider allow rules.

nodes.label: Forward every block to Telegram
nodes.rationale: The operator watches Telegram, not the terminal, so denials and questions must be relayed there.

nodes.label: Linux clean install walkthrough (Ubuntu 26.04)
nodes.rationale: It was walked end to end on a guest and quotes real failures verbatim so workarounds are trustworthy until tickets land.

nodes.label: Lockfile gate finds bun itself
nodes.rationale: Hooks inherit the invoking git process's PATH, so commits from SSH, scripts or agents used to die without bun on PATH; the gate now searches known bun locations.

nodes.label: Four install profiles (starter, luna, custom, operator)
nodes.norm_label: four install profiles (starter, luna, custom, operator)
nodes.rationale: Each profile pre-fills answers for a different adoption level while the installer still asks every applicable question.

nodes.label: Scope: project vs user
nodes.rationale: Project scope limits the install to one repo's .claude while user scope applies it once to every project, so the user picks the blast radius.

nodes.label: rtk name collision (Rust Type Kit)
nodes.rationale: implied: a different rtk package (Rust Type Kit) shares the binary name, so a failing rtk gain signals the wrong tool is installed.

nodes.label: Local CLI before MCP server
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context in every session that loads it, while a CLI costs nothing until called.

nodes.label: Five independent enforcement stages
nodes.rationale: Hook, commit, push, CI and merge each see something the others cannot, so important rules are checked at more than one stage.

nodes.label: Goals and non-goals
nodes.rationale: Safety must be structural, work must survive sessions and the model is not assumed trustworthy, so the scope excludes being an agent SDK.

nodes.label: Sanctioned merge script and GO file
nodes.norm_label: sanctioned merge script and go file
nodes.rationale: Reading the trust-path list from the default branch stops a PR from shrinking the list it is judged by.

nodes.label: Opt-in autonomy and passive observability
nodes.rationale: Each autonomy layer is a deliberate choice with an off-switch, and a monitor that guesses is worse than none.

nodes.label: The parts: operator, chief, worker, judge, guardrails, handover, backends
nodes.norm_label: the parts: operator, chief, worker, judge, guardrails, handover, backends
nodes.rationale: Splitting authority across distinct roles means no single session both writes and approves a change.

nodes.label: Revision channel with fail-safe asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Tool output is hostile data; narrowing needs no token because hostile text can only make a worker do less.

nodes.label: Single writer enforced by directory lock
nodes.norm_label: single writer enforced by directory lock
nodes.rationale: Prose coordination between armed sessions failed with duplicate dispatch, and two workers editing one file is a conflict a merge queue cannot untangle.

nodes.label: Structural over instructional
nodes.rationale: Prose in a context window decays with compaction and fails silently, whereas a refusal is observable.

nodes.label: One ticket from file to merge
nodes.norm_label: one ticket from file to merge
nodes.rationale: Each hand-off is a script with its own refusal, so dangerous transitions never rely on convention.

nodes.label: Trust and safety model
nodes.rationale: Assuming sessions can drift or read hostile text, the design bounds what a mistaken session can cost via five stages and separated authority.

nodes.label: Slash chief requests (/fleet, /go, /push, /halt)
nodes.rationale: Malformed reserved verbs refuse terminally and acks say queued, so no handler launches sessions, runs git or grants approval.

nodes.label: Stale command window (TELEGRAM_VERB_MAX_AGE_S)
nodes.rationale: Refusing commands older than 300 seconds prevents replay of queued commands after an outage.

nodes.label: Dormant profile candidates
nodes.rationale: Installs are kept but not enabled, and names are documentation candidates until follow-up work updates catalog-absence test assertions.

nodes.label: Commit gates (ticket reference, conventional format)
nodes.rationale: Every commit must carry a ticket reference and conventional format by default so history stays traceable; the rule can be dropped with commit.tracker none.

nodes.label: telegram-himmel plugin (fork)
nodes.rationale: Gating the getUpdates poller behind TELEGRAM_OWN_POLLER=1 ensures only the owner session polls the single bot-token slot.

nodes.label: Plugin portability classes (standalone, fork, harness-coupled)
nodes.rationale: Telling adopters which plugins assume the harness stops them installing something only useful in himmel context.

nodes.label: Handover and resume
nodes.rationale: Plain markdown handover docs let work and reasons survive the end of a session so users stop re-explaining.

nodes.label: qmd and graphify search
nodes.rationale: They point back to real files instead of extracted facts so the agent's sources stay inspectable.

nodes.label: Second brain and memory (luna vault)
nodes.rationale: Keeps work and decisions in plain linked markdown so the agent's sources can be opened and fixed, with search indexes rebuildable from files.

nodes.label: Honest fallback — discipline until (and after) the guard exists
nodes.norm_label: honest fallback — discipline until (and after) the guard exists
nodes.rationale: No fully clean trusted channel exists in the harness, so discipline plus capability scoping and diff review must carry the load.

nodes.label: Non-goals (§6)
nodes.rationale: The channel adds one narrow pre-declared exception and must not generally soften rejection of out-of-band instructions.

nodes.label: stuck-playbook (guardrail recovery)
nodes.rationale: implied: centralises recovery from guardrail stops.

nodes.label: Linux Grafana/Prometheus user-unit install
nodes.rationale: Installing nothing as root, with sha256-pinned tarballs and loopback-bound systemd user units, limits the privilege and supply-chain surface.

nodes.label: Open question: internal-fleet vs external interop
nodes.norm_label: open question: internal-fleet vs external interop
nodes.rationale: External interop needs authenticated transport and a dedicated uid, so nothing opens a socket until the operator rules.

nodes.label: qmd-quality-cadence
nodes.rationale: A weekly golden-set eval alerts on MRR drift so silent retrieval-quality regressions become visible.

nodes.label: Dedicated worktree at ~/.claude/graph-cadence/<slug>
nodes.rationale: Mutating steps would otherwise switch the branch and dirty the tracked graphify-out of the primary checkout live sessions use; it avoids /tmp so cleanup sweeps cannot orphan worktree registrations.

nodes.label: Standing ticket in publish PR subject
nodes.norm_label: standing ticket in publish pr subject
nodes.rationale: The CI commit-range gate requires a ticket ID on every commit and the old ticketless subjects likely motivated the manual bypass.

nodes.label: Check collection before query; never guess names
nodes.norm_label: check collection before query; never guess names
nodes.rationale: Falling back to ls/grep guessing silently reverts to pre-HIMMEL-33 behaviour, so a missing collection must trigger rebuild instead (HIMMEL-2222).

nodes.label: Concurrency guard
nodes.rationale: Auto-save races are last-write-wins and silently lose mutations, so the skill hashes before appending and fails closed.

nodes.label: Injection boundary
nodes.rationale: Clippings content is untrusted and injection-suspect notes are excluded, so source bodies are treated as inert data.

nodes.label: Quote guard
nodes.rationale: Verifying quotes verbatim before drafting prevents invented positions being attributed to past-you.

nodes.label: Deterministic topic key and rerun dedup
nodes.norm_label: deterministic topic key and rerun dedup
nodes.rationale: One deterministic key drives selection, heading, ordering and dedup so reruns cannot bypass the duplicate guard.

nodes.label: Confidence floor
nodes.rationale: Single-source or same-window evidence is noise; Pattern 2 is exempt from the domain rule because authors are inherently single-platform (HIMMEL-242).

nodes.label: Counting invariant (LUNA-43)
nodes.rationale: Write emits the file in one shot, so the evidence count must be computed from the finalised list before writing to avoid mismatched headers.

nodes.label: 14-day dedup window and deterministic slugs
nodes.rationale: Same pattern and subject yield the same slug so reruns do not duplicate proposals.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Dry-run must never write, so the agent aborts with a contract-violation error if it does.

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate (HIMMEL-1137)
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state, and synthesizing over it would produce patterns from corrupted evidence.

nodes.label: Four pattern-detection lenses
nodes.rationale: Concept clusters, author convergence, tag overpopulation and folder pressure each surface a distinct kind of vault restructuring signal.

nodes.label: Substantive-content gate (LUNA-43)
nodes.rationale: 8 of 20 synthesis pages were template-only boilerplate, which is dead weight at scale.

nodes.label: Known issues (audit cycle 2026-05-25)
nodes.rationale: implied: heuristic tag inference, grep-based proximity and Obsidian auto-save races need calibration on real clips.

nodes.label: claudex lane on a test VM
nodes.norm_label: claudex lane on a test vm
nodes.rationale: Lane proof runs off-station on one guest through the queue lock and guest-exec, with ssh pinned to known_hosts and refusal on any failed preflight so no unsafe session runs.

nodes.label: claudex guest
nodes.rationale: A linked clone isolates the claudex lane, with Codex login done by the operator inside the guest and auto permission mode instead of skip-permissions.

nodes.label: qmd-cadence scheduler
nodes.rationale: Scheduled at 05:00 after the vault-writing pipeline jobs so the reindex picks up their output instead of racing them.

nodes.label: qmd reindex runner
nodes.rationale: The completeness assert exists because qmd embed can hit its session cap and exit 0 with only part embedded, leaving a silently stale index.

nodes.label: Record-once model check
nodes.rationale: Replaying a recorded model artifact avoids paying a model call on every VM e2e run.

nodes.label: Floor
nodes.rationale: Some deterministic minimum must hold even when all other layers are absent.

nodes.label: Branch-aware force-with-lease rule
nodes.rationale: The hook only inspects the command string, so any ambiguous target such as HEAD, a variable or a non-origin remote is refused while explicit non-default origin branches are granted.

nodes.label: Scoped suite evidence default
nodes.rationale: The full-tree run takes a machine-wide lock (measured 2h20m with six workers waiting), so a scoped run on a different lock finishes in minutes.

nodes.label: SUITE_LOCK_WAIT queued vs parked distinction
nodes.rationale: A visible WAITING line distinguishes a queued worker (needs patience) from a parked one (needs a nudge), avoiding second-writer races from wrong nudges.

nodes.label: Duration knobs treat 0 or malformed as default; on/off switches honor 0
nodes.norm_label: duration knobs treat 0 or malformed as default; on/off switches honor 0
nodes.rationale: GNU timeout 0 disables the limit, so a zero duration would silently disable its guard, whereas explicit switches and the SUITE_LOCK_WAIT budget are sanctioned to take 0.

nodes.label: Real sleep reachable from test config is a hang waiting to happen
nodes.norm_label: real sleep reachable from test config is a hang waiting to happen
nodes.rationale: A sleeping suite is indistinguishable from a stuck one, so waits go through an injectable sleep command and timeouts act as a backstop turning hangs into verdicts.

nodes.label: ci:macos label and filtered suites dispatch
nodes.norm_label: ci:macos label and filtered suites dispatch
nodes.rationale: A full macOS run is 8 shards and 70-110 min and red from unrelated suites, so a fix worker proves only its own suites.

nodes.label: Failed suite retried once; pass on retry is a FLAKE
nodes.norm_label: failed suite retried once; pass on retry is a flake
nodes.rationale: Classifying retry-passes as flakes and ledgering them keeps them visible instead of silently counted as green.

nodes.label: macOS shell-unit on its own cadence
nodes.norm_label: macos shell-unit on its own cadence
nodes.rationale: Separating macOS into its own scheduled workflow keeps macOS reds from reddening CI or main and keeps PRs from spending macOS shards.

nodes.label: Scan roots — what the corpus covers
nodes.norm_label: scan roots — what the corpus covers
nodes.rationale: The '.' root is an include list so local runs do not collect worktree copies, so new top-level test trees must be added explicitly.

nodes.label: Machine-wide suite lock
nodes.rationale: Concurrent runs test the same tree and starve each other, so a second run refuses and names the holder.

nodes.label: Resume rotation (SUITE_ROTATE)
nodes.rationale: Sorted discovery meant a truncated run dropped the same 207-suite tail forever, so the next run starts where the last stopped, which makes the blind spot temporary.

nodes.label: Whole-run budget
nodes.rationale: Measurement showed the 7200s budget bounds an ordinary run (381 suites, only 174 reached), and a truncated run exits non-zero so it never reads as green.

nodes.label: Suite stdin isolation
nodes.rationale: No suite should be able to block an unattended run on a prompt or consume the remaining suite list.

nodes.label: Visible lock wait (SUITE_LOCK_WAIT)
nodes.rationale: A queued worker was indistinguishable from a parked one, and mixing them up can cause a second-writer race, so the wait prints a heartbeat naming the holder.

nodes.label: SKIP_LIST runner-gap ledger
nodes.rationale: Entries are repo-root-relative so they stay root-invariant and avoid basename over-reach; the README points to the live ledger because a duplicate copy drifts.

nodes.label: SUITE_REQUIRE_TOOL
nodes.rationale: Tool-only blockers run wherever the tool exists rather than being dead weight in SKIP_LIST.

nodes.label: SUITE_TIER declarative corpus reduction
nodes.rationale: Heavy suites are marked extended so per-PR runs stay fast without dropping them from the corpus.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit a pin
nodes.rationale: apply-drift-bump.sh moves the pin literal and synced_base together, refuses downgrades and restores files on error, which manual edits would defeat.

nodes.label: 72-hour release-age gate
nodes.rationale: implied: letting a release age before bumping avoids pinning to a very new, possibly bad release.

nodes.label: Operator-gated fork push
nodes.rationale: Pushing moves a branch on a remote the operator owns and an audited rebase is not the same as a human agreeing to publish it.

nodes.label: Never bump synced_base without a rebase
nodes.norm_label: never bump synced_base without a rebase
nodes.rationale: Bumping synced_base alone claims the fork carries an upstream base it never rebased onto and silences the drift guard while drift grows.

nodes.label: Fork branch protection ruleset
nodes.rationale: Approvals stay at 0 because the single operator account cannot approve its own PR and required reviews would block CLEAN merge state; chief GO and the judge are the review.

nodes.label: apply-drift-bump
nodes.rationale: Moves the pin literal and synced_base together and restores both byte-identical on failure so the pin never half-updates.

nodes.label: Upstream drift-fix cadence
nodes.rationale: It is the repair half of the detect-only fork-drift Action and runs locally because the private repo has Actions off by design (operator decision 2026-07-28).

nodes.label: resync-fork
nodes.rationale: Bumping synced_base would claim a base the fork never rebased onto, so it rebases in a scratch clone and audits that the delta stays additive.

nodes.label: Wizard coverage gap table (12 delta items)
nodes.norm_label: wizard coverage gap table (12 delta items)
nodes.rationale: Classifying each item as covered, ticketed or NOT-TICKETED lets the parent file tickets for uncovered gaps.

nodes.label: adopter-project / adopter-user install profiles
nodes.rationale: They carry concrete runnable values with no placeholders so himmelctl install --scope works first try on a bare checkout.

nodes.label: operator.install-profile.json
nodes.rationale: It is a reference artifact proving the v2 schema captures a fully loaded install, so machine paths are placeholders and it is not runnable as-is.

nodes.label: Caller-side policing of HIMMEL_UNINSTALL_REAL_HOME=1
nodes.rationale: A runtime refusal on fence-lifted-plus-override was rejected because it is indistinguishable from the legitimate wizard teardown, so the rule is enforced statically at callers via a mktemp-HOME check and allowlist.

nodes.label: uninstall.sh wet-run REAL_HOME fence
nodes.rationale: A 2026-09-03 incident where a mutation-test run swept the operator's real HOME showed that destructive runs the hook pipeline never sees need a self-carried guard.

nodes.label: Cadences armed by hand (not in wizard)
nodes.norm_label: cadences armed by hand (not in wizard)
nodes.rationale: These jobs are niche or riskier, so they are armed directly with the same verbs rather than offered by the wizard.

nodes.label: --semantic step exit-code classification
nodes.rationale: A skip is not a recovery, so benign skips (rc 3, 4) leave standing alerts while only a clean rc 0 clears them and real failures alert.

nodes.label: macOS breakage metric
nodes.rationale: Recording suites newly red versus the previous cadence run makes macOS regressions countable, with infra_suspect flagging incomplete lists.

nodes.label: A nightly OS red is a split slice, never a hold
nodes.norm_label: a nightly os red is a split slice, never a hold
nodes.rationale: No per-PR all-OS proof exists, so a PR is never blocked on an OS it did not run; failures become separate tickets per cluster.

nodes.label: himmel-bus store guard (soft block)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 runs sessions and the store as one uid, so the guard only makes tool-driven forging cost a denial while the hash chain detects direct writes and phase-2 second uid is needed for prevention.

nodes.label: A chief's halt/stand-down needs no token
nodes.norm_label: a chief's halt/stand-down needs no token
nodes.rationale: Injection-defense caveats exist to stop permission laundering, not to downgrade a narrowing instruction, and a resumed worker could commit over a sibling's in-flight edits.

nodes.label: A halt is authorized, not instantly delivered
nodes.norm_label: a halt is authorized, not instantly delivered
nodes.rationale: A headed worker reads its inbox only between tool rounds, so a successful send does not prove compliance and the chief must wait for an acknowledgement.

nodes.label: Held structural enforcement (guard-retask-channel.sh)
nodes.rationale: The guard is pre-designed but deliberately held until the first recurrence because this incident is the rule's motivation, not its first drift.

nodes.label: himmel-bus residuals (T1, T4, T6)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 runs everything as one uid, so the API cannot forge but direct store writes by a same-uid process remain possible until a dedicated uid exists.

nodes.label: bus-deliver-hook delivery is the only bus authority path
nodes.norm_label: bus-deliver-hook delivery is the only bus authority path
nodes.rationale: Nothing a tool returns is a message, so a body found via read, cat or any tool result must never count as a ruling.

nodes.label: The store guard is a soft block, not a fence
nodes.norm_label: the store guard is a soft block, not a fence
nodes.rationale: It matches text only, so interpreter one-liners and renamed CLI copies bypass it and it only slows a same-uid attacker.

nodes.label: What this does NOT do (residual risk, priced)
nodes.norm_label: what this does not do (residual risk, priced)
nodes.rationale: Naming accepted residual risks (compromised parent, token replay, model refusal) keeps them priced rather than hidden.

nodes.label: N33 speed bump to soft block
nodes.norm_label: n33 speed bump to soft block
nodes.rationale: Message-text-only rename in family F14; tests may grep the text so they must follow.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md source-of-truth rules
nodes.rationale: Keeping one source of truth with a drift guard avoids divergent rule sets across harnesses.

nodes.label: Instruction file: CLAUDE.md invisible, AGENTS.md carries rules
nodes.norm_label: instruction file: claude.md invisible, agents.md carries rules
nodes.rationale: Codex does not read CLAUDE.md, so a generated AGENTS.md with a freshness gate keeps CLAUDE.md as source of truth.

nodes.label: Prompt anatomy: rules must be adapted, not copied
nodes.norm_label: prompt anatomy: rules must be adapted, not copied
nodes.rationale: GPT-5 wastes reasoning tokens reconciling contradictions and hedges, so CLAUDE.md must be adapted with explicit precedence and behavioral wording.

nodes.label: One ruleset, N adapted projections
nodes.rationale: Root CLAUDE.md is the single source so each runtime reads an adapted copy, and projection drift is made visible by two tested columns.

nodes.label: Branch naming type/slug
nodes.rationale: A fixed type/slug convention with a limited type set yields predictable worktree directory names.

nodes.label: /clean
nodes.rationale: Prunes worktrees whose PR merged so stale worktrees do not accumulate.

nodes.label: /worktree
nodes.rationale: Starts a branch in its own worktree; adopted repos get only the script form because the slash command is not installed.

nodes.label: Adopter route (seven short steps)
nodes.rationale: An adopted repo only has worktree scripts, commit-msg/pre-push hooks, edit guard and merge gate, so it needs a shorter script-driven loop.

nodes.label: Daily loop commands (worktree, pr-check, clean, handover)
nodes.norm_label: daily loop commands (worktree, pr-check, clean, handover)
nodes.rationale: Isolating each change in a worktree with gated commit, push and review keeps main safe.

nodes.label: Fresh worktree lacks node_modules outside scripts/jira
nodes.norm_label: fresh worktree lacks node_modules outside scripts/jira
nodes.rationale: Only Jira deps are installed so other suites skip or fail in ways that look pre-existing; check the runner exists before calling it pre-existing.

nodes.label: Symptom: /worktree refuses branch or stale worktree lingers
nodes.norm_label: symptom: /worktree refuses branch or stale worktree lingers
nodes.rationale: Re-creating a worktree on a merged branch usually re-opens closed work, and pruning can discard uncommitted work, so both stay explicit.

nodes.label: C42-sweep-health check
nodes.rationale: Catches lost commits and stuck worktrees the prune sweep would otherwise skip silently, never reporting a false clean.

nodes.label: Guardrail hooks
nodes.rationale: A hook refusing the tool call cannot fall out of the context window like a prompt rule, so rules hold during long sessions.

nodes.label: himmel_agent SOUL markers
nodes.rationale: The SOUL is written for a GPT-anatomy model (precedence ladder, spec tags), not an open-model JSON-obedience style, and a test asserts this.

nodes.label: Axis 3: SOUL/persona
nodes.rationale: The senior SOUL hardcodes Codex as provider, so a new lane under it inherits a false provider claim.

nodes.label: Hard limits (untrusted data, secrets, confirm irreversible)
nodes.norm_label: hard limits (untrusted data, secrets, confirm irreversible)
nodes.rationale: These safety rules sit above identity and habit on the ladder so they hold for any lower-ranked instruction.

nodes.label: himmel mindset (six working rules)
nodes.rationale: Think-first, simplicity, surgical changes, goal-driven loops, maker is not checker and single writer per artifact keep autonomous work verifiable and conflict-free.

nodes.label: Precedence ladder
nodes.rationale: Contradictory directives waste a GPT-anatomy agent's reasoning tokens, so an explicit ladder (operator turn, context rules file, hard limits, SOUL, habit) resolves them.

nodes.label: Context-budget evidence audit (2026-10-02)
nodes.rationale: No profile has three attributable measured workers, so every contextBudget is retained until worker-burn lines carry a profile field.

nodes.label: Symptom: worker-burn.sh denied [Session Transcript Tampering]
nodes.rationale: The classifier reads a script opening transcripts as tampering though it only reads them, so the operator runs it instead.

nodes.label: Hook integrity
nodes.rationale: Pinning guards to committed blob hashes at session start stops an agent editing a guard mid-session.

nodes.label: Anchor-tamper class in worker write fence
nodes.norm_label: anchor-tamper class in worker write fence
nodes.rationale: Re-pinning off origin/<default> makes that ref security-relevant, so workers must be denied commands that could forge it.

nodes.label: Class (i): unanchored keyword/substring scan
nodes.rationale: A broad unanchored substring net is accepted, with overmatch on commit messages, because it fails closed and is the sole defence against remote repointing.

nodes.label: Class (ii): refspec destination gate
nodes.rationale: Gating on the refspec destination rather than enumerating remote spellings removes an axis that was defeated four times.

nodes.label: Declared residual (open) and signed hook-generation manifest
nodes.norm_label: declared residual (open) and signed hook-generation manifest
nodes.rationale: The fence is cheap coverage not closure, so gaps are stated explicitly and closure is planned via a signed manifest.

nodes.label: Fail-closed remote-set lookup for <a>/<b> destinations
nodes.rationale: Failing open when the remote set cannot be established would hand a bypass to any worker that could make the lookup fail.

nodes.label: Hook-integrity pin: monotonic re-pin
nodes.rationale: A session-start-absolute pin hard-blocked every running session after a legitimate hook merge to main, so the pin now re-pins when the change provably reached the trusted branch.

nodes.label: Three re-pin conditions (tip match, ancestor anchor, reachable prior blob)
nodes.norm_label: three re-pin conditions (tip match, ancestor anchor, reachable prior blob)
nodes.rationale: Requiring all three keeps re-pinning monotonic and rejects rewinds, unrelated content and unmerged feature-ahead edits.

nodes.label: Round 4: tokenised remote verb and stripped command-token anchor
nodes.norm_label: round 4: tokenised remote verb and stripped command-token anchor
nodes.rationale: Tokenising and anchoring on the stripped command token removes the adjacency and quoting axes instead of naming option or quote forms.

nodes.label: Hook integrity bypass for editing scripts/hooks
nodes.norm_label: hook integrity bypass for editing scripts/hooks
nodes.rationale: The integrity guard treats uncommitted hook edits as tampering, so a narrowly scoped, audited bypass anchored to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and a linked worktree lets legitimate edits proceed without opening a hole for workers.

nodes.label: PR plan job gating and matrix sizing
nodes.norm_label: pr plan job gating and matrix sizing
nodes.rationale: Skipping path-pure jobs and empty shard setup saves runners while failures of the plan default to running everything and sentinels keep required contexts reporting.

nodes.label: Shard assignment — duration ledger
nodes.rationale: Shards decide alone, so fallbacks are only safe when every shard takes them; any other failure refuses to avoid a false-green partition with duplicated or missing suites.

nodes.label: luna-correlate server
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the pilot because migration risk is low with 5 tools and custom validation retained.

nodes.label: Constraint-comment encoding offer
nodes.rationale: Encoding a do-not-remove constraint in a type, test or lint makes it enforceable so the comment becomes deletable.

nodes.label: Deviations from pinned upstream pstack skill
nodes.norm_label: deviations from pinned upstream pstack skill
nodes.rationale: Listing deviations lets a future re-sync check each one before overwriting the vendored copy.

nodes.label: COMMENT-REVIEW output contract
nodes.rationale: A fixed finding format and final count line let /pr-check parse results mechanically.

nodes.label: himmel-ops:comment-review agent (sonnet)
nodes.rationale: It has only Read, Grep and Glob and reports without deleting, keeping the review read-only and leaving adjudication to the main session.

nodes.label: himmel-bus server
nodes.rationale: Built new on v2 so it is not a remaining v1 migration.

nodes.label: Tasks and elicitation (protocol 2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: The next target revision adds tasks and elicitation, so per-server status is tracked as unverified unless a source file proves otherwise.

nodes.label: Relay authority limits (what you hold vs chief)
nodes.norm_label: relay authority limits (what you hold vs chief)
nodes.rationale: Only the chief holds GO and nonce authority, so the relay and judges hold only their own doc locks.

nodes.label: Escalation-mandatory event classes
nodes.rationale: Forwarding a FINDING, CR disposition, READY, operator message or non-lane BLOCKED as a plain RUN note is the misclassification failure mode.

nodes.label: Ops hand-back verdict line format
nodes.rationale: A single fixed-phrase verdict line keeps script output as data so free text never reaches the chief as an instruction.

nodes.label: Decision: the ops lane is the relay
nodes.norm_label: decision: the ops lane is the relay
nodes.rationale: The relay already has the right authority shape (no chief lock, no go.sh, no token sends, no inbox writes) and an escalation transport; a fresh judge-style child per script was rejected because it pays the first-turn floor every time.

nodes.label: Waiter
nodes.rationale: A single silent background command that exits on the first real event keeps the chief's wait cheap.

nodes.label: holds= and hreg= holds register signals
nodes.norm_label: holds= and hreg= holds register signals
nodes.rationale: A repeated BLOCKED bullet never moves tails=, so holds= is the only signal that a ruling may be owed.

nodes.label: Waiter launch permission rule
nodes.rationale: The allow rule is narrow with no glob before the path so a quote-spanning glob cannot let an arbitrary command match, and the chief never re-spells to dodge a refusal.

nodes.label: Telegram inbox and voice-authority limits
nodes.rationale: Operator rulings can reach a running chief from Telegram, but unverified voice lines and a 'yes' carry limited authority so they never change permissions or skip GO verification.

nodes.label: Phase 2b: page, ack, refuse re-dispatch
nodes.rationale: Paging once per rise, recording acks and refusing re-dispatch ensures a parked worker is acknowledged without sending sensitive fields off-host.

nodes.label: Cloud-init seed
nodes.rationale: The seed ISO is built with pycdlib so the host needs no genisoimage or sudo, and the password never leaks via argv, history or env.

nodes.label: Warn-only RED-control lint
nodes.rationale: It exits 0 always so a heuristic text-matcher cannot become an accidental gate, while flagging mutation controls that print RED confirmed without proving anything.

nodes.label: Five enforcement layers
nodes.rationale: Each stage sees something the others cannot, so invariants are checked where cheapest and the important ones twice.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker flow
nodes.rationale: The marker is advisory at push but a hard block at PR creation, so review is never skipped and reviewable docs are never zero-CR.

nodes.label: Cross-model review (Codex as second family)
nodes.rationale: A second model family (OpenAI GPT via Codex) makes review a cross-check rather than Claude grading its own work.

nodes.label: Finding severity and rulings (fixed/disproved/deferred)
nodes.rationale: Critical and Important findings block until fixed, disproved, or deferred with a ticket key, so nothing is silently dropped.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes (hard vs best-effort)
nodes.rationale: A hard reviewer must pass at the PR head while best-effort only holds on an open finding, which separates required from advisory review.

nodes.label: Session-sticky bypass convention
nodes.rationale: Claude cannot inject env vars into hook processes, so bypass vars must be set in the shell that launched Claude Code.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker pre-PR-create guard
nodes.rationale: Blocking gh pr create while a review-owed marker exists enforces review before PR; cwd-first repo resolution fixes foreign clones being un-gated and same-named branches false-blocking.

nodes.label: Hook timeout policy and latency SLO
nodes.norm_label: hook timeout policy and latency slo
nodes.rationale: An unset timeout inherits 600 s and a timed-out PreToolUse hook fails OPEN, so explicit measured 15 s / 60 s tiers bound hangs without firing under normal load.

nodes.label: Pre-push gate delivery: push from the branch's own worktree
nodes.norm_label: pre-push gate delivery: push from the branch's own worktree
nodes.rationale: Pre-push hooks lint the pusher's cwd tree, not the pushed commits, so pushing from the primary checkout lints main's files and fails OPEN; comparing the SHA to the worktree HEAD closes it.

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse hooks
nodes.rationale: Guardrail scripts fire before tool calls so risky operations are blocked structurally rather than by instruction; some are shipped via the plugin to avoid a settings self-mod veto.

nodes.label: SLO p95 < 1 s per hook
nodes.rationale: Measured ~7x load spread on Windows process start justifies the 15 s bound rather than a tight multiple of p95.

nodes.label: Cheap-lane branch provenance: codex/* convention
nodes.rationale: Absence of a marker is never inferred as cheap-lane, so the codex/ prefix serves as the positive provenance marker until a structural record exists.

nodes.label: CR gate enforcement matrix
nodes.rationale: Shows which harness reaches which review gate, since git hooks fire for any harness that runs real git.

nodes.label: Lane gate (merge review for Codex branches)
nodes.norm_label: lane gate (merge review for codex branches)
nodes.rationale: A cheaper implementation lane is reviewed by a Claude-family validating session because a worker never grades its own work.

nodes.label: Lane rubric R1-R4
nodes.rationale: Catches behavioral degradation of cheaper models (scope, attestation honesty, convention drift, self-report mismatch) that structural guards miss.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker rewritten on nearly every push
nodes.norm_label: review-owed marker rewritten on nearly every push
nodes.rationale: Code pushes write lane full and docs-only pushes write docs-audit, so the marker must be cleared only after the final push to avoid a follow-up commit re-blocking.

nodes.label: CHANGELOG generator
nodes.rationale: CHANGELOG is regenerate-on-demand rather than per-commit to avoid guaranteed merge conflicts, with --check providing a visible staleness surface.

nodes.label: Compaction-time Live state snapshot for audit
nodes.norm_label: compaction-time live state snapshot for audit
nodes.rationale: Recording what state was at compaction lets restoration be audited rather than trusted, with preservation unverified treated as a loss.

nodes.label: Chief rules stay in prose and hooks
nodes.norm_label: chief rules stay in prose and hooks
nodes.rationale: Rules are code reviewed in the repo, while tunable numbers move to config and live state stays in the fleet manifest.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_FLEET_CAP as gate policy
nodes.rationale: Raising the cap loosens a safety limit, so it lives in config.json policy where the launching env cannot raise it.

nodes.label: Gate-policy precedence (config.json only)
nodes.rationale: Policy ignores the process env and himmel.conf because only files guarded against agent writes may change a gate, so env prefixes cannot loosen review.

nodes.label: Why split by key class (both options)
nodes.norm_label: why split by key class (both options)
nodes.rationale: A vault-tracked file alone fails adopters without luna and config.json alone is unreviewable and env-overridable, so each key class gets the fitting home.

nodes.label: Salus ollama-cloud opt-in trust root
nodes.rationale: Sending PHI to ollama-cloud is an operator-only call, so defense in depth (symlink refusal, write guard) surrounds the config grant.

nodes.label: Crashed holder and crossed trust-file holders
nodes.norm_label: crashed holder and crossed trust-file holders
nodes.rationale: A crashed holder's lock blocks files until the 6-hour TTL and proven death, so explicit exits (grant, reap-dead sweep, force release, WRITE_HOLD_OK) are needed to avoid deadlock.

nodes.label: HOLD-ASK and the write barrier
nodes.rationale: Denying writes onto files held by another live worker or open PR prevents conflicts, with grant routes (any, chief, operator) matched to how sensitive the path is.

nodes.label: On-demand MCP server registry
nodes.rationale: Servers in ~/.claude.json load into every session and cost tool schemas everywhere, and obsidian-vault and graphify had zero calls in 14 days.

nodes.label: Secrets kept out of profile files
nodes.norm_label: secrets kept out of profile files
nodes.rationale: Profiles carry absolute home paths and must never hold keys in git, so secrets go to 0600 files injected at launch.

nodes.label: --strict-mcp-config lean launch lever
nodes.rationale: Lazy per-server spawn is not supported by Claude Code, and this flag is the one verified way to load only named servers.

nodes.label: MCP fleet tiered lean profiles
nodes.rationale: Every session spawns the full MCP fleet and lazy spawn is unsupported upstream, so --strict-mcp-config profiles load only the servers a lane needs.

nodes.label: MCP fleet-map tier admission (T1/T2/T3/TX)
nodes.rationale: Requiring each MCP admission to name its tier keeps local process counts bounded and prefers CLI-first where no server is needed.

nodes.label: Build artifacts gitignored (jira/bitbucket dist)
nodes.rationale: dist/ is TypeScript build output that is not tracked, so a fresh clone fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND until built.

nodes.label: TOOL-LOADED vs PROCESS-ENV vs SESSION-ONLY variables
nodes.norm_label: tool-loaded vs process-env vs session-only variables
nodes.rationale: Variables reach code differently (CLIs read the file, hooks read the live env), so documenting the split prevents the 'set it in .env but nothing happened' failure.

nodes.label: First push refusals (npm, scripts/jira audit, CR gate)
nodes.norm_label: first push refusals (npm, scripts/jira audit, cr gate)
nodes.rationale: Each refusal on the first push is a real gate with a named remediation, so expecting a few rounds avoids misreading them as bugs.

nodes.label: himmelctl install wizard
nodes.rationale: One wizard that walks the same question set and derives the right underlying command replaces the old adopter/contributor role fork.

nodes.label: Hook scope: user vs project
nodes.rationale: Universal safety hooks must apply to every session while himmel-dev-only hooks only make sense inside the repo, and duplication is idempotent and benign.

nodes.label: npm 11 requirement for pushing (apt npm 9.2 expired key)
nodes.norm_label: npm 11 requirement for pushing (apt npm 9.2 expired key)
nodes.rationale: apt's npm 9.2 has an expired registry key (2025-01-29) that makes npm audit signatures fail with EEXPIREDSIGNATUREKEY on every push, so npm 11 is pinned.

nodes.label: PHI vault .salus marker
nodes.rationale: The marker makes the claude-codex launcher refuse to start with no override from inside PHI-bearing directories.

nodes.label: qmd search bootstrap
nodes.rationale: qmd installs from a pinned local clone of a carried fork rather than bun add -g because that path EPERM-wedges and bun blocks postinstall scripts.

nodes.label: Required environment (foundational tools)
nodes.rationale: setup.sh verifies these tools at step 0 and fails fast with install hints, so the doc lists the minimum versions and why each is needed.

nodes.label: Wizard lanes question (codex/hermes review-only)
nodes.rationale: v1 ships Claude tiers as the only implementation lanes, so codex and hermes are offered only as cross-model review lanes and selecting one at the prompt is explicit consent.

nodes.label: Required .env values walkthrough
nodes.rationale: Per-variable help (what it is, where to get it) saves the operator from reading .env.example before filling each field.

nodes.label: AFK sudo approval flow with notice bot and TOTP
nodes.norm_label: afk sudo approval flow with notice bot and totp
nodes.rationale: A separate notice bot, root-owned helper and authenticator code ensure a session can request but never self-approve a privileged command.

nodes.label: Station config restore via Telegram (/config backups, restore)
nodes.norm_label: station config restore via telegram (/config backups, restore)
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator recover a deleted or key-losing station config remotely, gated by a TOTP code so a stolen chat alone cannot restore.

nodes.label: Golden image snapshotted unpersonalised
nodes.rationale: Re-de-personalising before snapshotting prevents shipping a personalised image with the machine-id/host-key collision v3 was cut to fix.

nodes.label: Linked clone inherits machine-id and host keys
nodes.norm_label: linked clone inherits machine-id and host keys
nodes.rationale: Shipping an unpersonalised golden image with a first-boot regeneration oneshot makes each clone create its own identity, so a clone baseline must be snapshotted after first boot.

nodes.label: Netplan matches on interface name, not MAC
nodes.norm_label: netplan matches on interface name, not mac
nodes.rationale: VBoxManage clonevm regenerates MACs so a MAC-pinned netplan gave every clone a NIC matching nothing (no DHCP, no ssh).

nodes.label: newest-good.tsv maintained snapshots
nodes.rationale: vm-maintain records the newest maintenance snapshot per VM and prunes only maint-* names so baseline snapshots survive.

nodes.label: No GUI in the guest
nodes.rationale: With no display manager or X server a guest clipboard round trip is unachievable, so workers should not waste effort verifying one.

nodes.label: Snapshot restore reverts machine config
nodes.rationale: A per-clone modifyvm fix would be silently undone by the next restore, so only image-level fixes persist.

nodes.label: Older suite-ready snapshots kept deliberately
nodes.rationale: himmel-ar-1's linked-clone disk chain still runs back through v1-v3, so deleting them would break the clone.

nodes.label: suite-ready-v4 default snapshot (HIMMEL-2738/2681/2747)
nodes.rationale: v4 adds guest additions, clipboard/drag-and-drop config, auto-login and node 24/bun runtimes to close the runtime-skew precondition of HIMMEL-2681.

nodes.label: suite-ready-v4 vs suite-ready-v4-auth
nodes.rationale: The credential-bearing v4-auth snapshot must never be cloned so OAuth credentials are not replicated into another VM.

nodes.label: Vacuous-pass trap for the next migration (v4 to v5)
nodes.norm_label: vacuous-pass trap for the next migration (v4 to v5)
nodes.rationale: A snapshot named for a new version on a clone with old guest content reports green while measuring stale software, and hand-upgrading a clone is rejected because it drifts from the golden image.

nodes.label: vm baseline snapshot and golden-image rails
nodes.norm_label: vm baseline snapshot and golden-image rails
nodes.rationale: Preserves the safety rails around ubuntu_new snapshots, clone creation and golden image rebuilds so operators do not reintroduce past image-level faults.

nodes.label: Tool-call census
nodes.rationale: It fills the per-session tool-call and error visibility gap using existing transcripts, with no live instrumentation.

nodes.label: Guardrail scope: global vs project
nodes.rationale: himmel ships the three guardrails at project level, so user-level copies would fire twice and a managed block keeps exactly one layer active.

nodes.label: Single-writer opt-out marker
nodes.rationale: Personal repos that commit straight to main need to bypass the on-main edit block locally, so the marker is gitignored and never propagates to clones.

nodes.label: AFK overnight-mode trust boundary
nodes.rationale: The persisted next-session file is untrusted input, so only the phrase in the current-turn user prompt may authorize the autonomous 11-phase run.

nodes.label: Highest-index N = M+1 numbering
nodes.rationale: count+1 would overwrite an existing file when numbering has gaps, which violates the append-only requirement.

nodes.label: One numbered next-session file per worker rule (HIMMEL-1830)
nodes.norm_label: one numbered next-session file per worker rule (himmel-1830)
nodes.rationale: Relaunch loads a single file, so splitting state and orders across two files orphans one half and breaks worker numbering.

nodes.label: Route learnings to skill edits (step 5a)
nodes.rationale: Learnings need an owner, so accepted skill-edit proposals go into one Jira ticket per session instead of being applied by a resumed worker in its own PR.

nodes.label: /lanes
nodes.rationale: Prints lanes actually available on this machine since the invariant delegation policy lives in CLAUDE.md, not machine state.

nodes.label: Lane dormancy (no defaultImplLane)
nodes.rationale: lanes.json deliberately has no defaultImplLane so unqualified impl dispatches refuse toward the native subagent path rather than silently picking a lane.

nodes.label: Lane routing & delegation
nodes.rationale: Delegation goes down Claude tiers by default; external lanes are gated and dormant unless explicitly opted in so no lane is silently picked.

nodes.label: Lanes registry and probes
nodes.rationale: Each lane declares a probe and quota so /lanes can report what is actually available on this machine, and a pre-commit guard keeps the volatile inventory out of CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Chief helper subagent model/effort table
nodes.rationale: Raising effort before tier and naming the model per helper kind controls spend, and dispatch guards read the call's model not the frontmatter.

nodes.label: Operator-ruled Opus classes
nodes.rationale: Audits, docs work, mockups and spec critics were about 87% of chief general-purpose Opus spend under standing operator rulings, so a tier move alone cannot cut spend and duplicate audits must be avoided.

nodes.label: Fable model-override deny on Agent (guard-agent-model.sh)
nodes.rationale: Fable was retired as judge default because Opus 5.5 high measured about 2.7x cheaper per verdict, and a model override on an in-process Agent call would silently bypass the frontmatter tier.

nodes.label: Agent dispatch must name a model (guard-subagent-model.sh)
nodes.norm_label: agent dispatch must name a model (guard-subagent-model.sh)
nodes.rationale: An unnamed model silently bills the parent tier, so every typed agent except fork must name one.

nodes.label: Escalation shape (Opus parent spawns Fable child)
nodes.norm_label: escalation shape (opus parent spawns fable child)
nodes.rationale: Fable is limited-release and conserved, so it handles planning and judgment while implementation goes to lower lanes.

nodes.label: Fold or delegate main-loop test
nodes.rationale: Following Anthropic guidance, a subagent is kept only for measured context bloat, parallel fresh-window work or a fresh view, and the fleet is split by context not problem type.

nodes.label: v1 lane scope (operator ruling 34)
nodes.rationale: A wizard/installer scoping decision limits v1 implementation lanes to Claude tiers, with other lanes available only on operator opt-in, based on user requests.

nodes.label: Merge-trust column is a view, not the trust gate
nodes.norm_label: merge-trust column is a view, not the trust gate
nodes.rationale: The trust verdict belongs to the lane gate, so the index only checks the column exists and a green row is a composite, not a ruling.

nodes.label: CI promotion path
nodes.rationale: implied: workflow_dispatch-only CI is advisory until it proves stability by consecutive green runs, speed and no open flaky quarantines.

nodes.label: Data-egress-safe gate lane
nodes.rationale: Sensitive (PHI/secret) artifacts must never reach cloud critics, so they receive Claude-session-local review only.

nodes.label: Human checkpoints
nodes.rationale: A human is required only where a verdict is irreversible outward or a trust-tier promotion, keeping everything else agent-adjudicated.

nodes.label: Trace to regression loop
nodes.rationale: Blocking review fails were never persisted, so the corpus lacked the failures that matter; one added emission fixes that without new storage.

nodes.label: Trust-tier promotion
nodes.rationale: Unquarantine is earned per lane through N clean gated merges and reverts on any regression, rather than being binary-forever.

nodes.label: Merge gate vs adoption gate
nodes.rationale: Separates 'is this output correct' from 'is this tool worth keeping' so a new gate mechanism must itself pass the adoption gate.

nodes.label: Turning the guard on (--context-guard compact|handoff|none)
nodes.rationale: The mode is fixed at launch because the hook reads it only from its own process env, so a worker cannot change it mid-session.

nodes.label: Gap: dynamic lane registry
nodes.rationale: The matrix is static, so a living registry is needed so orchestrators do not route by stale prose.

nodes.label: Agent Teams decision (PARKED until GA)
nodes.rationale: Parked because it is experimental and token cost scales linearly per active teammate, with nothing depending on it.

nodes.label: Machine-aware concurrency budget
nodes.rationale: Anthropic-enforced Workflow caps are a fixed ceiling the machine budget must live under, never consume.

nodes.label: Context rule: share among co-builders, isolate verifiers
nodes.norm_label: context rule: share among co-builders, isolate verifiers
nodes.rationale: Resolves the evidence contradiction by role so the reviewer is not anchored by the author's framing.

nodes.label: Four fan-out shapes with use-when/breaks-when
nodes.rationale: Naming each shape's failure edge lets the coordinator pick a shape that will not break on its task.

nodes.label: Slot classes (blast-radius routing)
nodes.rationale: Routing by blast radius with a different-family reviewer avoids self-grading, since a weak or self verifier is the most expensive bug.

nodes.label: Per-sprint re-audit
nodes.rationale: A verdict holds only for the models it was measured on, and a new model can flip it.

nodes.label: docs/internals/lane-calibration.md
nodes.rationale: implied: named as the live source of truth for lane status alongside /lanes.

nodes.label: Argument guard does not cover Codex
nodes.norm_label: argument guard does not cover codex
nodes.rationale: Codex hooks have no prompt-stage event, and in-prompt fixes bring the untrusted value inside the boundary they defend.

nodes.label: Anchor-logged branch delegation
nodes.rationale: Branch self-review became a deliberate logged decision made by the anchor so the branch never elects itself.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_REPO trust anchor
nodes.rationale: An environment-sourced anchor outside the reviewed repo prevents a crafted repo from planting its own trusted entry point; empty values are refused to avoid root-relative path hijack on Git Bash.

nodes.label: Review floor (panel critic responded)
nodes.rationale: Codex has no Claude self-review backstop, so a fully unavailable panel must fail closed instead of degrading to a lone free critic.

nodes.label: Step 0: resolve repo under review
nodes.rationale: cwd selects the repo under review while the HIMMEL_REPO trust anchor selects scripts, so a reviewed repo can never supply the code that reviews it.

nodes.label: Step 1: locate marker
nodes.rationale: implied: if there is no pending CR marker there is nothing to review or clear.

nodes.label: Step 2: lane check (docs-audit retained)
nodes.rationale: The code-critic panel is the wrong charter for docs-audit lanes, so the marker is retained for the Claude /pr-check.

nodes.label: Step 3: run the panel over the diff
nodes.norm_label: step 3: run the panel over the diff
nodes.rationale: Pinning the base SHA and head ensures every consumer reviews the same range and a moved checkout is refused rather than silently reviewed.

nodes.label: Step 4: record ledger evidence
nodes.rationale: The marker may be cleared only from persisted ledger evidence, with finding rows before availability rows so a failure cannot momentarily look clean.

nodes.label: Step 5: gate decision
nodes.rationale: Clearing only when critical and important counts are zero and parse consistently keeps the marker fail-closed on any ambiguity.

nodes.label: Baseline-before-change and parity rule
nodes.rationale: Without a clean-main baseline, post-change failures cannot be attributed to the change.

nodes.label: Build in linked worktree of a fresh clone (step 4)
nodes.norm_label: build in linked worktree of a fresh clone (step 4)
nodes.rationale: The clone is a primary checkout where block-edit-on-main refuses edits, and a shallow clone breaks the CR pre-push gate, so builds happen in a linked worktree of a full-depth clone.

nodes.label: Leak gate canary
nodes.rationale: A gate whose failure mode is silence needs a self-check that it flags fixture lines in every path spelling.

nodes.label: Mechanical leak gate (step 5)
nodes.rationale: A post-publish grep cannot unsend notification emails, so internal tokens and paths must be caught mechanically before any push or create call.

nodes.label: Never cherry-pick fork commits
nodes.rationale: Fork commits carry internal ticket IDs and diff context, so a cherry-pick is a leak vector and often lands on moved code.

nodes.label: Adopter /pr-check resolves himmel scripts from HIMMEL_REPO, not the reviewed repo
nodes.norm_label: adopter /pr-check resolves himmel scripts from himmel_repo, not the reviewed repo
nodes.rationale: Trusting a path baked into the reviewed repo's own hook would let a crafted repo execute arbitrary code when the runbook runs a script from the resolved root.

nodes.label: Arming a repo via install-cr-gate (baked primary-checkout path)
nodes.norm_label: arming a repo via install-cr-gate (baked primary-checkout path)
nodes.rationale: The baked path must name the primary checkout because a worktree path would break every adopter's push gate invisibly once the worktree is pruned.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit runs only on an armed repo (cr_trigger_repo_armed)
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit runs only on an armed repo (cr_trigger_repo_armed)
nodes.rationale: Posting @coderabbitai on a repo that never opted in would act on foreign repos, so the trigger hook only advises there and the critic panel carries the gate.

nodes.label: Anchor block-pr-check-args on HIMMEL_REPO not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
nodes.norm_label: anchor block-pr-check-args on himmel_repo not claude_project_dir
nodes.rationale: In a foreign-repo review CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the reviewed repo, so a guard located through it could be forged or never fire; a guard must not be located by the thing it guards against.

nodes.label: core.hooksPath pointing outside the repo
nodes.rationale: Writing into a directory shared by other repos would arm repos the operator never named and collide with the existing slot owner, so the gate goes into the repo's own .git/hooks and the installer reports whether the gate fires or is inert.

nodes.label: Host scope: GitHub only
nodes.rationale: The post-PR gate needs gh and fails closed on unreadable PR state, so on other hosts the marker can never clear; the installer warns at install time and widening is a separate ticket rather than weakening gate 5.

nodes.label: Prompt-stage hooks (wired in neither lane)
nodes.rationale: No UserPromptSubmit or UserPromptExpansion hook is wired because .claude/settings.json is operator-only, and the Codex lane has no prompt-stage event.

nodes.label: CR gate in an adopter's own repo
nodes.norm_label: cr gate in an adopter's own repo
nodes.rationale: The pre-push hook bakes in himmel's gate path at install time and fails closed if moved, so the repo under review is selected by cwd alone.

nodes.label: Symptom: /pr-check step 0 canonical fence refused
nodes.rationale: The isolation screen reads only EnterWorktree-pinned sessions, so denying EnterWorktree in worker settings removes the pin that caused 10-12 h BLOCKED stalls.

nodes.label: Himmel/adopter/refuse lane resolution
nodes.rationale: Lane decided against HIMMEL_REPO by inode so a crafted repo cannot make its own scripts run, and branch self-review stays possible on the himmel lane.

nodes.label: Anchor-logged delegation to branch copy
nodes.rationale: The anchor, not the branch, decides and logs delegation so a branch never elects itself to run its own review unlogged.

nodes.label: Fences inherit nothing rule
nodes.rationale: Each bash fence is a separate process, so printed values must be carried forward as substituted literals.

nodes.label: /pr-check takes no argument (ruling 2026-08-31)
nodes.rationale: The old path argument was pasted as literal text enabling shell injection and a cd that could not outlive its fence, so the surface was deleted.

nodes.label: Verdict-scratch resets
nodes.rationale: Stale verdicts from prior runs would leak into step 4 cross-checks and mask orphans, so scratch files are reset through the sanctioned write path.

nodes.label: /pr-check usage: no arguments
nodes.rationale: cwd selects the repo under review and an argument is ignored or refused by a hook, so a stale path cannot silently review the wrong repo.

nodes.label: Live review-gate e2e
nodes.rationale: Shell suites only see a stubbed gh, so a real throwaway private repo is needed to prove the gate; it is on-demand and refuses CI to avoid side effects.

nodes.label: Ask git for hook location instead of re-deriving it
nodes.norm_label: ask git for hook location instead of re-deriving it
nodes.rationale: Five review rounds found hand-derived hook paths wrong in new ways (core.hooksPath, relative paths, worktrees), so git's own `--git-path hooks` resolution is used.

nodes.label: Deliberate fail-open decisions of the ref-transaction guard
nodes.norm_label: deliberate fail-open decisions of the ref-transaction guard
nodes.rationale: The hook fires on every ref update, so failing closed on an unresolved origin/main or a broken shim target would brick fetch, stash and tags repo-wide.

nodes.label: Main-branch reference-transaction guard
nodes.rationale: reference-transaction is not disabled by --no-verify and server-side branch protection returns HTTP 403 on this private repo, so a git hook is the only way to refuse unpublished commits on main.

nodes.label: Shim target stored in git config, shim is static
nodes.norm_label: shim target stored in git config, shim is static
nodes.rationale: Embedding the target path in the hook file was exploitable or broken by newlines; git config round-trips arbitrary bytes exactly and nothing is parsed from hook file content.

nodes.label: Symptom: commit/push to main refused even with --no-verify
nodes.norm_label: symptom: commit/push to main refused even with --no-verify
nodes.rationale: reference-transaction is not disabled by --no-verify, closing the bypass that landed d05ef8ca and three earlier commits directly on main.

nodes.label: Non-npm license sweep (marketplace/plugins + scripts)
nodes.rationale: Confirms every plugin license (MIT or Apache-2.0) is compatible with an MIT-top-level project and that no unattributed third-party code exists outside LICENSE/NOTICE files.

nodes.label: claude-statusline (vendored) and hud
nodes.rationale: The hud renderer superseded the bash bar, which is kept as an opt-in rollback fallback since the upstream fork is archived.

nodes.label: Where graph-cadence failures show up
nodes.rationale: Multiple surfaces (run log, ledger, flow-run ledger, doctor C33) ensure an unknown or failed state never renders as healthy.

nodes.label: graphmap-cadence scheduler
nodes.rationale: A separate OS-scheduler sibling of pipeline-cadence because a graph refresh is a deterministic script, not a claude session, and the AST/semantic split follows artifact churn rather than cost.

nodes.label: Jira auth lookup order (env, himmel.conf, credentials dir, keyring, .env)
nodes.norm_label: jira auth lookup order (env, himmel.conf, credentials dir, keyring, .env)
nodes.rationale: A token in the keyring wins over .env so secrets stay out of plaintext files when possible.

nodes.label: himmel-jira slash commands
nodes.rationale: implied: each command maps to one Jira operation, and a matching skill auto-triggers it on Jira intent.

nodes.label: jira-refresh skill
nodes.rationale: Refreshes the cached projects, issue types and transitions when the metadata cache is stale.

nodes.label: Sharing the graph via the graph-data branch
nodes.norm_label: sharing the graph via the graph-data branch
nodes.rationale: One station pays for the semantic pass and every other station fetches the result for free, with scans and checks to avoid leaking secrets or host paths.

nodes.label: Luna graph freshness (semantic job, paused by default)
nodes.norm_label: luna graph freshness (semantic job, paused by default)
nodes.rationale: The luna vault is rebuilt AST-only so its markdown only gets LLM extraction from a separate, capped, initially paused job.

nodes.label: Delta-class judging policy
nodes.rationale: A later push needs a judge only when its delta touches trust paths or judged findings, which saves the scarcest usage budget.

nodes.label: Cold-spawn-per-message delivery
nodes.rationale: A warm child with piped stdin never fired a turn because interactive claude replies only at EOF, so closing stdin on a cold spawn is what makes the one turn run.

nodes.label: bwrap sandbox for legs
nodes.rationale: It hides ~/.config/himmel and makes verdicts read-only, at the cost of tool compatibility and needing unsandboxed paths for go.sh and write-verdict.sh; VM first to limit risk.

nodes.label: env -S escape decoding in the Bash arm
nodes.norm_label: env -s escape decoding in the bash arm
nodes.rationale: env splices decoded -S words back into argv, so anything not fully modelled stays denied; a text decoder cannot close the class and the structural upgrade would deny by effect.

nodes.label: Hook-wiring changes ride the owning worker's PR
nodes.norm_label: hook-wiring changes ride the owning worker's pr
nodes.rationale: Since workers can now edit their own worktree's settings.json, the operator no longer hand-edits it per hook-wiring change.

nodes.label: Live-settings write guard (git-dir == git-common-dir discriminator)
nodes.rationale: A plain glob-deny rule cannot tell the primary checkout from a linked worktree and blocked harmless worktree-copy edits; protection should follow repo layout, not machine paths.

nodes.label: Textual Bash/PowerShell arm, accepted false denies and known residuals
nodes.norm_label: textual bash/powershell arm, accepted false denies and known residuals
nodes.rationale: The hook matches command text rather than parsing effects, so it deliberately trades false denies and listed residual misses for a blunt, fail-closed check.

nodes.label: luna fetch-health probes
nodes.rationale: --probe reuses the shared registry and never writes the state file so a single-source check cannot perturb the scheduled run's bookkeeping.
