nodes.label: Setup script trailing || true and bounded builds
nodes.norm_label: setup script trailing || true and bounded builds
nodes.rationale: A non-zero setup script prevents the session from starting, so a failed step should cost only a tool.

nodes.label: Cloud snapshot cache and refresh
nodes.rationale: Setup must finish within about five minutes for a snapshot to be taken, and a changed script, hosts or expiry rebuild it, so rev bumps are needed to propagate changes.

nodes.label: One-time operator setup (setup script, skills, plugin profile)
nodes.norm_label: one-time operator setup (setup script, skills, plugin profile)
nodes.rationale: The setup script ends with || true because a non-zero script blocks the session from starting.

nodes.label: Decisions file migration and bounding
nodes.rationale: Moving superseded rulings verbatim into a decisions file keeps the Live state lean without losing any ruling.

nodes.label: Himmel checkout resolution order (HIMMEL_REPO, canonical paths, error)
nodes.norm_label: himmel checkout resolution order (himmel_repo, canonical paths, error)
nodes.rationale: Never uses the cwd git toplevel so a foreign repo shipping its own chief.sh can never win over himmel's.

nodes.label: /chief command
nodes.rationale: Lets a chief be started or handed over from any directory, bound to the project the session runs in rather than himmel's own project key.

nodes.label: rtk rewrite fail-open guard
nodes.rationale: rtk find rejects compound predicates and ignores -prune, breaking runbook clip scans, so only those rewrites are suppressed while all other rewrites keep their token savings.

nodes.label: No rtk git rewrite inside .claude/worktrees
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's worktree-isolation screen refuses commands running rtk with git operands and nothing hook-visible marks pinned sessions, so the rewrite is withheld by cwd.

nodes.label: Symptom: git refused as 'runs rtk with a git command among its operands'
nodes.norm_label: symptom: git refused as 'runs rtk with a git command among its operands'
nodes.rationale: The rtk hook rewrites git to rtk git and the isolation screen cannot establish the executable, so suppressing the rewrite in worktree cwds lets plain git through.

nodes.label: RTK (Rust Token Killer) install
nodes.rationale: RTK proxies common commands to save tokens, and the name collision with another rtk means the install must be verified.

nodes.label: Expected 'No hook installed' RTK banner
nodes.rationale: rtk's self-check looks for its own bare hook signature, which himmel replaces with a guard, so the warning is benign and running rtk init -g would re-add the bare entry.

nodes.label: 'No hook installed' banner is benign
nodes.rationale: himmel uses rtk-hook-guard.sh instead of a bare rtk hook entry, so rtk's self-check cannot find its signature even though rewriting works; re-running rtk init -g would re-add the replaced bare entry.

nodes.label: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
nodes.rationale: Strips irrelevant command output before it enters context for 60-90% token savings, and the hook is reconciled to a guard wrapper because rtk init -g appends duplicate bare entries.

nodes.label: PreToolUse RTK hook
nodes.rationale: It rewrites Bash commands for token savings but skips find with compound predicates because rtk find rejects them at runtime.

nodes.label: Smoke demo trust and side-effect rules
nodes.norm_label: smoke demo trust and side-effect rules
nodes.rationale: Hook trust is keyed to absolute path and --from runs target hooks unsandboxed, so the runner bypasses trust deliberately and blanks ambient credentials.

nodes.label: end-session-wiki.json config fields
nodes.rationale: Per-repo persistent controls let users disable, dry-run, tune or route capture without environment changes.

nodes.label: Crystallization (LLM upgrade)
nodes.rationale: A mechanical note is a valid baseline, and a fail-open best-effort LLM pass upgrades it to a real synthesis without ever blocking session end.

nodes.label: luna backfill-sessions
nodes.rationale: Imports historical session transcripts into the vault create-only and idempotently so nothing is overwritten except via explicit recovery modes.

nodes.label: luna crystallize-note
nodes.rationale: Upgrades a mechanical session note into a real synthesis via a Max-billed interactive claude run, fail-open so it never blocks the hook.

nodes.label: Injection scan
nodes.rationale: About 36% of public skills carry prompt-injection vectors, so every tool is scanned before install.

nodes.label: Trust-posture tiers
nodes.rationale: Verification effort should match blast radius, since a trusted-but-hostile hook breaks the whole session's trust boundary.

nodes.label: Firecrawl thin-body escalation (opt-in)
nodes.rationale: It is credit-conscious and applies the G-1 privacy gate so internal URLs are never shipped to a third-party scraper.

nodes.label: Open POC item: real-model claudex step
nodes.norm_label: open poc item: real-model claudex step
nodes.rationale: Not run because the guest holds no codex credential and host gateway reach was not authorised, and a key in the guest could spend the codex bank.

nodes.label: What the POC does not prove
nodes.norm_label: what the poc does not prove
nodes.rationale: The sandbox bounds where not what, so in-root destruction and credentials already in the box are not stopped by srt.

nodes.label: Verdict: PROCEED with changes
nodes.rationale: The mechanism works but needs launcher assertions, an AppArmor profile, a push broker and a curated domain list before adoption.

nodes.label: The v1 gate
nodes.rationale: Since all first-party servers are on v2, a global lint prevents regression to the v1 SDK while never reporting vendored or external servers as compliant.

nodes.label: Drop candidates are prompts to look, not verdicts
nodes.norm_label: drop candidates are prompts to look, not verdicts
nodes.rationale: Zero calls over few sessions means nothing and a rarely-used tool may be a deliberate safety net, and dropping changes live behaviour so apply goes VM-first.

nodes.label: Alert rules and cadence-alert webhook delivery
nodes.norm_label: alert rules and cadence-alert webhook delivery
nodes.rationale: Grafana can only POST webhooks and no Alertmanager exists, so one contact point routes to cadence-alert for a single dedupe path and log.

nodes.label: Failure-mode coverage map
nodes.rationale: Each incident-postmortem failure mode maps to a rule that does not depend on the failing component itself.

nodes.label: Lock-serialized re-pin transaction with rename-based dead-lock reclaim
nodes.norm_label: lock-serialized re-pin transaction with rename-based dead-lock reclaim
nodes.rationale: Renaming a dead lock directory instead of rm -rf ensures exactly one contender wins the steal and racing sessions cannot half-write the record.

nodes.label: Deny and name the replacement
nodes.rationale: additionalContext alone does not produce compliance, while a refusal with a copy-pasteable replacement and a documented bypass keeps an audit trail of what ran.

nodes.label: Fail-open vs fail-closed policy
nodes.rationale: The right default follows what a false positive costs: security fences fail closed while watchdogs and workflow nudges fail open so they never block calls on their own bugs.

nodes.label: Silent-duplicate merge trap
nodes.rationale: Two branches that each add an entry to a frozen ordered list merge textually clean but leave a duplicate, so a clean auto-merge is not evidence of correctness.

nodes.label: End-side hooks enqueue, don't fan out
nodes.norm_label: end-side hooks enqueue, don't fan out
nodes.rationale: Stop and SessionEnd hooks spawning detached trees cause unbounded fan-out that leaks kernel pool, so they go through a bounded queue.

nodes.label: Two hook wirers with disjoint inventories
nodes.norm_label: two hook wirers with disjoint inventories
nodes.rationale: A hook filed in the wrong inventory gets wired into both targets via installMissingEntries and runs twice per session.

nodes.label: Fold decision reads flipping tasks, not the mean
nodes.norm_label: fold decision reads flipping tasks, not the mean
nodes.rationale: A class may fold only when no task does worse in the fold arm, since a mean can hide regressions on individual tasks.

nodes.label: Judge replay leak isolation
nodes.rationale: Each replay gets a scratch repo with only the judged head's ancestry and denied fetch tools so no later history gives the outcome away.

nodes.label: Breadcrumb-file verdict method
nodes.rationale: File presence is a more reliable verdict than the JSON envelope or rc, which can be misleading in headless runs.

nodes.label: Finding: empty --settings overlay leaves project hooks INTACT
nodes.norm_label: finding: empty --settings overlay leaves project hooks intact
nodes.rationale: The breadcrumb hook fired in both the control and corrected treatment runs, so an absent-hooks overlay does not strip project hooks; a hooks-redeclaring overlay remains untested.

nodes.label: Methodology correction: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV with POSIX --settings path gave false STRIPPED
nodes.norm_label: methodology correction: msys_no_pathconv with posix --settings path gave false stripped
nodes.rationale: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 disables path rewriting for every argv element, so native claude.exe got an unconverted POSIX path and failed before reaching settings-merge logic.

nodes.label: Probe 3e: settings overlay hook inheritance test
nodes.norm_label: probe 3e: settings overlay hook inheritance test
nodes.rationale: Stripping hooks would bypass guardrails for writer roles, while inheriting all could hang a headless worker on an interactive-shaped hook, so the behaviour had to be measured.

nodes.label: Git Bash leading-slash argv mangling
nodes.rationale: MSYS converts leading-slash args to Windows paths for native executables, causing false negatives; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL or a // prefix neutralise it.

nodes.label: Probe 1 / 1b: /compact via --resume and --continue (PASS)
nodes.rationale: Once argv mangling was removed, a real compact_boundary event appeared, so /compact works headlessly.

nodes.label: Probe 2: dontAsk allowlist (PASS)
nodes.rationale: permission_denials is the only structural signal of a denial because rc reflects max-turns exhaustion, not the denial.

nodes.label: Probes 3/3b/3c/3d: skill pack mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Of four mechanisms tested only plain cwd/.claude/skills/ delivered auth, discovery and execution together; --bare --add-dir loses auth, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR doesn't register skills, and a minimal --plugin-dir manifest silently never loads.

nodes.label: Probe 4: --json-schema needs --max-turns >= 2
nodes.rationale: With --max-turns 1 structured_output silently comes back null instead of raising a schema error.

nodes.label: Probe 5: cross-cwd --resume (PASS)
nodes.rationale: Confirms documented cross-directory resume support on CLI 2.1.250.

nodes.label: Probe 6: bank usage delta (~3 points five_hour)
nodes.norm_label: probe 6: bank usage delta (~3 points five_hour)
nodes.rationale: Measuring the batch cost shows the harness was never near the 85% skip threshold.

nodes.label: Probe 7: dual-shell allowlist nondeterminism (none seen, n=2)
nodes.norm_label: probe 7: dual-shell allowlist nondeterminism (none seen, n=2)
nodes.rationale: Checks whether the model's shell choice varies run to run when only Bash shapes plus Write are allowlisted.

nodes.label: claude-p P0 probe results
nodes.rationale: Gives the dispatch-substrate migration plan measured facts about claude -p behaviour read from artifacts rather than exit codes.

nodes.label: Probe 3e result: --settings overlay vs. project hooks
nodes.norm_label: probe 3e result: --settings overlay vs. project hooks
nodes.rationale: Records a measured answer so hook inheritance for profile workers can be designed on evidence rather than guesswork.

nodes.label: Local-versus-cloud parity diff
nodes.rationale: Diffing a read-only probe run locally and in the cloud reveals where the cloud environment diverges, so each gap is closed or documented.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit posts a status, not a check-run
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit posts a status, not a check-run
nodes.rationale: The gate queried check-runs that never exist for CodeRabbit so the in-flight block never fired, and mocked fixtures hid the wrong shape; it now reads the statuses list and matches creator.id.

nodes.label: Install CodeRabbit CLI with vendor installer
nodes.norm_label: install coderabbit cli with vendor installer
nodes.rationale: The npm package is a different product, so the vendor curl installer places coderabbit and cr in ~/.local/bin where checks look.

nodes.label: Opt-in web search: DeepSeek (HIMMEL-6269)
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek is PRC-hosted with retention and training risk, so it is off by default and hard-denied for salus/PHI.

nodes.label: No merge-approval exemption for automation
nodes.rationale: An unattended runbook that merges on green CI would turn the review requirement into a formality where bypasses are least noticed.

nodes.label: MAIN-RED advisory merge gate
nodes.rationale: The gate is advisory so green PRs keep merging, and the HOLD on a real blocker is enforced by the chief withholding GOs.

nodes.label: Red main classes (merge skew, timing, caller environment)
nodes.norm_label: red main classes (merge skew, timing, caller environment)
nodes.rationale: Ranked by how often each reddened main over 30 days, so the likeliest cause is checked first.

nodes.label: Opt-in Jira auto-transition on merge
nodes.rationale: It used to fire on every merge and closed tickets with sibling work still owed, which no heuristic can detect, so the caller decides.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_PROTECTION_SOURCE (classic/ruleset/either/both)
nodes.rationale: It is a fixed literal rather than an env seam because widening choices must not be steerable by an ambient variable on a merge gate.

nodes.label: Solo mode (himmel.mergeMode solo)
nodes.rationale: Lets a one-person adopted project use merge-on-green without a chief while relaxing no gate it can run, failing closed on invalid values.

nodes.label: Capability classes (build/query/none)
nodes.rationale: Qwen embedding needs a GPU for whole-corpus builds but CPU suffices for single queries, so hosts are classed and only set is gated.

nodes.label: Switching a machine: copy, then swap
nodes.norm_label: switching a machine: copy, then swap
nodes.rationale: qmd embed --force drops every vector first, breaking search for hours, so a re-embedded copy is built and swapped in.

nodes.label: Measured cost and quality (golden set)
nodes.rationale: Measurements show Qwen wins every vector-bearing cell on the 38-query golden set at a CPU cost acceptable for queries, justifying the opt-in.

nodes.label: Model-mismatch trap
nodes.rationale: qmd never checks which model made a vector, so a same-dimension mismatch silently returns garbage; three checks catch it.

nodes.label: Embed model options (gemma, qwen, remote)
nodes.rationale: Qwen retrieves better but is larger and needs a GPU to build, so each machine opts in; the station uses remote OpenRouter Qwen3-8B by operator ruling.

nodes.label: Rolling back by hand
nodes.rationale: A running daemon keeps the old file open and the stale -shm makes readers report a malformed database, so step order matters.

nodes.label: MCP v2 migration target (protocol 2025-11-25, SDK 2.4.0)
nodes.rationale: Protocol revision and SDK major are independent, so the target pins stable 2.4.0 rather than the stale alpha warning.

nodes.label: Test with plugin-test.sh, not raw bun test (HIMMEL-366)
nodes.norm_label: test with plugin-test.sh, not raw bun test (himmel-366)
nodes.rationale: A fresh worktree installs only scripts/jira deps so raw bun test starts RED and masks real regressions; the helper installs first so the baseline is GREEN.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_OWN_POLLER gate
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows one poller per bot token, so only the designated owner session polls and others keep outbound tools without stealing the slot.

nodes.label: Windows ps probe fallback delta (looksLikeServer)
nodes.rationale: MSYS ps on Windows throws on -o args=, which upstream swallowed and skipped the kill while overwriting bot.pid, leaving two live pollers (HIMMEL-1858).

nodes.label: Upstream-watch protocol (re-apply four fork hunks)
nodes.rationale: Counting hunks from memory once silently reintroduced the Windows two-poller bug, so the marker grep is the source of truth.

nodes.label: telegram-himmel README
nodes.rationale: Documents the fork of telegram@claude-plugins-official v0.0.7 and the deltas that stop sessions stealing the single poll slot.

nodes.label: macOS EULA constraint
nodes.rationale: Apple's licence permits macOS only on Apple hardware, so the lane is local operator-approved repro only and never in CI.

nodes.label: Image choice: sickcodes/docker-osx vs dockur/macos
nodes.rationale: docker-osx has a documented headless SSH mode needed by a chief-driven runner, whereas dockur/macos setup is interactive only.

nodes.label: Daemon off switch (flag file)
nodes.rationale: SessionStart relaunches the daemon each session, so a persistent flag is needed to keep it off while GPU is contended.

nodes.label: Daemon RSS ceiling recycle
nodes.rationale: The daemon's native memory grows over hours (6.8 GB after ~4.5 h), so SessionStart recycles it in a detached child to avoid stalling the session.

nodes.label: Salus local-only index and egress gate
nodes.norm_label: salus local-only index and egress gate
nodes.rationale: A collection the egress matrix denies for remote providers must live in its own local-model index so local and remote vectors never mix.

nodes.label: Shared HTTP daemon instead of per-session stdio
nodes.norm_label: shared http daemon instead of per-session stdio
nodes.rationale: Claude Code spawns every enabled plugin's MCP server per session, so stdio loaded the same index into RAM each time (HIMMEL-592); one shared daemon removes that footprint.

nodes.label: Usage-cap watchdog (auto-arm-on-cap.sh)
nodes.rationale: It is the detect half of auto-resume on a usage cap, and as a watchdog it surfaces its own malfunctions visibly because a broken watchdog must be seen.

nodes.label: Scheduler backend for auto-arm resume
nodes.rationale: Without an OS scheduler backend (at/atd or crontab) an armed resume silently never fires.

nodes.label: VM maintenance run and probe
nodes.rationale: Keeps the VM tooling and logins current and snapshots in place with a secret scan, because a snapshot holding a login must never be cloned.

nodes.label: Fatal vs non-fatal setup steps
nodes.rationale: Core tools are required for a usable system so steps 1-6 abort, while later steps log failures and continue.

nodes.label: GET /api/board (drift summary and chain read)
nodes.rationale: It answers absent with a reason when its input is missing, so the page never shows a made-up count.

nodes.label: GET /api/roadmap live read
nodes.rationale: It reads its sources on every request, with no static render or republish, so the board never goes stale.

nodes.label: Board lane writes (POST /api/roadmap/write)
nodes.rationale: Validating key, status and sector before any child runs and taking the write lock with an audit row keeps Jira writes safe and traceable.

nodes.label: Librarian proposals
nodes.rationale: Proposals only: a fixVersion move or a close needs operator approval or a recorded standing rule.

nodes.label: Local tracker mode
nodes.rationale: Without Jira the Board reads the local tracker store through the tracker seam, which uses an argv child never a shell string.

nodes.label: Multi-project Board enumeration from mirror root
nodes.norm_label: multi-project board enumeration from mirror root
nodes.rationale: Enumerating project directories under the mirror root lets the Board work in any repo, not only himmel's, whatever JIRA_PROJECT_KEY names.

nodes.label: Ticket drawer
nodes.rationale: The board is inert and writes are held while a drawer is open to avoid accidental moves.

nodes.label: GET /api/roadmap/history stage history
nodes.rationale: A failed read answers 502 'history unavailable' so the drawer never shows an unavailable history as an empty one.

nodes.label: Tidy up drift refresh (POST /api/board/drift-refresh)
nodes.rationale: It replaces focus-drift.txt through a temp file only on a clean sdrift line, so a failed run keeps the old file.

nodes.label: Board page (#/board)
nodes.rationale: One Board entry replaced the separate Roadmap and Kanban pages so ticket status, drift and chains are read live from one place.

nodes.label: Known-findings preflight (step 2.8)
nodes.rationale: Closing recurring finding classes before round 1 avoids spending critic rounds on already-catalogued issues.

nodes.label: known-findings.json artifact (class schema)
nodes.rationale: A single JSON source of truth with one entry per recurring class lets three consumers share the same adjudications instead of drifting copies.

nodes.label: Classes 2026-10-29 snapshot table
nodes.rationale: implied: a snapshot table gives readers the class inventory at a glance while --list stays the live source.

nodes.label: Correction ladder rungs (design/gate/advisory/prompt/human)
nodes.rationale: Recording the top rung each class has reached makes promotion toward structural enforcement measurable and lets a missing rung fail loudly.

nodes.label: Critic prompt feed (already adjudicated block)
nodes.rationale: Telling critics not to re-raise adjudicated classes unless code regressed cuts repeat findings on fresh diffs.

nodes.label: Measure detector noise before shipping
nodes.rationale: A detector that fires on every PR buries the checklist it is meant to sharpen, so noise is measured not estimated.

nodes.label: Red-first pair must be discriminating
nodes.rationale: Pairs that pass against both correct and broken detectors let two defects reach review, so flipping the one token under test must change the verdict.

nodes.label: /cr-learnings-refresh feed (STALE/PONYTAIL/PROPOSE-CLASS lines)
nodes.rationale: Re-mining the ledger and CodeRabbit learnings export keeps evidence fresh and surfaces new-class candidates without deleting anything automatically.

nodes.label: 2026-08-23 measurement (why these classes)
nodes.rationale: Measuring App review comments showed learning usage counts overstate what CodeRabbit still re-raises, so detector classes follow actual raises.

nodes.label: /pr-check step 2.8 pre-panel self-review
nodes.rationale: Blocking on open hits before step 3 forces the session to fix, waive or check each known class before the critic panel spends a round on it.

nodes.label: Attribution and promotion rules (print-only)
nodes.rationale: Recurrence thresholds across branches and a 30-day window keep promotion proposals evidence-based while a human decides any rung change.

nodes.label: 2026-09-02 refresh findings
nodes.rationale: Recording that the CSV tail was fully covered and why items were declined prevents the next refresh from lowering the bar or re-litigating.

nodes.label: Weekly standards cadence
nodes.rationale: A lean-invoke weekly proposals file turns ladder data into one preferred target per class, with expiry so proposals do not rot.

nodes.label: Lesson-loop write-fence (block-lesson-enforcement-writes.sh)
nodes.rationale: The lessons-to-tickets loop is PROPOSE-ONLY, and a deny-list of write verbs never converged over adversarial review rounds, so the fence inverted to an allow-list of proven readers and fails closed because a fully automated worker has no human to mis-serve.

nodes.label: Dispatcher contract (HIMMEL_LESSON_LOOP=1)
nodes.rationale: The fence is inert without the marker by design for zero always-on cost, so uncovered workers must never receive lessons-to-code work.

nodes.label: Write-fence for the propose-only lesson loop
nodes.norm_label: write-fence for the propose-only lesson loop
nodes.rationale: Round 4 inverted a deny-list of known writers into an allow-list of proven read-only verbs because enumerating every way to write a file is an open set that converged slowly.

nodes.label: CI minutes (billed beside wall)
nodes.rationale: Billed minutes are stored as 'unknown', never 0, when billing is absent so a missing answer is not mistaken for free; reruns replace the row to keep the run id unique.

nodes.label: Idempotency and append-only digest
nodes.rationale: With no compute timestamp the same inputs give the same bytes, so a ticket's record is appended only when its digest changes.

nodes.label: Ticket join keys and pseudo-tickets (_chief, _unattributed)
nodes.rationale: Chief sessions are pooled under _chief with no allocation because an allocation rule would change every ticket's record whenever the range changes.

nodes.label: Phase-cost rows
nodes.rationale: One cumulative row per (day, session, phase) gives the cost view a single record to read, and unpriced models never borrow another model's price.

nodes.label: PR/CI join (opt-in, fail closed)
nodes.rationale: An unknown fact is never stored, so any gh failure aborts the whole run before anything is appended, keeping previous versions untouched.

nodes.label: Per-ticket usage record
nodes.rationale: It joins session token counts with review-ledger data once so a ticket's cost and review rounds are answered from one record.

nodes.label: Daily himmel-doctor cadence
nodes.rationale: A daily doctor run means a standing FAIL is seen within a day rather than nine.

nodes.label: Renumber of 2026-10-07
nodes.rationale: The temporary planning versions v1.0.3..v1.0.43 were never shipped patches but milestones, so they became minors.

nodes.label: Patch / minor / major rule
nodes.rationale: Patches fix a shipped minor, minors are milestones of planned work, and majors mark breaking changes, so each number signals scope.

nodes.label: Docs site publishing via GitHub Pages
nodes.norm_label: docs site publishing via github pages
nodes.rationale: A daily scheduled deploy plus a manual trigger publishes the Starlight site without redeploying on every docs push, and raw file paths stay unchanged.

nodes.label: Symptom: git checkout -- <path> denied
nodes.rationale: A deny entry beats any allow and git restore falls to the classifier, so a safe literal script is the structural fix for TDD RED restores.

nodes.label: Policy directory from passwd home, not $HOME
nodes.norm_label: policy directory from passwd home, not $home
nodes.rationale: Deriving the home from the account's passwd entry stops a planted $HOME from substituting a forged policy file.

nodes.label: Arithmetic and assignment fold (arith_fold)
nodes.rationale: Opaque for scoping is not opaque for scanning, because real bash assigns the seam in the current shell via (( )) and $(( )) bodies, so those bodies must be scanned for seam assignments.

nodes.label: Positive command-position subshell scoping rule
nodes.rationale: A blacklist of nesting shapes was abandoned because each round found the next false ALLOW, so only positively recognised real subshells are scoped and everything else folds to the un-scoped deny.

nodes.label: block-chokepoint-env-prefix.sh sanctioned-script env-prefix guard
nodes.rationale: The native permission matcher bails on VAR= shapes, so an env-prefixed call to a sanctioned script falls to classifier judgment; this guard gives that class a structural home.

nodes.label: Per-tool spawn inventory and graphify hook pricing
nodes.norm_label: per-tool spawn inventory and graphify hook pricing
nodes.rationale: Counting processes per tool call shows where graphify's stock hook entries add cost on high-frequency tools like Read and Glob, so pricing targets those.

nodes.label: graphify optional CLI and on-demand MCP server
nodes.norm_label: graphify optional cli and on-demand mcp server
nodes.rationale: The MCP server is registered on demand rather than in ~/.claude.json so normal sessions avoid loading its 10 tool schemas.

nodes.label: Machine-generated PR gets no CodeRabbit review
nodes.norm_label: machine-generated pr gets no coderabbit review
nodes.rationale: check-ci.sh classifies a PR touching only graphify-out artifacts and treats the absent CR review as expected, so waiting on it would stall.

nodes.label: /check-ci
nodes.rationale: Token-free merge-gate watcher returning a single exit code so merge-on-green costs near zero tokens.

nodes.label: CI release: heavy CI after review (planned)
nodes.norm_label: ci release: heavy ci after review (planned)
nodes.rationale: Starting heavy jobs only after the review gate passes avoids burning runner hours on a head a reviewer is about to send back.

nodes.label: Zero-review-object shapes at a head
nodes.rationale: Clean, rate-limited or skipped runs mint no review object, so zero threads over an unreviewed head is the best-effort case and is owed the exact-head critic panel rather than a gate.

nodes.label: Symptom: check-ci.sh --pr N prints usage, no gate ran
nodes.norm_label: symptom: check-ci.sh --pr n prints usage, no gate ran
nodes.rationale: Exit 64 distinguishes a usage error from a genuine cannot-evaluate so callers do not record a result for a gate that never ran.

nodes.label: A green rollup is not a clean review
nodes.norm_label: a green rollup is not a clean review
nodes.rationale: A green check rollup sat over six unresolved review threads on PR #2209, so gating must use check-ci.sh exit 0 rather than ticks or finding counts.

nodes.label: Loop review threads to convergence
nodes.rationale: After any fix and push a prior clean round is stale for the new head, and check-ci.sh exit 3 backstops unresolved threads.

nodes.label: Clean /pr-check is not a clean thread state
nodes.norm_label: clean /pr-check is not a clean thread state
nodes.rationale: The CodeRabbit App reviews only after gh pr create, so pre-push passes (PR #1262, #2209) cannot see later unresolved threads and check-ci must be looped to exit 0.

nodes.label: lane-quality trajectory fields
nodes.rationale: Scoring red-before-green, denial recovery and verify-before-claim from transcripts needs no model call and no bank draw.

nodes.label: Host fallback for fork and dependabot runs
nodes.norm_label: host fallback for fork and dependabot runs
nodes.rationale: Fork PRs and dependabot get a read-only token and no secrets so they cannot pull the private package; they run the host path instead of a red job.

nodes.label: When a branch merges main in
nodes.norm_label: when a branch merges main in
nodes.rationale: Each merge-in costs a full CI, review and GO round (open-to-merge median 2.2 h), so it happens only for conflicts, a needed fix, final-head proofs or a sibling's plugin bump.

nodes.label: No push trigger and strict-up-to-date off
nodes.norm_label: no push trigger and strict-up-to-date off
nodes.rationale: Per-merge main runs cost ~2,300 runner hours and strict mode would serialise merges and kill fleet parallelism, so main is verified on a schedule instead.

nodes.label: Main CI cadence: cron, not per merge
nodes.norm_label: main ci cadence: cron, not per merge
nodes.rationale: A per-merge run produced about 52 runs a day with half cancelled as superseded, so main is swept by cron and on-demand dispatch instead.

nodes.label: Updating multiple luna vaults (/luna-upgrade-all)
nodes.rationale: A dry-run-first, per-vault-confirmed, backup-before-apply sweep avoids clobbering customized vaults while saving a manual /luna-upgrade per vault.

nodes.label: Offer commit for single-writer vaults
nodes.rationale: upgrade.sh never commits and autosync is off by default, so a dirty tree would silently never land.

nodes.label: Always scope collections; lex first plus vec
nodes.norm_label: always scope collections; lex first plus vec
nodes.rationale: Measured on a 38-query golden set, scoping raised hybrid MRR from 0.57 to 0.83 because the large luna collection swamps unscoped vector hits.

nodes.label: himmel.jsonl golden set (200 queries)
nodes.rationale: Only public himmel docs are named so the set can live in the repo; private sets stay outside and are passed by flag or env var.

nodes.label: Alternatives considered (midpoint, PERT, story points, bootstrap)
nodes.norm_label: alternatives considered (midpoint, pert, story points, bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: Listing rejected alternatives lets a reviewer challenge the model choice.

nodes.label: DoD refusal
nodes.rationale: Refusing an under-specified estimate forces the input to be fixed (split or plan-first) instead of quoting a number that cannot be trusted.

nodes.label: Log-normal estimate record (median, sigma, mean, P80)
nodes.norm_label: log-normal estimate record (median, sigma, mean, p80)
nodes.rationale: Log-normal fits better than variant A (sigma 0.77 vs 0.65) and versions must add means, not medians.

nodes.label: PILOT-MEASURE status
nodes.rationale: The calibration set was only 24 merged tickets and survivorship biases sigma low, so adoption waits for n >= 60 pairs and two shipped versions.

nodes.label: Version mode (Fenton-Wilkinson and Monte Carlo)
nodes.rationale: Monte Carlo inside first-fit is too slow, so Fenton-Wilkinson gives the fast check and Monte Carlo is the cross-check.

nodes.label: Deferred escape
nodes.rationale: Counting deferrals that later caused escapes measures the claim that deferral lets bad bugs through.

nodes.label: Escape (escaped defect)
nodes.rationale: A broken real flow must be fixed in the version in progress, which is not done while an escape is open.

nodes.label: Escape class
nodes.rationale: A broken real flow must be fixed in the current version, so the version is not done while it is open.

nodes.label: Hardening class
nodes.rationale: Features that work but would fail silently need monitoring to turn worked when tried into keeps working.

nodes.label: Follow-up placement table
nodes.rationale: A first-match-wins table keeps a frozen version's set fixed while routing escapes and hardening to the right version.

nodes.label: Class refinement process
nodes.rationale: Classes are judgement calls, so version-close review of misses and reclasses tunes them, changing only by operator ruling.

nodes.label: Archive costs and ceilings
nodes.rationale: Stating that segments rotate at 256 KiB but are read whole and never pruned avoids false claims of constant-time polling.

nodes.label: bus wait receive path
nodes.rationale: Blocking on the caller's own inbox with a timeout lets workers receive messages without the delivery hook, with distinct exit codes for timeout vs error.

nodes.label: Delivery and recovery (append/read/commit, halt, unhalt)
nodes.rationale: Read does not commit so delivery is at-least-once, and a bad cursor halts fail-closed with an explicit notice rather than silently replaying.

nodes.label: Identity and registration CLI (register, bind, rebind, adopt, succeed)
nodes.norm_label: identity and registration cli (register, bind, rebind, adopt, succeed)
nodes.rationale: Identity as (name, pid, start time) plus single-use names and stamped successions prevents spoofing and lets workers survive chief succession.

nodes.label: .graphify-backend file-declared backend
nodes.rationale: The env declaration cannot reach the PreToolUse hook in-session, so a per-run file supplies the same declaration under strict agreement rules.

nodes.label: .graphify-corpus staged-copy declaration
nodes.rationale: A scratchpad copy classifies as nothing and would be denied, so a marker declares origin while real roots always beat it and every use is ledgered.

nodes.label: Memory snapshot and rollback
nodes.rationale: Restore never clobbers another writer and moves added files aside rather than deleting, so compaction passes are safely reversible.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier is Claude Code's own judgement, not a himmel script, so its denials are only logged and Codex needs a stand-in fence.

nodes.label: Codex parity
nodes.rationale: Codex wires almost the same guards as Claude but adds block-terminal-write-fence, which stands in for the classifier Codex lacks.

nodes.label: Switching the Claude account procedure
nodes.rationale: An account switch changes the usage budget for every worker and chief and can invalidate caches and overrides, so it is done at a boundary in a fixed order.

nodes.label: Weekly budget override voids on account switch
nodes.norm_label: weekly budget override voids on account switch
nodes.rationale: The override is bound to the account that set it, so it must be invalid under a new login, and only the operator may set it.

nodes.label: claude.ai connectors in the cloud
nodes.rationale: A connected connector is not enabled in the cloud session, so the brief must not assume context7 or Atlassian availability.

nodes.label: Plugin hooks in the cloud (probe findings)
nodes.norm_label: plugin hooks in the cloud (probe findings)
nodes.rationale: A probe showed plugin and repo hooks fire and treat the clone as primary checkout, so the session must work in a worktree.

nodes.label: PR body contract (completes-ticket, Ticket coverage)
nodes.rationale: Requiring one line per ask as done or deferred to a ticket means no ask is silently dropped and ready-check can verify coverage.

nodes.label: What a cloud session has and lacks
nodes.norm_label: what a cloud session has and lacks
nodes.rationale: Because a cloud session lacks local tools and state, the local shepherd stays mandatory for pr-check, the review gate and merge.

nodes.label: Local shepherd for cloud PRs
nodes.rationale: Scripting the mechanical half of the shepherd lets a clean candidate go to GO and merge without a shepherd worker.

nodes.label: Substitutes for handover and lock in cloud
nodes.norm_label: substitutes for handover and lock in cloud
nodes.rationale: With no handover doc, queue lock or inbox, state moves to GitHub and Jira: one ticket, one branch, one PR and CLOUD-DONE comments.

nodes.label: Done-truth audit procedure
nodes.community_name: Live-proof test — when a ticket may be Done
nodes.rationale: Reopening only on concrete failing evidence, never a row that could not be run and never a live worker's ticket, avoids false reopens.

nodes.label: Live proof row criteria
nodes.community_name: Live-proof test — when a ticket may be Done
nodes.rationale: A row must run against main or the running system, name the command, show an observable and be able to fail, so it is genuinely discriminating evidence.

nodes.label: qmd probe runs out of band with cached verdict
nodes.norm_label: qmd probe runs out of band with cached verdict
nodes.rationale: A cold qmd status took 11.5s and contributed to SessionStart timeouts that killed the hook and lost the advisory, so the hook serves a cached verdict and refreshes detached.

nodes.label: qmd index trust advisory (silent unless wrong)
nodes.norm_label: qmd index trust advisory (silent unless wrong)
nodes.rationale: Every SessionStart line is paid for in every session, and a daily 'fine' banner trains readers to skip the real warning, so it prints only on STALE/INCOMPLETE/MISSING/UNREADABLE/UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: UNVERIFIED reporting and bounded probe
nodes.rationale: Silent non-verdicts recreated the hole where the check quietly stopped checking, and only an inner timeout can report a hang that an outer one merely kills.

nodes.label: Anchor working-tree compare (not a ref)
nodes.rationale: Refs live in the common git dir a worker can write, so a ref-based base could be moved onto the edit, whereas the primary checkout is protected from worker edits.

nodes.label: Write-channel backstop
nodes.rationale: Whatever later runs a written file cannot be enumerated, so the backstop denies the write channel rather than the executor.

nodes.label: No claude -p / headless invocation rule (HIMMEL-128)
nodes.rationale: Programmatic dispatch such as a future /harvest-clips must use the same Skill-tool call shape rather than headless runs.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:luna-ingest skill
nodes.rationale: implied: the skill holds the runbook so wrappers never duplicate it.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:roadmap-clips skill
nodes.rationale: implied: the skill holds the runbook so the wrapper never duplicates it.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:telegram-clip skill
nodes.rationale: implied: the skill is the single source of truth for the runbook.

nodes.label: worker-digest: failures as class keys
nodes.rationale: Class sub-keys come from closed vocabularies, never journal text, so digests stay safe and aggregatable.

nodes.label: /afk-lockdown
nodes.rationale: A Telegram verb that only narrows (disables the station) needs no TOTP code because it cannot widen anything, serving the lost-phone case.

nodes.label: Notice bot and request nonce
nodes.rationale: A session could write any text into the bridge bot's chat, so facts come from a second root-only bot and a nonce binds each code to one request root described.

nodes.label: Turning it off
nodes.rationale: Offers narrowest-first root-only switches so the operator can reduce the attack surface and a session cannot undo any of them.

nodes.label: himmel-ops plugin
nodes.rationale: It is ALWAYS-tier because it carries the harness-meta operational skills like stuck-playbook and the minerva pipeline.

nodes.label: inject-minerva-critic PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: It injects the critic loop when brainstorming or writing-plans fires without /minerva; it matches by substring so retained aliases still trigger it, and is warn-only and fail-open.

nodes.label: cloud-route (/cloud-route)
nodes.rationale: Classifies tickets for the cloud lane and never launches because claude --cloud needs a TTY and spends credit.

nodes.label: fanout (/fanout)
nodes.rationale: Routes work items to lanes by type per the Subagent policy instead of per-dispatch judgement, with refusal enforced by a real validator.

nodes.label: memory-compound (/memory-compound)
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md content past 200 lines or 25 KB is silently dropped at load, so compaction into searchable vault notes avoids partial recall; it is operator-run because classification needs judgement.

nodes.label: release-manager skill
nodes.rationale: Every placement into a release is a reasoned ruling with sector, ground and reason rather than a count gate.

nodes.label: ticket-standard skill
nodes.rationale: Refuses drafts missing Plan, DoD or proof while parking them in an intake queue so nothing is discarded and style never blocks filing.

nodes.label: Symptom: PR merge blocked (--admin)
nodes.rationale: The repo has no branch protection so --admin bypasses nothing useful yet the classifier hard-vetoes it; the fix is not emitting it.

nodes.label: spawn-low haiku override limitation
nodes.rationale: The model override is not persisted through the inbox queue, so busy-session messages later run at the default model; deferred to a follow-up.

nodes.label: Triage verdicts ignore/ack/spawn-low/spawn-high
nodes.rationale: Verdicts map message value to cost: drop trivial messages and spawn cheap haiku or default-model runs for real ones.

nodes.label: Trust-path gate (exit 21, trust-reviewed GO mac)
nodes.rationale: Reading the pattern list from the default branch rather than the PR head means a PR cannot shrink its own gate, and a separate mac domain keeps an ordinary GO from being relabelled.

nodes.label: Handover state location modes (inline / vault / external)
nodes.norm_label: handover state location modes (inline / vault / external)
nodes.rationale: Inline state breaks from git worktrees while vault/external roots resolve from anywhere, so vault is recommended; duplicated modes are unsupported because the resolver reads a single root.

nodes.label: HANDOVER_DIR precedence reconcile
nodes.rationale: Project pin, user-scope pin and config files outrank .env, so a new choice would silently not take effect unless reconciled.

nodes.label: /handover-setup command
nodes.rationale: It is the single interactive place the state-root location is chosen, so every later session resolves it the same way without hardcoded paths.

nodes.label: Forks keep upstream LICENSE and document fork delta
nodes.norm_label: forks keep upstream license and document fork delta
nodes.rationale: Keeping the upstream license and a documented delta makes divergence from upstream auditable.

nodes.label: Mirrored commands must be edited together (HIMMEL-459)
nodes.norm_label: mirrored commands must be edited together (himmel-459)
nodes.rationale: The project copy is the bootstrap path and the plugin copy is reachable from any cwd, and they drifted once when only one was updated.

nodes.label: Stock Ubuntu has two PATH layers; non-interactive shells see only one
nodes.norm_label: stock ubuntu has two path layers; non-interactive shells see only one
nodes.rationale: ~/.bashrc early-returns for non-interactive shells so installer-added dirs vanish from scripts, so probes must state their shell layer and gates must resolve tools by known paths.

nodes.label: Auto-install with --ignore-scripts
nodes.rationale: --ignore-scripts is mandatory so no third-party postinstall script runs inside a pre-push gate.

nodes.label: uv.lock and hashed requirements pinning
nodes.rationale: Hand-edited requirements.txt files bypass tamper detection, so they are regenerated with hashes rather than patched.

nodes.label: Feature flags registry
nodes.rationale: Ships new behaviour dark with a 14-day expiry and bans flags around safety rails so flags cannot rot or disable guards.

nodes.label: You're in control section
nodes.rationale: Transparency (plain files, off switches, named network exceptions) builds trust that guards are the user's to lift.

nodes.label: Guard off switches (env vars)
nodes.rationale: Nearly every guard is bypassable via an env var in the launching shell so users can override, while secret-leak scans and the human-only public merge stay deliberately hard.

nodes.label: First protected project ten-step trail
nodes.rationale: The steps were run end to end on a clean VM so each step states the folder to run from and the expected output, and a mismatch tells the user to stop.

nodes.label: Symptom: Bash command stopped by permission prompt
nodes.norm_label: symptom: bash command stopped by permission prompt
nodes.rationale: Headless prompts resolve as silent DENY at rc=0, so the artifact must be verified rather than the return code.

nodes.label: Symptom: Jira write denied by classifier
nodes.norm_label: symptom: jira write denied by classifier
nodes.rationale: The hook approves only when every compound segment is a recognised-safe binary, so shape rather than the write itself causes denial.

nodes.label: Symptom: queue-lock.sh release denied [Merge Without Review]
nodes.norm_label: symptom: queue-lock.sh release denied [merge without review]
nodes.rationale: The classifier reads the session narrative (a merge just happened) not the payload, so the hook approves the exact bare literal shape.

nodes.label: Symptom: Write/Edit under /tmp refused (stray .git)
nodes.rationale: block-edit-on-main walks up ancestors, so a stray empty /tmp/.git from a fixture git init makes every temp write fail closed.

nodes.label: Never reshape a command to dodge a guardrail
nodes.norm_label: never reshape a command to dodge a guardrail
nodes.rationale: Guardrails are structural on purpose (structural over instructional), so a remaining denial is correct and should be deferred to the operator.

nodes.label: Symptom index
nodes.rationale: Mapping each guardrail symptom to a literal-command or structural remedy gets a blocked agent unstuck without workarounds.

nodes.label: Gates derive input from the guarded thing
nodes.norm_label: gates derive input from the guarded thing
nodes.rationale: A hand-maintained block list is a second copy of the truth that drifts and silently stops covering new features.

nodes.label: The five failure modes
nodes.rationale: Each failure mode is fixed at the lowest layer that can fix it, and each guardrail was added after a recorded failure.

nodes.label: Handover as readable markdown, not a memory backend
nodes.norm_label: handover as readable markdown, not a memory backend
nodes.rationale: Recording ship state in plain markdown preserves the why that paraphrase loses and lets humans read, correct and diff memory.

nodes.label: Pure-reader exporter and honest liveness
nodes.rationale: Guessing instrumentation is worse than none: crashed sessions never write an end record and a 10s scrape timeout caused 53 flap pages, so the timeout was set to 30s from measurement.

nodes.label: One writer per queue (directory lock)
nodes.rationale: Prose coordination failed three ways in one night, and mkdir is atomic with no check-then-create window.

nodes.label: Structural beats instructional escalation rule
nodes.rationale: Prose in a context window is a probability rather than a constraint, so the second drift escalates to a hook, gate or classifier instead of stronger prose.

nodes.label: Evidence-pool substrate (LUNA-83)
nodes.rationale: State is encoded by folder location instead of a lifecycle enum, keeping the model simple.

nodes.label: One-time backfill: /migrate-clip-lifecycle (LUNA-86)
nodes.rationale: Clips processed before LUNA-84 still sit in the inbox, and a six-form link rewrite avoids silently dangling .md-suffixed synthesis citations.

nodes.label: Quota-gauge (cross-lane quota observability)
nodes.rationale: It is passive and fails open so observing quota can never break, route, arm or block a session.

nodes.label: Epic / Task / Standalone item types
nodes.rationale: Three item types let multi-task bodies of work, units inside them, and one-offs each get an appropriate durable markdown structure.

nodes.label: Jira-keyed IDs with #N fallback
nodes.rationale: Jira keys give stable external IDs when available while a running #N keeps offline work trackable; counters are state-root-wide so buckets never collide (HIMMEL-129).

nodes.label: Two bucket axes (source-repo vs time-horizon)
nodes.rationale: The name sets are kept disjoint so /handover bucket can dispatch to the right axis by name alone.

nodes.label: init (new state) vs register (adopt existing state)
nodes.norm_label: init (new state) vs register (adopt existing state)
nodes.rationale: init refuses non-empty state and register is idempotent so partial bootstraps and existing state are handled without data loss.

nodes.label: source_buckets_extra field (HIMMEL-307)
nodes.rationale: Extra source buckets must be disjoint from time-horizon names and built-ins so /handover bucket axis dispatch stays unambiguous.

nodes.label: Bucket resolution (HIMMEL-129)
nodes.rationale: Longest-prefix Jira routing and explicit-only extra buckets keep multi-source work disambiguated without extra buckets capturing prefix-routed tickets.

nodes.label: Three-step canary protocol
nodes.rationale: Limiting the worker to acquire, append LIVE, append WRAPPED and release keeps the canary a minimal lane health probe.

nodes.label: Lane canary
nodes.rationale: Unit suites check only the generated command, so a no-op worker per lane verifies a worker actually starts, registers, receives its brief and writes a bullet.

nodes.label: digest-bump issue flow
nodes.rationale: The repo lets no workflow open a PR, so a rebuild opens an issue with the sed line and CI never changes by itself.

nodes.label: Bounce-safe stop/restart guard
nodes.rationale: Stopping the proxy while a client is connected would break in-flight work, so the script refuses unless forced.

nodes.label: Codex device-code re-login flow
nodes.rationale: Plain OAuth needs a localhost callback, while the device flow works over SSH with no local browser; the device URL and code are sensitive and must not reach shared logs.

nodes.label: request-retry and max-retry-interval keys
nodes.rationale: An upstream codex 502 ends a worker's turn and the only credential then cools down (503), so bounded retries soften transient failures.

nodes.label: Optional second codex credential
nodes.rationale: A second codex-*.json gives the cooldown another credential to fall back to, at the cost of two subscriptions' usage on one proxy.

nodes.label: doc-invariants CI job
nodes.rationale: Runs whole-tree invariant gates against a clean checkout where committed source and tooling are the same tree, and runs on the public mirror because Actions is disabled on private.

nodes.label: Silent-green gotchas (marker, staging, grep -q)
nodes.rationale: A no-op gate is indistinguishable from a passing one, so the marker, orphan staging step and avoiding grep -q under pipefail must be explicit to avoid silently removing the check.

nodes.label: Gates execute working-tree tooling, CI backstop
nodes.norm_label: gates execute working-tree tooling, ci backstop
nodes.rationale: Materializing tooling from the index was rejected because it does not close the hole (hook scripts still read from disk), so working-tree execution is kept and a clean-checkout CI job backs it up.
nodes.source_location: ### Gates execute working-tree tooling — and the CI backstop

nodes.label: Headline: rule file nearly free; skills near drop-in; hooks per-harness
nodes.norm_label: headline: rule file nearly free; skills near drop-in; hooks per-harness
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md and shared skill directories carry over, but each harness's hook schema and fail posture differ, so wiring is per-harness.

nodes.label: Harness prioritization: Codex primary, Cursor second, Gemini/Copilot deferred
nodes.norm_label: harness prioritization: codex primary, cursor second, gemini/copilot deferred
nodes.rationale: Operator has Codex-primary users with free OAuth usage while Gemini and Copilot have no free tier to justify porting cost.

nodes.label: himmelctl ui --service
nodes.rationale: A background service on a fixed port with a stable bookmark keeps the config UI running across logins.

nodes.label: Jira Sector opt-in change
nodes.rationale: jira create broke on every install lacking a Sector field, so Sector is now sent only when jira.sectorField is set.

nodes.label: Checked installation inventory
nodes.rationale: INSTALLED is defined narrowly (registry record or cached version dir) so the inventory can be compared against a station observation without implying enabled state.

nodes.label: Bulk guard on rm-run
nodes.rationale: Capping at 20 attempted moves per run limits the blast radius of a bulk fixVersion change and errs toward holding.

nodes.label: Embedding/rerank/enrichment are content egress
nodes.rationale: These lanes send full content, not metadata, so they must be gated like extraction.

nodes.label: publish-graph-map curator
nodes.rationale: The raw GRAPH_REPORT is 150KB+ and too big to track, so a ~10KB curated MOC keeps navigational value git-diffable and qmd-useful.

nodes.label: /memory-compound command
nodes.rationale: implied: it is a thin entry point that delegates to the himmel-ops:memory-compound skill runbook.

nodes.label: merge-public seven gates
nodes.rationale: Repo pin, fresh PR state, head identity, CI check, audit preflight, confirmed merge and CLAUDECODE self-refusal together stop retarget races, moved heads and agent-initiated calls.

nodes.label: Separate script rather than shared repo-class switch
nodes.norm_label: separate script rather than shared repo-class switch
nodes.rationale: A flag that inverts a safety boundary is the failure mode avoided; the public script's pin narrows what a human-only script may touch while merge-on-green's widens a boundary an agent runs under.

nodes.label: daylight factor
nodes.rationale: Uses each date's own latitude from the local location file so daylight stays correct across a relocation, with a region-centroid fallback.

nodes.label: lunar_phase factor
nodes.rationale: Computed offline from date alone, giving a factor with zero network and zero PHI (Posture-A).

nodes.label: block-busy-loop.sh plugin sleepless busy-loop deny
nodes.rationale: A while/until loop with no sleep spins a core at 100% CPU, and shipping it in the plugin lane makes it fire in adopter repos too.

nodes.label: --deep component scan
nodes.rationale: Inventories reusable components into a note section and deduped library, kept off by default to preserve the light MVP path.

nodes.label: Shell suites entrypoint and os-verify
nodes.rationale: One entrypoint shared with CI keeps local and CI corpora identical, and an on-demand dispatch-only os-verify avoids spending scarce macOS runners on every PR.

nodes.label: /minerva command
nodes.rationale: implied: it is a thin entry point that delegates to the himmel-ops:minerva skill runbook.

nodes.label: Oversized PR split by default
nodes.rationale: Splitting is the default over another review round, keeping whole is a signed recorded ruling, and trust-path or very large briefs escalate to the operator who alone can override.

nodes.label: uninstall-manifest.tsv
nodes.community_name: Uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps

nodes.label: uninstall.sh (updating doc ref)
nodes.community_name: Uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps

nodes.label: Uninstall manifest rows (owner, where, uninstall action)
nodes.community_name: Uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps
nodes.norm_label: uninstall manifest rows (owner, where, uninstall action)
nodes.rationale: The page mirrors the manifest the uninstaller reads and a test fails on drift, so the footprint list stays truthful.

nodes.label: Undo the install
nodes.community_name: Uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps
nodes.rationale: A single previewable, confirm-first command removes himmel's wiring while keeping operator state and anything the install record cannot prove it owns.

nodes.label: Uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps
nodes.community_name: Uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps
nodes.norm_label: uninstall flags, exit codes and eight steps
nodes.rationale: Destructive teardown is fail-closed with distinct exit codes and a live-HOME safety fence so it cannot run unconfirmed against a real home folder.

nodes.label: Plugins / marketplace and hooks.json description key
nodes.norm_label: plugins / marketplace and hooks.json description key
nodes.rationale: Codex before rust-v0.143.0 rejects the top-level description key, so a manual sanitizer exists for older pinned installs.

nodes.label: Skills and slash commands under Codex
nodes.norm_label: skills and slash commands under codex
nodes.rationale: Project slash commands do not auto-load in Codex, so thin tracked .agents/skills wrappers shell the same harness-neutral scripts without duplicating logic.

nodes.label: Approval-window / permission contract (ratified 2026-07-07)
nodes.rationale: Only Claude Code has a native semantic classifier and the fleet will not reimplement a weaker copy, so the contract is deterministic guard plus escalation plus post-hoc validation.

nodes.label: Codex-direct probe evidence: terminal write bypassed hook
nodes.norm_label: codex-direct probe evidence: terminal write bypassed hook
nodes.rationale: A patch-tool write was denied while a terminal write passed, showing the fix is structural (extend the hook matcher) rather than a classifier copy.

nodes.label: Codex worker / lane surfaces
nodes.rationale: Codex supervision scripts provide observability around an external harness, not the primary guard fence, so many cells remain unverified.

nodes.label: External lane worker
nodes.rationale: A separate harness process gives OS-level isolation and its own artifacts, so the parent reviews artifacts and branch state rather than trusting a final message.

nodes.label: Hermes one-shot lane (invoke.sh / dispatch-trusted.sh)
nodes.rationale: It has the clearest model/toolset selector and defaults to the todo toolset because one-shots auto-approve and run unattended.

nodes.label: Hermes one-shot and Codex spawn paths impl-dormant
nodes.norm_label: hermes one-shot and codex spawn paths impl-dormant
nodes.rationale: By operator ruling native Claude subagents are the default, so an unqualified impl dispatch refuses toward that path instead of picking a dormant lane.

nodes.label: Per-dispatch model selection
nodes.rationale: Probes proved it works on the one-shot lane via --model while native delegate_task is global-pin-only, so lane choice determines model control.

nodes.label: Gap: permission-window parity across lanes
nodes.rationale: Each lane handles approval prompts differently (stdin-closed, bypassPermissions, auto-approve), so a single matrix of which prompts stall is needed.

nodes.label: Job registry and MCP-fleet reap
nodes.rationale: The sandbox leaks MCP processes invisible to the app-server fingerprint, so the dispatcher records its child pid and reaps descendants itself.

nodes.label: Stuck PRs and stuck tickets scans
nodes.norm_label: stuck prs and stuck tickets scans
nodes.rationale: The tick fields do not say why a PR or ticket is stuck, so manual scans give per-item causes and dispositions.

nodes.label: worker-impl profile
nodes.rationale: Kept thin on purpose because the measured worker first-turn floor is dominated by built-in tool schemas, not by plugin or MCP rosters.

nodes.label: gitleaks: anchor allowlist regexes; pre-push scans staged INDEX
nodes.norm_label: gitleaks: anchor allowlist regexes; pre-push scans staged index
nodes.rationale: Unanchored allowlists suppress real secrets containing the literal, and staged secrets from one session block every session's push.

nodes.label: qmd: bun-shim PATH illusion, resumable embeds, index sharing and surgery
nodes.norm_label: qmd: bun-shim path illusion, resumable embeds, index sharing and surgery
nodes.rationale: The DB rather than config is authority on index contents and a shared index carries document text, so sensitive collections must be audited and never shared.

nodes.label: Auto-memory to vault loop
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md is paid for every turn and cannot grow unbounded, so durable learnings are distilled into searchable vault notes while the index stays lean.

nodes.label: Recommended pipeline cadence
nodes.rationale: Explicit cheap model pins keep scheduled jobs from inheriting the operator's default tier, making daily synthesis affordable.

nodes.label: Automatic vs scheduled vs manual capture tiers
nodes.norm_label: automatic vs scheduled vs manual capture tiers
nodes.rationale: Automatic capture only writes a session summary, so users must know which paths need explicit invocation to avoid silent gaps.

nodes.label: Clips / session-capture loop
nodes.rationale: Turns raw session output and inbox clips into triaged, synthesized content so knowledge compounds stage by stage.

nodes.label: Hook logs and raw transcript security
nodes.norm_label: hook logs and raw transcript security
nodes.rationale: Logs can contain pasted secrets, so they live outside any repo with owner-only permissions to prevent being committed.

nodes.label: Crystallization fields and mechanical baseline
nodes.rationale: Notes are first written mechanically and optionally upgraded by a best-effort LLM pass, so a note staying crystallized: false is a valid baseline rather than a failure.

nodes.label: Session note frontmatter fields
nodes.rationale: Optional epic/task keys are omitted rather than null so Dataview and frontmatter consumers treat absent keys consistently and notes stay scannable.

nodes.label: Three separate vault pipelines
nodes.rationale: Session capture, clip pipeline and memory-compound are often conflated, and only session capture writes sessions/.

nodes.label: Target vault resolution order
nodes.rationale: First-match-wins order with fail-closed skipping prevents a malformed config or missing vault from misrouting sensitive sessions or creating phantom vaults.

nodes.label: End-session wiki hook
nodes.rationale: A SessionEnd hook auto-captures each session into the Luna vault so no manual note-taking is needed.

nodes.label: Luna vault setup
nodes.rationale: Several later sections depend on the author's personal Obsidian vault, so the vault is flat at ~/Documents/luna and skippable as a unit.

nodes.label: Obsidian Web Clipper templates
nodes.rationale: Pre-built JSON templates installed by drag-and-drop let clipped pages land in Clippings/ in a consistent shape.

nodes.label: Vault resolution precedence (4 tiers)
nodes.rationale: A first-match-wins order lets per-repo config override global defaults while invalid input fails closed instead of misrouting.

nodes.label: luna loop: capture, ingest, link, recall
nodes.norm_label: luna loop: capture, ingest, link, recall
nodes.rationale: Automated capture and nightly linking make the vault fill and connect itself without user effort.

nodes.label: Luna-area docs convention
nodes.rationale: Operator-facing reference docs live in the repo while personal-state artifacts live in the state repo.

nodes.label: Star map of sample vault
nodes.rationale: It is drawn from a sample vault of invented notes, never a real one, to show linked clusters without exposing private notes.

nodes.label: End-session-wiki SessionEnd hook registration
nodes.rationale: Settings.json is backed up before any write and an Overwrite/Append/Skip prompt avoids clobbering existing SessionEnd hooks.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:contra skill
nodes.rationale: implied: holds the full CONTRA runbook so the command wrapper can stay thin.

nodes.label: relay-cost eval (HIMMEL-6992)
nodes.rationale: It asks what one relayed message costs and whether a cheaper way delivers it as correctly (operator decision 158).

nodes.label: Judge hand-off and replay
nodes.rationale: Replaying counterexamples against the real script guards against a wrong model, and stale or unchecked evidence cannot support a safety claim.

nodes.label: Morning report page (#/report)
nodes.rationale: A ledger of reported shifts ensures each shift lands in exactly one morning report even if it closes after midnight.

nodes.label: Shift cut rule and half-open window
nodes.norm_label: shift cut rule and half-open window
nodes.rationale: A half-open [opened, closed) window means a PR merged at the close instant belongs to exactly one shift.

nodes.label: Shift page (#/shift)
nodes.rationale: A shift spans the whole fleet between cuts with one writer of shifts.jsonl so PR credit and waiting rows are attributed once.

nodes.label: Tool health page (#/toolhealth)
nodes.rationale: Rolls up tool calls, failures and recovery on the server with explicit denominators so unknowns read as unknown, not 0 %.

nodes.label: Secrets manifest and secrets-doc drift gate
nodes.norm_label: secrets manifest and secrets-doc drift gate
nodes.rationale: A single metadata-only source generates both the wizard's secrets walk and the .env.example block so the two can never drift apart.

nodes.label: Secrets tile Account step (UI login)
nodes.rationale: The always-on UI needs a login, which can be created once from an ad-hoc UI and later changed only with --set-login in the user's own terminal.

nodes.label: Board lanes writing to Jira / local tracker
nodes.norm_label: board lanes writing to jira / local tracker
nodes.rationale: Dragging a card or setting Sector acts at once through the tracker seam with the same token gate, lock and audit so the board stays consistent.

nodes.label: Check this install strip
nodes.rationale: It runs read-only doctor checks and counts findings outside setup too, so a clean setup never sits beside a failure the user cannot see.

nodes.label: Config UI (himmelctl ui)
nodes.rationale: It is the only surface that writes, and it binds to loopback behind a per-launch token with dry-run-then-confirm switches to keep changes safe.

nodes.label: Shift page and shifts.jsonl
nodes.rationale: A shift is the whole fleet between cuts rather than one chief's run, so the page shows what waits on the user without acting.

nodes.label: Operator login and session cookie
nodes.rationale: A scrypt hash in the OS keyring and a global rate limit protect the one loopback login, since all clients share one address.

nodes.label: Dual-read fallback pattern for old names (legacyNamesOn)
nodes.norm_label: dual-read fallback pattern for old names (legacynameson)
nodes.rationale: Readers accept new names first and old names as fallback so producers and consumers can flip at different times without breakage.

nodes.label: N44 fleet manifest key legs to workers
nodes.norm_label: n44 fleet manifest key legs to workers
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL-8204 batch M3a has the reader take workers first and fall back to legs under legacyNamesOn, so old manifests keep working.

nodes.label: N45 board wire keys legs/leg_time/leg to workers/worker_time/worker
nodes.norm_label: n45 board wire keys legs/leg_time/leg to workers/worker_time/worker
nodes.rationale: normalizeBoard takes the new keys first and falls back to the old ones with no switch, because board.mjs emits the old keys until its M1 flip.

nodes.label: N45 board wire keys legs, leg_time, leg to workers, worker_time, worker
nodes.norm_label: n45 board wire keys legs, leg_time, leg to workers, worker_time, worker
nodes.rationale: board.mjs emits the old keys until its M1 flip, so the browser reader must fall back to the old keys until then.

nodes.label: N46 Jira label leg-blocked, [leg-sync], ?leg= renames
nodes.rationale: The sync reads both old and new label and comment forms so a ticket flagged before the rename is not flagged or noted twice, and old reads are removed only after a one-time Jira cleanup.

nodes.label: N46 Jira label leg-blocked, [leg-sync], ?leg= to worker-* names
nodes.norm_label: n46 jira label leg-blocked, [leg-sync], ?leg= to worker-* names
nodes.rationale: A Jira ticket and its mirror comment keep the name they were written under, so readers accept both names and a one-time cleanup runs before removal.

nodes.label: leg-blocked / [leg-sync] / ?leg= to worker-blocked / [worker-sync] / ?worker=
nodes.rationale: Renames Jira-facing identifiers to worker vocabulary with a one-time relabel cleanup so old labels do not become unfindable.

nodes.label: ANSI-C ($'...') fail-closed deny
nodes.rationale: Escape bodies are not decoded because a wrong decode risks a false ALLOW, so any such git segment is denied outright.

nodes.label: Dispatched-worker write fence (block-worker-write-fence.sh)
nodes.rationale: A dispatched worker must not forge a hook-integrity pin or repoint the origin default-branch anchor that the re-pin trusts, so command-text fences deny those and the hook fails closed for workers.

nodes.label: Delivery vs. enablement of plugin hooks
nodes.norm_label: delivery vs. enablement of plugin hooks
nodes.rationale: A hook present in the plugin hooks.json is inert if himmel-ops is toggled false per machine, so the gap was closed by probing the live enabled value and force-enabling rather than re-wiring settings chains.

nodes.label: Shared joiner across anchor class and GLM-lane shape matchers
nodes.norm_label: shared joiner across anchor class and glm-lane shape matchers
nodes.rationale: A divergent second copy is the ticket's recurring defect, and a dormant fence left rotten fails the day its lane returns.

nodes.label: Odd/even trailing-backslash parity rule
nodes.rationale: An escaped literal backslash ends the line, so joining on any trailing backslash would erase a real command boundary and fail open.

nodes.label: Quoting normalization (anchor_unquote) shared by both classes
nodes.norm_label: quoting normalization (anchor_unquote) shared by both classes
nodes.rationale: One shared normalizer avoids the drift where class (ii) was normalized and class (i) left open.

nodes.label: Round 5: line-continuation join before flattening
nodes.rationale: Bash deletes backslash-newline before parsing, so joining upstream of newline-to-semicolon flattening removes the axis.

nodes.label: Six defeated axes: remove the axis, don't append a spelling
nodes.norm_label: six defeated axes: remove the axis, don't append a spelling
nodes.rationale: Each failed round fixed the previous axis by adding list members, so future fixes should remove axes instead.

nodes.label: GLM lane (removed)
nodes.rationale: The lane was deleted but parity_guard still refuses that engine as untrusted to stay fail-closed.

nodes.label: Write-authority / external-write fence dimension
nodes.rationale: Write-authority is the load-bearing parity dimension but not a deny-guard hook, so it gets its own row so no cell is home-less.

nodes.label: Opt-in axes: scope, install profile, channel, plugin profile
nodes.norm_label: opt-in axes: scope, install profile, channel, plugin profile
nodes.rationale: Nothing is a package deal and each choice has a cost, so adopters are shown what each lands and costs before picking.

nodes.label: Three meanings of profile
nodes.rationale: Install profile, saved profile file and plugin profile are independent choices that are easily conflated, so they are named once.

nodes.label: Converge in place with himmelctl, not reinstall
nodes.norm_label: converge in place with himmelctl, not reinstall
nodes.rationale: ensure is additive and preserves recorded per-item choices, whereas uninstall then install would discard the wiring being preserved.

nodes.label: /backlog-reconcile
nodes.rationale: Defaults to dry-run and applies only on explicit operator approval, avoiding the earlier close-sweep's heavy agent fan-out.

nodes.label: Ubuntu desktop guest
nodes.rationale: X11 with Wayland disabled is required for clipboard and full-screen support in VirtualBox.

nodes.label: Destructive-command guard
nodes.rationale: Denying rm -rf, force pushes and hard resets before the Bash call runs prevents irreversible damage that cannot be undone afterwards.

nodes.label: Corpus resolution via shared primitives
nodes.rationale: Policy lives in the matrix while membership resolution stays with the existing guards to avoid duplicating or hardcoding paths.

nodes.label: Metered OpenRouter workers
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter sessions pay a real per-session prompt cost, so a credit-floor gate refuses launches when the balance is unknown or below the floor.

nodes.label: Not health-checked status
nodes.rationale: No scheduled canary proves the OpenRouter and DeepSeek launchers end to end, so users should check the provider before relying on them.

nodes.label: claude-deepseek launcher
nodes.rationale: Runs Claude Code against DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, gated by an opt-in, the egress matrix and a minimum balance.

nodes.label: CI image pinning decisions
nodes.rationale: Digest and sha256 pins make a tampered or re-rolled upstream artifact fail the build; pip hashes are skipped because nothing bumps the transitive closure.

nodes.label: Who can publish the image (digest-pin consumers)
nodes.norm_label: who can publish the image (digest-pin consumers)
nodes.rationale: GHCR access is per repository so any write holder can overwrite tags; consumers therefore pin by @sha256 digest, never by tag.

nodes.label: Own-inbox wake hold
nodes.rationale: Holding with a Monitor on the worker's inbox lets chief-owned blockers resolve instead of wrapping immediately, bounded to four hours.

nodes.label: Worker profiles and context defaults (worker-impl)
nodes.rationale: Profiles narrow the plugin set and MCP roster and inject the standing worker rules so briefs need not repeat them, with model-specific autocompact ceilings.

nodes.label: Worker context guard (compact|handoff)
nodes.rationale: Blocking ordinary work past a context-fill ceiling forces a worker to checkpoint or hand off before its context degrades.
nodes.source_location: What the chief must also do (a)

nodes.label: Convergence argument for shell-text-parsing guards
nodes.rationale: Text-parsing shell commands to enforce a guard keeps finding new alias shapes (PR 2353, 6+ judge rounds), so a convergence argument or a ponytail ceiling is required.

nodes.label: Guard escape tests block
nodes.rationale: Hand-written bypass rows triggered a safety classifier stop, so rows come only from the generated corpus and stops are never retried by rephrasing.

nodes.label: Inherited PR block and dispositions
nodes.rationale: A clean merge does not mean a PR is current, so the worker must pick MODERNIZE, REWORK or CLOSE and keep the original authors' credit.

nodes.label: Surface tickets route through minerva
nodes.rationale: One config UI shipped a single fact as two findings because nobody asked which existing surface already computed it, so a lint-clean spec is required first.
nodes.source_location: What the chief must also do (g)

nodes.label: Pre-granted follow-ups block
nodes.rationale: A ruling that only selects scope the dispatch already wrote down widens nothing, so it avoids being read as instruction poisoning by an auto-mode classifier.

nodes.label: Tier line (Opus/Fable only)
nodes.rationale: Requiring a categorized reason before an expensive model launches enforces 'raise effort before tier' while the free text keeps validation from falsely rejecting paraphrases.

nodes.label: Why each brief part is load-bearing
nodes.norm_label: why each brief part is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Each brief part exists because its absence caused a recorded failure such as wrong base, edit collisions, or unclosed tickets.

nodes.label: Merge only on chief GO quoting token
nodes.norm_label: merge only on chief go quoting token
nodes.rationale: Merging is gated on an explicit chief GO that quotes the worker token so a worker cannot self-authorise a merge.

nodes.label: Ship order: commit, push, pr-check, open PR
nodes.norm_label: ship order: commit, push, pr-check, open pr
nodes.rationale: One push per review round and a fixed order keep CI cost down and keep review rounds clean.

nodes.label: The chief
nodes.rationale: A persistent operator-facing session owns the shift and holds GO authority but never implements, keeping orchestration separate from implementation.

nodes.label: The reviewers
nodes.rationale: Every change is reviewed twice with a hard reviewer required at head so zero responders counts as a missing review, not a clean one.

nodes.label: Workers
nodes.rationale: One ticket, one worktree, one PR keeps work isolated and merge gated on the chief's GO.

nodes.label: Emergency /lockdown
nodes.rationale: A narrowing-only station-reset flag lets the operator stop all agent dispatch if the Telegram account is compromised, with no remote unlock.

nodes.label: Messaging a running chief via /chief
nodes.rationale: Appending to an inbox file watched by the chief delivers operator authority without starting a session or changing permissions.

nodes.label: himmel-gh dispatcher verb/state matrix
nodes.rationale: Refusing PR create on main/merged bases and admin merges prevents common slips, with narrow explicit overrides (flags consumed by the guard, admin env set in the launching shell because Claude cannot inject env vars into hook processes).

nodes.label: gh-pr-create skill
nodes.rationale: PR creation is team-visible, so title and body are confirmed first and always passed explicitly to avoid interactive hangs.

nodes.label: Config audit log, backups and restore
nodes.norm_label: config audit log, backups and restore
nodes.rationale: Makes a lost or shrunken station config loud and recoverable, logging key names only and restoring via a TOTP-gated bridge process.

nodes.label: himmel-secrets exec --require unit wrapping
nodes.rationale: Without --require a unit started before the wallet opens runs secretless and exits 0, looking healthy; refusing makes systemd retry.

nodes.label: Secrets keyring resolver order
