nodes.rationale: Serving secrets from env, credentials dir, keyring, then legacy .env keeps shell consumers unchanged while moving secrets off plaintext disk.

nodes.label: Station profiles
nodes.rationale: Allows named per-station behaviour sets tracked in the vault, selected only via untracked/env sources so tracked files cannot choose a profile.

nodes.label: Same-uid limitation of restore TOTP (ponytail)
nodes.rationale: Seed, backups and audit log share a uid with sessions, so TOTP defends only against a forged Telegram sender; a root-owned store is the upgrade path.

nodes.label: Blind >> onto .env glues onto last key
nodes.norm_label: blind >> onto .env glues onto last key
nodes.rationale: Without a trailing newline an append corrupts the previous key silently, so a leading newline guarantees separation.

nodes.label: .env first occurrence wins; empty value is absent
nodes.norm_label: .env first occurrence wins; empty value is absent
nodes.rationale: Shell and Python loaders must share one policy so an appended value is not shadowed by an empty placeholder and probes do not report credentials missing.

nodes.label: load_dotenv takes key names as arguments
nodes.norm_label: load_dotenv takes key names as arguments
nodes.rationale: A bare call loads only defaults, so a presence check looks like a loader defect when it is a call-shape defect.

nodes.label: Support matrix and install channels
nodes.rationale: Tiering Linux and macOS as supported and Windows/WSL as dropped states honestly what is CI-proven.

nodes.label: Cloud environment is created by dialog paste
nodes.norm_label: cloud environment is created by dialog paste
nodes.rationale: The platform offers no command, API or readback for cloud environments, so the dialog is the only creation path.

nodes.label: What stays local versus in the cloud
nodes.norm_label: what stays local versus in the cloud
nodes.rationale: Private vault data, handover state, Jira tokens and non-Claude lanes must not or cannot reach the cloud VM.

nodes.label: Local shepherd for cloud PRs
nodes.rationale: The cloud session never merges; a local shepherd runs the coverage lint, suites, CI and the ready check before the chief merges on GO.

nodes.label: No secrets in cloud environment variables
nodes.norm_label: no secrets in cloud environment variables
nodes.rationale: Everyone who uses the environment can read its variables, so a secret there would leak; Jira goes through the Atlassian connector instead.

nodes.label: /cloud-route ticket classification
nodes.rationale: Only small, well-scoped Claude-only tickets suit the cloud lane, so tickets are classified before launch.

nodes.label: Checked-in single source for dialog contents
nodes.norm_label: checked-in single source for dialog contents
nodes.rationale: With no platform mechanism to detect dialog drift, himmel keeps the content in one repo source and checks the dialog against it.

nodes.label: Extract only explicit dated values
nodes.rationale: Inferring from relative statements like 'worse lately' would fabricate health data.

nodes.label: Forge-aware PR thread commands (GitHub GraphQL vs Bitbucket REST)
nodes.norm_label: forge-aware pr thread commands (github graphql vs bitbucket rest)
nodes.rationale: Bitbucket Cloud has no GraphQL, so its flat comment+parent model is mapped into the same thread abstraction with an identical 6-char prefix cache.

nodes.label: Per-PR 6-char prefix thread cache
nodes.rationale: Keying by (owner, repo, PR-N) lets reply/resolve commands expand short prefixes into full thread ids.

nodes.label: Enforcement-path deny-list classes
nodes.rationale: A lesson must not weaken the fences, hooks, validators, settings or rule files that would catch it.

nodes.label: steps.json count field is provisional
nodes.rationale: The step-count field name was not confirmed against a live response when authored, so it must be verified before production use.

nodes.label: qmd Updated figure is a proxy (source-file mtime)
nodes.norm_label: qmd updated figure is a proxy (source-file mtime)
nodes.rationale: qmd's Updated is MAX(modified_at) of source files, not a refresh timestamp, so the banner states both readings rather than asserting staleness to avoid a daily-wrong warning.

nodes.label: Required collections opt-in (QMD_STALENESS_REQUIRE_COLLECTIONS)
nodes.rationale: A station missing a whole collection scores perfectly on freshness and completeness, and the required set is per-station policy the script cannot infer.

nodes.label: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction
nodes.rationale: Correcting all best-lag p-values together at q=0.1 controls false discoveries across many comparisons.

nodes.label: Boundary B+C (only factors.cache touches network)
nodes.rationale: Confining network access to one gated, logged tool keeps all joins offline so the operator's date-by-place data never leaves the machine.

nodes.label: Cache location (LUNA_CORRELATE_CACHE_DIR)
nodes.rationale: The tests point the cache at a per-run temp dir (HIMMEL-370) so they can never write through to the real operator cache.

nodes.label: Candidate signals only, never diagnosis or causation
nodes.norm_label: candidate signals only, never diagnosis or causation
nodes.rationale: Correlation outputs are exploratory and must not be read as medical diagnosis or proof of cause.

nodes.label: Era split at Fitbit to Galaxy boundary (2025-01-01)
nodes.norm_label: era split at fitbit to galaxy boundary (2025-01-01)
nodes.rationale: The device change shifts sensor baselines, so splitting prevents the step change from contaminating correlations.

nodes.label: kp factor
nodes.rationale: Global geomagnetic index joined by date only, so no location is needed and the high/low split uses the geomagnetic-storm cutoff Kp>=5.

nodes.label: GFZ Potsdam Kp archive source
nodes.rationale: Adopted because it is a public institution, CC BY 4.0, needs no auth, and the plain file download transmits no PHI or location.

nodes.label: Lag sweep (best lag per pair)
nodes.rationale: Testing lags -3..+3 days finds the strongest timing, and the lag-profile chart shows whether the best lag is a real peak or selection noise.

nodes.label: M3 dashboard methodology
nodes.rationale: Combines lag sweep, era split and FDR correction so many comparisons yield only candidate signals, with the inflation from best-lag selection disclosed.

nodes.label: Median split for continuous location factors
nodes.norm_label: median split for continuous location factors
nodes.rationale: Continuous factors have no universal high/low cutoff, so the median is a generic rule with no per-factor magic number.

nodes.label: codex-cli 0.153 SessionEnd timeout clamp
nodes.rationale: Over-declared SessionEnd timeouts are clamped to 3s with a loud warning and can kill a hook mid-flight, so himmel-ops declares timeout 3 and detaches the body.

nodes.label: Verdict-only amend of producer-written findings
nodes.rationale: Recording only an id and closed-vocabulary verdict removes the last reviewer-authored bytes from the shell fence, closing an injection surface.

nodes.label: Producers self-write findings; session amends verdict only
nodes.norm_label: producers self-write findings; session amends verdict only
nodes.rationale: Retyping reviewer text into a shell fence breaks on apostrophes, so only an id and closed-vocabulary verdict are passed.

nodes.label: Availability records always appended
nodes.rationale: The chokepoint needs an avail ok row to certify a review happened, so a clean zero-finding review must still be recorded.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit is the GitHub App only (best effort)
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit is the github app only (best effort)
nodes.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-07: findings are tracked on the PR in GitHub, and each CLI round cost an extra paid codex panel row.

nodes.label: Out-of-scope blocking finding deferred, never downgraded
nodes.norm_label: out-of-scope blocking finding deferred, never downgraded
nodes.rationale: Recording as sug or disproved would be false, so a truthful third exit with ticket and reason is provided.

nodes.label: deferred verdict (requires ticket)
nodes.rationale: Real but out-of-scope findings need an honest exit that is neither agreed (re-raised forever) nor disproved (a lie).

nodes.label: Excluded-from-blocking rule (all disproved or deferred)
nodes.rationale: Requiring every verdict to be disproved or deferred keeps the rule fail-closed so mixed disproved/unaddressed cannot slip through.

nodes.label: Orphan check (phase-A candidates missing from aggregate)
nodes.norm_label: orphan check (phase-a candidates missing from aggregate)
nodes.rationale: A candidate dropped in the carry-forward must read as unaddressed so a forgotten step fails closed instead of shipping a false-clean.

nodes.label: Structural not instructional signal
nodes.rationale: Prose does not enforce, so the blocking count is derived from persisted verdicts rather than asserted by the session.

nodes.label: VERDICT line format (agreed/disproved/conflict/unaddressed/deferred)
nodes.rationale: A single standard verdict line lets every reader parse the same adjudication structurally instead of from prose.

nodes.label: Cap gate
nodes.rationale: Limits open residual tickets per unreleased version (15 by default) and ranks newcomers so follow-ups do not crowd out planned work.

nodes.label: Verdict (CR)
nodes.rationale: Each finding gets one disposition, and 'fixed' only comes from promotion on a clean round so claims of fixing are verified.

nodes.label: Follow-up (residual)
nodes.rationale: Work found by review and deferred must be filed as its own linked ticket so it is counted and not lost; docs use the plain word while labels keep 'residual'.

nodes.label: Follow-up budget
nodes.rationale: A monitor, not a quota: beyond 15 open follow-ups new ones compete on rank.

nodes.label: Follow-up depth
nodes.rationale: implied: tracking follow-ups of follow-ups lets depth 2 or more be sent to the backlog instead of the current version.

nodes.label: Operator-directed
nodes.rationale: Work filed on explicit operator instruction should not be throttled by the follow-up budget.

nodes.label: Verdict labels: by-design vs disproved
nodes.rationale: Recording a true-but-intended finding as disproved wrongly counts an accurate finding against the critic in cr-tune scoring.

nodes.label: Judge J1407A verdict on PR #1407
nodes.rationale: Concrete case where codex-1 and codex-2 true claims were recorded disproved because the round adjudicated 'keep the behavior'.

nodes.label: File deferred items as real tickets
nodes.norm_label: file deferred items as real tickets
nodes.rationale: Anything not in Jira drops out of the where-are-we ledger and morning report and is silently lost.

nodes.label: Gate 4g (missing-comment-review, exit 14)
nodes.rationale: It makes the comment review non-skippable: a misjudged skip costs a retry, never a pass, and an unreadable counter refuses closed.

nodes.label: Step 3.7 comment review (full lane, after reviewer stage 3.5)
nodes.norm_label: step 3.7 comment review (full lane, after reviewer stage 3.5)
nodes.rationale: Comments need semantic judgment that a deterministic lint cannot provide, so an agent reads the diff's added comments and reports which to delete.

nodes.label: comments ledger row
nodes.rationale: The row records the review at its head so the gate can verify it covers all comments added up to the tip.

nodes.label: Findings adjudication (kill / MUST KILL verdicts)
nodes.rationale: MUST KILL may be deferred with a ticket because the fix is a rename, extract or restructure outside the diff's purpose.

nodes.label: Skip reasons: codex-lane, agent-not-loaded
nodes.rationale: The Codex lane has no Agent dispatch and the plugin may not be loaded, so only these two skip reasons are allowed and ledger-append.sh refuses others.

nodes.label: shadcn-mcp README
nodes.rationale: Upstream ships no Claude plugin, so himmel wraps the shadcn CLI MCP server for the design profile (HIMMEL-4012).

nodes.label: Burned phase-1 rows
nodes.rationale: A tuner climbed against that sealed half so it was rotated out and its rows are not comparable.

nodes.label: Sealed targets not met
nodes.rationale: Every flip was noise-sized, so no edit is justified and targets move to HIMMEL-8158.

nodes.label: Trim arm listing (3257 tokens)
nodes.rationale: Trimming the listing lowered cost per run while keeping open and sealed accuracy at or above climb.

nodes.label: Telegram bridge onboarding
nodes.rationale: Setup is scaffold-only and never writes access.json or starts the bridge, because the allowlist is a prompt-injection surface and a blind start could 409-conflict a live poller.

nodes.label: Bun bridge vs plugin bridge mutual exclusivity
nodes.norm_label: bun bridge vs plugin bridge mutual exclusivity
nodes.rationale: Both bridges own getUpdates for the same bot token, so only one may run at a time.

nodes.label: Privileged auto-commands /arm /mergepub /restart
nodes.rationale: Executed by the trusted bridge rather than a Claude session so the agent is never in the trust path, and they ship disabled with fail-closed guards and an audit log.

nodes.label: /restart rung 1 vs rung 2
nodes.rationale: Rung 1 respawn inherits the supervisor's frozen environment and only picks up file-based changes, while rung 2 has no executor on any platform.

nodes.label: Check-then-start bridge procedure
nodes.rationale: Blind-starting a second poller causes a 409 getUpdates conflict storm, so status must be checked first and pkill bun is forbidden.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_AUTO_ACTIONS enablement
nodes.rationale: Explicit per-op enablement, with merge-public EXPLICIT_ONLY, prevents an operator running =1 from silently inheriting the public merge capability.

nodes.label: Instance-scoped kills
nodes.rationale: Name-matching alone once let a test fixture SIGKILL the operator's live bridge, so kills require instance ownership evidence.

nodes.label: approve/deny AFK requests over SSH
nodes.rationale: Refusing unless run as operator_user keeps SSH from adding a new approver, with the helper making all other checks.

nodes.label: ensure is converge-only unless --prune
nodes.rationale: Unwiring an item is higher-risk, so it needs separate consent and is never bundled into the same prompt.

nodes.label: gaps is a static report, not a gate
nodes.norm_label: gaps is a static report, not a gate
nodes.rationale: It diffs saved profiles rather than probing live state, so it informs and exits 0 instead of blocking.

nodes.label: scope set refuses items wired in both scopes
nodes.norm_label: scope set refuses items wired in both scopes
nodes.rationale: Fail-closed behavior prevents a half-migrated install where an item is active in both scopes.

nodes.label: Four migration from-states
nodes.rationale: Each legacy situation (old adopt.sh wiring, hand setup, old remote, stale hook wiring) needs a different detect/converge/rollback path.

nodes.label: Adopter config file ~/.himmel/config.json
nodes.rationale: A single runtime config document that older files migrate into, never rejecting or dropping user values, lets luna and bridge subsystems read one source.

nodes.label: himmelctl ensure
nodes.rationale: Converging and disabling are separately consented so an operator is not forced to accept unwanted disables to get one wanted convergence.

nodes.label: himmelctl install rough edges (user scope, headless --from-profile)
nodes.norm_label: himmelctl install rough edges (user scope, headless --from-profile)
nodes.rationale: Project scope copies the checkout onto itself and headless installs refuse without a profile, so user scope and a hand-seeded profile cache complete the install.

nodes.label: himmelctl status
nodes.rationale: A read-only diff of desired vs actual state is the shared pre/post-check primitive for later verbs, and opt-in subsystems report n/a so a fresh install does not look red.

nodes.label: Installer places git hooks by default; ticket discipline on
nodes.norm_label: installer places git hooks by default; ticket discipline on
nodes.rationale: Without a config file framework hooks skip every commit, so himmel writes native gates directly and enforces ticket references unless opted out.

nodes.label: HIMMELCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD handling
nodes.rationale: Unattended apt installs need sudo, so the password goes only to stdin and is scrubbed from child environments to avoid leaks.

nodes.label: Always-on UI service (himmel-ui.service)
nodes.rationale: A systemd user unit on a fixed port with a persistent mode-600 token keeps the bookmarked URL valid across restarts.

nodes.label: himmelctl install scopes
nodes.rationale: Project and user scopes let adopters choose between per-repo wiring and machine-wide guards, with each step optional and reversible.

nodes.label: Event-time flow families (last_failure_timestamp, stalled_current)
nodes.rationale: Expiring old failures simply disappear so they cannot page, and dead-pid starts are split into abandoned so only actionable hangs page.

nodes.label: Luna git divergence gauges
nodes.rationale: A gitleaks false positive silently blocked pushes with no visible signal, so local-refs-only counts expose it without a fetch that would violate passivity.

nodes.label: Passivity invariant
nodes.rationale: The exporter is a pure reader so observing can never alter ledgers, kill processes or enforce policy, and missing data stays missing rather than fabricated.

nodes.label: GET /sessions.json per-session endpoint
nodes.rationale: Per-session ids are unbounded and cannot be Prometheus labels, so a second read shape of the same ledger serves detail without letting table and gauges disagree.

nodes.label: Window-folded counters
nodes.rationale: Counters folded from a sliding ledger window decrease as rows age out, so alerts use event-time families instead to avoid phantom spikes from counter resets.

nodes.label: Cleanups in capped batches
nodes.rationale: The 20-file cap comes from the history-comment prune data (median merge touched 21 files), preventing open-ended cleanup PRs.

nodes.label: Code review (CR) gate hardening
nodes.rationale: Repeated fixes ensure merges require resolved review findings and a trust-reviewed GO on trust-path PRs so a vacuous green cannot merge.

nodes.label: Shell guard and auto-approve hardening
nodes.rationale: implied: shell parsing has many bypass shapes (brace expansion, fd-dup, env wrappers), so guards fail closed on shapes they cannot parse.

nodes.label: macOS portability and nightly triage effort
nodes.norm_label: macos portability and nightly triage effort
nodes.rationale: Windows and macOS run on a nightly cadence, so slices of HIMMEL-3719 and HIMMEL-3699 fix bash 3.2/BSD tool failures to make macOS a supported platform at v1.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.10
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release dominated by guard hardening and macOS portability fixes ahead of v1.

nodes.label: Release v1.0.0 (2026-09-30)
nodes.rationale: First stable v1 release (HIMMEL-3603) with macOS declared supported and PR CI narrowed to impacted suites.

nodes.label: Per-suite --allow-tools grant as permission boundary
nodes.rationale: claude plugin eval never prompts and has no --permission-mode flag, so the narrowest explicit tool grant per suite is the only permission control.

nodes.label: /plugin-eval
nodes.rationale: Runs exactly one eval suite for one plugin and never all suites, avoiding CI or cadence wiring costs.

nodes.label: Eval suite qmd collections-scoping
nodes.rationale: Asserting zero out-of-scope calls rather than bounding in-scope count avoids false failures when a legitimate turn makes two scoped calls.

nodes.label: Eval suite read-link-vault-first (RED control)
nodes.rationale: prompt.md is natural language because a literal slash command was intercepted by the dispatcher in the WITHOUT arm before any model turn ran.

nodes.label: Eval suite telegram-clip-basic
nodes.rationale: Grades a Telegram-shaped prompt on clip filename and frontmatter; it needs --scaffold because case.yaml declares a scaffold_script.

nodes.label: Plugin evals (on-demand, billed)
nodes.rationale: Each eval run is a billed call against the subscription budget, so evals are on-demand only and never wired into CI.

nodes.label: Subagents inherit the parent window; no per-subagent control
nodes.norm_label: subagents inherit the parent window; no per-subagent control
nodes.rationale: The Agent tool selects only a model tier, not a context mode, so context must be chosen at the parent's arming.

nodes.label: HIMMEL project
nodes.rationale: Default project for the jira CLI covering himmel engineering, infra and tooling, with all himmel Epics.

nodes.label: LUNA project
nodes.rationale: Separate project for Luna vault work so Luna-specific tickets are tracked apart from himmel infra.

nodes.label: Standalones as Stories convention
nodes.rationale: Standalones were historically untracked in Jira; from 2026-05-19 they are filed as Stories in their topical project for traceability.

nodes.label: Theme label (theme-<slug>)
nodes.rationale: At most one theme label per ticket lets roadmap and tracker read the theme first and fall back to plan themes only when absent.

nodes.label: Deadline misses stop the whole process tree
nodes.norm_label: deadline misses stop the whole process tree
nodes.rationale: Signalling only the direct child left descendants running outside the concurrency bound and overlapping the retry, recreating the fan-out the queue removes.

nodes.label: claude-headless.sh EXIT trap can kill launching session
nodes.norm_label: claude-headless.sh exit trap can kill launching session
nodes.rationale: An early refusal path exits before the wrapper assigns its own CLAUDE_PID, so the trap kills the inherited session PID; env -u CLAUDE_PID is the interim guard.

nodes.label: Registry-driven implementation dispatch
nodes.rationale: One Bash dispatcher with no wrapper agent supervising the worker, and an unqualified dispatch refuses rather than silently spending a GPT-backed subscription budget (operator ruling 2026-08-19).

nodes.label: Scripts requiring bash 4+ (mapfile)
nodes.rationale: These scripts use mapfile, which fails on macOS system bash 3.2, so users must install bash 4+ or port to a read loop.

nodes.label: macOS additions (bash 4, at, coreutils, bun tap, stale marker guard, scheduled token)
nodes.norm_label: macos additions (bash 4, at, coreutils, bun tap, stale marker guard, scheduled token)
nodes.rationale: macOS ships bash 3.2, has no GNU timeout, and cron cannot read the login Keychain, so extra steps are needed.

nodes.label: macOS alpha scope (not a full bootstrap)
nodes.norm_label: macos alpha scope (not a full bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: No macOS CI/VM exists, so the script is only mock-tested and wires just the auto-arm chain bits using crontab, since atrun is off by default and SIP-fragile.

nodes.label: leg_ledger: digests into worker ledgers
nodes.rationale: The digest is written last as a commit marker, making recording idempotent per session under a flock.

nodes.label: Four slices merged with aliases (V3, V1, V2, V5, plus V4a-1)
nodes.norm_label: four slices merged with aliases (v3, v1, v2, v5, plus v4a-1)
nodes.rationale: These slices merged before the no-alias ruling, so they left forwarders, command aliases and read-both env names that HIMMEL-6647 must remove.

nodes.label: Family F10 overnight to afk rename (slice V3)
nodes.norm_label: family f10 overnight to afk rename (slice v3)
nodes.rationale: implied: afk describes the autonomous mode regardless of time of day, so the overnight vocabulary is replaced consistently.

nodes.label: Family F9 console to chief rename (slice V5)
nodes.norm_label: family f9 console to chief rename (slice v5)
nodes.rationale: Groups the command, script, skill, agent and hook renames of the console role to chief under owner HIMMEL-6647.

nodes.label: N01 CONSOLE_* to CHIEF_* env vars
nodes.norm_label: n01 console_* to chief_* env vars
nodes.rationale: V5 renamed the console role to chief, but 314 lines in 49 files still use the old operator-typed and script-local env names.

nodes.label: No-alias breaking-change ruling (2026-10-24)

nodes.norm_label: pr 1d: chief leftovers (n01, n23-n27, n36, n39)

nodes.norm_label: n36 hooks console-compact-reinject.sh, guard-console-foreground.sh to chief names
nodes.rationale: Hooks are registered in .claude/settings.json, requiring an operator edit; new names not live (0/2) and two test names have no ruled name.

nodes.label: Never invent a message-id rule
nodes.rationale: A fabricated id would defeat --msg-id idempotency, so the skill stops and asks instead.

nodes.label: Cadence runner platform-specific format twins
nodes.rationale: Reading only the extension the current platform executes keeps a dormant twin from pinning a false-stale floor.

nodes.label: himmel-doctor diagnostic
nodes.rationale: A read-only severity-grouped diagnostic (except --fix) surfaces environment drift; C28 distinguishes declined, failed-partway and never-asked consent rather than conflating them.

nodes.label: auto-arm scheduler backend
nodes.rationale: Status mirrors what arm-resume.sh selects so usage-cap auto-resume cannot silently no-op on a missing or dead backend.

nodes.label: Pre-commit gates and their CI copy
nodes.norm_label: pre-commit gates and their ci copy
nodes.rationale: Contributors without hooks or using --no-verify skip every pre-commit gate, so each gate is mirrored in CI from its BASE copy (a PR cannot weaken the gate that judges it) or declared local by nature.

nodes.label: librarian-cadence
nodes.rationale: implied: schedules the librarian daily with a flow-run row and failure alert, and remains a dry run unless the operator arms with --apply.

nodes.label: Promote-only orphan recovery (HIMMEL-3205)
nodes.rationale: Re-promotes a finished but un-promoted extraction so the cost of a second extraction is not paid after a runner was killed mid-flight.

nodes.label: Direct-eval mode (--eval)
nodes.rationale: Hooks never see graphify calls made by scripts, so non-hook callers run the same evaluation directly instead of keeping a private policy copy.

nodes.label: Kimi/moonshot retirement
nodes.rationale: The backend itself was retired, not de-listed for quality, so rows are deleted and moonshot falls to default deny.

nodes.label: refresh-graph-map orchestrator
nodes.rationale: It extracts from a scratchpad copy so extraction never touches a live vault, and a concurrency knob eases rate limits though it is only a band-aid.

nodes.label: Four judge-question fields (grade/prior/answer/flipped)
nodes.rationale: Recording the prior before asking makes the judge flip rate (M3) measurable by grep.

nodes.label: Fleet manifest arming
nodes.rationale: Keeping the worker set in a manifest the tick re-reads removes the need to restart the waiter on every dispatch and wrap.

nodes.label: Waiter script relay (R0) wrapping workers
nodes.rationale: Scripting wraps and merges absorbs routine worker closes without a wake, with a 240 s bound that keeps the heartbeat under consumers' 300 s floor.

nodes.label: Fleet manifest
nodes.rationale: A manifest re-read on every sample means a dispatch or wrap needs no waiter restart, and it is updated only on successful launch or close.

nodes.label: Removal ratchets are one-shot helpers
nodes.rationale: Run forever, a removal ratchet catches nothing new and fails on unrelated work, so it is run once by hand under scripts/one-shot/ and kept out of suites, hooks and CI.

nodes.label: Eval results metrics and rules
nodes.rationale: Porting eval-compare's candidate/baseline and noise-band verdict into gauges lets regressions and staleness alert passively.

nodes.label: himmel-health dashboard
nodes.rationale: An operator-facing view ordered by whether himmel is healthy and what to do, with inert provisioning templates so a missing provider path cannot break Grafana.

nodes.label: eval-compare regression gate
nodes.rationale: A regression is judged against a noise band (CI overlap or configured band) so run-to-run noise is not flagged as a regression.

nodes.label: Chokepoint fixtures and the seam guard
nodes.norm_label: chokepoint fixtures and the seam guard
nodes.rationale: The guard enforces only on the anchor checkout so scratch copies can set seams per call while a real-copy run inside a Claude session exits 96 by design.

nodes.label: Corpus/replay containment via sandbox runner
nodes.rationale: A hook or harness bug must still meet a filesystem fence, and destructive execution stays VM-only, so replay runs in a confined sandbox that refuses rather than falling back to the host.

nodes.label: T13(b) marker-only exemption
nodes.rationale: A per-line lexical carve-out could not tell real pgrep from shadowing functions and each fix left a new bypass, so it was removed in favour of one hardened trailing marker.

nodes.label: test-audit skill for writing/reviewing tests
nodes.rationale: Rejects junk tests (self-comparison, source grep, unrelated-failure controls) and requires RED-before-green so assertions prove behaviour.

nodes.label: test-ws5-invariants.sh and renames
nodes.rationale: T13(b) uses a full-tree diff so rename pairing applies, correcting an earlier false positive from a per-file pathspec.

nodes.label: Ubuntu server cloud-init guest
nodes.rationale: NIC and port forward are set in separate modifyvm calls because a combined call aborts on a rule-exists error and leaves the NIC bridged.

nodes.label: attack-the-premise
nodes.rationale: After two fixes sharing an assumption fail, test the assumption instead of starting a third fix.

nodes.label: build-the-lever
nodes.rationale: A rerunnable script can be reviewed and redone, whereas hand edits can only be redone.

nodes.label: make-operations-idempotent
nodes.rationale: Steps must survive running twice and dying halfway.

nodes.label: migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
nodes.rationale: With no external users, a compatibility layer is dead weight and should be removed in the same change.

nodes.label: outcome-oriented-execution
nodes.rationale: Planned intermediate breakage is acceptable in phased migrations to reach a verified end state without throwaway compatibility code.

nodes.label: test-behavior-not-implementation
nodes.rationale: Tests should fail when behavior breaks and pass when internals are restructured.

nodes.label: Advisory skill scan: SkillSpector Stage 1 (HIMMEL-5913)
nodes.rationale: Wrapper refuses unless provider is ollama because the upstream default sends skill text to build.nvidia.com.

nodes.label: No-egress provider requirement (SKILLSPECTOR_PROVIDER=ollama)
nodes.rationale: Upstream defaults an unset provider to nv_build, which sends the skill text to build.nvidia.com, so the wrapper refuses to run unless the provider is ollama.

nodes.label: Partial scan is never clean
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 never returns SAFE alone, so truncated listings, capped skills, incomplete skills and wrapper failures are recorded as flagged or unavailable rather than clean.

nodes.label: Pinned commit sha for tree and contents fetch
nodes.norm_label: pinned commit sha for tree and contents fetch
nodes.rationale: Resolving the ref to one sha makes the scanned text a single revision of the clipped text.

nodes.label: Phase 3.7 advisory skill scan (--skill-scan)
nodes.rationale: A clipped skill gets an opt-in, advisory SkillSpector Stage 1 scan so the reader checks the flagged line before adopting it, while the pilot's false positives mean it must never block or change trust_tier.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up (HIMMEL-2134)
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump reaches the repo but not the machine, and the drift check reads synced_base rather than the installed artifact, so the staleness is otherwise invisible.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump updates the repo but not the machine, and drift guards read the synced pin rather than the installed artifact, so the catch-up steps must run unconditionally.

nodes.label: update-marketplaces
nodes.rationale: It re-syncs manual marketplaces that nothing else refreshes, failure-isolated per row, with distinct exit codes separating 'could not look' from 'looked and found broken'.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up steps (HIMMEL-2134)
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump can reach the repo but never the machine, and the drift check cannot see that staleness.

nodes.label: Base verification on a fence (chief ruling 66)
nodes.norm_label: base verification on a fence (chief ruling 66)
nodes.rationale: Arming on a base whose merged PR after-report was still running left a dependent worker building on an unverified base.

nodes.label: Codex adversarial pass removed
nodes.rationale: It sat dormant, used the same OpenAI budget as the panel codex critic, agreed on only 6% of findings versus 23%, and the re-runs-the-suite hypothesis was disproved.

nodes.label: One-suite-run invariant
nodes.rationale: Only the after-report Summary comment is consumed by PR gates so no merge or CR path re-runs the suite against a head that already carries one.

nodes.label: Auto-action guards (operator-identity, typed-only, forward-refuse)
nodes.rationale: Forwarded, captioned or non-operator /arm commands are the prompt-injection vectors, so they fall through to powerless chat or are refused and audited.

nodes.label: Auth model B2 (trusted bridge, operator-identity)
nodes.rationale: The bridge parses the structured command itself and the agent is never trusted, so injected body content cannot arm anything.

nodes.label: EXPLICIT_ONLY_OPS (merge-public must be named)
nodes.rationale: Blanket =1/all aliases must not let an operator running arm-resume silently inherit the privileged merge capability (a review finding).

nodes.label: merge-public op (/mergepub, Telegram-authorized public merge)
nodes.rationale: Makes the operator's typed Telegram command the only way a public squash-merge is authorized, with a 12-hex SHA floor to blunt prefix-grinding attacks.

nodes.label: restart op (bridge bouncing itself)
nodes.rationale: It sits in the ordinary tier because it does no git write and its worst case is a bridge that comes back up, with the supervisor's POLLER_MAX_FAILS breaker as a backstop against restart loops.

nodes.label: Telegram /arm remote auto-action
nodes.rationale: Gives the operator a sanctioned bounded privileged action from Telegram without placing the spawned agent in the trust path.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_AUTO_ACTIONS activation flag (default OFF)
nodes.rationale: A per-op enable-list mirroring HIMMEL_INITIATIVE grammar means users learn one convention while every op stays disabled by default.

nodes.label: One owner per guard hook
nodes.rationale: A hook wired from two settings layers runs twice per call, costing two bash startups and duplicate log rows.

nodes.label: Adopted-features e2e stage
nodes.rationale: It checks that each feature works from an adopted scratch project with the staged tree hidden.

nodes.label: Lane quota gauges
nodes.rationale: Only live, unexpired readings are emitted and unavailable banks appear as comments, so no quota value is ever fabricated.

nodes.label: Verdict: safe after named fixes
nodes.rationale: The guard covers catastrophic classes and the default toolset exposes no terminal, so no separate sandbox is needed once the named gaps are fixed.

nodes.label: Context-window budgeting per provider
nodes.rationale: The provider-enforced window can differ from a slug's marketing maximum (Codex gpt-5.5 at 272K vs about 1M on the OpenAI API), so hardcoding a larger value would over-budget prompts the backend rejects.

nodes.label: himmel_agent main tier (alpha)
nodes.rationale: It gives a capable main puller for engineering, research and vault work when Claude capacity is scarce, but it stays experimental until it has more live mileage.

nodes.label: parity_guard pre-tool guard
nodes.rationale: It keeps the secret-read fence, self-protection and catastrophic-shell blocks in step with what Claude/himmel enforce, while dropping routine write/git fences.

nodes.label: Provider routes (NVIDIA NIM + OpenRouter chain, superseded)
nodes.norm_label: provider routes (nvidia nim + openrouter chain, superseded)
nodes.rationale: Free routes come first and fail open down the chain with a visible note; the block is kept for history and so a rebuild does not 'fix' the unwired routes.

nodes.label: Tier coupling: capability follows the model
nodes.norm_label: tier coupling: capability follows the model
nodes.rationale: The pre-tool guard cannot tell at call time which model will answer, so full control is tied structurally to the trusted premium model with no free fallback.

nodes.label: A classifier refusal files its own request
nodes.norm_label: a classifier refusal files its own request
nodes.rationale: The model calling afk-run itself reads as circumventing the classifier and is refused, so a PermissionDenied hook files the request from the refused call's own bytes.
nodes.source_location: ### A classifier refusal files its own request

nodes.label: RUN_KIND_SHIPPED compiled switch
nodes.rationale: Being a compiled constant, a config edit cannot turn the run kind on; only a release plus re-install can.

nodes.label: Executor re-check order
nodes.rationale: Re-checking hash, identity, config and floor at exec time ensures nothing changed between approval and run, and the code is spent regardless.

nodes.label: Frozen request record
nodes.rationale: Freezing argv, file hashes, inode identity and cwd at request time lets exec detect any change after the operator approved.

nodes.label: Mode switch allowlist/all
nodes.rationale: Allowlist mode limits runs to argv a class names, while all mode permits any argv as operator or root, trading safety for flexibility.

nodes.label: Never-remote floor
nodes.rationale: A root-owned word-set check is a seatbelt that config cannot remove, refusing requests naming disk wipe, secrets, main history, approval system or guards-off targets, though it is not a full policy.

nodes.label: open_regular and descriptor-held exec
nodes.rationale: Opening via O_PATH, fstat and fstatfs and exec from the held descriptor stops path swaps and device/FIFO side effects from changing what runs.

nodes.label: The run kind
nodes.rationale: The run kind freezes one argv, shows it to the operator and runs exactly that once, so approval is for a specific command.

nodes.label: Spent TOTP steps
nodes.rationale: A code valid for one request must not be reusable for another in the same 30-second step, so ended requests spend the step (replay refusal).

nodes.label: Approving over SSH
nodes.rationale: Lets the operator approve when the phone is out of reach while keeping nonce and code out of argv and recording via=ssh in the ledger, as required by the ticket over the design spec.

nodes.label: Classifier-denial tap and hardening
nodes.rationale: Lets a chief see a repeated or escalating classifier denial within one tick rather than only when a worker reports it.

nodes.label: input_head and reason_tag never leave the host
nodes.norm_label: input_head and reason_tag never leave the host
nodes.rationale: These fields are only best-effort redacted, so only worker:count:class may be sent and a test pins which files may name them.

nodes.label: Opt-in MCP launch via mcp-gate
nodes.rationale: Claude Code eagerly spawns every plugin MCP server, so default-OFF gating avoids a bun process in sessions that never use Telegram (HIMMEL-591).

nodes.label: Quote-aware shell tokenizer inlined byte-for-byte
nodes.rationale: Hook-integrity pins launched hooks, not sourced libs, so neither hook sources the tokenizer and a drift test with a --sync mode keeps the copies identical.

nodes.label: --prime and --warm-session cache flags
nodes.rationale: These flags measure the prefix cache the way a user meets it, so cold prefix writes do not distort per-question cost.

nodes.label: Realistic arms (HIMMEL-9314)
nodes.rationale: Pasted-context arms are one-turn prompts with no tools, so fused arms pay cache writes on all output; realistic arms measure a session as a worker actually runs it.

nodes.label: luna enrich-chat-notes
nodes.rationale: Each provider is egress-matrix-gated under the enrichment purpose so only claude is permitted and the others are refused legibly.

nodes.label: luna fold-chat-history
nodes.rationale: implied: folds exported provider chat history into the vault create-only and idempotently with a dry-run first to avoid damaging existing notes.

nodes.label: Adoption trail pages
nodes.rationale: It lays adoption out as levels, each stating what it turns on, what it changes and how to turn it off.

nodes.label: /cloud-route
nodes.rationale: Classifies tickets for cloud suitability from touched files, hooks and ask count, prints launch lines but never launches, keeping the operator in control.

nodes.label: Cloud-route classes (BLOCKED, HOOK-BYPASS, LOCAL-NATIVE, CLOUD-OK)
nodes.rationale: First-match-wins classes keep tickets that need local state, hooks or trust paths out of the cloud, where hooks do not run.

nodes.label: /cloud-route command
nodes.rationale: Automates the mechanical part of routing a ticket to the cloud lane, leaving the credit-spending launch to the operator.

nodes.label: Gap-audit offer (HIMMEL-5836)
nodes.rationale: Surfaces non-green read-only checks with remedies without running anything until the operator agrees.

nodes.label: Gap-audit offer (HIMMEL-5836)
nodes.rationale: Print-only offer of non-green checks so nothing runs until the operator agrees.

nodes.label: block-jira-compound-write
nodes.rationale: implied: Jira writes inside pipes, loops or heredocs cannot be audited, so only bare CLI calls are allowed.

nodes.label: block-write-into-main-checkout
nodes.rationale: It protects the primary checkout from git writes, permitting only the exact worktree add shape for adopted primaries.

nodes.label: guard-pr-check-literal
nodes.rationale: It refuses gate-script commands it cannot resolve from their literal text, so variables, globs and cd-prefixes fail.

nodes.label: Request and rm-run ruling flow
nodes.rationale: Batching requests into a single bounded model ruling that reads only disk keeps decisions auditable and reproducible.

nodes.label: Bug placement at filing
nodes.rationale: Placing at filing instead of silently defaulting ensures no ticket is filed without at least a proposed version.

nodes.label: Invoke Jira CLI by absolute path
nodes.norm_label: invoke jira cli by absolute path
nodes.rationale: dist/ is an untracked build artifact existing only in the main repo root, so a relative path from a worktree gives MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

nodes.label: Ad-hoc harness work gets a ticket
nodes.norm_label: ad-hoc harness work gets a ticket
nodes.rationale: Conventional commits make the ticket optional, so a 'quick fix' would silently ship ticketless.

nodes.label: Ticket discipline in every repo
nodes.rationale: The commit-msg gate is himmel-local, and work items silently accumulated outside Jira in other repos (drifted twice in ggs-local).

nodes.label: Project-boundary heuristic
nodes.rationale: Filing where the definition of done lands avoids misfiling between HIMMEL and LUNA; jira move fixes misfiles without manual close and recreate.

nodes.label: Verify every Jira write
nodes.rationale: Silent failures such as missing dist/ look identical to success in the transcript unless the echo line is asserted.

nodes.label: Jira Sector custom field (optional)
nodes.rationale: Tagging tickets with a coarse product area shows where effort goes and which area is starved, and together with the epic-or-standalone rule it stops orphan tickets.

nodes.label: Jira dedup against tracked projects
nodes.rationale: Dedup uses the operator's tracked projects from the jira cache, never a hardcoded project, so users without Jira get no spurious suggestions.

nodes.label: Intake/Reversion/Discharge procedure
nodes.rationale: One claim-rule-apply procedure ensures every request is idempotently written to Jira and receipted before the chief is told.

nodes.label: Lease and hand-off
nodes.rationale: A lease with epochs prevents two batches ruling at once and lets intents be resolved by readback after a hand-off.

nodes.label: No count gates rule (decision 104)
nodes.rationale: Rulings weigh effort, delivery, sector and dependency chain rather than quotas or caps.

nodes.label: READY check rows
nodes.rationale: UNKNOWN fails so a release is never declared tag-ready on missing evidence.

nodes.label: jira-list skill
nodes.rationale: Falls back to JIRA_PROJECT_KEY when no project is named.

nodes.label: Change one setting (setting groups table)
nodes.rationale: Each row states scope, effect time, verify and reverse steps so users can change and undo a setting safely without reading the full map.

nodes.label: Delivery chain (ticket to handover)
nodes.rationale: Each step from ticket to merge has an enforcing gate so work reaches main only through a reviewed PR.

nodes.label: Gate classification: HARD / auth-gated / warn-only
nodes.rationale: Classification is derived from what each script's code does, not how docs describe it, so users know which vetoes can be bypassed.

nodes.label: git gates (pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push)
nodes.rationale: git gates control what can be committed and pushed; --no-verify skipping the pre-push stage is deliberate and visible rather than a loophole to close.

nodes.label: User vs project hook scopes
nodes.rationale: The universal hook set must follow the operator outside the repo while the himmel-dev guardrail stack stays checked in at project scope; inject-initiative is wired at both with session-id dedup.

nodes.label: Session gates (Claude Code hooks)
nodes.rationale: Hooks gate live-session tool calls (edits on main, secret reads, PR creation, merges) and bypass via env vars in the launching shell, since per-call prefixes never reach hooks.

nodes.label: Structural enforcement at three layers
nodes.rationale: Rules are enforced structurally via git hooks, Claude Code hooks and sanctioned scripts instead of trusting the model to remember them.

nodes.label: Branch + PR workflow
nodes.rationale: Never editing on main, worktree per ticket, ticketed conventional commits and squash merges keep main clean and changes traceable.

nodes.label: Contributor walkthrough (full loop)
nodes.rationale: Using a docs-only toy change keeps attestation simple while still exercising the full gate sequence.

nodes.label: Primary checkout
nodes.rationale: No feature edits land in the main working tree so feature work stays isolated in worktrees.

nodes.label: Worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: Feature work in a worktree keeps the primary checkout on main clean.

nodes.label: Portable export via .pre-commit-hooks.yaml
nodes.rationale: Worktree isolation was only structurally enforced in himmel while other repos like luna relied on prose, so two gates are exported for opt-in.

nodes.label: Claude SessionStart hooks
nodes.rationale: The update check reads local refs and detaches the fetch so an offline or slow remote cannot stall session start.

nodes.label: Symlink resolver 40-hop fail-closed cap (accepted cost)
nodes.rationale: The ticket ratified failing closed over silently emitting an unresolved path, at parity with the kernel's ELOOP limit, accepting a false positive on pathologically deep worktree-local chains.

nodes.label: Worktree-isolation gap (primary checkout vs linked worktree via .git entry)
nodes.norm_label: worktree-isolation gap (primary checkout vs linked worktree via .git entry)
nodes.rationale: An autonomous session did feature work on a PR branch in the primary checkout, so the guard distinguishes a .git directory (primary) from a .git file (linked worktree) to force isolation.

nodes.label: load-dotenv strips trailing comment only after whitespace
nodes.norm_label: load-dotenv strips trailing comment only after whitespace
nodes.rationale: Unstripped inline comments in .env.example produced an impossible ticket pattern that rejected every commit, while requiring whitespace keeps URL fragments intact.

nodes.label: pre-commit run --commit-msg-filename false Passed
nodes.rationale: A message file outside the repo is filtered out so the hook runs on nothing; an instrument only counts as evidence once shown to go red on a must-fail case.

nodes.label: Durability: checkpoint and resume
nodes.rationale: Without checkpointing each step a restart duplicates subagents.

nodes.label: EDIT_ON_MAIN_OK launching-shell switch
nodes.rationale: The hook runs in a process that never sees a per-call prefix, so the off switch must be set in the shell that launches Claude Code.

nodes.label: Starter refuses edit tools, not shell writes
nodes.norm_label: starter refuses edit tools, not shell writes
nodes.rationale: The starter hooks gate Edit/Write tools and git commits/pushes only, so a shell redirect to a file and other paths remain open.

nodes.label: Manual install recovery appendix
nodes.rationale: Exists only for when the installer cannot run and the portable core is still needed; it is not a supported second path.

nodes.label: Commit the install before branching
nodes.rationale: A worktree is cut from committed history, so an uncommitted install leaves worktrees with no hooks and no protection.

nodes.label: .single-writer opt-out
nodes.rationale: A personal repo edited in place does not fit the review-gated worktree rule, so a per-checkout local opt-out lifts only the edit-tool hook.

nodes.label: Ticket ID in commit messages
nodes.rationale: himmel's conventions assume Jira-style or #number references, so adopters can override with TICKET_ID_PATTERN or disable with TICKET_ID_REQUIRED=0.

nodes.label: Lean floor reconcile on /himmel-update
nodes.rationale: A whitelist reconciler forces drifted plugins back to the template floor, with settings.local.json as the only persistent override.

nodes.label: Lean plugin set
nodes.rationale: Every enabled plugin injects context at session start, and additive installs drift the enabled set upward, so a whitelist reconcile keeps context cost low.

nodes.label: qmd orphan-process incident
nodes.rationale: The qmd launcher forwards no signals, so `timeout N qmd query` killed node and orphaned five bun children running at ~99% CPU for ~15 h.

nodes.label: Claude invocation billing rule
nodes.rationale: Headless claude -p draws the same subscription budget as interactive use, so unattended sites must preflight usage.

nodes.label: Claude invocation billing (claude -p draws subscription budget)
nodes.norm_label: claude invocation billing (claude -p draws subscription budget)
nodes.rationale: Measurements showed headless calls drain the same subscription budget as interactive sessions, so pre-run usage state rather than invocation shape is the cost control.

nodes.label: Subagent transcript layout and usage attribution
nodes.norm_label: subagent transcript layout and usage attribution
nodes.rationale: Globbing only top-level jsonl files is blind to subagent spend (50.06% of a measured window) and counting lines instead of requestIds inflates totals by ~83%.

nodes.label: Rule: unattended sites route through usage-preflight
nodes.norm_label: rule: unattended sites route through usage-preflight
nodes.rationale: The retired no-headless-claude gate checked marker presence only and added friction without controlling spend, so usage-preflight is the real drain control.

nodes.label: N07 CADENCE_BANK_* to CADENCE_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: V1 renamed bank to usage; the bare CADENCE_BANK has no ruled name yet (pending-N2892).

nodes.label: N12 bank-* scripts to usage-* scripts
nodes.norm_label: n12 bank-* scripts to usage-* scripts
nodes.rationale: A longer name that merely contains one of these (e.g. test-bank-preflight.sh) has no ruled name unless its usage- twin exists.

nodes.label: PR 1b: usage leftovers (N07-N12, N37)
nodes.rationale: Callers move and the forwarder is deleted in one PR because deleting bank-preflight.sh first would break every CR script and the console kit.

nodes.label: Implementation-subagent usage guard (IMPL_GUARD_HARD)
nodes.rationale: Refuses heavy implementation subagents near window limits to keep runs from starting on a nearly full window; haiku and light types are exempt.

nodes.label: 5h and 7d usage gauges
nodes.rationale: Every Claude session draws from the same subscription windows, so long or parallel runs can exhaust the 5-hour window and must be visible.

nodes.label: Dry-run, confirm, apply contract
nodes.rationale: A non-interactive Bash call hits EOF on the confirm prompt and exits 0 having changed nothing, so the exit code alone would misreport success.

nodes.label: luna-upgrade skill fallback to engine
nodes.rationale: The lean plugin floor can disable obsidian-triage by policy, so a plugin-independent engine fallback prevents the vault upgrade from failing (HIMMEL-1153).

nodes.label: Dry-run then confirm then apply
nodes.rationale: The operator confirmation is the load-bearing safety gate protecting user content.

nodes.label: Fail-closed version stamp
nodes.rationale: Not writing the stamp on conflict or failure keeps the vault reading as update-available so the re-run is safe and idempotent.

nodes.label: Vault-first lookup order
nodes.rationale: Escalating from enriched hit to thin hit to live fetch minimizes network use, and a missing vault is normal for adopters so it falls straight to live fetch.

nodes.label: Vault-first link reading (LUNA-78)
nodes.rationale: The clip pipeline has usually already captured the full body, so reading the vault first avoids needless network fetches and Grok.

nodes.label: Merge order for dependency chains
nodes.rationale: Planning merge order on every merge event avoids merge skew between dependent PRs.

nodes.label: Dirty-primary detector deliberately ungated by worker marker
nodes.norm_label: dirty-primary detector deliberately ungated by worker marker
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL_WORKER is only exported by telegram lanes and subagents inherit it unmarked, so a marker-gated detector would never fire on the incident's shape.

nodes.label: merge-forward-check --no-fetch (claudex path)
nodes.rationale: The claudex lane forbids git fetch, so a no-fetch mode that refuses on a stale local origin/main lets red PRs merge forward safely.

nodes.label: Primary-checkout write prevention/detection pair
nodes.rationale: block-edit-on-main only covers Edit/Write tools, so Bash-mediated writes into the primary checkout need a post-hoc detector after an incident went unnoticed for 18 minutes.

nodes.label: Subagent-result cap watchdog
nodes.rationale: When subagents hit the cap their tool results carry the limit text while main-loop calls succeed and the usage cache reads low, so existing detection paths miss it.

nodes.label: Lifecycle exit-2 and warn-only wiring via additionalContext
nodes.norm_label: lifecycle exit-2 and warn-only wiring via additionalcontext
nodes.rationale: Non-permission events have no permission gate, so context is delivered through the additionalContext JSON channel instead of a deny.

nodes.label: Critic panels need periodic validation and exactly one config
nodes.norm_label: critic panels need periodic validation and exactly one config
nodes.rationale: An inverted critic reports dirty diffs clean, and a second per-lane config copy drifts, so each tool keeps one repo-root config as the source of truth.

nodes.label: compound-distill
nodes.rationale: A billed single claude run needs explicit opt-in and a token ceiling, and defaults to dry-run so nothing is written to canonical memory files.

nodes.label: --base-cases-local local reproduction option
nodes.rationale: Reproducing the failing suite at the merge-base in a scratch worktree proves the red is inherited, while a PR-caused case must still REFUSE.

nodes.label: Covering-run fallback (HIMMEL-5124) polarity gap
nodes.rationale: Main CI runs only on cron or dispatch, so the next covering run usually carries the fix and the polarity rule cannot express red at the merge-base but fixed later.

nodes.label: Chief's board
nodes.rationale: The chief needs one static page showing fleet size, worker phases and what needs attention, and the page runs no server.

nodes.label: Fleet and run view (AG-UI)
nodes.rationale: Lists every live Claude session and its run so the user can inspect tool calls and failures.

nodes.label: Directories carrying old names (owner HIMMEL-6646)
nodes.rationale: Whole directories with old names (e.g. console-kit with 387 files) need a single owner and a table entry because renaming them is large.

nodes.label: N06 leg-impl/leg-bus/leg-vm to worker-impl/worker-bus/worker-vm
nodes.rationale: implied: part of the leg-to-worker terminology rename (family F2, slice V4a), with the new name live 3/3.

nodes.label: N07 CADENCE_BANK_* to CADENCE_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: implied: part of the bank-to-usage rename (F3, V1); the bare CADENCE_BANK has no ruled name (pending-N2892) and CADENCE_USAGE_LEG still holds LEG.

nodes.label: N08 BANK_LIFT_* to USAGE_LIFT_*
nodes.rationale: implied: keeps the lift env vars consistent with the bank-to-usage rename (F3, V1); all 6 new names are live.

nodes.label: N09 CODEX_BANK_* to CODEX_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: implied: aligns Codex probe and cache env vars with the usage naming (F3, V1); three strings have no ruled name yet.

nodes.label: N10 CLAUDEX_BANK_* to CLAUDEX_USAGE_*
nodes.rationale: implied: aligns claudex warn/refuse/ok env vars with usage naming (F3, V1); new name live 3/4.

nodes.label: N11 PARKED-BANK to PARKED-USAGE
nodes.rationale: It is a marker token the tick parses and written handover docs also carry it, so the rename must cover both code and docs.

nodes.label: N12 bank-* scripts/files to usage-* scripts/files
nodes.norm_label: n12 bank-* scripts/files to usage-* scripts/files
nodes.rationale: A longer name that only contains one of these (test-bank-preflight.sh, block-bank-lift-writes.sh) has no ruled name unless its usage- twin exists.

nodes.label: N13 clear-cr-marker.sh and cr-*.sh to review-*/coderabbit-*.sh
nodes.norm_label: n13 clear-cr-marker.sh and cr-*.sh to review-*/coderabbit-*.sh
nodes.rationale: The registry names only nine; scripts/cr/cr-trigger-ledger.sh is the CI-release ledger not the CodeRabbit one, and the pattern can catch third-party cr-*.sh so each hit needs reading.

nodes.label: N14 CR_MARKER*/CLEAR_CR_MARKER_*/SETUP_CR_MARKER to REVIEW_MARKER*
nodes.rationale: SETUP_CR_MARKER is test-local and the <git-dir>/cr-pending/ directory keeps its name (OD-3).

nodes.label: N16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* helpers
nodes.norm_label: n16 leg-* helper scripts to worker-* helpers
nodes.rationale: The plan names only seven helpers at plan rows 28-36 for this rename; every other leg-*.sh script belongs to N42.

nodes.label: N17 leg-digest* to worker-digest*
nodes.rationale: implied: the digest scripts and the directory follow the leg-to-worker terminology change, so the directory rename is split under owner HIMMEL-6646.

nodes.label: N18 close-wrapped-leg.sh to close-wrapped-worker.sh
nodes.rationale: The CLOSE_WRAPPED_LEG_* env names are tracked separately in N38, so this row covers only the script file names.

nodes.label: N19 console-kit directory to chief-kit
nodes.rationale: It has the largest blast radius (1462 lines in 388 files), so it is renamed last, and the plan's symlink at the old path is dropped by the no-alias ruling.

nodes.label: Tests follow their ruled script (test- plus new name)
nodes.norm_label: tests follow their ruled script (test- plus new name)
nodes.rationale: The table names scripts not tests, so each test is expected to follow its script in the same PR to avoid orphaned names; the rename PR confirms it.

nodes.label: Names needing an operator ruling (not in approved table)
nodes.norm_label: names needing an operator ruling (not in approved table)
nodes.rationale: No table row names these paths, so the page proposes no new name and sends them to the operator instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Preview an update (--check, --versions)
nodes.rationale: Previews fetch refs but never move HEAD, so users can see what would change before touching the working tree.

nodes.label: Update steps
nodes.rationale: /himmel-update, himmel-update.sh and himmelctl update are the same engine, with project scope needing a re-run of adopt because copies are not refreshed by the download update.

nodes.label: Working principles block (six defaults)
nodes.rationale: These are general engineering defaults, not himmel invariants, so they sit at user scope where every project gets them once instead of every himmel session paying for them.

nodes.label: Bank (usage)
nodes.rationale: A subscription usage budget (5-hour and 7-day) must be checked before launching work, via a preflight token.

nodes.label: Bank lift
nodes.rationale: Only the operator may relax the weekly bank check, so every agent write to it is denied.

nodes.label: Operator-only usage lift (no env bypass)
nodes.rationale: Raising the weekly budget is the operator's call, so agent writes are refused under every path spelling with no bypass, and a forged lift is bounded at read time.

nodes.label: Environment dump and transcript read denial
nodes.norm_label: environment dump and transcript read denial
nodes.rationale: Two GitHub tokens reached 33 and 29 session transcripts through shapes the guard did not know, and transcripts hold every earlier tool result verbatim.

nodes.label: Glued option value scan
nodes.rationale: Whole-word tokenizing missed `--file=.env` and `-f.env`, which really read the secret, so glued values are split and scanned as a closed false negative.

nodes.label: Nested shell body re-scan (fail-closed depth 4)
nodes.rationale: A body the guard cannot read fully counts as unreadable, so denying beyond depth 4 is fail-closed.

nodes.label: Positional quoted-pattern exemption
nodes.rationale: A per-flag arity table would be an unbounded enumeration whose gaps become false negatives, so a positional rule accepts false positives, since a false positive costs a cycle while a false negative leaks a secret.

nodes.label: GitHub token prevention/detection pair
nodes.rationale: Prevention via block-read-secrets cannot catch tokens appearing in tool input or output, so a post-tool scan alerts without ever echoing the value.

nodes.label: Guardrail and hook bypasses in scope
nodes.norm_label: guardrail and hook bypasses in scope
nodes.rationale: The PreToolUse hooks and pre-commit/pre-push gates are the structural enforcement layer, so defeating them defeats himmel's safety model.

nodes.label: Secret handling in scope
nodes.rationale: implied: credentials in .env, API keys or tokens being read, logged or committed are the highest-impact leak path.

nodes.label: Upstream-watch cadence (daily, delta-gated, zero tokens)
nodes.rationale: The operator ruled on 2026-09-01 that upstream monitoring should run daily, not as a token-spending poller, so it is pure bash and never invokes claude.

nodes.label: Steering-cull verdicts (SHIP/KEEP/...)
nodes.rationale: A probe is valid only if it passes baseline and fails with the rule deleted, so SHIP-UNMEASURED marks rules the model answers from general judgement.

nodes.label: Per-session multi-vault routing
nodes.rationale: Each session is routed to the vault its own repo configures so a single --all pass does not cross-contaminate vaults.

nodes.label: Recrystallize mode (--recrystallize)
nodes.rationale: Reheal skips content-bearing uncrystallized notes, so this mode closes the gap with a bounded one-run-per-note LLM pass.

nodes.label: Reheal mode (--reheal)
nodes.rationale: Recovers husk notes in place when their transcripts later become salvageable, without any auto-delete.

nodes.label: Token-usage warning
nodes.rationale: Backfilling many notes at once makes downstream pipeline stages cost tokens proportional to the session count.

nodes.label: Seeding the vault with historical sessions
nodes.norm_label: seeding the vault with historical sessions
nodes.rationale: Backfill imports many notes at once and downstream triage/synthesis can burn many tokens, so dry-run and batching are advised.

nodes.label: Husk-skip gate
nodes.rationale: Sessions with no salvageable content would produce content-free Transcript unavailable notes, so the write is skipped.

nodes.label: Reheal and recrystallize recovery modes
nodes.rationale: Reheal handles husk notes only while recrystallize closes the gap for content-bearing but uncrystallized notes such as backfilled sessions.

nodes.label: Handover system
nodes.rationale: One worker is one file so a resuming session cannot read half the picture, and the queue lock is structural because prose coordination failed three ways in one night.

nodes.label: Keepalive-or-wrap rule
nodes.rationale: Bounded waits are kept warm with a sub-50-minute arm, open-ended waits wrap with a resume brief, because 16 of 17 measured cold wakes came from workers that armed nothing.

nodes.label: Behaviour-key precedence order
nodes.rationale: A fixed order (env, project, local, profile, default conf, legacy .env, default) makes each key's winner predictable.

nodes.label: Chief may not go structurally dead
nodes.norm_label: chief may not go structurally dead
nodes.rationale: A chief once sat dead for 58 minutes with an empty fleet because nothing starts a new turn in an idle interactive session, so a synchronous Stop block is needed.

nodes.label: compound-extract
nodes.rationale: A read-only, no-LLM deterministic extract that emits only key bullets (never a doc body) so the downstream distill input stays small.

nodes.label: handover librarian
nodes.rationale: Archives finished handover docs and old notes by moves only, never delete or overwrite, and is dry-run by default.

nodes.label: Lesson check-or-guardrail question
nodes.rationale: Forcing each lesson to name the check that would have caught it (or `check: none`) shows whether guardrails exist, measured by the sweep's check share.

nodes.label: handover-resume behavior contract
nodes.rationale: The contract is kept as the reference that resume.sh must satisfy.

nodes.label: v2 numeric ID scan across both namespaces
nodes.norm_label: v2 numeric id scan across both namespaces
nodes.rationale: A bare numeric ID could be a Jira-keyed or legacy #N item, so both namespaces are scanned within one repo.

nodes.label: Never hardcode ./handovers/ rule
nodes.rationale: The single-root resolver and the HANDOVER_DIR bridge depend on every script resolving the handover directory through handover_root.

nodes.label: Typed privileged Telegram ops
nodes.rationale: Only whole typed messages from the allowlisted operator may trigger privileged actions, with each op off by default.

nodes.label: Session note path and slug convention
nodes.community_name: Session note path and slug convention
nodes.norm_label: session note path and slug convention
nodes.rationale: UTC-based paths with an 80-char slug budget reserving room for a collision suffix guarantee deterministic names and that the hook never overwrites an existing note.

nodes.label: Bounded Stop queue (durable dir + one worker)
nodes.norm_label: bounded stop queue (durable dir + one worker)
nodes.rationale: Detached end-of-session work fanned out N unbounded process trees that leaked kernel pool handles, so a singleton worker bounds concurrency while durable entries keep work from being lost.

nodes.label: Stop queue escape hatches
nodes.rationale: Losing the bound is acceptable but losing the work is not, and adopters on unseen platforms must never be bricked by a missing env name.

nodes.label: Secrets never reach a queue entry
nodes.norm_label: secrets never reach a queue entry
nodes.rationale: An entry records argv and env on disk, so detach_queued is used only for the outer re-exec and secret-bearing relay calls stay on plain detach_run.

nodes.label: Sweeper-status alert trigger
nodes.rationale: A dead or stalled sweeper on an otherwise git-clean vault would be swallowed by clean early returns, so an independent RED/YELLOW/GREEN heartbeat trigger fires within a 90 minute latency budget.

nodes.label: Doc-literal accept row
nodes.rationale: A hand-declared per-CLI row pinned by a test makes doc, parser and gate agree, since a doc is part of the interface.

nodes.label: Rename gates and exemptions
nodes.rationale: CI gates read registry direction as mode and permit only keep rows and an inline old-term-ok marker, so retired names cannot creep back unnoticed.

nodes.label: Rename steps in order
nodes.rationale: Registry row first, shared reader, same-PR writers/docs/tests, migrated stored records and a removal ticket keep every consumer consistent.

nodes.label: Codex blocks run as separate processes
nodes.norm_label: codex blocks run as separate processes
nodes.rationale: A measured probe showed shell variables do not cross blocks, so every needed value must be printed to the transcript and carried as a literal.

nodes.label: Fence contract and refused shapes
nodes.rationale: The worktree-isolation guard statically refuses command shapes it cannot verify, so fences must avoid the enumerated shapes.

nodes.label: Single-quote untrusted substituted values
nodes.rationale: Pasted literals are parsed by the shell, and only single quotes keep attacker-influenced branch names and titles inert.

nodes.label: Ambiguous-id guard for .md collisions
nodes.rationale: [[Clippings/foo.md]] can belong to two different clips, so the move is refused only when the colliding sibling actually exists.

nodes.label: Canonical-URL dedup (never deletes)
nodes.rationale: Title fallback is rejected because distinct clips can share generic titles, so dedup acts only on exact canonical-URL match and leaves duplicates for operator review.

nodes.label: Clippings/_deferred.md backlog
nodes.rationale: A single living page lists work the pipeline logged but deliberately did not do, such as fan-out refs, tail-skips and safety flags.

nodes.label: Atomic per-clip graduation with revert
nodes.rationale: mv is the only destructive op and any failure reverts the move and link edits so no clip is lost or left with stale links.

nodes.label: Six-form literal link rewrite
nodes.rationale: Clip names contain regex metacharacters and synthesis pages cite with .md, so literal fixed-string matching of all six forms prevents silent dangling links and prefix-sibling clobbering (HIMMEL-1882).

nodes.label: Stuck-in-inbox tracking (HIMMEL-1713)
nodes.rationale: Surfacing clips that never reached _evidence/ stops a quiet '0 graduated' result from reading as a healthy no-op.

nodes.label: Synthesis-link index and eligibility rules
nodes.rationale: A clip graduates only after harvest, triage and synthesis evidence all exist, with the .md suffix normalised so .md-cited clips are not stuck.

nodes.label: himmel --merge-into-live behavior (HIMMEL-6008)
nodes.rationale: The himmel live graph is mostly AST nodes from the hourly ast-update, so markdown extraction is merged in rather than promoted over it to avoid shrinking the graph.

nodes.label: Publish task schedule (every 6h at :35, opt-in)
nodes.rationale: The :35 offset sits 20 minutes clear of the hourly AST task because this step is not free-and-instant and would otherwise contend for ast-update's promote lock.

nodes.label: graphify ast-update wrapper
nodes.rationale: Taking the semantic job's promote lock (skip-not-wait) prevents the free AST re-parse from racing the weekly semantic refresh's write.

nodes.label: CI guardrail
nodes.rationale: Detects abusive GitHub Actions use so the chief can hold dispatches.

nodes.label: Critic verdict files (.critic-spec-rN.md / .critic-plan-rN.md)
nodes.rationale: Saving each critic return verbatim with a verdict last line lets the operator signing step hash and verify the last round (HIMMEL-8353).

nodes.label: send-file --by-request form
nodes.rationale: When the operator asks to see an unpassed page it is sent marked NOT PASSED so that copy can never be mistaken for a signable page.

nodes.label: Spec/plan critic check before send
nodes.rationale: A signature page must not reach the operator unless the critics passed on the exact bytes, so SPEC CLEAN/PLAN CLEAN and a CONTENT-SHA256 line are required.

nodes.label: Spec sign page generation
nodes.rationale: A shared generator ties the page to its md via shas and a spec-source tag, so the critic reads exactly what the operator signs.

nodes.label: Keep the -chief suffix in a scoped name
nodes.norm_label: keep the -chief suffix in a scoped name
nodes.rationale: Compaction re-injection and guards recognise a chief only by a launch-time -n name ending in -chief, and next derives the successor's name from its doc, so a mistake propagates down the chain.

nodes.label: Symptom: failed commit reverted files I never touched
nodes.norm_label: symptom: failed commit reverted files i never touched
nodes.rationale: pre-commit's stash/reapply fails when Obsidian rewrites a tracked file mid-hook and the rollback silently reverts other unstaged files, so a no-stash wrapper is the reliable fix.

nodes.label: CONSULT / CONSULT-ANSWER protocol
nodes.rationale: A consult answer is advice only and cannot carry RETASK, tokens or GO lines, so it cannot become an authority channel.

nodes.label: The grant kind
nodes.rationale: Lets one classifier-refused Bash call run once in the worker's own session after approval, with nothing running as root, to keep privilege minimal.

nodes.label: Gateway topology: multiplexed vs per-profile
nodes.rationale: A bot token may belong to only one profile because two profiles polling the same token fight over getUpdates, so migration refuses duplicates.

nodes.label: Keeping hermes updated (editable checkout, resync)
nodes.rationale: Upstream force-pushes main, so the update step resyncs only when nothing local would be lost, to avoid permanently failing the update chain without discarding user work.

nodes.label: Recover broken venv pip
nodes.rationale: uv-created venvs ship without pip, so the editable refresh fails until ensurepip restores it.

nodes.label: Version review checklist lines
nodes.rationale: A fixed step list ensures each review has refreshed data and the same three lines, with a manual ticket-ref check run by hand before release.

nodes.label: Weekly roll-up (velocity, cost, health series)
nodes.rationale: One roll-up supplies all trend lines so the review reads it and never recomputes; no-data series are null rather than 0 to avoid false trends.

nodes.label: Manual security review checklist
nodes.rationale: A fixed eight-item list (input, authn/authz, secrets, command injection, SSRF, deserialization, path traversal, races) makes a manual review repeatable; the attestation records conscious review, not perfection.

nodes.label: Node-less machine bootstrap shim
nodes.rationale: himmelctl itself needs node, so a clean machine needs a shim that installs node before handing off.

nodes.label: Deprecated machine-setup/ubuntu.sh shim
nodes.rationale: Wiring is now delegated to himmelctl so the provisioning script keeps its toolchain role without duplicating himmel wiring.

nodes.label: Opt-in MCP launch (HIMMEL-591)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code eagerly spawns every enabled plugin MCP server and has no lazy spawn, so a default-off gate avoids holding a bun process in sessions that never correlate.

nodes.label: Installer-drift pass (--only drift)
nodes.rationale: Converging only allow-listed items and loudly reporting the rest keeps updates safe while still surfacing drift that needs the operator.

nodes.label: The update chain (six-item dependency chain)
nodes.rationale: Ordered items (pull, marketplace, jira, qmd, hermes, luna) abort on the first genuine failure because later items depend on earlier ones, with no rollback.

nodes.label: Retired-plugin removal offer
nodes.rationale: Machines provisioned before the caveman plugin was dropped still carry it, so one helper with three entry points offers removal without hanging or removing silently.

nodes.label: Eval feedback loop
nodes.rationale: Each eval result drives one change and the next run re-measures it, closing the loop on the eval-runs ledger.

nodes.label: pdd_share: proof-first share of merged PRs
nodes.norm_label: pdd_share: proof-first share of merged prs
nodes.rationale: It measures how many merged PRs had DoD and Proof sections before work started and RED then GREEN evidence, with no model call.

nodes.label: Train/test keep rule
nodes.rationale: Requiring both train and test to gain beyond noise stops changes tuned on the open half from overfitting.

nodes.label: 7-day Testing-token expiry and exit code 75
nodes.rationale: Testing-mode refresh tokens expire about weekly, and going Production needs a CASA Tier 2 assessment that is out of scope for alpha personal use.

nodes.label: Commit anchor for semantic judgements
nodes.rationale: Judgements go stale when a repo changes direction, so each carries ingest_spec_version and upstream_commit to show whether it still applies.

nodes.label: Semantic fields (concepts, solves, maps_to, value_tier, value_reason)
nodes.norm_label: semantic fields (concepts, solves, maps_to, value_tier, value_reason)
nodes.rationale: A controlled concept vocabulary and a legitimate none value for maps_to keep tags clusterable and meaningful; the layer is a model pass so it only runs on a ranked slice.

nodes.label: The op kind: station ops
nodes.rationale: Named, versioned, reviewed scripts run only from a root-owned installed copy matching a hash manifest so privileged actions are fixed and auditable rather than free-form.

nodes.label: WebFetch redirect for walled hosts (redirect-webfetch-walled-hosts.sh)
nodes.rationale: WebFetch gets HTTP 402 on walled hosts, so denying with a paste-ready alternative fetcher saves a wasted call; one plugin source serves both himmel and adopter repos.

nodes.label: fetch-url
nodes.rationale: Walled hosts like x.com need a stealth fetcher without cookies or Chrome profiles, so WebFetch is redirected to it by a hook.

nodes.label: research path
nodes.rationale: Rungs are injected callables and the Reddit rung refuses queries other than the operator's own, so there is no silent fall-through or unreviewed egress.

nodes.label: quiet-run background lifetime and signal semantics (HIMMEL-2221)
nodes.norm_label: quiet-run background lifetime and signal semantics (himmel-2221)
nodes.rationale: A background quiet-run is a live child of the session, so it must be counted before closing and TERM/INT/HUP reap the whole command tree.

nodes.label: require-quiet-run.sh bare test-suite bounce
nodes.rationale: Prose and advisory context did not produce compliance, so by the structural-over-instructional rule the hook denies and names the exact quiet-run replacement.

nodes.label: Suite concurrency budget (machine-wide semaphore)
nodes.rationale: Test suites share a machine, so a bounded slot semaphore with stale-slot reclamation prevents oversubscription; an invoked-program-level deny was removed because it false-denied heredoc text.

nodes.label: Running a brand-new suite before first commit
nodes.norm_label: running a brand-new suite before first commit
nodes.rationale: RED-first runs of a new suite must work before anything is committed, while path checks still refuse files outside the worktree.

nodes.label: Local suite-result ledger
nodes.rationale: Appending one row per suite run makes local catches countable without ever altering a suite's exit code.

nodes.label: gh-pr-review skill
