nodes.rationale: A review needs an explicit verdict, so unclear verdicts are asked about instead of guessed.

nodes.label: Handover state lives in separate state repo
nodes.norm_label: handover state lives in separate state repo
nodes.rationale: Personal handover state is centralized in the user's own state repo, so himmel's handovers/ is a stub and no durable state belongs in himmel.

nodes.label: Shared refs/stash hazard
nodes.rationale: All worktrees share one refs/stash, so a stash drop in one session destroyed another chain's entry.

nodes.label: Token vocabulary (machine-readable)
nodes.rationale: A fixed vocabulary lets test-guard-conformance.sh parse cells reliably, so synonyms are forbidden.

nodes.label: Persistent scratch root ~/.himmel/scratch
nodes.rationale: Treating a clone there like a scratchpad clone lets work survive between sessions without a .single-writer marker.

nodes.label: Instagram shared throttle (HIMMEL-4306)
nodes.rationale: A shared gap, daily cap, backoff and cooldown budget stops 100 clips from running in one burst and tripping Instagram blocks.

nodes.label: Handover budget
nodes.rationale: Turn, cache-read and context-fill limits force a handover before the chief's context cost grows; estimated fill is excluded because it can read high after a cache-heavy turn.

nodes.label: Dependency split: test-harness vs user-runtime
nodes.rationale: Test VMs only need bash git jq to run suites, while adopters need the full runtime, so the sets must not be conflated.

nodes.label: SSH connect and rsync staging
nodes.rationale: Two rsync calls are needed because scripts and docs/setup require different destination shapes that fixtures expect.

nodes.label: graphify install re-adds absolute path to tracked settings
nodes.norm_label: graphify install re-adds absolute path to tracked settings
nodes.rationale: An absolute binary path breaks adopters and leaks the maintainer's username, so the portable fail-open command must be restored after each install and the Codex entry deleted because it starved the hook chain.

nodes.label: Break-glass ops
nodes.rationale: Away-from-station operations are individually opt-in and need a one-time confirm code in the private chat to bound risk.

nodes.label: Manual pass (7 items)
nodes.rationale: A human checklist verifies Inventory bundle behaviour, header and safety toggles that automated tests do not cover.

nodes.label: Decision: A2A input never carries authority
nodes.norm_label: decision: a2a input never carries authority
nodes.rationale: Authority comes from out-of-band facts (RETASK nonce, GO file, pid-proven identity) that A2A cannot carry, and an A2A peer is an unauthenticated remote.

nodes.label: humanizer (blader/humanizer)
nodes.rationale: Optional second pass rewriting drafts in the writer's voice without changing claims, adopted after a pass over user-facing docs found edits unslop leaves alone.

nodes.label: no-comments + comment-sicko
nodes.rationale: Prunes ticket-history and workaround comments from the tree on demand with zero listing tokens.

nodes.label: pstack plugin (10 skills)
nodes.rationale: Ten disable-model-invocation skills shipped as one uninstallable plugin keep listing tokens at zero and removal one step.

nodes.label: pstack create-formal-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Generates code-grounded checks where tests reach poorly; E12 found a real queue-lock defect.

nodes.label: pstack maintain-formal-verification-skill
nodes.rationale: Keeps generated verification aligned with code and distinguishes drift from real defects; value unmeasured until a verify skill exists.

nodes.label: pstack statechart
nodes.rationale: Bounded model-check runtime giving readable shortest counterexamples for concurrency defects; runs local processes so source read is mandatory.

nodes.label: unslop (cursor/plugins pstack)
nodes.rationale: Removes AI-tells from human-facing docs to reduce reword passes; pilot close condition never ran so the KPI is unmeasured.

nodes.label: Compound-cd known limitation
nodes.rationale: Parsing cd out of the command would require a tokenizer, which is out of this hook's scope, so the exposure is accepted and the pending audit still reports the marker.

nodes.label: cwd selects the repo; resolved himmel checkout selects the scripts
nodes.norm_label: cwd selects the repo; resolved himmel checkout selects the scripts
nodes.rationale: Git already answers which repo is meant via git-common-dir, so a --repo flag would add a second resolution source for the same datum.

nodes.label: .env is himmel's, not the target's (load_dotenv pinning)
nodes.norm_label: .env is himmel's, not the target's (load_dotenv pinning)
nodes.rationale: A cwd-following load_dotenv would read the adopter's .env and silently drop CR_REQUIRE_CROSS_MODEL=true, a fail-open the fix would have introduced; the primary-checkout wrapper is needed because --root is a silent no-op when .env is missing in a linked worktree.

nodes.label: Fork-to-upstream PRs remain gated
nodes.rationale: A PR to another repo still originates from a local branch whose pending marker should block, so the hook advises about the target mismatch and keeps checking the source marker.

nodes.label: Clear marker only via clear-review-marker.sh, never bare rm
nodes.norm_label: clear marker only via clear-review-marker.sh, never bare rm
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier reads a bare marker rm as a CI Bypass and may deny unrelated writes, whereas the script re-derives the verdict from the CR ledger and is strictly stronger.

nodes.label: Blast-radius pass
nodes.rationale: Proved a real defect missed by shipped suites on 6 of 6 guard and gate PRs, so it is default-on for those diffs.

nodes.label: Claude-only floor and availability escape hatch
nodes.norm_label: claude-only floor and availability escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Opens only for absent lanes and fails closed for attempted-but-failed lanes, so adopters without external reviewers can still clear honestly.

nodes.label: Cross-model adjudication verdicts
nodes.rationale: Every panel finding must receive at least one explicit verdict so none is orphaned.

nodes.label: verify-before-critical rule (HIMMEL-178)
nodes.rationale: Hallucinated Critical findings derail overnight fix batches and burn tokens, so cited content must be verified in the diff.

nodes.label: Step 3.5: CodeRabbit is the GitHub App
nodes.norm_label: step 3.5: coderabbit is the github app
nodes.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-07 made the App the gate, so local CLI wrapper and gate scripts were deleted and every finding is tracked on the PR.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit is best effort
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is a CI-only reviewer beside the local panel and must never be a bottleneck, so its absence never blocks while an existing finding still does.

nodes.label: cc-codex offload shim
nodes.rationale: implied: a guarded source line in ~/.bashrc exposes the cc-codex function without breaking shells where the checkout is absent.

nodes.label: spawn-claudex dispatch path
nodes.rationale: Dispatching through claude-codex itself avoids re-implementing the launcher's PHI/egress/env/proxy trust-boundary guarding.

nodes.label: Haiku 5.5 lane facts
nodes.rationale: Records the model's specs, pricing and prompting caveats so routing to it is based on measured facts and known low-effort failure modes.

nodes.label: Haiku 5.5 lane-quality eval (2026-10-07)
nodes.rationale: Tests the claim that Haiku 5.5 is much cheaper at equal acceptance, read as a screen since n=1 per cell.

nodes.label: Lane-fit eval: Haiku 5.5 vs Sonnet 5.5 vs codex gpt-6.1-sol
nodes.norm_label: lane-fit eval: haiku 5.5 vs sonnet 5.5 vs codex gpt-6.1-sol
nodes.rationale: Because every lane passed all hidden checks, the comparison separates lanes on cost, turns, wall time and judge scores instead of correctness.

nodes.label: Lane-quality eval harness
nodes.rationale: Routing should follow measured quality per lane and model, using one frozen task set so adding a model adds one run.

nodes.label: OpenRouter eval lane repricing
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reports cost at 5x list price for the gateway slug, so cost is repriced from token usage and marked up 1.2 to match the real balance.

nodes.label: Routing verdict per work type
nodes.rationale: Changes routing only where the eval says ROUTE, and keeps trust paths off Haiku by invariant rather than by eval result.

nodes.label: lane-quality repeats and judge calibration
nodes.rationale: Repeats with bootstrap CIs and judge-vs-acceptance calibration show how far the LLM judge can be trusted.

nodes.label: Deferred finding disposition before GO
nodes.rationale: Past the round cap a Critical or Important finding must never be silently dropped, so it needs a recorded fix-here or follow-up.

nodes.label: Trust-path PR review
nodes.rationale: The trust list is read from the default branch so a PR cannot shrink it, and such PRs need an independent adversarial review.

nodes.label: Fleet: chief and workers
nodes.rationale: The fleet model fixes who may write what and who may spawn whom, with a single writer per artifact and the chief owning approval and merge.

nodes.label: GO / GO file
nodes.rationale: The file itself is the merge authorisation at one head sha so no message can substitute for it.

nodes.label: Ready-check
nodes.rationale: Numbered pre-GO checks on one PR head ensure the chief signs only a mergeable PR.

nodes.label: Trust path
nodes.rationale: Files that decide whether changes are safe must be approved by an independent reviewer on the exact commit, since the authoring agent could otherwise switch a safety check off.

nodes.label: completes-ticket / --jira-transition decision
nodes.rationale: Closing the Jira ticket is a per-brief decision because a default close would end multi-PR tickets early, and the flag only closes the first [KEY] of a PR title.

nodes.label: Fork PRs (himmel adapters) merge path
nodes.rationale: Merges into forks are limited to an allowlist read from the default branch so a worktree edit cannot widen what the chief may merge.

nodes.label: Review ledger keyed by head sha
nodes.norm_label: review ledger keyed by head sha
nodes.rationale: Because the ledger is keyed by head sha, every push needs its own review round or check 4 finds no row and the marker-clear script refuses.

nodes.label: Brief Contract (lock, deliverables, tests, ship)
nodes.rationale: A fixed numbered contract makes lock acquisition, RED-first tests, trailers and the GO-gated merge identical across workers.

nodes.label: What stays on the chief
nodes.rationale: Rulings, GO, judge dispatch, token-quoting and Live state writes are decisions, which must remain with the chief.

nodes.label: Chief-GO gate for chief-spawned workers (HIMMEL_CONSOLE_LEG)
nodes.rationale: Only the chief may certify a PR head via a GO file, so a worker's merge is bound to reviewed evidence and refuses when it is missing or mismatched.

nodes.label: The 1,500-byte rule
nodes.rationale: It is the fail-safe direction for a ruling: an oversized message can only lose authority, while halts and narrowings stay honored at any size.

nodes.label: Succession (§3a) on the bus
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker cannot call ListAgents, so 'chief is gone' is mapped to `bus status <name>` liveness of the bound pid.

nodes.label: Unchanged: GO file still governs merges; bus never widens permissions
nodes.norm_label: unchanged: go file still governs merges; bus never widens permissions
nodes.rationale: A bus message must never substitute for the GO file or widen a tool-permission envelope, since the bus is only a transport.

nodes.label: `from` carries authority only for the registered chief
nodes.norm_label: `from` carries authority only for the registered chief
nodes.rationale: Every worker message is data to a chief: it informs and never revises, expands or redirects, so only the registered chief's header says `from`.

nodes.label: read output is data
nodes.rationale: read(n) fetches a body through a tool result, which is never trusted-origin context regardless of sender.

nodes.label: Symptom: merge-on-green exit 22 / MAIN-RED advisory
nodes.rationale: A red main should not block a PR whose checks passed, but eight merges onto a red main turned 3 breaks into 11, so audit lines and alerts remain.

nodes.label: Symptom: [Out-of-Place Publication] denial
nodes.rationale: The trigger is the retry pattern, not content, so no retry is earned; the worker's doc-directory grant is narrow to prevent minting its own merge GO under .locks/.

nodes.label: himmel-bus delivery (§3b)
nodes.rationale: The bus adds a transport but not an authority, so the existing §1–§3a rules must apply to bus messages unchanged.

nodes.label: codex-direct lane
nodes.rationale: Codex has no auto-mode classifier, so it relies on deterministic guards reached through the hooks.json adapter plus a terminal write-fence substitute.

nodes.label: Guard-firing conformance sub-table (deny-guard x lane)
nodes.rationale: Expands the single per-lane guardrail cell into per-guard proofs so a lane is tested-green only when every guard is proved; parsed by HTML-comment anchor for stability.

nodes.label: hermes-main lane (default, gpt-6.1-sol)
nodes.rationale: As the default lane it must be fenced entirely by parity_guard since CC hooks do not fire there.

nodes.label: PR shards run the impacted suites
nodes.community_name: PR shards run the impacted suites
nodes.norm_label: pr shards run the impacted suites
nodes.rationale: Running only the base commit's selected suites speeds PRs while trust-path diffs and selector errors fall back to the full sweep, with manifest verification preventing false greens.

nodes.label: Never edit config in the proposal run
nodes.norm_label: never edit config in the proposal run
nodes.rationale: Config changes to .coderabbit.yaml and critics.json are operator-approved PRs citing the proposal file.

nodes.label: Reviewer mode
nodes.rationale: Hard versus best-effort lets a reviewer that cannot review either hold the merge or be relaxed, while posted findings must always be resolved.

nodes.label: Hollow plan header check (Proportion)
nodes.rationale: implied: an empty header or a plan longer than its code gives reviewers nothing verifiable and wastes effort.

nodes.label: Rabbit hole check (shell-text guard parsing)
nodes.rationale: Parsing shell text to enforce a guard can grow without bound, so a plan must argue convergence or carry a ceiling and a filed structural fix.

nodes.label: Untraced invariants check
nodes.rationale: Every spec invariant needs a named acceptance test fed real sources, otherwise a stub could make the violation impossible and prove nothing.

nodes.label: fork-1 advisory cross-model panel lane
nodes.rationale: A free-cloud critic panel catches the same-family popularity trap of Claude reviewing Claude, while the Claude critic stays the gate and failure is fail-open (HIMMEL-414 WS4).

nodes.label: Base and graft (optional fan-out design)
nodes.rationale: Fanning out read-only candidates against a hidden rubric and grafting onto one base keeps one coherent design while exploring non-trivial or hard-to-undo architectures.

nodes.label: Design tree frontier rounds
nodes.rationale: Asking the whole frontier per round avoids guessing at answers not yet heard while not serialising independent questions.

nodes.label: Eight standing grill questions
nodes.rationale: Every grill must feed effort-assess with slice size, tail driver, G1, RED, collisions, version headroom and follow-up class so estimates are not vacuous (HIMMEL-3996, 6929).

nodes.label: Invariants and Fact ownership sections
nodes.rationale: The terminal lint (HIMMEL-4375) needs each rule and each surface fact to have a named test or single owner, built by grep not memory.

nodes.label: Mode (interactive vs autonomous gates)
nodes.rationale: Decides once up front whether to pause for the operator, since in autonomous mode the critics are the gate and no human is present.

nodes.label: himmel-ops scripts resolver (fallback chain)
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is empty in a Codex skill shell (HIMMEL-606), so a fallback chain locates the scripts dir; both copies are kept byte-identical.

nodes.label: One front door (HIMMEL-2039)
nodes.rationale: Grill, brainstorm and build requests all landing in minerva avoids a second grilling skill that would stop at shared understanding.

nodes.label: Spec location: state repo specs/<type>/ bucket
nodes.norm_label: spec location: state repo specs/<type>/ bucket
nodes.rationale: The default docs/superpowers/specs/ is gitignored in himmel and CLAUDE.md keeps internal specs out of the repo (HIMMEL-8205).

nodes.label: Stage 1a: Grill (design tree interrogation)
nodes.rationale: Interrogating the idea as a design tree in rounds ensures nothing is silently assumed before any design is written (HIMMEL-2039).

nodes.label: Stage 1b: Brainstorm to spec
nodes.rationale: The spec must carry an estimate record, alternatives and definition of done because Stage 2 refuses to start without them.

nodes.label: Stage 2: Spec critic (adversarial)
nodes.rationale: A fresh opus subagent red-teams the spec, capped at 3 rounds so review cannot loop forever and open findings go to the operator.

nodes.label: Stage 3: Plan
nodes.rationale: The writing-plans handoff is halted before execution so plan critic and lint run first, and plans save to the state repo because the default path is gitignored.

nodes.label: Stage 4: Plan critic (adversarial)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the spec critic on the plan so the implementation plan is red-teamed before hand-off, with verdict files kept beside the spec.

nodes.label: Terminal: lint then hand-off
nodes.rationale: Auto-handoff to subagent-driven-development only when autonomous and the execute step is active makes the loop continuous, while interactive mode lets a human choose.

nodes.label: session-analyzer
nodes.rationale: Gives a local, read-only, no-network ranking of tool and hook friction from session transcripts.

nodes.label: spawn-claudex --effort flag
nodes.rationale: It refuses `max` (undocumented juice) and `ultra` (silently falls back to xhigh) at parse time to prevent misleading effort levels.

nodes.label: Codex weekly subscription usage budget preflight
nodes.norm_label: codex weekly subscription usage budget preflight
nodes.rationale: A capped worker dies mid-run and the work is lost, so dispatch refuses at the threshold before any worktree side-effect, while failing open on read errors so a cold log never bricks dispatch.

nodes.label: Judge output has no tier field
nodes.norm_label: judge output has no tier field
nodes.rationale: Tier is derived in code from the subscores so the judge never assigns it.

nodes.label: Five 0-5 scoring dimensions
nodes.rationale: Factual reliability, resources, reach, focus fit and substance judge signal from evidence in the dossier rather than from follower count or outside knowledge.

nodes.label: clip-body path
nodes.rationale: The clip's captured body is already the harvest, so no external call or key is needed; a /blob/ file URL stays here because luna-ingest would re-ingest the README.

nodes.label: github-ingest path
nodes.rationale: NEVER pass --research in batch dispatch because it is interactive and web-search-costing, and the batch must stay light and side-effect-bounded.

nodes.label: HIMMEL-128 Skill-tool-only dispatch contract
nodes.rationale: implied: batch dispatch must go through the Skill tool only, never claude -p or direct API calls, to keep it bounded.

nodes.label: Thinness gate (single-source predicate)
nodes.rationale: A shared mechanical predicate replaces eyeballing so a skeleton clip is not marked ok with an empty body.

nodes.label: harvest-clips Phase 4 dispatch decision
nodes.rationale: Moved out of harvest-clips.md so the always-loaded body stays small and this loads on demand.

nodes.label: Launch-log read limited to first 8192 bytes
nodes.community_name: Launch-log read limited to first 8192 bytes
nodes.norm_label: launch-log read limited to first 8192 bytes
nodes.rationale: A pid or session-log path appended after the prefix is never seen, leaving the row on an obsolete process.

nodes.label: Finished bg row pid fallback (|| agPid)
nodes.community_name: Finished bg row pid fallback (|| agPid)
nodes.norm_label: finished bg row pid fallback (|| agpid)
nodes.rationale: A finished row's pid may be stale or reused, so using it can make a completed leg look alive and raise a false attention flag.

nodes.label: Collector liveness heartbeat (SessionStart)
nodes.rationale: A dead collector leaves every other integrity signal green and the rate decaying toward zero, looking like good news that ends the programme, so the collector must assert its own liveness.

nodes.label: hook_inventory (heartbeat payload)
nodes.rationale: Separates 'a recorder ran' from 'the configuration named every verb', since they fail separately and notify is the only producer of interrupt rows.

nodes.label: No window trimming and no liveness inference from events
nodes.norm_label: no window trimming and no liveness inference from events
nodes.rationale: Trimming reintroduces short-window bias that pushes the rate up, and a quiet week and a dead hook produce identical silence.

nodes.label: Classify notifications at report time, not in the hook
nodes.norm_label: classify notifications at report time, not in the hook
nodes.rationale: A hook-side filter fails in the dangerous direction, recording nothing and reading as a quiet week if the type vocabulary changes.

nodes.label: Seven hook entries wiring (pre, post, notify, postfail, denied, permreq, heartbeat)
nodes.norm_label: seven hook entries wiring (pre, post, notify, postfail, denied, permreq, heartbeat)
nodes.rationale: Each entry is a new array element or top-level key so it merges cleanly against in-flight hook-wiring branches.

nodes.label: scripts/trust README (R0 shadow ledger)
nodes.rationale: Documents a zero-behaviour-change recorder so the approval-interrupt rate can be measured before deciding whether the larger trust programme is worth building.

nodes.label: Plugin PreToolUse(Skill) critic injector (inject-minerva-critic.sh)
nodes.rationale: It closes the no-/minerva bypass so brainstorming and writing-plans always trigger the adversarial critic loop, and stays advisory and fail-open so it cannot block a Skill call.

nodes.label: Judge write guard (HIMMEL_CONSOLE_JUDGE)
nodes.rationale: Confining a judge's writes to its own verdict locations stops it forging a sibling judge's verdict or writing its own GO.

nodes.label: Adopting a fork
nodes.rationale: A clone runs one pre-commit config, so forks with their own config must merge its hooks into the core config.

nodes.label: Guide recommendations deliberately not adopted
nodes.rationale: The finish-the-whole-task autonomy block, under-formatting advice and async dispatch pattern would conflict with himmel's halt carve-outs, structured artifacts and RETASK threat model.

nodes.label: Three false-positive mitigations
nodes.rationale: Compile-framed asks, unfamiliar languages and base64 in tool_result content look adversarial to safeguards and raise false-positive refusal risk.

nodes.label: Anthropic output content-filter trips on policy text and minified blobs
nodes.community_name: Anthropic output content-filter trips on policy text and minified blobs
nodes.norm_label: anthropic output content-filter trips on policy text and minified blobs
nodes.rationale: The filter scans generated output, so downloading canonical policy docs keeps the trigger text out of model output and context.

nodes.label: Safeguards refusal-fallback drops the [1m] suffix
nodes.community_name: Anthropic output content-filter trips on policy text and minified blobs
nodes.rationale: The fallback picks the bare 200k model so contexts past 200k overflow and stall unattended sessions, making auto-compact the only recovery path.

nodes.label: Code kit CLI tools (ast-grep, shfmt, bats)
nodes.norm_label: code kit cli tools (ast-grep, shfmt, bats)
nodes.rationale: They are CLI tools with 0 listing tokens, tracked as drift rows in upstreams.json.

nodes.label: Opt-in role kits (code, code-ui)
nodes.rationale: Kits stack on base and compose per task so a worker pays listing cost only for the capabilities it needs.

nodes.label: Fixture git config from primary checkout poisons every worktree
nodes.community_name: Fixture git config from primary checkout poisons every worktree
nodes.norm_label: fixture git config from primary checkout poisons every worktree
nodes.rationale: Worktrees share the primary .git/config, and a prose read-only instruction is not a sandbox, so fixture work needs isolated HOME/GIT_CONFIG and git -C everywhere.

nodes.label: Pruned git worktree directory falls through to the PRIMARY repo
nodes.community_name: Fixture git config from primary checkout poisons every worktree
nodes.norm_label: pruned git worktree directory falls through to the primary repo
nodes.rationale: git walks up to the primary .git without error, so detect with rev-parse --show-toplevel and save a staged patch first.

nodes.label: qmd install, collections and embedding
nodes.rationale: Semantic search needs the qmd fork, ~2.1 GB of models and an embedded index, so the steps are idempotent and resumable.

nodes.label: N19 console-kit directory to chief-kit
nodes.rationale: It has the largest blast radius (1462 lines in 388 files), so it is renamed last, and the no-alias ruling drops the planned symlink.

nodes.label: PR 6: directory moves (M)
nodes.rationale: It waits for HIMMEL-6296 and open console-kit PRs, and path-keyed files move in the same PR because no symlink stays at the old path.

nodes.label: haiku false pick on o17 (check-ci vs pr-check)
nodes.norm_label: haiku false pick on o17 (check-ci vs pr-check)
nodes.rationale: implied: haiku confused check-ci with himmel-ops:pr-check, the only non-exact miss unlike opus and sonnet.

nodes.label: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.community_name: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.norm_label: dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.rationale: Keeps liked-but-unshipped in-house items searchable and borrowable instead of rebuilt.

nodes.label: qmd (local BM25+vec index)
nodes.community_name: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.rationale: Already-local markdown index is the preferred extension point over adding new runtimes.

nodes.label: >100KB auto-externalize + BM25 retrieval (parked)
nodes.community_name: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.rationale: Indexing oversized output locally loses nothing and avoids flooding context; extend qmd if ever needed.

nodes.label: CR context-graph for large-repo reviews (parked)
nodes.community_name: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.rationale: A persistent codebase graph would help reviews exceeding one window; himmel isn't large-repo yet, and qmd would be extended instead of adding an MCP runtime.

nodes.label: emergence-to-self-improvement crystallization (parked)
nodes.community_name: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.rationale: Would crystallize emerging vault clusters into self-improvement candidates; design documented but not necessarily built.

nodes.label: worktree-isolation plugin (parked)
nodes.community_name: Dynamic index of parked in-house ideas
nodes.rationale: Extraction of the worktree pattern would make it work for any repo; filed but not built.

nodes.label: Residue scan advisory (step 2.9)
nodes.rationale: Scaffolding for one-time transitions should be dropped or given an expiry, but the false-positive rate is unmeasured so it stays advisory.

nodes.label: Install manifest lint
nodes.rationale: A closed schema with DAG and probe-shape checks catches malformed install manifest entries before himmelctl's install engine consumes them.

nodes.label: Admission
nodes.rationale: A ledger record of each entry into a frozen version keeps the gate and the admitter auditable.

nodes.label: Frozen scope
nodes.rationale: Fixing the ticket set on the freeze date makes later additions explicit through the intake gate.

nodes.label: Intake
nodes.rationale: Once a version is frozen, new work must pass a recorded gate so scope cannot creep silently.

nodes.label: Intake gate
nodes.rationale: Requiring a named kind (critical, regression, must, receipt) makes each admission to a frozen version justified and auditable.

nodes.label: Receipt
nodes.rationale: implied: work dispatched now and closed within a day should be recordable without disturbing frozen scope.

nodes.label: [1m] model-name suffix lever (untested)
nodes.rationale: A direct proxy probe with the suffix returned HTTP 400, but Claude Code strips the suffix before the provider sees it, so the probe tested a request shape never sent and is recorded to stop re-probing the wrong layer.

nodes.label: claudex 900k context window operator ruling
nodes.rationale: The operator raised the lane's declared window to 900000 despite doubled billing, while the 900K figure is hermes' own measurement and the CLIProxyAPI path stays unmeasured.

nodes.label: CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW 272000 default
nodes.rationale: It was a deliberate 2x billing-cliff choice backed by two independent sources (openai/codex#32486 and hermes) at ~350-372k, and is left unchanged so the launcher does not warn on every default invocation.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS lever (applied)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code clamps unknown models to a hardcoded 200000 window, so CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW was inert until this env var declared the window with the same value.

nodes.label: Epic
nodes.rationale: An epic is one capability with its own done-condition, so it stays a deliverable body of work and never a container for a whole sector.

nodes.label: Sector
nodes.rationale: Gives an abstract, cross-version grouping wider than any one feature so epics and tickets can be organised without confusing it with Jira epics or Components.

nodes.label: Subtask
nodes.rationale: implied: a step small enough to share its parent ticket's PR needs no separate worker or PR.

nodes.label: Ticket
nodes.rationale: One ticket = one worker = one worktree = one PR keeps work units isolated and traceable.

nodes.label: Version
nodes.rationale: A version is a focus bucket with a soft cap and a P80 date plus scope so every goal stays near, real and proof-of-concept backed.

nodes.label: Judge subagent TTL predictions, baseline, ledger
nodes.norm_label: judge subagent ttl predictions, baseline, ledger
nodes.rationale: The 1h tier costs a 0.75 W write premium that only pays when idle gaps over 5 minutes occur; the baseline showed none so judges ship on 5m (+42% cost avoided).

nodes.label: Judge ledger recipe
nodes.rationale: Appending one row per judge run lets the TTL decision be re-scored against break-even once resumed-judge data exists.

nodes.label: Tiebreak rules (last aggregate, main sleep session)
nodes.norm_label: tiebreak rules (last aggregate, main sleep session)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic stable picks (greatest source string, first session in API order) keep output reproducible without secondary sort keys.

nodes.label: core.hooksPath gate
nodes.rationale: A stale hard-coded core.hooksPath after a repo rename silently skipped every pre-commit and pre-push hook, so setup now aborts on it.

nodes.label: qmd-burst-proof
nodes.rationale: An on-demand proof that the qmd daemon handles 10 parallel vec queries, to run after a daemon or pin change.

nodes.label: CI-green merge gate
nodes.rationale: The repo has no branch protection, so GitHub will not block a merge over red or pending CI; this gate is the structural 'ready to merge implies green' enforcement.

nodes.label: Detector only ever adds to main's deny rules (A-E)
nodes.norm_label: detector only ever adds to main's deny rules (a-e)
nodes.rationale: The original text regexp missed many spellings that merged with no gate, so new rules only add denies and nothing the old detector denied can pass.

nodes.label: Head TOCTOU pin of --match-head-commit
nodes.rationale: Without a pin a separate gh pr merge could land a different commit than the head the gates read.

nodes.label: PR lookup fails closed
nodes.rationale: A transient gh/auth error used to exit 0 and let a trust-path PR through with no GO, so an unresolved lookup on a real merge now denies at the cost of a retry.

nodes.label: Single plain command deny rule (six residuals closed)
nodes.norm_label: single plain command deny rule (six residuals closed)
nodes.rationale: Every parse rule in the hook became a bypass across panel rounds, so one deny rule requiring an unquoted single plain gh command replaced quote-stripping and prefix/redirect handling.

nodes.label: /afk-shift unattended runs
nodes.rationale: Lets work continue while the user is away, stopping at a green reviewed PR by default so the merge remains a human decision.

nodes.label: Chief and workers fleet
nodes.rationale: One chief coordinates and approves merges while workers each own one ticket, so work scales in parallel yet stays checked.

nodes.label: Evals and measured numbers
nodes.rationale: himmel publishes measured results with sample sizes rather than promises, so claims can be checked.

nodes.label: Merge gate
nodes.rationale: Refuses a Claude Code session's merge while CI is red, findings are open or the reviewer has not passed, enforcing review by structure rather than memory.

nodes.label: /pr-check review
nodes.rationale: A second model reads the change and the session rules on each finding against code, because review by the author alone is not independent.

nodes.label: Judgment layer for new finding classes
nodes.community_name: Judgment layer for new finding classes
nodes.norm_label: judgment layer for new finding classes
nodes.rationale: A learning that merely restates a rule already enforced by a lint check or .coderabbit.yaml is not a new class, to avoid duplicate coverage.

nodes.label: /archive-clips (stage 4)
nodes.rationale: Graduates only fully-chained clips and rewrites inbound links boundary-safely to avoid dangling links.

nodes.label: /harvest-clips (stage 1)
nodes.rationale: Idempotent harvest marks clips with harvested_at so reruns do not reprocess.

nodes.label: /synthesize-clips (stage 3)
nodes.rationale: Writes proposals only and never restructures, so the vault is not changed without review.

nodes.label: /triage-clips (stage 2)
nodes.rationale: Idempotent triage marks processed: true so each clip is summarized once.

nodes.label: Fail-open / fail-closed
nodes.rationale: Hygiene guards fail open and fences fail closed so that evaluation failure has a predictable effect.

nodes.label: Fence
nodes.rationale: A fence confines writes or egress, fails closed and cannot be lifted by the session, distinguishing it from a speed bump.

nodes.label: Nudge
nodes.rationale: Hooks that steer habits fail open on their own errors, unlike security fences which fail closed.

nodes.label: Speed bump
nodes.rationale: Documenting a guard as stopping only accidental shapes sets honest expectations that a determined caller can route around it.

nodes.label: VM-owned queue with two daemons
nodes.rationale: A single-writer ledger on the VM and sequential claim handling give claim exclusivity without distributed CAS, while the client degrades to direct dispatch if the VM is unreachable.

nodes.label: Memory guard gap: Bash writes are opaque
nodes.norm_label: memory guard gap: bash writes are opaque
nodes.rationale: A Bash command line is opaque to a payload-inspecting guard and gating Bash would be leaky and noisy, so a SessionStart state check detects violations from any writer.

nodes.label: Over-install e2e stage
nodes.rationale: It proves installing a candidate over a previous release keeps secrets, rules and scope and stays idempotent.

nodes.label: Four working principles (understand, simplicity, surgical, verify)
nodes.norm_label: four working principles (understand, simplicity, surgical, verify)
nodes.rationale: The smallest change in the wrong place is a second bug, so changes must be minimal, traceable to the request and verified by a failing-then-passing check.

nodes.label: RTK.md
nodes.rationale: implied: imported so the rtk tool-output filtering instructions load with the global CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Dependency-upgrade e2e stage
nodes.rationale: It proves upgrading baseline dependency versions to station targets causes no new doctor FAIL.

nodes.label: Declaring a plugin is not installing it (HIMMEL-434)
nodes.norm_label: declaring a plugin is not installing it (himmel-434)
nodes.rationale: A marketplace.json entry installs on no machine and marketplace update only re-syncs installed plugins, so new plugins need an explicit install and migration off external sources that could shadow the SHA pin.

nodes.label: Chokepoint
nodes.rationale: A single sanctioned script per privileged action, registered with its seam variables, keeps those actions controllable.

nodes.label: Seam variable
nodes.rationale: Seam variables are only honoured from the launching shell; a per-call prefix is denied to prevent in-session tampering.

nodes.label: Changing the matrix process
nodes.rationale: The matrix is enforcement-path config, so widening a cell must be a human-merged diff and a self-evolving loop is structurally denied writes.

nodes.label: Default-deny and hard salus deny invariants
nodes.norm_label: default-deny and hard salus deny invariants
nodes.rationale: PHI-bearing salus content must never reach a cloud provider, so unknown cells deny and salus denies are hard with no recordable override.

nodes.label: Jina embedding/rerank allow rows
nodes.rationale: Jina has no-training terms on customer request data (Jina legal 10.4), so it is allowed narrowly for embedding and rerank only.

nodes.label: OpenRouter remote qmd embedder/reranker rule
nodes.rationale: Blind A/B winners were adopted by operator ruling, with explicit hard salus denies ahead of allows so the verdict and row order stay pinned.

nodes.label: qmd per-collection egress enforcement
nodes.rationale: qmd model config is per index not per collection, so salus lives in its own local-only index and every remote role is gated against each collection.

nodes.label: Research path Reddit lane (reviewed outside matrix)
nodes.norm_label: research path reddit lane (reviewed outside matrix)
nodes.rationale: The matrix keys corpus content leaving the machine and this lane sends only the operator's typed query and public ids, so it carries no row.

nodes.label: Hardening
nodes.rationale: A working feature that would fail silently needs an alarm; hardening is that maturity step, not software-security hardening.

nodes.label: Maturity ladder
nodes.rationale: Gives features and sectors a shared scale (Idea, POC, Usable, Proven, Hardened) so progress and the hardening step are defined.

nodes.label: Reason code
nodes.rationale: Requiring one of five codes forces every hardening follow-up to name the specific missing alarm.

nodes.label: Judge-triggered delta stops on repeated class
nodes.norm_label: judge-triggered delta stops on repeated class
nodes.rationale: Refusing a delta when a NO-GO class repeats prevents relabelling findings to buy extra rounds and forces a layer decision instead.

nodes.label: Three-round cap with delta round
nodes.rationale: A branch-scoped counter stops new commits from buying fresh review rounds, escalating to the chief after round 3 instead of re-running.

nodes.label: Step 4.9 round-4 cap disposition
nodes.rationale: The cap removes the next correction review to stop endless rounds, while Critical and escape-class findings still block and hardening/polish items are deferred with tickets.

nodes.label: Step 4.8 unresolved-thread gate
nodes.rationale: An unresolved CodeRabbit thread is a merge blocker like a Critical finding, so the gate fails closed on query errors.

nodes.label: Dispatch changed workflows before READY
nodes.rationale: ready-check.sh check 10 needs a completed workflow_dispatch run at the PR head, and a run at an older head proves nothing.

nodes.label: Step 6.5 critic-score footer
nodes.rationale: Showing per-model tallies and absent critics lets the operator see transient drop-outs.

nodes.label: Marker clearance via clear-review-marker.sh, never rm
nodes.norm_label: marker clearance via clear-review-marker.sh, never rm
nodes.rationale: A raw rm is flagged as [CI Bypass] by the classifier and the script re-derives the verdict from the ledger at the exact SHA, making it stronger.

nodes.label: Promote agreed findings to fixed
nodes.rationale: Agreed findings must be terminalized so the ledger is clean, and hand-amending is forbidden to keep audit integrity.

nodes.label: Suggestions-only round closes at round 1
nodes.rationale: Deferring Suggestions avoids repeated paid review rounds on low-value findings, except on trust-path changes.

nodes.label: Trust paths list
nodes.rationale: A change to a file that guards safety checks could disable them, so the agent that wrote it may not approve it.

nodes.label: No-checkout route for outside PRs
nodes.rationale: Reviewing the diff from a pinned ref with no checkout ensures none of an outside PR's files execute on the station.

nodes.label: Outside-PR full review (ready-check item 16)
nodes.rationale: Outside contributions need every review record at the exact head so a new head starts over and no unreviewed text slips through.

nodes.label: luna-index-hygiene
nodes.rationale: Keeps graphify's own output out of the luna index while moving (never deleting) stale in-vault output, dry-run unless --apply.

nodes.label: Effective allowance min(7, span_days x 0.5)
nodes.rationale: The absolute cap let one heartbeat in the last minute certify a whole dead week, so no more than half the window may go unaccounted for.

nodes.label: HEARTBEAT_MAX_GAP_DAYS = 7
nodes.rationale: A per-week rate must not be computed over a window where the collector went a full week unproven; shorter refuses on ordinary idleness, longer hides a stopped recorder.

nodes.label: PROVEN means not obviously stopped (rate is a floor, up to 2x understated)
nodes.norm_label: proven means not obviously stopped (rate is a floor, up to 2x understated)
nodes.rationale: The residual error is inherent to any gap-based liveness check and is stated rather than claimed away.

nodes.label: Stale claude marker guard (CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION)
nodes.rationale: open -a hands the caller's environment to an app, so apps first launched from a claude Bash tool keep the marker and every claude started from them saves no transcript.

nodes.label: Proposal evidence bar
nodes.rationale: Requiring at least 3 disproved rows from one cluster stops thin signals from driving config changes.

nodes.label: himmel-bus delivery hook
nodes.rationale: It is a nudge not a fence, so it is dark unless enabled and fails open on its own errors while honoring the hook additionalContext size cap.

nodes.label: /cr-scores, /cr-tune, /cr-learnings-refresh
nodes.rationale: Let operators see per-critic scoring and tune reviewers using the ledger, with proposals never auto-applied.

nodes.label: /pr-check
nodes.rationale: Runs local multi-agent code review before PR; its shell avoids bare positional refs because the Skill tool would substitute and clobber them.

nodes.label: /handover-resume
nodes.rationale: Thin token-lean wrapper on the handover skill's resume op so sessions cold-start from a tracked item's brief.

nodes.label: /handover-setup
nodes.rationale: First-time bootstrap persisting HANDOVER_DIR so handover commands know where state lives.

nodes.label: Delta round
nodes.rationale: A narrow fourth round reviewing only the diff and blocking only on Critical or escape findings limits endless review cycles.

nodes.label: Round
nodes.rationale: A single counter per panel run bounds review iterations at three.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.rationale: Separates checks that stop work moving to the next stage from session guards, to avoid mixing vocabulary.

nodes.label: Guard
nodes.rationale: Guards judge a call's text before it runs; the name defines a role and a file name containing 'guard' does not imply it.

nodes.label: No-argument rule (adopter lane deleted)
nodes.rationale: A pasted path argument broke shell quoting and the cd could not outlive its fence, so the argument lane was removed.

nodes.label: /upstream-file
nodes.rationale: The dupe gate runs first because a competing PR burns tokens and maintainer goodwill.

nodes.label: block-merged-pr-commit.sh merged-PR branch commit guard
nodes.rationale: It is a hygiene guard rather than a security boundary, so every uncertain path fails open and only a positively confirmed merged-branch commit blocks.

nodes.label: Scheduled claude System32-cwd incident
nodes.rationale: A hand-rolled schtasks job fires with default cwd C:\Windows\System32, running claude outside the repo and wasting the autonomous run.

nodes.label: Invariant deny-guard set
nodes.rationale: Only hard-block deny-guards are parity-relevant; enumerating non-deny hooks per lane would produce spurious GAPs that swamp real ones.

nodes.label: Trust-tier rubric (source-read-mandatory / validate-before-adopt / docs-claim-trusted)
nodes.rationale: Scales scrutiny of each adopted tool to its risk surface (hooks, secrets, network egress).

nodes.label: engram (memory layer)
nodes.rationale: Persistent memory across sessions cuts 're-explain the same context' turns; source must be read because it touches what the agent remembers.

nodes.label: rtk (tool-output filtering)
nodes.rationale: Filtering tool-output noise keeps the context window useful longer and avoids re-launching long sessions.

nodes.label: nizos/tdd-guard
nodes.rationale: Enforces TDD structurally via a PreToolUse hook; because it sees and alters every tool call, the rubric makes implementation-read mandatory.

nodes.label: Advisory
nodes.rationale: implied: some checks should inform without ever blocking, so they exit 0.

nodes.label: CI workflow and runner
nodes.rationale: CI runs manual-only on a public fork with free runners and zero credentials, so secrets cannot leak.

nodes.label: Per-suite temp root
nodes.rationale: Killed suites never run their cleanup traps, which left about 149,600 /tmp entries behind, so the runner deletes each suite's own temp dir.

nodes.label: Allow rule
nodes.rationale: The native matcher compares literal command text, so shapes it refuses fall to the classifier unless a hook approves them.

nodes.label: Attestation trailer
nodes.rationale: Trailers in the first commit record platform testing and security review for pre-push and ready-check enforcement.

nodes.label: Vault auto-commit stall cadence
nodes.rationale: It remediates only two closed classes of hook refusal under handovers/, all-or-nothing and at most once per 24h, so it never rewrites content or bypasses hooks.

nodes.label: Automated review
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is spelled out and never abbreviated CR so the pre-PR gate is not confused with one best-effort CI reviewer.

nodes.label: Brief
nodes.rationale: A per-worker header holds ticket, worktree, base sha, token, chief and contract, and wins over the preface on disagreement.

nodes.label: Bypass flag
nodes.rationale: A session-wide switch set in the launching shell is a controlled, registered way to switch one guard off.

nodes.label: CI release
nodes.rationale: Heavy CI jobs start only after the review gate passes via the ci:go label, saving CI cost without letting anything merge by itself.

nodes.label: Polish
nodes.rationale: Nice-to-have improvements covered by existing checks are not filed so they never hold a version back.

nodes.label: Ponytail comment
nodes.rationale: Marking deliberate simplifications with a ceiling and upgrade path distinguishes them from forgotten TODOs.

nodes.label: Architecture strategy: statusline-pattern (himmel-as-LOGIC, fork-as-vendor)
nodes.rationale: Keeping triage logic in himmel keeps runbooks independent of any upstream skill and forks minimal.

nodes.label: /afk-shift
nodes.rationale: Runs unattended multi-ticket shifts in one session with in-process subagents, distinct from /chief which uses a lock and successor.

nodes.label: /chief
nodes.rationale: A chief dispatches workers and gates merges but implements nothing itself, keeping orchestration separate from implementation.

nodes.label: bus skill (himmel-bus)
nodes.rationale: A protocol card with a trust split and 1500-byte ruling cap keeps bus messages safe and bounded.

nodes.label: Agentic OS
nodes.rationale: Defines himmel as a harness over Claude Code (not an agent SDK) so a fleet of sessions runs as one software factory.

nodes.label: Arming (scheduled launch)
nodes.rationale: Launching sessions on a schedule enables unattended runs.

nodes.label: Chief
nodes.rationale: Holds the queue lock, GO authority and token mint but does no implementation, so authority and implementation stay separate.

nodes.label: Consolidator
nodes.rationale: Reconciles several judges' outputs so the chief does not absorb N separate judgments.

nodes.label: Dependency chain
nodes.rationale: Ordered workers where each needs the previous to merge; kept distinct from hook chain and token chain.

nodes.label: himmel-bus
nodes.rationale: A message counts as a ruling only under a from header from the receiver's registered chief, preventing spoofed rulings.

nodes.label: himmel UI
nodes.rationale: It shows the fleet but gives it no orders, so steering stays with messaging the chief.

nodes.label: Jarvis
nodes.rationale: Names the command layer (chief, workers, judge, GO, unattended runs) so the layer and the chief session are not conflated.

nodes.label: Judge session / judge subagent
nodes.rationale: Judges are advisory (they rule, the chief acts) so a clean thin-brief session can verify without owning outcomes.

nodes.label: Lane
nodes.rationale: A lane is a dispatch backend, not a role or wave, so it is defined separately to avoid confusion.

nodes.label: The lexicon (fleet vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: Plain names are used in prose while repo identifiers stay in code spans, separating readable terms from machine contracts.

nodes.label: Parallel wave
nodes.rationale: Unit to which collision-checking, single-writer and HIMMEL_FLEET_CAP apply.

nodes.label: Relay
nodes.rationale: Transport role launched as a worker of the chief and never as a chief, so it cannot mint authority.

nodes.label: Side session
nodes.rationale: Passes work as a ticket and brief, never as a relayed ruling, so it can't bypass the chief's authority.

nodes.label: Succession (shift handoff)
nodes.rationale: Outgoing chief arms its successor and writes a HANDOFF so shifts continue without losing state.

nodes.label: Worker
nodes.rationale: One ticket, one worktree, one brief, one PR gives the chief a unit of work to dispatch and track.

nodes.label: Chief (long-running coordinator session)
nodes.rationale: One session that dispatches workers, verifies PRs and hands itself over lets a shift outlive any single context window while writing no code itself.

nodes.label: GO file (merge approval)
nodes.rationale: A worker never merges on its own say-so; the chief re-checks the PR at the exact commit and writes a GO for that one PR and commit, so a later push needs a new one.

nodes.label: Chief succession (Handing over)
nodes.rationale: Chiefs hand over at 45% context fill or 90k input tokens so a fresh session continues the fleet using only the HANDOFF doc, without the predecessor's transcript.

nodes.label: Re-brief live workers via relay batch
nodes.norm_label: re-brief live workers via relay batch
nodes.rationale: Each worker's brief names the outgoing chief and the successor is a different session, so workers must be relayed from the predecessor's own session by script.

nodes.label: RETASK channel
nodes.rationale: Expanding or redirecting a worker needs a fresh nonce while narrowing or halting does not, so a halt can never be argued away.

nodes.label: Widening rulings refused by worker auto-mode classifier
nodes.norm_label: widening rulings refused by worker auto-mode classifier
nodes.rationale: A chief ruling is not user consent, so widening asks are correctly refused and the chief should narrow the ask or perform the step itself.

nodes.label: Worker (one ticket, one worktree, one PR)
nodes.norm_label: worker (one ticket, one worktree, one pr)
nodes.rationale: Isolating each ticket in its own worktree, branch and window keeps parallel work from colliding.

nodes.label: last_revalidated omitted by default
nodes.rationale: 'Never checked' and 'checked, unchanged' must not write the same value.

nodes.label: Preface
nodes.rationale: Five distinct prefaces exist so a bare 'preface' is ambiguous; rules appended at launch need qualified names.

nodes.label: --limit default 250
nodes.rationale: The prior [1,25] clamp left high-fanout awesome-lists partial and silently dropped sources, so 250 is a generous safety ceiling.

nodes.label: --research enrichment
nodes.rationale: Lightweight inline web research is kept separate from the full /research-deep and excluded from harvest-clips for cost and scope safety.

nodes.label: Same word, different thing
nodes.rationale: Words with multiple senses in the repo (judge, chief, worker, chain, wave) need disambiguation rules to avoid confusion.

nodes.label: Background Bash task snapshots the foreground cwd at launch
nodes.community_name: Background Bash task snapshots the foreground cwd at launch
nodes.norm_label: background bash task snapshots the foreground cwd at launch
nodes.rationale: Foreground cwd drifts across worktrees, so background jobs must cd explicitly before every step to avoid silent wrong-branch results.

nodes.label: Background-task notification exit code is the last command in the chain
nodes.community_name: Background-task notification exit code is the last command in the chain
nodes.norm_label: background-task notification exit code is the last command in the chain
nodes.rationale: A trailing echo masks an earlier failing gate, so the actual output must be read for the verdict.

nodes.label: check-ci.sh un-maskable verdict line
nodes.rationale: Piped callers misread the exit code, so the verdict is emitted as a line that cannot be masked.

nodes.label: graphify pin bumps (fork-drift)
nodes.rationale: The graphify version pin is bumped repeatedly to track fork-drift issues so the pinned tool stays aligned with upstream.

nodes.label: HIMMEL-1344 arms-registry canonical handover identity
nodes.rationale: The registry keys on a canonical handover identity, written and consumed in lockstep, so writer and reader cannot disagree on what counts as the same handover.

nodes.label: private-to-public propagation catch-ups
nodes.rationale: implied: the public mirror drifts from the private tree, so recurring consolidation catch-ups re-baseline it.

nodes.label: Console, leg and judge orchestration
nodes.rationale: implied: consoles supervise legs and judges with GO files, tick monitoring and queue locks so multi-agent work stays safe and observable.

nodes.label: Provenance ledger and uninstall (HIMMEL-3332)
nodes.rationale: Recording what each install overwrote or created lets ledger-mode uninstall surgically remove only what himmel brought.

nodes.label: Packaged release and tarball install (HIMMEL-3059)
nodes.rationale: A checksummed, attested tarball plus AUR package allows non-git installs and updates with a read-only install tree.

nodes.label: Releases v0.1.0 and v0.1.0 pre-releases
nodes.rationale: Public projections of private history (HIMMEL-2705, HIMMEL-1899) that established the public repo baseline.

nodes.label: Release v0.2.0 (2026-09-10)
nodes.rationale: First stable tag after the v1 public projection, per HIMMEL-2922.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.1
nodes.rationale: implied: first v0.3 pre-release adding leg profiles by skill set and chokepoint guard hardening.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.2
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release for console judge role, relay write-deny and lean leg profiles.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.3 (2026-09-13)
nodes.rationale: implied: tiny release rolling cli-proxy-api and migrating plugin records to @himmel.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.4
nodes.rationale: implied: large pre-release adding console/judge features, Windows alpha, and tarball install.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.5
nodes.rationale: implied: small pre-release fixing queue-lock takeover and leg-identity bugs.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.6
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release centered on the provenance ledger and ledger-mode uninstall.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.7
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release adding headless leg mode, fleet UI and standalone uninstaller.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.8
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release building tarball layout, attestation and identity slices of HIMMEL-3059/3525.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.0-pre.9
nodes.rationale: implied: pre-release adding AUR/tarball provenance round trips and v1 bug-freeze enforcement.

nodes.label: claude --bare never reads OAuth; use --safe-mode for a hookless run
nodes.community_name: claude --bare never reads OAuth; use --safe-mode for a hookless run
nodes.norm_label: claude --bare never reads oauth; use --safe-mode for a hookless run
nodes.rationale: --bare restricts auth to API keys so it fails on subscription auth, while --safe-mode skips project guardrails and keeps ambient auth.

nodes.label: bash 5.1+ treats literal & in ${var//pat/repl} as matched text
nodes.community_name: bash 5.1+ treats literal & in ${var//pat/repl} as matched text
nodes.norm_label: bash 5.1+ treats literal & in ${var//pat/repl} as matched text
nodes.rationale: The behavior is version-dependent and corrupts naive escapers, so sed with \& gives an unambiguous literal on every version.

nodes.label: Bash tool strips one backslash level vs a .sh file
nodes.community_name: Bash tool strips one backslash level vs a .sh file
nodes.norm_label: bash tool strips one backslash level vs a .sh file
nodes.rationale: Bash-tool one-liners deliver backslashes differently than files, which produced false-positive review findings, so backslash code must be validated in a real .sh file with a pinning test.

nodes.label: HERMES_YOLO_MODE auto-approval
nodes.rationale: hermes -z auto-approves every tool call, so the guard is the only layer and classifier-only catches are open by construction.

nodes.label: bun test cwd is per-suite; scripts/telegram runs from repo root
nodes.community_name: bun test cwd is per-suite; scripts/telegram runs from repo root
nodes.norm_label: bun test cwd is per-suite; scripts/telegram runs from repo root
nodes.rationale: The telegram suites use repo-root-relative paths and the ENOENT errors name source files, misleading people into hunting a nonexistent wiring bug.

nodes.label: answer-ab: tokens to a correct answer
nodes.norm_label: answer-ab: tokens to a correct answer
nodes.rationale: The retrieval goal is the cost of reaching a correct answer, not the size of one call.

nodes.label: eval-runs ledger
nodes.rationale: One shared ledger shows how an eval has done across commits, with config hashed apart from git sha so a config forms one series.

nodes.label: What each number means table
nodes.rationale: Display names may change while ledger keys stay fixed so series remain continuous.

nodes.label: Gitignored config overlay does not exist in a fresh worktree
nodes.community_name: Gitignored config overlay does not exist in a fresh worktree
nodes.norm_label: gitignored config overlay does not exist in a fresh worktree
nodes.rationale: The tool silently falls back to the tracked default and resurrects items the overlay disabled, so run from the primary or copy the overlay.

nodes.label: scripts/bitbucket AGENTS.md pointer
nodes.rationale: Keeps CLAUDE.md the single source of rules for the directory so edits are not duplicated.

nodes.label: Hermes browser CDP fallback asks operator to enable remote debugging
nodes.community_name: Hermes browser CDP fallback asks operator to enable remote debugging
nodes.norm_label: hermes browser cdp fallback asks operator to enable remote debugging
nodes.rationale: Granting remote debugging hands over full browser takeover and the relayed message reads like phishing, so chat profiles drop the browser toolsets.

nodes.label: Hermes quarantines project skills by scanner verdict; /worktree collides
nodes.community_name: Hermes quarantines project skills by scanner verdict; /worktree collides
nodes.norm_label: hermes quarantines project skills by scanner verdict; /worktree collides
nodes.rationale: Hermes has no per-project allowlist, so the accepted policy keeps the scanner on and rewords flagged patterns rather than disabling the guard.

nodes.label: gh-pr-checks skill
nodes.rationale: Auto-triggers on CI status intent for a specific PR number, excluding Jira and local checks to avoid mis-routing.

nodes.label: gh-pr-comment skill
nodes.rationale: Redirects thread replies to /gh-pr-reply so general comments and thread replies are not confused.

nodes.label: gh-pr-list skill
nodes.rationale: Maps 'my PRs' phrasing to --author "@me" since gh has no --mine flag.

nodes.label: gh-pr-view skill
nodes.rationale: Asks when a bare number could be a Jira ticket or a PR because the two runners hit different systems.

nodes.label: Kernel upgrade without reboot breaks docker networking
nodes.community_name: Kernel upgrade without reboot breaks docker networking
nodes.norm_label: kernel upgrade without reboot breaks docker networking
nodes.rationale: The update replaces the running kernel's modules directory so netfilter modules cannot load, which mimics a docker/iptables bug until the reboot.

nodes.label: Branch with no upstream: git pull errors, automation reads it as no update
nodes.community_name: Branch with no upstream: git pull errors, automation reads it as no update
nodes.norm_label: branch with no upstream: git pull errors, automation reads it as no update
nodes.rationale: Wrappers swallowing stderr make the repo look silently stale, so check git branch -vv and set the upstream.

nodes.label: macOS qmd ggml_metal_library_init_from_source error is benign
nodes.community_name: macOS qmd ggml_metal_library_init_from_source error is benign
nodes.norm_label: macos qmd ggml_metal_library_init_from_source error is benign
nodes.rationale: GPU embedding succeeds despite the message, and himmel documents it rather than suppressing stderr because a blanket filter would hide real errors.

nodes.label: rtk token-proxy rewrites top-level Bash-tool commands
nodes.community_name: rtk token-proxy rewrites top-level Bash-tool commands
nodes.norm_label: rtk token-proxy rewrites top-level bash-tool commands
nodes.rationale: rtk replaces git diff with a stat summary and can write summary text into redirected files, so use rtk proxy git diff and never redirect into important files.

nodes.label: sed '/<!--/,/-->/d' swallows file body on single-line comments
nodes.community_name: sed '/<!--/,/-->/d' swallows file body on single-line comments
nodes.norm_label: sed '/<!--/,/-->/d' swallows file body on single-line comments
nodes.rationale: The closing address is only tested on later lines, so the range deletes real content and makes guards vacuously pass.

nodes.label: pre-commit shellcheck crashes printing non-ASCII lines under non-UTF-8 locale
nodes.community_name: pre-commit shellcheck crashes printing non-ASCII lines under non-UTF-8 locale
nodes.norm_label: pre-commit shellcheck crashes printing non-ascii lines under non-utf-8 locale
nodes.rationale: commitBuffer fails when a finding must print em-dash or emoji lines, so keep such lines finding-free or use targeted disables.

nodes.label: Three consecutive blocked actions park a session behind an invisible modal
nodes.community_name: Three consecutive blocked actions park a session behind an invisible modal
nodes.norm_label: three consecutive blocked actions park a session behind an invisible modal
nodes.rationale: The modal is invisible to external liveness checks and cannot self-recover, so the operator should change approach after two same-shape refusals.

nodes.label: unrecognized_model from proxy masquerades as context-window failure
nodes.community_name: unrecognized_model from proxy masquerades as context-window failure
nodes.norm_label: unrecognized_model from proxy masquerades as context-window failure
nodes.rationale: The rejected slug leaves the default model that the proxy 400s on, including compaction, so the compaction error prints first and misleads diagnosis.

nodes.label: Compatibility doctrine (workers run full setup)
nodes.rationale: Workers must be interchangeable and land outputs in compatible shapes, so every lane needs the same guardrails, substrate and ship-flow.

nodes.label: Lane-parity index table
nodes.rationale: One row per lane with tested and asserted columns shows where lane compatibility is proven versus only claimed.

nodes.label: Single-writer
nodes.rationale: One writer per shared artifact avoids conflicting writes, with a sentinel allowing deliberate main commits in vaults and state repos.

nodes.label: N31 watchdog (deferred, ambiguous)
nodes.rationale: The glossary scopes the rename to auto-arm hooks and names no new id, and a wall-clock killer is a run timeout, so each hit needs reading first.

nodes.label: N42/N43 unruled leg-*.sh and console-*.sh scripts
nodes.community_name: N42/N43 unruled leg-*.sh and console-*.sh scripts
nodes.norm_label: n42/n43 unruled leg-*.sh and console-*.sh scripts
nodes.rationale: They are not in the approved rename table, so a rename of them needs a ruling.

nodes.label: PR 5: docs prose and message text (D)
nodes.community_name: PR 5: docs prose and message text (D)
nodes.norm_label: pr 5: docs prose and message text (d)
nodes.rationale: implied: message text such as 'speed bump' to 'soft block' is prose-only and low risk.

nodes.label: Ticket lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Jira statuses are being aligned to the dev loop, while the dependency graph stays a check rather than a status.

nodes.label: Keep catalog current rule (generator + CI check)
nodes.norm_label: keep catalog current rule (generator + ci check)
nodes.rationale: Description columns are machine-generated from command frontmatter and CI fails on drift, so the catalog cannot silently go stale.

nodes.label: Versions mirror GitHub release tags
nodes.rationale: One Jira version per published tag keeps Jira fixVersions consistent with real releases, with v1.0.0 as a hand-made GA scope.

nodes.label: Tracker
nodes.rationale: The TRACKER variable selects the ticket backend (jira, local or none) so runs work without Jira.

nodes.label: Watchdog
nodes.rationale: Deliberately fail-open so a resource monitor can arm a resume or force a handover as usage caps near without becoming a blocker.

nodes.label: 'Blocked on you' list
nodes.rationale: Each milestone report ends with a clickable URL or path per line plus the one action wanted, because 'held for your review' with no link leaves the operator unable to act.

nodes.label: Planning session handoff to chief
nodes.rationale: The plan, eval artifacts, release versions and single-writer designation must be in durable places before the planning session closes, since the chief never reports back to it.

nodes.label: Pre-dispatch trust-path check
nodes.rationale: A chief cannot manufacture operator permission, so trust paths must be traced and granted up front or the task narrowed, since the classifier may refuse mid-flight expansions.

nodes.label: Bus delivery guarantees (at-least-once, fail-closed halt)
nodes.rationale: A tampered cursor halts the log fail-closed so tampering is surfaced, while consumers must tolerate replays.

nodes.label: Emergencies are always current (decision 109)
nodes.rationale: Evidenced emergencies must start repair at once, so they go in the current version without waiting for a ruling.

nodes.label: Operator scoped records (declare, freeze, decision)
nodes.rationale: Only a scoped, signed operator record can supersede a ruling, since a bare decision number authorizes nothing.

nodes.label: Bus identity (name, pid, start time)
nodes.rationale: Only the launcher binds identity, and callers are stamped by their nearest claude ancestor, so a session cannot register or impersonate itself.

nodes.label: Passive observability taps (fail-open)
nodes.rationale: A telemetry gap is always cheaper than a bricked session, so taps record and never block, slow or ask.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion is Claude-only, degrades to prose
nodes.community_name: AskUserQuestion is Claude-only, degrades to prose
nodes.norm_label: askuserquestion is claude-only, degrades to prose
nodes.rationale: The only real risk is a model calling a nonexistent tool at a confirm gate, so three gates carry a plain-text fallback guard and cosmetic sites are left alone.

nodes.label: Codex config.toml surface
nodes.rationale: Permissions and hook wiring live in config.toml rather than .claude/settings.json, so the port must target that surface.

nodes.label: Status context: statusLine is Claude-only
nodes.rationale: Codex has no visual statusline, so advisory context should flow through a Codex-native context path reusing existing ledgers, offline and fail-open.

nodes.label: Sanctioned review thread resolve path
nodes.rationale: One CLI path requires a valid reason and posts a reply before resolving so every resolution is traceable.

nodes.label: Non-deny hooks excluded from per-lane map
nodes.community_name: Non-deny hooks excluded from per-lane map
nodes.norm_label: non-deny hooks excluded from per-lane map
nodes.rationale: Auto-approvers, watchdogs and marker checks have no non-native analog and are not runtime denies, so mapping them creates false gaps.

nodes.label: Symptom: Bash line containing 'enable' refused in worktree-pinned session
nodes.community_name: Symptom: Bash line containing 'enable' refused in worktree-pinned session
nodes.norm_label: symptom: bash line containing 'enable' refused in worktree-pinned session
nodes.rationale: It is a harness-level guard rather than a himmel hook, so reshaping the text would be dodging and the over-breadth should be reported upstream.

nodes.label: Symptom: large heredoc denied by chokepoint guard
nodes.community_name: Symptom: large heredoc denied by chokepoint guard
nodes.norm_label: symptom: large heredoc denied by chokepoint guard
nodes.rationale: The guard fails closed when its evaluation budget is exhausted, so a deny means nothing ran.

nodes.label: Symptom: background task stopped for low memory at zero pressure
nodes.community_name: Symptom: background task stopped for low memory at zero pressure
nodes.norm_label: symptom: background task stopped for low memory at zero pressure
nodes.rationale: Zero pressure and oom_kill 0 mean the kill is unexplained, so no cause should be named without control.

nodes.label: CR_PROFILE paid-by-default
nodes.rationale: Operator accepted paid-by-default since the free lane was removed; CR_PROFILE=none is the escape when spend is unwanted.

nodes.label: Cursor / Copilot / Gemini deep-dive
nodes.rationale: Per-harness audit decides port/guard/accept based on fail-open defaults, hook formats and usage availability.

nodes.label: Flow-audit follow-ups
nodes.rationale: The audit deliberately left owner tickets instead of another broad implementation pass, requiring no-token preconditions before live Codex probes.

nodes.label: Degradation posture (panel fail-open, verdict fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: Hard-blocking on panel death would turn a third-party outage into a repo-wide merge freeze, so panel availability degrades open while missing verdicts still block.

nodes.label: CR_PROFILE tier selection
nodes.rationale: The panel derives its tiers from CR_PROFILE as the single authority, because hand-computed tier filters previously drifted the panel to free-only and dropped the paid codex critic.

nodes.label: Paid-by-default codex critic
nodes.rationale: The free lane was removed because gptoss/kimi had noisy 12-13% agreed rates and qwen3coder kept erroring, so paid codex is the deliberate default.

nodes.label: Per-member and total-panel hang protection
nodes.rationale: Bounds a single critic (240s) and the whole run (900s) so many slow members cannot hold the review for N times the per-member budget.

nodes.label: Symptom: denial after quoted/prefixed/piped spelling of a ship step
nodes.community_name: Symptom: denial after quoted/prefixed/piped spelling of a ship step
nodes.norm_label: symptom: denial after quoted/prefixed/piped spelling of a ship step
nodes.rationale: Allow rules match text, so only the bare literal spelling matches and one retry of it is permitted before going BLOCKED.

nodes.label: Symptom: late fix gated against stale pre-edit content
nodes.community_name: Symptom: late fix gated against stale pre-edit content
nodes.norm_label: symptom: late fix gated against stale pre-edit content
nodes.rationale: Plain pre-commit run lints the staged index and stashes unstaged files, so an unstaged fix is invisible until re-added.

nodes.label: Bun suites per-suite cwd rule
nodes.rationale: luna-vitals resolves paths relative to its own dir while telegram resolves repo-root-relative, so the wrong cwd yields ENOENT that looks like a broken import.

nodes.label: Quiet reporters are deliberate
nodes.rationale: A noisy default reporter buries the PASS/FAIL summary and costs extra tail/grep round-trips.

nodes.label: Subagents: .codex/agents vs .claude/agents
nodes.rationale: Formats differ (toml vs md frontmatter) so himmel subagents don't auto-carry and are ported only when needed.

nodes.label: Chief wake-up budget
nodes.rationale: Waking the chief only on an actual change keeps the idle chief at zero full-context turns, with monitor cost dominated by the emit.

nodes.label: On-demand connectors (discovery only)
nodes.rationale: Connectors are configured in Chrome or claude.ai, so himmel only lists them for discovery rather than managing them.

nodes.label: The .env split (himmel.conf, config.json policy, .env secrets)
nodes.rationale: Behaviour and policy settings move to ~/.himmel while secrets stay in .env until the keyring work completes.

nodes.label: Confirm the update target
nodes.rationale: The update acts on the checkout holding the script, not the current directory, and refuses dirty trees, so version, tree, branch and fork must be checked first.

nodes.label: OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD zero-egress pin
nodes.rationale: The structural guarantee already keeps bare model names off the cloud; the pin is belt-and-suspenders, and it must be set at OS scope because the ollama binary reads it itself.

nodes.label: Queue lock
nodes.rationale: Enforces one writer per handover document through a release token.

nodes.label: Read outside working directory hangs an unattended session
nodes.norm_label: read outside working directory hangs an unattended session
nodes.rationale: Such reads always prompt even in auto mode and nobody answers overnight, so safe outside paths are pre-listed in permissions.additionalDirectories.

nodes.label: Verification checklist
nodes.rationale: Separating CORE from per-integration checks lets adopters verify only what they installed.

nodes.label: Arize Phoenix
nodes.rationale: One local trace store links eval rows to Claude Code OTel traces by session id; scoped to trace store only, with ELv2 license noted.

nodes.label: /code-review ultra (built-in)
nodes.rationale: Most expensive multi-agent cloud tier, placed above heavy CR on the cost ladder to lower missed-criticals on the biggest/riskiest PRs.

nodes.label: firecrawl /v2/scrape API
nodes.rationale: Rescues thin-body web clips as an opt-in, budget-capped escalation lane to protect the free tier; REST over urllib avoids AGPL SDK concerns.

nodes.label: obsidian-second-brain research toolkit
nodes.rationale: Provisional because no active Grok/Perplexity subscription backs it and the vault-first capture pipeline already covers X and YouTube; it was never evaluated at install time.

nodes.label: pele (obsidianmd/pele)
nodes.rationale: Renders themed Mermaid diagrams in the docs site with a far smaller download (5.4 MB to 972 KB) and no per-diagram restyling.

nodes.label: skill-factory / autoresearch
nodes.rationale: Aims for higher-quality generated skills; generated skills are sandbox-tested in a throwaway worktree before real use.

nodes.label: test-audit (openclaw)
nodes.rationale: Reduces tests that stay green when their subject breaks through a write-time authoring gate and evidence record before test removal.

nodes.label: Verified floors by platform
nodes.rationale: Each floor is linked to a run that proves it and marked unverified otherwise, so no value is assumed without evidence.

nodes.label: context7 plugin
nodes.rationale: Fetches current library documentation on demand to avoid stale training data, kept on-demand to limit MCP overhead.

nodes.label: handover plugin
nodes.rationale: It is ALWAYS-tier and versioned as markdown so session state survives across sessions with append-only next-session files.

nodes.label: himmel-bus plugin
nodes.rationale: Provides a private chained local message store for session-to-session messages (early status, not a himmelctl install item).

nodes.label: luna-correlate plugin
nodes.rationale: Only factors.cache touches the network and outputs are candidate signals only, to keep analysis offline and avoid diagnostic or causal claims.

nodes.label: Playwright plugin
nodes.rationale: Offers browser automation for e2e work, installed but disabled by default to keep sessions lean.

nodes.label: Alert roles limited to chief and worker
nodes.norm_label: alert roles limited to chief and worker
nodes.rationale: Subagent, bridge and other hit rates swing with cold starts, so alerting on them gives false alarms (a dry run showed subagents 4.2 pts under baseline with nothing wrong).

nodes.label: Cache hit-rate metric and windows
nodes.rationale: Hit = cache_read over all prompt tokens, compared across a RECENT and a BASELINE window so a drop shows against the system's own history.

nodes.label: metrics.json schema (schema 1)
nodes.rationale: A versioned schema lets the morning report and the board read the metrics file reliably, with null pct fields when a window has no tokens.

nodes.label: cache-health state files
nodes.rationale: metrics.json, history.jsonl and alert-state.json separate current metrics, the run history that supplies our own baseline, and hysteresis state; online figures like 76.5%/40% are not a baseline.

nodes.label: jira release commands
nodes.rationale: Only writer of release state and runner of request batches.

nodes.label: Release lease epoch
nodes.rationale: The epoch makes a successor RM safe because acquire refuses any epoch other than the one named.

nodes.label: Four pre-launch checks
nodes.rationale: Each check (stale backlog bug, literal em-dash Tier line, design-profile OAuth login, live session owning the worktree) previously cost a chief a dead worker when skipped.

nodes.label: Worker API-lane switch (WORKER_SESSION_API_LANE)
nodes.rationale: Per-call env prefixes are refused by guards so workers never reached the API lane; an opt-in seam from the launching shell fixes this while staying default OFF and spend-controlled.

nodes.label: Context mode as an arming-time choice
nodes.norm_label: context mode as an arming-time choice
