nodes.rationale: Choosing context per arm instead of station-wide replaces the [1m] settings suffix, because measurement showed the suffix alone is a no-op on this account.

nodes.label: Fleet-size cap (provisional 4)
nodes.rationale: 9-11 concurrent workers exhausted a week's usage bucket in under 48 hours, so a cap of 4 is a provisional headroom-leaving limit pending a measured burn rate.

nodes.label: gateAllow registry list
nodes.rationale: Allow rules evaluated before the auto-mode classifier give deterministic routing, while push rules are omitted because a wildcard would admit --no-verify.

nodes.label: Which model strings accept the [1m] suffix
nodes.norm_label: which model strings accept the [1m] suffix
nodes.rationale: Zero-spend statusline measurement showed Fable silently strips the suffix, so a 1m chief arm gets only the autocompact half and says so in the log.

nodes.label: Sanctioned operator-ruled 1M opt-in
nodes.rationale: implied: a well-formed brief line with a non-empty reason lets an operator deliberately override the refusal for one worker while keeping all other guards intact.

nodes.label: Per-profile context ceilings (contextMode/autocompact)
nodes.rationale: Declaring ceilings in the profile registry lets a design worker get 1M without env or brief overrides while other profiles stay at 200000.

nodes.label: Role-matched plugin profile for every launch path
nodes.norm_label: role-matched plugin profile for every launch path
nodes.rationale: Launch paths that previously ran with the operator's full plugin set now refuse rather than silently fall back, keeping each role's plugin set lean.

nodes.label: Sonnet and Opus autocompact ceilings with context guards
nodes.norm_label: sonnet and opus autocompact ceilings with context guards
nodes.rationale: Raised ceilings are an operator ruling whose cost is stated by the JSONL table rather than chosen from it.

nodes.label: Host key verification failure troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: A git insteadOf rewrite turns the HTTPS clone of claude-obsidian into SSH, which fails strict checking without a known_hosts entry.

nodes.label: Plugin install sequence, scope and direct install
nodes.norm_label: plugin install sequence, scope and direct install
nodes.rationale: User scope suits personal plugins while project scope shares them on clone, at a supply-chain trust cost for outside contributors.

nodes.label: Lean profile (disabled by default plugins)
nodes.rationale: Shipping the minimal plugin set avoids re-creating a maximal 31-plugin install on every machine.

nodes.label: Claude Code plugins section
nodes.rationale: The plugins are luna-dependent or personal-workflow tools, not required for core himmel, so install only what is needed.

nodes.label: security-guidance recommended OFF
nodes.rationale: It duplicates the stronger /pr-check critic panel and CodeRabbit gates while costing a model call per turn and extra process spawns tied to a kernel-handle leak.

nodes.label: Two-tier plugin profile (ALWAYS / ON-DEMAND / NOT INSTALLED)
nodes.norm_label: two-tier plugin profile (always / on-demand / not installed)
nodes.rationale: Rarely used plugins cost session-start context tokens, so they are left disabled or uninstalled and enabled on demand.

nodes.label: Install a single plugin: user vs project scope
nodes.norm_label: install a single plugin: user vs project scope
nodes.rationale: User scope records the plugin for you everywhere, while project scope commits it for collaborators but ships a trust-registry decision.

nodes.label: N37 BANK-holding upper-case names to USAGE
nodes.norm_label: n37 bank-holding upper-case names to usage
nodes.rationale: Script-local and test names holding BANK are renamed to USAGE in place per plan row 66, while registry rows with a concrete new name take that name, so the rename stays consistent with the registry.

nodes.label: N38 LEG-inside upper-case names (pending-N2892)
nodes.rationale: Plan row 66 renames script-local names in place in the owning slice, but the registry has no new name yet, so 35 of the 36 names are left pending.

nodes.label: N39 CONSOLE-inside upper-case names (pending-N2892)
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL_CONSOLE and HIMMEL_CONSOLE_* are kept under OD-1, so only the 11 script-local names remain and they have no ruled name yet.

nodes.label: N43 other console-* scripts (needs a ruling)
nodes.norm_label: n43 other console-* scripts (needs a ruling)
nodes.rationale: These console-* script and file names are not in the approved rename table, so a rename needs a ruling first.

nodes.label: OD-1: HIMMEL_CONSOLE and HIMMEL_CONSOLE_* kept
nodes.rationale: implied: these public env vars are deliberately exempted from the rename to avoid breaking existing users.

nodes.label: Plan row 66: rename script-local names in place
nodes.norm_label: plan row 66: rename script-local names in place
nodes.rationale: Script-local names are renamed within the owning slice rather than through the registry, so each slice stays self-contained.

nodes.label: BANK_CACHE_FILE to USAGE_MONITOR_CACHE_FILE
nodes.rationale: A registry row gives BANK_CACHE_FILE a concrete new name, which is already live.

nodes.label: CONSOLE_WAIT_BANK to CHIEF_WAIT_USAGE
nodes.rationale: A registry row gives CONSOLE_WAIT_BANK a ruled name that combines the chief and usage renames.

nodes.label: CONSOLE_WAIT_LEG_EVENT to CHIEF_WAIT_WORKER_EVENT
nodes.rationale: The only LEG-inside name with a ruled new name, so it is live while the other 35 are pending.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_STOP_GUARD_BANK_PREFLIGHT to HIMMEL_STOP_GUARD_USAGE_PREFLIGHT
nodes.rationale: A registry row gives this env var a concrete new name, which is live.

nodes.label: Isolated worker execution with hard limits
nodes.norm_label: isolated worker execution with hard limits
nodes.rationale: Running in a separate worker keeps cost and context out of the chief, and timeouts and heap caps bound TLC; no retries or widened constants avoid false assurance.

nodes.label: Optional evidence, not a merge gate
nodes.norm_label: optional evidence, not a merge gate
nodes.rationale: In the VM trial the with-skill arm missed a bug that the no-skill arm found, so a clean report cannot replace the judge.

nodes.label: Pinned tla2tools and statechart tree digests
nodes.norm_label: pinned tla2tools and statechart tree digests
nodes.rationale: Sha256 and tree-digest pins with no auto-download ensure only reviewed code executes, refusing on any mismatch.

nodes.label: running-a-chief.md
nodes.rationale: Referenced as source of the relay-before-release rule to model separately.

nodes.label: chief-template.md
nodes.rationale: implied: the parent template that these sections were split out from and that points to them.

nodes.label: Measurement discipline
nodes.rationale: Vacuous exit 0 and skips credited as passes hide failures, so artifacts must be verified and skips tallied separately.

nodes.label: MSYS spawn economics
nodes.rationale: Spawn cost roughly triples under contention and the hook chain runs on every Bash call, so hot-path spawns multiply by call volume.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes (hard vs best-effort)
nodes.rationale: Holding hard reviewers while relaxing best-effort ones means an unavailable CodeRabbit never makes the operator wait.

nodes.label: Alibaba Model Studio free qwen lane
nodes.norm_label: alibaba model studio free qwen lane
nodes.rationale: It adds free parallel implementation/critic capacity alongside Codex without replacing the main provider.

nodes.label: CR critic tier (production hermes lane)
nodes.rationale: An independent model-family reviewer gives /pr-check a cross-family second opinion, with a fail-closed verdict and fail-open transport so a transport problem never turns the panel red.

nodes.label: HERMES_HOME / HERMES_PY / HERMES_INVOKE_TIMEOUT
nodes.rationale: The scripts do not all fall back to the same install root, so both variables are exported explicitly; the timeout bounds a stuck parity_guard deny-retry loop.

nodes.label: Quick start: install and configure hermes
nodes.norm_label: quick start: install and configure hermes
nodes.rationale: himmel never writes the user's hermes identity, so the base install and config are left to hermes's own tooling and himmel only points at it.

nodes.label: model_aliases routing lever
nodes.rationale: The -z one-shot path auto-detects the provider from -m and overrides config, while a bare qwen name falls through to codex and fails, and model_aliases is checked first.

nodes.label: Iteration budget exhaustion detection (rc 126)
nodes.rationale: A run that hits its max_turns budget still exits 0, so invoke.sh greps the banner and overrides rc so truncated runs cannot read as clean passes.

nodes.label: parity_guard deny-loop bound (rc 124/125)
nodes.rationale: hermes feeds a deny back as a tool result with unbounded max_iterations, so himmel bounds it with a wall-clock timebox and an identical-deny escalation abort.

nodes.label: OVER-DENYs: hermes denies, Claude Code allows
nodes.norm_label: over-denys: hermes denies, claude code allows
nodes.rationale: Fail-closed write fence and blanket MCP refusal are deliberate strictness, not defects.

nodes.label: Hermes himmel_agent default and the ox-alpha record
nodes.norm_label: hermes himmel_agent default and the ox-alpha record
nodes.rationale: The lane-adoption rule requires measuring a lane's backend rather than assuming it, and the record is kept as history after the trial expired.

nodes.label: OpenRouter free-tier watcher
nodes.rationale: Under the free-only policy, churn in the free-model catalog is the main risk, so it is watched with suggestions only and no registry edits.

nodes.label: Other delegation-lane dispatch chokepoints
nodes.rationale: Pins only the exact dispatch shape because the lanes.json bestFor field is authoritative and restating its prose would create a drifting second copy.

nodes.label: Paid-by-default critic panel posture
nodes.rationale: The free lane was removed deliberately (noisy gptoss/kimi at 12-13% agreed-rate, erroring qwen3coder), so the paid codex anchor runs by default.

nodes.label: Review gate card
nodes.rationale: It writes only the per-machine overlay critics.local.json and states the ruled rate-limit behaviour so the shared critics.json is never touched.

nodes.label: jira-create skill
nodes.rationale: Asks for missing type, title or required fields instead of guessing.

nodes.label: jira-init skill
nodes.rationale: A skill cannot prompt for secrets, so it points to the slash command which can.

nodes.label: Single literal absolute-path engine command
nodes.rationale: The unattended cadence runs with cwd at the vault and its engine-allow hook refuses compound shapes, $ tokens and plugin-cache paths, so a literal himmel-repo path is required.

nodes.label: Report-only, filesystem-only lint
nodes.rationale: Auto-fixing in v1 is avoided and egress-locked vaults block network tools, so the operator decides what to act on from the engine output alone.

nodes.label: Intake gate for a frozen version
nodes.norm_label: intake gate for a frozen version
nodes.rationale: A frozen version should take no new ticket without a recorded reason, so admissions leave a ledger row.

nodes.label: Override and admissions ledger
nodes.rationale: Chief overrides need an auditable append-only record, though the console marker is spoofable by same-uid callers until signed state replaces it.

nodes.label: Ledger-driven uninstall removal (provenance ledger)
nodes.rationale: Folding the provenance ledger into per-unit verdicts lets uninstall remove only what himmel created and restore what it replaced, failing closed to keep overwrite-prone rows when the ledger is unreadable.

nodes.label: --purge-state --keep-backups retain-move
nodes.rationale: Moving ledger and backups together into one retained directory avoids a permanent orphaned backups dir and loses nothing.

nodes.label: Reading verdicts and backup retention
nodes.rationale: A single resolved predicate governs when backups and snapshots may be deleted so a held backup is never lost.

nodes.label: TTY [r]estore/[d]elete saves live file first
nodes.rationale: Restore or delete would overwrite or destroy the operator's current bytes, so a sidecar copy is saved first and the action is skipped if the save fails.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge graph rules
nodes.rationale: Queries return a scoped subgraph that is much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Search before writing the brief's Prior art line
nodes.norm_label: search before writing the brief's prior art line
nodes.rationale: Workers and judges inherit the Prior art line while chiefs searched notes in only 19% of sessions, so a bounded qmd and graph search is required and subagents must be told the route.

nodes.label: Bench acceptance criteria
nodes.rationale: Lean must not cost more tokens and may lose at most one pass of five per probe, otherwise the rule that lost its teeth is restored inline.

nodes.label: Bench probes P0-P3
nodes.rationale: Four prompts judge intent from the transcript, with a reset before every sample so mutations do not leak between runs.

nodes.label: Ruled rename table (leg→worker, console→chief, bank→usage)
nodes.rationale: The approved table is the only authority for new file names, so paths it names get a definite new name.

nodes.label: Operator vs Adopter working-principles variants
nodes.rationale: The project CLAUDE.md is held to a byte budget, so the general engineering principles ship at user scope instead, idempotently and non-destructively.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md lean-invoke measurement
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is the one preload block every harness pays, so demoting rationale to hooks and docs saved ~6.7 KB per session while enforced directives stayed inline.

nodes.label: Upstream-owned ## graphify section
nodes.rationale: Kept verbatim as the installer writes it so reinstalls and upgrades are no-ops rather than conflicts, with himmel's own rules placed outside and winning on conflict.

nodes.label: Skill/command 120-char description cap
nodes.rationale: Every description byte is paid at each session start and nothing self-limits, so capping at 120 chars cut listings 59% while keeping trigger phrases to protect routing.

nodes.label: Routing eval
nodes.rationale: It measures which skill, command, agent or MCP tool a model picks from the rendered listing, using cases mined from real misroutes.

nodes.label: Chief-spawned worker context hand-off (guard-worker-context-handoff.sh)
nodes.rationale: Work in progress must be pushed or handed off before auto-compaction summarises context; the 75% of autocompact ceiling threshold leaves room for the checkpoint.

nodes.label: Worker checkpoint/handover at 75% of autocompact ceiling
nodes.norm_label: worker checkpoint/handover at 75% of autocompact ceiling
nodes.rationale: Measured over 399 workers, compaction fired between 157k and 176k, so 150k sits just before the earliest compaction while 60% and 65% thresholds only added relaunches or stopped workers early.

nodes.label: What the guard does not cover (idle compaction, batch jumps)
nodes.norm_label: what the guard does not cover (idle compaction, batch jumps)
nodes.rationale: A second trigger fires after about 54 minutes idle and the guard checks only between calls, so some compactions pass without a deny at any share.

nodes.label: Fail-open, scope and bypass
nodes.rationale: A false block strands a worker that nobody watches, so the hook fails open on every infrastructure gap.

nodes.label: Two modes: compact and handoff
nodes.rationale: Compact lets a worker checkpoint and continue through compaction, while handoff stops it so a successor resumes from a RESUME doc.

nodes.label: Guard off by default (operator ruling 2026-10-07)
nodes.rationale: Workers auto-compact anyway, and an always-on guard stopped every opus worker at 13 % fill, so the operator ruled it off unless a mode is set.

nodes.label: One-line commit form (-m paragraphs + --trailer)
nodes.rationale: A newline in a Bash command is denied, so a multi-line git commit -m cannot run and paragraphs and trailers are used instead.

nodes.label: Past the threshold: allowed hand-off calls
nodes.norm_label: past the threshold: allowed hand-off calls
nodes.rationale: Only the calls needed to commit, push and record state are allowed so the worker can reach an unlock without doing ordinary work.

nodes.label: PreCompact behavior
nodes.rationale: Claude Code does not document what follows a refused auto-compaction, so the refusal is only the second line of defence behind the threshold.

nodes.label: Share 73 on Sonnet profiles
nodes.rationale: At the 450000 ceiling a share of 75 rounds up to 340000 tokens, only 3158 before the earliest Sonnet compaction, while 73 gives 330000 and about 13000 tokens of room.

nodes.label: Share 87 on Opus profiles (operator decision 751)
nodes.rationale: The ruling is a checkpoint at 700000 with an 800000 ceiling, and share 87 rounds up to exactly 70 % (700000), whereas 88 would give 710000.

nodes.label: Threshold: 75 % of autocompact ceiling
nodes.rationale: The deny must land before the earliest observed compaction (157k of a 200k ceiling), and 75 % leaves 7000 tokens to commit, push and write the CHECKPOINT bullet.

nodes.label: Every unlock (CHECKPOINT, RESUME doc, WRAPPED, BLOCKED)
nodes.norm_label: every unlock (checkpoint, resume doc, wrapped, blocked)
nodes.rationale: Each unlock proves state is saved or handed off; BLOCKED frees only hand-off calls because it is a hand-off to the chief, not permission to keep working.

nodes.label: auto-action audit log and op-aware auditResult
nodes.norm_label: auto-action audit log and op-aware auditresult
nodes.rationale: Op-aware result labels keep forensic queries correct for the irreversible merge outcome, since merge-public relays a different rc space than arm-resume.

nodes.label: telegram profile
nodes.rationale: Its value is deny-by-default correctness so no ambient full plugin/MCP surface leaks into an unattended bridge run, not a token cut.

nodes.label: Reply flush timer and atomic cursors
nodes.norm_label: reply flush timer and atomic cursors
nodes.rationale: A separate ~1s flush timer delivers replies within a second instead of up to 30s, and tmp+rename cursors prevent torn offsets on crash.

nodes.label: Channels must use empty entry
nodes.rationale: Channel posts have no from user and fall back to sender_chat.id, so a non-empty allowFrom never matches and all posts would be dropped.

nodes.label: Channel consolidation pattern
nodes.rationale: Forwarding many sources into one allowlisted channel avoids allowlisting each source group, at the cost that anyone with post rights drives the bridge.

nodes.label: Group and channel allowlist (access.json groups)
nodes.rationale: Gating by chat_id fails closed so non-allowed groups can never drive the bridge, though allowlisting trusts every member.

nodes.label: Group triage classifier gate
nodes.rationale: A cheap classifier before spawning a bounded Claude run saves cost on chatter, and it is fail-open (errors become spawn-high) so actionable messages are not lost.

nodes.label: requireMention per-group mode
nodes.rationale: Groups shared with a sibling bot need @mention-only mode so the bridge does not answer messages meant for the other bot; it fails open while the username is unresolved so it never silently goes quiet.

nodes.label: trustAnonymousAdmins flag
nodes.rationale: Anonymous admin posts carry the shared GroupAnonymousBot id so the operator floor never matches and messages are dropped; the flag opts a group in to guaranteed enqueue at the cost of trusting every admin.

nodes.label: Single getUpdates owner per token
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows one getUpdates consumer per token, and a second poller causes 409 Conflict storms that make the bridge deaf.

nodes.label: Pointing himmel at your VM
nodes.rationale: VM scripts resolve guests by VirtualBox name through a registry, so adopters must match or add an entry.

nodes.label: vmsdk.py Python venv
nodes.rationale: System python is often externally managed (PEP 668), so a dedicated venv is used for paramiko, python-dotenv and pycdlib.

nodes.label: Persistent after-report clones and suite-ready-v4 snapshot
nodes.norm_label: persistent after-report clones and suite-ready-v4 snapshot
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier refuses clone deletion and linked-clone disk chains depend on older snapshots, so clones are restored to a baseline rather than deleted.

nodes.label: VM secret boundary
nodes.rationale: A snapshot is durable, so a leaked .env would outlive the VM; copies exclude secrets and the guest is scanned before snapshot.

nodes.label: Skill pass is NON-GATING
nodes.rationale: An LLM-in-the-loop, VM-dependent, billing-consuming test must never block a merge.

nodes.label: VM = run wild; real machine = allowlist
nodes.norm_label: vm = run wild; real machine = allowlist
nodes.rationale: A VM is throwaway and holds no operator data, so skipping permissions is acceptable there, unlike the operator's real machine.

nodes.label: Four merge gates
nodes.rationale: Gates 3 and 4 fail closed while gates 1 and 2 fail open on API error, balancing safety with availability.

nodes.label: Act when a step's conditions are met
nodes.norm_label: act when a step's conditions are met
nodes.rationale: Asking after a verified GO wastes operator time, so escalation is reserved for denials, irreversible acts, or choices without a safe default.

nodes.label: Adapt upstream PRs first
nodes.rationale: Community PRs are often already verified and staying close to upstream keeps the fork rebaseable.

nodes.label: Adversarial review never converges; gate on standard panel
nodes.norm_label: adversarial review never converges; gate on standard panel
nodes.rationale: An adversarially prompted critic keeps surfacing ever narrower findings (13 rounds observed) while the standard panel returned 0/0/0, so convergence is gated on the standard panel.

nodes.label: Unsupported messages must come from actually asking the tool
nodes.norm_label: unsupported messages must come from actually asking the tool
nodes.rationale: A failed query is not evidence of absence, so 'asked, no' and 'could not ask' need distinct return codes and wording.

nodes.label: Chain ASAP: arm the next session without idling
nodes.norm_label: chain asap: arm the next session without idling
nodes.rationale: Idle quota not spent before its window resets evaporates, so continuation should be armed for the soonest slot on every surface.

nodes.label: A chief must not idle between notifications
nodes.norm_label: a chief must not idle between notifications
nodes.rationale: Only the chief sweeps for blockage, so it must act as enabler rather than just react to completions.

nodes.label: citation-guard Critical is a pointer, not the finding
nodes.norm_label: citation-guard critical is a pointer, not the finding
nodes.rationale: The wrapper is synthesized when a citation cannot be anchored, so the wrapped finding must be adjudicated on its own merits since a dropped citation is unverified, not disproved.

nodes.label: Auto-mode classifier as semantic layer over allow-list
nodes.norm_label: auto-mode classifier as semantic layer over allow-list
nodes.rationale: The classifier blocks semantically risky actions like self-merge to main that the allow-list alone permits.

nodes.label: Clips are pointers, not self-contained notes
nodes.norm_label: clips are pointers, not self-contained notes
nodes.rationale: The clip body is just intro text and the signal is at the source URL, so harvest must come before triage.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit quiet incrementals post no review object
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit quiet incrementals post no review object
nodes.rationale: A clean incremental yields only a commit status, not a check-run or review, so the thread query is the truth and polling for a review object is futile.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit replies are not the review
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit replies are not the review
nodes.rationale: A Review failed then Review finished pair is a rate-limit race on CodeRabbit's side, and the review object lands minutes after the ack.

nodes.label: Open companion PR with issue when fix is unambiguous
nodes.norm_label: open companion pr with issue when fix is unambiguous
nodes.rationale: An issue filed alone gets its fix taken by someone else's PR within hours, and the credit goes with it.

nodes.label: Cross-platform requirements: Linux and macOS, bash 3.2-safe
nodes.norm_label: cross-platform requirements: linux and macos, bash 3.2-safe
nodes.rationale: A single-platform script silently breaks adopters on Linux and macOS, and macOS ships bash 3.2.

nodes.label: A failing lane is almost always our credential or config
nodes.norm_label: a failing lane is almost always our credential or config
nodes.rationale: Diagnosing the local process and credential before rerouting avoids trusting a status line that only checks a credential file exists.

nodes.label: Attribute post-merge failures against baseline and pristine upstream
nodes.norm_label: attribute post-merge failures against baseline and pristine upstream
nodes.rationale: Most new failures after an upstream merge are new upstream tests failing on your platform, so a single baseline mis-blames the merge.

nodes.label: Generic example names in public-facing docs
nodes.norm_label: generic example names in public-facing docs
nodes.rationale: Real vault or project names leak personal context with no illustrative value.

nodes.label: Hook or permission PRs need independent adversarial review
nodes.norm_label: hook or permission prs need independent adversarial review
nodes.rationale: An independent reviewer turned three self-reviewed guard PRs from GO to NO-GO on 2026-09-24, showing self-review is insufficient for guard changes.

nodes.label: Tests must be hermetic and never touch operator data
nodes.norm_label: tests must be hermetic and never touch operator data
nodes.rationale: Redirecting HOME and using temp roots, with a snapshot check on the real dir, prevents tests from reading or mutating real user state.

nodes.label: Implementor tier floor
nodes.rationale: The cheapest model tier can return subtly wrong code that review must catch, costing more than the tier delta saved.

nodes.label: Machine-generated PRs never get a CodeRabbit review
nodes.norm_label: machine-generated prs never get a coderabbit review
nodes.rationale: An absent review blocks nothing, so the ordinary merge gate is the whole gate for dependabot and regenerated-artifact PRs.

nodes.label: Mannered prose anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Naming the failure mode explicitly works better than general brevity rules since mannered prose is orthogonal to length.

nodes.label: Auto-memory confidence and staleness frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Semantic memory without staleness marking structurally forgets wrong, so stale recalled memories are rechecked or deleted.

nodes.label: Run merge from the parent repo, not the worktree
nodes.norm_label: run merge from the parent repo, not the worktree
nodes.rationale: --delete-branch checks out main locally and the parent worktree already holds it.

nodes.label: Metered-lane structure
nodes.rationale: Raw dispatch bypasses ACL preflight, model pins, ledger logging and quota preflight, so dispatch must go through the sanctioned script.

nodes.label: Name who files a handed-off ticket
nodes.norm_label: name who files a handed-off ticket
nodes.rationale: Same-hour concurrent filings evade the search-before-filing rule and produce duplicate tickets.

nodes.label: Never hardcode or assume a PR number
nodes.norm_label: never hardcode or assume a pr number
nodes.rationale: PR and issue numbers share one sequence, so a parallel session can take last+1 and a merge of a guessed number once merged the wrong PR.

nodes.label: No PR where outside contributors are never merged
nodes.norm_label: no pr where outside contributors are never merged
nodes.rationale: A record of closed-unmerged outside PRs signals that a PR will not be accepted, so an issue is the right channel.

nodes.label: Never resolve conflicts by reflex --theirs/--ours
nodes.rationale: A written diff analysis catches the non-obvious cases where removed content is load-bearing, and 'trivial, take theirs' hides the justification.

nodes.label: Never tell a child to route around its session's guards
nodes.norm_label: never tell a child to route around its session's guards
nodes.rationale: Such a brief invites escalation past guards like guard-pr-check-literal, so the child should report the denial as a finding.

nodes.label: Four non-convergence signatures
nodes.rationale: Different round patterns call for different responses (cap, close the class, document the bound, or keep going on distinct real defects).

nodes.label: Operator-blocked is not worker-complete
nodes.rationale: Waiting on operator actions should not stop work since design passes and next dispatches need no operator.

nodes.label: Run the panel once per head
nodes.norm_label: run the panel once per head
nodes.rationale: The ledger dedups on (head, finding_id), so a second run reports a suppressed 0/0/0 and wastes a paid model call.

nodes.label: Parked and queued workers look identical
nodes.norm_label: parked and queued workers look identical
nodes.rationale: Nudging a healthy queued worker creates a second-writer race, so check lock state first and brief workers to commit before long verification.

nodes.label: gh pr merge right after push returns not mergeable
nodes.norm_label: gh pr merge right after push returns not mergeable
nodes.rationale: GitHub has not yet computed mergeability for the new head SHA, so poll until non-UNKNOWN or wait about 8s.

nodes.label: Projection fixes need a second control on the delivery path
nodes.norm_label: projection fixes need a second control on the delivery path
nodes.rationale: 'The rule is right' and 'the shipped thing is fixed' are separate claims since the delivery mechanism may not run or may replay a range.

nodes.label: Recovered work in a dead worker's tree is presumed half-baked
nodes.norm_label: recovered work in a dead worker's tree is presumed half-baked
nodes.rationale: A worker killed mid-edit can leave a half-applied edit that looks finished, so recovered work re-enters as an ordinary gated diff.

nodes.label: Diff red CI failing set against previous run
nodes.norm_label: diff red ci failing set against previous run
nodes.rationale: The diff proves both that the fix landed and that remaining failures are pre-existing, which the new run alone cannot show.

nodes.label: Automated review sizing and cost ladder
nodes.norm_label: automated review sizing and cost ladder
nodes.rationale: Never zero automated review, but spend scales with risk from docs-audit subagent up to /code-review ultra as the last-resort most expensive tier.

nodes.label: Rising severity across rounds means stop and simplify
nodes.norm_label: rising severity across rounds means stop and simplify
nodes.rationale: Flat or rising severity signals a wrong design, and panel severity labels are unreliable in both directions so they must be re-derived.

nodes.label: Rulings to running agents can silently fail to render
nodes.norm_label: rulings to running agents can silently fail to render
nodes.rationale: Queued delivery to a running agent is lossy, so quote-back is demanded and silence is treated as non-consent.

nodes.label: Internal specs and plans are work artifacts, not reference docs
nodes.norm_label: internal specs and plans are work artifacts, not reference docs
nodes.rationale: They belong in the state repo because some carry private context and code-repo docs/ is operator reference and OSS-public only.

nodes.label: Splice probes into the suite's own directory, never /tmp
nodes.norm_label: splice probes into the suite's own directory, never /tmp
nodes.rationale: Suites resolve the script under test relative to their own location, so a probe elsewhere yields a spurious rc like 127.

nodes.label: Stage explicit paths; never git add -A
nodes.norm_label: stage explicit paths; never git add -a
nodes.rationale: Concurrent sessions and wrong-package-manager builds drop untracked artifacts that git add -A would sweep into the commit.

nodes.label: Stale-base worktree: rebase onto origin/main, not reset --soft
nodes.norm_label: stale-base worktree: rebase onto origin/main, not reset --soft
nodes.rationale: reset --soft leaves old files in the index so the commit silently reverts every change main gained since.

nodes.label: Tests pin our seams, never other products
nodes.norm_label: tests pin our seams, never other products
nodes.rationale: Permanent cases re-proving third-party behavior add maintenance without testing our integration.

nodes.label: Timebox and soak before filing upstream
nodes.norm_label: timebox and soak before filing upstream
nodes.rationale: Real usage must first prove we understand the problem and our workaround is insufficient, which also makes a stronger issue.

nodes.label: Trace caller chain before trusting before/after measurement
nodes.norm_label: trace caller chain before trusting before/after measurement
nodes.rationale: A safety flag can silently disable the pass being measured, making identical output the expected result of an unrun pass.

nodes.label: Verify the artifact, not return code or status
nodes.norm_label: verify the artifact, not return code or status
nodes.rationale: Return codes, status fields and usage counts are reports about work and can look successful when nothing landed.

nodes.label: Verify universal-quantifier claims before writing them
nodes.norm_label: verify universal-quantifier claims before writing them
nodes.rationale: A false 'every X has Y' misleads every future session, so counts must be run first.

nodes.label: Decision states (ADOPT, PILOT-MEASURE, REJECT, re-audit states)
nodes.norm_label: decision states (adopt, pilot-measure, reject, re-audit states)
nodes.rationale: Each eval ends in one recorded ADR state so a settled question is not re-opened, and REJECTs stop the same tool being re-evaluated.

nodes.label: Goal articulation and vanity-metric trap
nodes.rationale: %-token-reduction is an input cost, not an outcome, and can hide needed context while making sessions worse.

nodes.label: Measurement protocol (before/after and measure-during)
nodes.rationale: Adoption must rest on outcome-per-session evidence from a real workday, not on byte counts or synthetic demos.

nodes.label: Axis 2: Context window
nodes.rationale: Without an explicit window Claude Code assumes ~200k and compacts early, and the registry value and launcher knob do not derive each other.

nodes.label: Axis 5: Harness choice
nodes.rationale: Hermes one-shot and full-session spawn trade off isolation and durability differently, so choose by actual need.

nodes.label: Axis 1: Latency budget
nodes.rationale: GLM took about 205s against a 240s shared timeout, causing spurious timeouts, so per-lane overrides are needed.

nodes.label: Axis 7: Measure before trust
nodes.rationale: A pass streak only gates dispatch and says nothing about outcome per session, so readiness must be measured not asserted.

nodes.label: Axis 4: Prompt family
nodes.rationale: Unmatched model names silently fall into the open family, which may not suit the new model.

nodes.label: pollen / aq factors (daily-mean)
nodes.rationale: Served via the air-quality API, which has a shorter history, so historical date ranges fail loud and captured fixtures support offline replay tests.

nodes.label: pressure factor (daily-min)
nodes.rationale: Daily-min exposes the front-passage pressure drop, a prime migraine trigger.

nodes.label: Grid-corner fetch with no operator coordinates
nodes.norm_label: grid-corner fetch with no operator coordinates
nodes.rationale: The privacy guarantee rests on the fetcher only sending bbox grid corners, not on Open-Meteo's own grid snapping.

nodes.label: Open-Meteo location data source (M2)
nodes.rationale: Piloted rather than adopted because it is a new external dependency not yet proven on a real workload, and requests carry only bbox grid corners, never operator coordinates.

nodes.label: Operator working-conventions
nodes.rationale: Consolidates habits that lived only in volatile per-user memory notes into a versioned, reviewable doc that survives a memory prune.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit is the App, and only the App
nodes.norm_label: coderabbit is the app, and only the app
nodes.rationale: The CLI was a second charge against the same rate-limited account and forced extra paid codex panel rows for a signal the App already posts on the PR.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit best-effort rule and gates
nodes.rationale: Seven finished PRs sat about 7h because docs taught sequencing around CodeRabbit, so the rule became a pre-commit gate rather than prose.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:luna-upgrade-all skill
nodes.rationale: implied: the skill is the single source of truth for the runbook.

nodes.label: Diagnose disabled-by-policy vs unconfigured plugin state
nodes.norm_label: diagnose disabled-by-policy vs unconfigured plugin state
nodes.rationale: The plugin directory is tracked in git so its presence proves nothing; only enabledPlugins config shows whether it is enabled, so reporting must not falsely claim 'not installed'.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage:luna-upgrade skill
nodes.rationale: implied: the skill is the primary path and the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Ambient pointer must not outrank running checkout
nodes.norm_label: ambient pointer must not outrank running checkout
nodes.rationale: Scanning $HOME let an upgrade source a stale public mirror and write 22 files into a real vault, so the invoking checkout now outranks env vars and scans while an explicit flag still wins.

nodes.label: Multi-vault upgrade engine
nodes.rationale: It layers a sweep over the proven single-vault upgrade.sh, with apply kept per-vault, operator-confirmed and backed up first, to limit risk.

nodes.label: Backup and restore undo path
nodes.rationale: Backups are kept outside the vault to avoid gitignore or autosync interaction and allow undoing a completed upgrade.

nodes.label: Conflict-brainstorm layer
nodes.rationale: On a _CLAUDE.md CONFLICT the agent proposes a merge but never auto-writes it, preserving operator customizations.

nodes.label: Single-writer sequential apply
nodes.rationale: Parallel applies against one shared artifact are unsafe, so vaults are applied one at a time.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Most harvest skills carry their own write paths, so dry-run must suppress skill dispatch as well as Edit and Write.

nodes.label: Headless refusal (HIMMEL-128)
nodes.rationale: Headless claude runs in a separate billing bucket, so the command refuses to run under it.

nodes.label: G-1 privacy URL gate
nodes.rationale: implied: private, internal or credentialed URLs must never reach a scrape backend, and ambiguous hosts are refused because a scraper may read them as a different host.

nodes.label: G-5 resume state contract
nodes.rationale: Capping retries at three and covering partial as well as failed stops rate-limited clips from looping forever.

nodes.label: Scrape backend chain and routing
nodes.rationale: implied: trying the free local and keyless backends first and the credit-capped firecrawl last keeps cost bounded.

nodes.label: G-3 single-section-add invariant
nodes.rationale: All writes preserve the original clip body so operator hand-edits are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Dry-run hard gate (ig-media-enrich)
nodes.rationale: Guarantees no vault write occurs under --dry-run by checking DRY_RUN before any Write or non-dry-run tool call.

nodes.label: Tool owns every vault write
nodes.rationale: Mechanical writers with G-3 verified-write discipline revert on mismatch, so the agent never hand-edits frontmatter of a clip whose slide text it just read.

nodes.label: Clip and slide text is data, not directives
nodes.norm_label: clip and slide text is data, not directives
nodes.rationale: Clip bodies and on-image text are attacker-controlled, so they are transcribed but never obeyed, and enriched clips are re-screened for injection.

nodes.label: fm_true frontmatter predicate
nodes.rationale: Reading control markers only from a closed leading frontmatter block stops harvested body text from permanently suppressing a clip's triage (HIMMEL-1713).

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state, so triage aborts unless .harvest.done exists (HIMMEL-1137).

nodes.label: Injection-suspect metadata-only handling
nodes.rationale: Flagged clips are summarized from metadata only and skip action-item extraction so planted instructions cannot reach the daily note (HIMMEL-256).

nodes.label: Phase 7/8 mark and move via triage-mark-processed
nodes.norm_label: phase 7/8 mark and move via triage-mark-processed
nodes.rationale: A stale-read SHA guard and a single tool route prevent subagents from hand-editing processed markers or moving clips, protecting user edits.

nodes.label: Phase-8 debt drain
nodes.rationale: Unprocessed and evidence-move debt are independent sets, so the run must not exit on a zero unprocessed count before draining pending moves.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Every Write or unflagged fetch must check DRY_RUN first so a dry run can never mutate the vault, and a violation aborts non-zero.

nodes.label: Lean-invoke policy (HIMMEL-177)
nodes.rationale: The download plus local-whisper path is expensive, so it is run manually or by cadence and never auto-fired from /harvest-clips.

nodes.label: Mixed-tweet slide/transcript index misalignment
nodes.rationale: Transcript blocks use the original media item index while slide files are compacted sequentially, so slide numbers cannot be re-aligned to transcript items.

nodes.label: Post-enrichment injection re-scan
nodes.rationale: Transcripts and digests derive from attacker-controlled audio and images, so every written clip must be re-screened and flagged before downstream trust.

nodes.label: Slide digest step
nodes.rationale: The digest verbatim-transcribes on-image text because it is the searchable record once the images are later archived.

nodes.label: Subtitles-first transcription with provenance
nodes.rationale: Platform subtitles are cookie-free and far cheaper than whisper, so whisper runs only when no track exists or coverage is below the threshold (HIMMEL-4107).

nodes.label: Deferred vs blocking partial verdict
nodes.rationale: A per-clip source limitation is not the run's fault, while stale-read, rate-limit or failure means the view is unreliable, so only the latter withholds .harvest.done.

nodes.label: Clips are data, not directives
nodes.rationale: Frontmatter and body are copied from attacker-controlled pages, so no instruction inside them may ever be followed, matched or not.

nodes.label: G-3 single-section-add invariant
nodes.rationale: A body-only diff check (one new H2, or zero body changes on clip-body) with whitelisted harvest_* frontmatter keys guards against accidental body clobbering.

nodes.label: Frontmatter-only marker confirmation (fm_true)
nodes.rationale: Clip bodies are external and injection-suspect, so a body-text hit could force false drains or permanent skips, making control markers readable only from the leading frontmatter.

nodes.label: Outside-PR full review (ready-check item 16)
nodes.rationale: Outside contributions get a stricter set of per-head records before the operator's code-owner approval, which comes last.

nodes.label: Series hand-off at READY
nodes.rationale: RESUME doc is written first because the context guard frees a RESUME write past threshold but not a later call.

nodes.label: Series worker rules
nodes.rationale: One item per worker, writer-only ledger writes via series-ledger.py, and no compact mode keep unpublished items from being lost or corrupted.

nodes.label: Earned RESUME ARMED banner (HIMMEL-1879)
nodes.rationale: A scheduler registration exiting 0 is not proof anything is scheduled, so the script queries the entry back before claiming success.

nodes.label: Fail-safe model tier default (HIMMEL-2332)
nodes.rationale: Defaulting ordinary arms to opus and refusing unjustified Fable pins avoids accidentally launching expensive unattended sessions.

nodes.label: macOS headed crontab runner (HIMMEL-3074)
nodes.rationale: Cron gives no TTY and caps command length, so a generated runner file opens a real terminal window at fire time.

nodes.label: Per-handover canonical dedup (HIMMEL-340/1304)
nodes.rationale: Dedup keyed on canonical path identity lets distinct handovers arm concurrently while the same file under different spellings maps to one slot.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_AUTO_ACTIONS privileged-op gating
nodes.rationale: Privileged bridge ops are default OFF and enabled one by one, and aliases enable only arm-resume and restart, so merge-public must always be named explicitly.

nodes.label: SessionEnd hook cancelled at exit
nodes.rationale: Claude Code gives SessionEnd hooks a shared 1.5s budget that plugin timeouts cannot raise, so hooks detach and lost work is classified by what a cancel costs.

nodes.label: model key carries no [1m] suffix
nodes.rationale: A suffix is a station-wide default nobody chose per worker and some families silently strip it, so the key stays bare and context mode is set at arming time.

nodes.label: Caveat: no rows is not no usage
nodes.norm_label: caveat: no rows is not no usage
nodes.rationale: Fail-open means an unwritable sink or the kill switch silently drops records, so check the environment and sink before reading sparse data as zero usage.

nodes.label: 0-cost, fail-open telemetry contract
nodes.rationale: Telemetry must never break the instrumented skill, so there are no tokens, network or LLM calls and telemetry_emit always returns 0.

nodes.label: next-session resume_cwd frontmatter (HIMMEL-2147)
nodes.rationale: Omitting resume_cwd makes arm-resume.sh auto-detect the handover file's own repo, which is wrong for a handover parked in a different state repo.

nodes.label: Global Claude config (~/.claude CLAUDE.md and RTK.md)
nodes.norm_label: global claude config (~/.claude claude.md and rtk.md)
nodes.rationale: Copying the personal user-scope files on every machine keeps behaviour consistent, and CLAUDE.md needs RTK.md present because it imports it.

nodes.label: Jira / backend seam
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context every session while a CLI costs nothing until called, so a hook routes to the CLI and keeps MCP for ops without a CLI verb.

nodes.label: Backend tier
nodes.rationale: A routing registry enforces CLI-over-MCP preference.

nodes.label: Service-agnostic backend-routing guard (block-backend-tier.sh)
nodes.rationale: Prefer cli over api over mcp tiers per a registry; CLI paths resolve against the primary checkout because the dist/ artifact never exists in linked worktrees, which had left the guard inert there.

nodes.label: MCP policy tracking (HIMMEL-4676)
nodes.rationale: Observe-mode audit shows what the registry is missing before any server is switched to enforce, and the tracker must never stall a call on its own bug.

nodes.label: Prefer local Jira CLI over Atlassian MCP
nodes.norm_label: prefer local jira cli over atlassian mcp
nodes.rationale: The CLI costs fewer tokens than MCP schemas and payloads, dogfoods shipped code, and transition takes a status name in one call.

nodes.label: Runtime-registered server easel
nodes.rationale: Easel is a built-in Claude Code plugin not found in any config, so documenting it explains why file searches miss it and how policy classes it.

nodes.label: Which guards to disable and which to keep
nodes.norm_label: which guards to disable and which to keep
nodes.rationale: Secret-read and destructive-command guards fail closed around irreversible harm at no cost, while ticket, attestation and similar gates are convention-specific.

nodes.label: Flake handling (retry once, FLAKE ledger)
nodes.rationale: Retrying a failed suite once and recording a pass-on-retry as a FLAKE in a per-repo ledger separates flaky suites from real failures and prompts a ticket on repeats.

nodes.label: Hook-integrity recorder fails open
nodes.rationale: A failed or killed integrity recorder must not deny every hook or brick a session, so a failing member is skipped alone and neighbours keep running.

nodes.label: Usage-scarcity routing to codex-exec
nodes.rationale: While Claude weekly usage is scarce, fanning chunks to codex-exec first and Sonnet only where codex cannot push or hit the network conserves the scarce bucket.
nodes.source_location: What the chief must also do (f)

nodes.label: Headless codex exec must fail loud (four holes)
nodes.norm_label: headless codex exec must fail loud (four holes)
nodes.rationale: Without a headed TUI nobody sees a wedge, so watchdog, stdin, hook timeouts and a rogue-exec guard were added.

nodes.label: Untrusted-worktree refusal in exec dispatch
nodes.rationale: An untrusted tree runs codex exec with no himmel hooks, as a VM audit showed a force push succeeding, so the dispatcher refuses to start.

nodes.label: Where codex-exec cannot act (commit, hook-fenced writes, single writer)
nodes.norm_label: where codex-exec cannot act (commit, hook-fenced writes, single writer)
nodes.rationale: The sandbox pins workspace-write and fences terminal writes, so the parent commits and push/PR/network chunks go to Sonnet or the parent.

nodes.label: Usage-scarcity routing rule (codex-exec first)
nodes.rationale: While the Claude weekly budget is scarce, routing implementation to codex-exec draws the codex budget instead, with Sonnet only where codex cannot act.

nodes.label: claude-obsidian plugin
nodes.rationale: It is ON-DEMAND (disabled by default) so its vault skills and MCP server cost nothing until explicitly enabled.

nodes.label: Codex reasoning-effort knob
nodes.rationale: Astra guidance recommends low over none/minimal, so low or medium is advised pending model-aware effort validation.

nodes.label: openai-codex plugin (codex@openai-codex)
nodes.rationale: Worker lanes need it installed only for its cached companion script, so it stays disabled by default.

nodes.label: qmd CLI pinned fork install
nodes.rationale: Installing from a pinned-SHA fork clone avoids upstream bun global install, which EPERM-wedges, and carries the signal-forwarding fix until tobi/qmd#1029 is resolved upstream.

nodes.label: qmd shared HTTP singleton daemon
nodes.rationale: One shared daemon on localhost:8181 loads the read-only index runtime once rather than per session, accepting a shared crash blast radius.

nodes.label: qmd plugin (qmd@himmel)
nodes.rationale: It is ALWAYS-tier because it is a harness-operational plugin and its plugin tier is the MCP tier, so disabling it disables the search server.

nodes.label: Tiered vendor posture
nodes.rationale: Large established vendors track upstream latest while smaller community plugins are pinned with a drift advisory, per the operator ruling of 2026-08-28.

nodes.label: Dispatch chokepoint invariants
nodes.rationale: Refusing background, workspace-redirect and sandbox-widening flags keeps the sandbox and worktree boundary structural rather than instructional.

nodes.label: Watchdog timeout and flow-run ledger
nodes.rationale: An unbounded wait let wedged headless runs hang invisibly, so a timebox, tree kill and ledger rows were added.

nodes.label: Successor start and worker relay protocol
nodes.norm_label: successor start and worker relay protocol
nodes.rationale: A worker is yours only once it quotes back, and LIVE before RELAYED would strand workers not yet re-briefed.

nodes.label: ACTION ZERO startup sequence
nodes.rationale: Locks, head, usage and worker state must be verified in one batch before acting, so the chief does not relay stale or false state.

nodes.label: Dispatching a worker
nodes.rationale: A child inherits nothing, so the brief must be self-contained and queued workers' files disjoint to keep a single writer.

nodes.label: Handing over to successor chief
nodes.rationale: Handover at a fill threshold with worker re-briefing keeps workers from refusing the successor and preserves continuity.

nodes.label: Live state block
nodes.rationale: It is re-injected after compaction and handover, so the chief's authority-bearing state survives context loss.

nodes.label: Merges: READY, GO, merge
nodes.rationale: The GO is a file write that requires ready-check to pass, so no PR merges on an unverified head or open review threads.

nodes.label: Monitors (tick, usage, CI, notes repo, telegram)
nodes.norm_label: monitors (tick, usage, ci, notes repo, telegram)
nodes.rationale: Limited to five because every event wakes a full-context turn; tick and Telegram run inside the waiter so an idle chief costs no turns.

nodes.label: RETASK channel with nonce per child
nodes.norm_label: retask channel with nonce per child
nodes.rationale: A fresh nonce per child means a revision is genuine only if quoted directly, which blocks injected instructions in tool results.

nodes.label: evidence_pending recorded-debt marker
nodes.rationale: Because the marker travels with the file across mv and is removed only at the verified commit point, it means exactly that a completed Phase 8 is still owed.

nodes.label: Scheduled maintenance cadence
nodes.rationale: Pure-code scheduling avoids model turns and paid calls while keeping every test VM and the station updated, deferring while workers are live.

nodes.label: Lesson record schema (frontmatter and JSONL forms)
nodes.norm_label: lesson record schema (frontmatter and jsonl forms)
nodes.rationale: Two serializations with identical fields let both markdown artifacts and machine-written streams carry the same provenance.

nodes.label: Session note body structure
nodes.rationale: Fixed h2 sections with _None._ placeholders keep the shape predictable for future-Claude, and the collapsed Raw Conversation callout preserves forensic value without cluttering the page.

nodes.label: Optional crystallizer-only Lessons section
nodes.rationale: Only genuine reusable lessons are recorded, fail-open so a malformed line never blocks session capture, with validity checked out of band.

nodes.label: Luna AI-First Vault Rule mapping
nodes.rationale: Mirrors Luna _CLAUDE.md section 0 (preamble, wikilinks, confidence markers) so session notes let Claude decide relevance in seconds.

nodes.label: N31 watchdog (auto-arm hooks only) to auto-relaunch
nodes.norm_label: n31 watchdog (auto-arm hooks only) to auto-relaunch
nodes.rationale: Deferred and ambiguous because the glossary scopes the rename to auto-arm hooks only and a wall-clock killer is a run timeout, so each hit needs reading.

nodes.label: consolidate apply flow (preflight + re-runnable steps)
nodes.rationale: Identity-checked preflight and idempotent sub-steps let a mid-flow failure be resumed without duplicates or half-changed refs, dirs, and Jira.

nodes.label: Lingering epic detection
nodes.rationale: Re-scoped epics with no closed sub-tasks are flagged regardless of age because they need decomposition, not just a nudge.

nodes.label: Stale tiers (warming/stale/zombie)
nodes.rationale: Graduated age thresholds (30/60/90 days default) escalate attention without treating deliberately parked or done items as stale.

nodes.label: bucket move (time-horizon vs source-repo)
nodes.rationale: Name-based axis dispatch lets one command move items either by horizon or by relocating the directory.

nodes.label: jira-link upgrade flow
nodes.rationale: Adopting any pending intent record first and clearing it only after the final step prevents a crash from losing the nonce and creating a duplicate issue.

nodes.label: Jira create outcomes (success / unknown / skipped)
nodes.rationale: An unknown outcome must never auto-fall back to #N because the remote issue may exist, whereas a skipped create is safe to automate.

nodes.label: Pending-new-item intent record
nodes.rationale: Keying the record on (source-bucket, type, slug) rather than the renamed branch keeps it discoverable on resume and avoids duplicate Jira items.

nodes.label: Provisional branch allocation by attempted creation
nodes.norm_label: provisional branch allocation by attempted creation
nodes.rationale: Letting atomic git branch creation arbitrate avoids a check-then-create race where concurrent runs adopt each other's branch.

nodes.label: Concurrency out of scope (HIMMEL-1132)
nodes.rationale: Preventing concurrent duplicate creates needs cross-process locking, which was excluded by decision and tracked separately as HIMMEL-1132.

nodes.label: Failed create is OUTCOME-UNKNOWN
nodes.rationale: A timeout or non-zero exit can arrive after Jira accepted the request, so falling through to local #N would strand a real remote issue under a different identity.

nodes.label: Intent record store (one file per identity)
nodes.norm_label: intent record store (one file per identity)
nodes.rationale: One file per identity in a directory removes shared mutable state, because read-modify-write of a shared map loses updates; atomic rename alone only prevents torn JSON.

nodes.label: Internal specs live in state repo (HIMMEL-409)
nodes.norm_label: internal specs live in state repo (himmel-409)
nodes.rationale: Internal design/plan/decision artifacts belong in the state repo rather than the code repo's docs/, which is for operator-facing and public reference.

nodes.label: Load-bearing invariant: no live record means nothing outstanding
nodes.norm_label: load-bearing invariant: no live record means nothing outstanding
nodes.rationale: The guarantee follows from durability of the step-2 record, not its ordering, and it concerns outstanding attempts, never whether a remote issue exists.

nodes.label: Per-attempt idempotency nonce (handover-idem-<nonce>)
nodes.rationale: The nonce command is pinned verbatim because an LLM executing prose would improvise differently across sessions, producing mismatched labels and a missed lookup.

nodes.label: Nonce is not a hash of item identity
nodes.norm_label: nonce is not a hash of item identity
nodes.rationale: Labels are permanent, so an identity-keyed marker would make creation idempotent forever and wrongly adopt an old closed ticket for a legitimate later item with the same name.
nodes.source_location: Why the nonce is NOT a hash

nodes.label: Post-create steps must converge on resume
nodes.norm_label: post-create steps must converge on resume
nodes.rationale: Every post-create step is filesystem-observable, so a resume re-derives state by re-running them, which makes a per-step progress journal unnecessary.

nodes.label: Lookup verdict table (PRE-CREATE vs POST-ATTEMPT)
nodes.rationale: Keying on whether a create has been issued, not how the invocation began, stops a timed-out first run from matching the zero-result row and issuing a second create.

nodes.label: Panel exit 7 input-pin mismatch stop
nodes.rationale: Stopping in the block that captured the rc avoids recording a review of inputs already known to be stale.

nodes.label: Docs-audit lane and five-dimension charter
nodes.rationale: A docs-only PR needs a focused factual-accuracy audit plus a real non-Claude responder rather than the full 6-reviewer matrix.

nodes.label: Anchor
nodes.rationale: Gate writers run from the primary checkout's copy so bytes a branch controls never run as the gate.

nodes.label: Relative literal spelling for scripts/cr calls
nodes.norm_label: relative literal spelling for scripts/cr calls
nodes.rationale: Worker allow rules match relative literals, so an absolute path made the classifier nondeterministic and denied external-critic calls.

nodes.label: Panel exit 6 certify refusal
nodes.rationale: If the citation-guard digest cannot be minted the run cannot be certified, so the CR marker stays held for that SHA.

nodes.label: Panel exit 7 input-pin mismatch abort
nodes.rationale: A mismatch means diff, review and ledger stamp would describe different things, so degrading to claude-only would be wrong and the run must abort.

nodes.label: rtk proxy git diff retry
nodes.rationale: Token-proxied git returns a stat summary rather than a unified diff, so the script retries once through rtk proxy to get a real diff.

nodes.label: Impacted suite verdicts (PASS/CI/SKIP/BLOCKED)
nodes.rationale: Decision 775: the station runs little and CI runs the rest, so each suite gets one accounted verdict.

nodes.label: Main red advisory and triage classes
nodes.norm_label: main red advisory and triage classes
nodes.rationale: The merge gate only makes a red main visible (advisory) while the chief triages as test-only, real blocker or complex fix, keeping main-red rare and fixed fast.

nodes.label: auto-approve-safe-bash pre-Bash gateway
nodes.rationale: Claude's native matcher refuses commands with simple expansion and denies silently in headless mode, so a hook that reads the literal command and only ever grants allow is the structural fix.

nodes.label: impacted-suites.sh literal allow exception
nodes.rationale: This required /pr-check gate step was sometimes denied by the classifier as Out-of-Place Publication and parked the worker, so it is granted only when bytes match the anchor's.

nodes.label: queue-lock.sh lock verb allow exception
nodes.rationale: The shape fell through to the auto-mode classifier which wrongly denied release as a merge without review, so a tightly guarded whole-command grant was added.

nodes.label: Impacted suites selection
nodes.rationale: Sweeping the owning directory misses suites in other directories that reference a changed file (PR #2261), so selection follows basename references.

nodes.label: CI-equivalent runner for JS/TS suites
nodes.rationale: A node:test suite can pass under node --test yet fail under a guessed bun test, causing false reds, so the exact CI command is read from ci.yml.

nodes.label: Suite evidence (ready-check item 19)
nodes.rationale: A suite CI runs is run once in CI so workers on the station run only what their PR changed, saving local cost.

nodes.label: Five CI lanes
nodes.rationale: Each lane maps 1:1 to an adapter and a compute source (self-hosted, private GHA, act, public fork, local) so work can spill to whatever capacity is available.

nodes.label: Routing order (route or defer, never skip)
nodes.norm_label: routing order (route or defer, never skip)
nodes.rationale: Deferring applies backpressure so a job stays queued and is never dropped.

nodes.label: Voice transcription via whisper.cpp
nodes.rationale: Local offline multilingual transcription is free and private, and failures reply explicitly rather than silently dropping the voice note.

nodes.label: Whisper model guidance (small vs medium)
nodes.rationale: small garbled mixed Hebrew/English notes, so medium is recommended despite higher CPU cost and timeout risk on long notes.

nodes.label: Luna upgrade engine VM test
nodes.rationale: A deterministic, claude-free roundtrip proves the upgrade engine refreshes owned files and preserves user content.

nodes.label: Skill-pass VM e2e (non-gating)
nodes.rationale: It dogfoods the full /luna-upgrade user path, but being LLM-driven, VM-dependent and billing-consuming it must never block a merge.

nodes.label: Roadmap tracker
nodes.rationale: Gives a static release and kanban view by Jira version built from the Jira mirror.

nodes.label: PR comment attribution callout
nodes.rationale: Comments post under the operator's account, so the callout is the only sign an agent wrote them.

nodes.label: Handover token grammar
nodes.rationale: Quoted tokens trip gitleaks generic-api-key on entropy and stall the vault autosync commit, so every minting site emits one grammar allowlisted by a single anchored rule.

nodes.label: Relay path (1)
nodes.rationale: A relay from the last accepted chief is the stronger proof because the sender identity authenticates the change.

nodes.label: Stranded worker rule
nodes.rationale: A worker with no verifiable successor keeps its sealed scope to READY and declines expansion, so it is neither lost nor hijacked.

nodes.label: Token chain path (2)
nodes.rationale: When the old chief is gone, possession of the outgoing token is the only available evidence, so it is accepted only then and treated as weaker.

nodes.label: Succession verdict table S1-S8
nodes.rationale: A fixed verdict table prevents replayed tokens or tool-result text from redirecting a worker.

nodes.label: Decision: build scripted delivery
nodes.rationale: A scripted delivery is no worse than a Sonnet relay call on fidelity and needs no relay model call, though not proven cheaper end to end.

nodes.label: Path option shifts cost to the receiver
nodes.norm_label: path option shifts cost to the receiver
nodes.rationale: The path option is free for the sender but costs the receiver one extra Read turn, about 8 times a warm Sonnet message, so it is not cheaper end to end.

nodes.label: On-by-default and opt-out procedure
nodes.rationale: Reconcile rewrites the template map verbatim, so a permanent opt-out must also be recorded as a false override in settings.local.json or the next reconcile re-enables the plugin.

nodes.label: Merge precedence: connector under --det, LLM under --llm
nodes.norm_label: merge precedence: connector under --det, llm under --llm
nodes.rationale: The merge engine prefers deterministic sources, so swapping the flags would let note-derived values silently overwrite wearable readings.

nodes.label: Own-client OAuth flow (not the OAuth Playground)
nodes.norm_label: own-client oauth flow (not the oauth playground)
nodes.rationale: The Playground mints tokens under Google's own client ID and restricted Health scopes reject them with unauthorized_client.

nodes.label: PHI privacy and secret handling
nodes.rationale: Vitals are personal health information, so tokens stay in the gitignored .env and artifacts must not reach public repos or uncontrolled cloud sync.

nodes.label: Review artifact then merge and write (no auto-write to 50-Vitals)
nodes.norm_label: review artifact then merge and write (no auto-write to 50-vitals)
nodes.rationale: Health data is PHI, so the connector writes a reviewable JSON artifact and landing it in 50-Vitals stays a manual step.

nodes.label: Deterministic values win over LLM on overlap
nodes.norm_label: deterministic values win over llm on overlap
nodes.rationale: Structured parses are more reliable than LLM prose extraction so merge routes them to a pool that takes precedence.

nodes.label: Alpha status and re-consent exit 75
nodes.rationale: Testing-mode OAuth refresh tokens expire in about 7 days, so exit 75 raises a re-consent reminder.

nodes.label: sleep.json edge-case fixture
nodes.rationale: A main night, a nap and a cross-midnight session test main-session selection and local end-date attribution.

nodes.label: Date extraction by category (daily/sample/interval)
nodes.rationale: Each data category stores its civil date at a different path, and sleep may lack civilEndTime, so a fallback from endTime plus endUtcOffset is needed.

nodes.label: Degraded sleep stage data handling
nodes.rationale: Unparseable stage timestamps would make the remaining valid stages under-count sleep, so sleep_hours is omitted while in-bed hours (from the session interval) still emit.

nodes.label: Durable artifact warnings field
nodes.rationale: Stderr warnings are lost, so recording them additively in the artifact keeps clean pulls byte-identical while preserving derivation-time loss; warning text embeds the dataPoint index so merge's exact-text dedup means the same event.

nodes.label: Categorical/no-data/rollup-only types excluded from series
nodes.rationale: Config enums, bulky waveforms, food definitions and multi-nutrient arrays are not simple vitals, and some types have no data or list 400s.

nodes.label: writeSeries overlay and merge-warning limitations
nodes.rationale: Overlay-only writes are intentional, so metrics absent from artifact rows are never rewritten and the operator must repair stale series manually.

nodes.label: Per-type mapping table (dataTypeId to field, unit, aggregate)
nodes.norm_label: per-type mapping table (datatypeid to field, unit, aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Multiple same-day points must collapse to one series value, and many numeric values arrive as JSON strings that need coercion.

nodes.label: Derived rhr_bpm from heart-rate samples
nodes.rationale: The Fitbit daily resting-HR aggregate stopped in 2024-09, so a 5th-percentile estimate from the live Samsung HR feed substitutes for it.

nodes.label: Sleep metric migration note
nodes.rationale: sleep_hours used to mean time-in-bed, and because writeSeries only overlays emitted rows, old CSV values are not auto-reconciled and need a one-time repair.

nodes.label: luna-vitals connectors README
nodes.rationale: Describes the opt-in, inert-until-configured Google Health connector so operators know layout, status and setup.

nodes.label: 50-Vitals/_series.md registry
nodes.rationale: It defines each metric's scale so qualitative notes map to numeric values consistently.

nodes.label: /fanout
nodes.rationale: Routes work items to the lane the invariant routing policy requires and refuses invalid plans so destructive work is never routed below judgement.

nodes.label: /minerva
nodes.rationale: Single front door running grill-to-plan in one pass with adversarial critic loops, hardening an idea into an implementation plan.

nodes.label: Destructive items must be judgement/Fable
nodes.rationale: Judgement work with an unrecoverable failure mode must not be downgraded to a cheaper tier.

nodes.label: Fanout work-type to lane routing table
nodes.norm_label: fanout work-type to lane routing table
nodes.rationale: Restates the CLAUDE.md Subagent policy so the validator has something to check against.

nodes.label: /fanout command
nodes.rationale: Fan-out was a habit; a destructive worktree cleanup once went to Sonnet, so lane selection must be a lookup.

nodes.label: Sealed half of routing cases
nodes.rationale: Sealed results appear only as aggregates because a per-case pick or outcome would hint at what the case expects.

nodes.label: Open and sealed seed split
nodes.rationale: Tuning reads only the open half while the sealed half grades the keep rule, so train-up with test-flat gets reverted instead of overfitting.

nodes.label: Job environment is an allowlist, not denylist
nodes.norm_label: job environment is an allowlist, not denylist
nodes.rationale: The worker outlives its starting session and a name-pattern denylist misses unguessable credential names like GGS_MQTT_PASS, so only named variables cross to another session's job.

nodes.label: Per-(hook,session) dedup and nothing-dropped-silently
nodes.rationale: A re-fired session's newest payload supersedes its stale one while every expiry, abandon or corrupt removal logs a row so no work vanishes silently.

nodes.label: Controlling the VM CI runner
nodes.rationale: One script with pre-approved literal forms lets the chief switch the VM runners on and off, with an off kill switch, because routed shards fail until the guest image is rebaked.

nodes.label: Symptom: vm-runner.sh on|off|status denied
nodes.rationale: Only exact literals are pre-approved, so a denial means the typed text differs and widening the rule or bypassing the script is forbidden.

nodes.label: Plugin-bump recheck (version above base)
nodes.rationale: Requiring a strictly higher plugin version lets himmel-update refresh version-keyed caches so two contents never ship under one version.

nodes.label: Fail closed: config error is not none
nodes.norm_label: fail closed: config error is not none
nodes.rationale: An invalid config must not offer the operator-ack route, so its only route is fix the config and nothing releases a hold on a guess.

nodes.label: Adopter profile limits: lanes probed, hardening printed
nodes.norm_label: adopter profile limits: lanes probed, hardening printed
nodes.rationale: Installing CLIs or running machine-wide hardening would mean the installer asserting something it cannot stand behind, so it reports lanes honestly and prints a checklist.

nodes.label: Non-interactive adopter profile install
nodes.rationale: --default-scope only presets a wizard answer, so skipping the wizard needs a shipped placeholder-free profile.

nodes.label: What parity_guard.py enforces under hermes
nodes.rationale: CC PreToolUse hooks do not load under hermes, so parity_guard is the sole fence and its coverage per deny-guard must be stated.

nodes.label: Amend cutover and same-uid ceiling
nodes.rationale: Rows before the first signed amend are honoured unsigned so in-flight work is not re-blocked, and the same-uid signer ceiling means the check stops forged lines but not the sanctioned path.

nodes.label: CR ledger amends: only a signed adjudication lowers a finding
nodes.norm_label: cr ledger amends: only a signed adjudication lowers a finding
nodes.rationale: The ledger is append-only JSONL, so any appended line could mark a Critical finding disproved; an HMAC under the GO key makes only the sanctioned writer's lowering amends count.

nodes.label: Sample → judge → apply → gate flow
nodes.rationale: Deterministic seeded sampling, stage-then-commit writes and a binary precision exit code make the audit reproducible and safe to wire into a gate.

nodes.label: Refuted/stale lessons are superseded, never edited
nodes.norm_label: refuted/stale lessons are superseded, never edited
nodes.rationale: Supersession as the only edit preserves the audit block as a historical record of why a lesson was retired.

nodes.label: Health page (#/health)
nodes.rationale: Answers whether the project is working right now from three independent sources so one missing source never blanks the page.

nodes.label: Project picker and Shared scope
nodes.rationale: Rows judging the machine or himmel itself are counted once under Shared so they do not inflate each project's own verdict.

nodes.label: Health verdict rule (Act now / Needs a look / All clear)
nodes.norm_label: health verdict rule (act now / needs a look / all clear)
nodes.rationale: A simple fail/warn/alert mapping gives one unambiguous verdict word.

nodes.label: Weekly roll-up trends
nodes.rationale: The server serves a precomputed roll-up read-only so the browser recomputes nothing.

nodes.label: /himmel-report command
nodes.rationale: Turns a wrong refusal or review point into a redacted issue draft and a local lesson, sending nothing without an explicit yes.

nodes.label: block-docker-privesc.sh root-equivalent container guard
nodes.rationale: Docker group membership is root-equivalent and lets an agent bind-mount host paths writable, bypassing file permissions, block-read-secrets and block-edit-on-main.

nodes.label: block-unresolved-cr-merge.sh CodeRabbit merge-remark gate
nodes.rationale: It structurally enforces the operator's rule never to merge over unresolved CodeRabbit remarks (structural over instructional), using positive evidence only.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit availability arming per repo
nodes.rationale: A repo without the App has no status on any head so an armed gate would block forever; a non-versioned local git config cannot be inherited by forks or deleted by a PR.

nodes.label: Machine-generated PR class (dependabot, graph-publish)
nodes.rationale: Some PRs never receive an App review so absent was their steady state and blocked them forever; the classifier was later deleted once best effort made silence tolerated everywhere.

nodes.label: Review freshness (B2) retired
nodes.rationale: CodeRabbit is best effort, so a stale review anchor is now just a NOTE like an absent review, and what the head owes is zero unresolved threads plus the exact-head critic panel.

nodes.label: Chief context defaults (1m, autocompact auto)
nodes.rationale: Chiefs are exempt from the standard worker context default because a long-running coordinator benefits from the 1M context, with an opt-down via --context standard.

nodes.label: Collision-check and single-writer fan-out rules
nodes.rationale: Disjoint file sets and exactly one writer per artifact prevent parallel workers from clobbering each other, and an explicit model avoids drawing on the scarcer parent quota.

nodes.label: Launch line env -u prefix
nodes.rationale: The prefix clears inherited CLAUDE_* variables so the chief does not answer to its launcher's name or lose its transcript and context-fill reading.

nodes.label: Worker tabs (HIMMEL_WORKER_SESSION_TABS)
nodes.rationale: Opening workers as tabs in one Konsole window per chief reduces window clutter while a crashed worker kills only its own tab.

nodes.label: Plain launch reports 1M window; --autocompact moves compaction only
nodes.norm_label: plain launch reports 1m window; --autocompact moves compaction only
nodes.rationale: Measurement showed removing the [1m] suffix leaves a 1M window on this account, so only --autocompact actually changes the cost driver.

nodes.label: Worker launcher pins standard context (--autocompact 200000)
nodes.rationale: The pin was moved from prose convention into a structural wrapper so ad-hoc launcher copies cannot weaken the worker ceiling.

nodes.label: Token boundary ownership policy
nodes.rationale: Optimizers compose only when each targets a different boundary, and token burn is a vanity metric so outcomes are measured instead.

nodes.label: Prompt-cache responder path
nodes.rationale: Single-day dips after idle sessions are false positives, so action triggers only on read-ratio materially below baseline for 3+ days.

nodes.label: Downgrade-safety sampling rule
nodes.rationale: Reviewing every output of a cheap batch erases the savings, so validation is sampled with escalation to the frontier lane on failure.

nodes.label: Token-economy invariants (one owner, license gate, measurement gate)
nodes.norm_label: token-economy invariants (one owner, license gate, measurement gate)
nodes.rationale: Prevents conflicting optimizers, rejects non-OSI licenses on the public MIT path, and requires measured real-session deltas rather than vendor percentages.

nodes.label: RTK (dev command output owner)
nodes.rationale: Kept the dev-output boundary on 2026-07-02 because it is Apache-2.0 and a challenger needs an OSI license plus a measured win.

nodes.label: Design-kit plugins (design / design-motion / design-reference profiles)
nodes.rationale: Design plugins are on-demand and profile-scoped because measured usage was too low to justify riding the ALWAYS tier.

nodes.label: Two-tier plugin profile (ALWAYS / ON-DEMAND)
nodes.rationale: Separating availability from activation keeps default sessions lean while cached plugins remain opt-in per profile.

nodes.label: mattpocock/skills domain-modeling
nodes.rationale: Keeps coined terms landing once in docs/glossary.md under the plain name; adopted after a pre-fixed n=1 pass bar where the skill beat baseline on one check and lost none.

nodes.label: lean-skills plugin
nodes.rationale: Gives plans, debugging and review one written workflow; usage eval found zero organic invocations so a TRIM of two uncalled skills saves tokens.

nodes.label: writing-for-agents (mattpocock/skills)
nodes.rationale: Keeps steering files short by proposing cuts read-only, run on demand to avoid listing cost.

nodes.label: minerva pipeline (/minerva)
nodes.rationale: An adversarial critic between each stage red-teams every artifact before it advances from idea to plan.
