nodes.label: minerva Skill-tool PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: Closes the no-/minerva bypass so the critic loop still fires without forking the upstream plugin; kept advisory and fail-open so it never blocks a Skill call.

nodes.label: Repo map (WORKER_SESSION_REPO_MAP, off by default)
nodes.rationale: It stays off because the K7 A/B showed no gain: 15/15 answers found with and without it at the same token cost.

nodes.label: Hook-chain smoke demo
nodes.rationale: Hook breakage is silent and fail-open, so an end-to-end proof in a throwaway clone is needed after any hook or runner change.

nodes.label: Test running guidance
nodes.rationale: Suites resolve helpers relative to cwd and fail under ambient load, so run from repo root and compare against main before blaming the branch.

nodes.label: Exit-code-swallowing pipeline deny
nodes.rationale: Piping a gate into tail makes $? tail's status; an orchestrator recorded CLEAR_RC=0 when the gate had exited 16 and wrongly believed the CR gate cleared.

nodes.label: himmelctl update drift pass
nodes.rationale: The drift pass prints the skills collection as NOT auto-fixed and moves on, so it should run the install ensure step or name the exact remedy command.

nodes.label: Uninstall / offboard
nodes.rationale: Teardown is destructive, so it is fail-closed and a provenance ledger keeps the user's own pre-existing state rather than guessing ownership.

nodes.label: Install-provenance round trip
nodes.rationale: It checks that uninstall removes exactly what install brought, tagging too-much and too-little directions.

nodes.label: --unattended policy gate
nodes.rationale: It refuses any entry not marked upgrade.unattended in the registry so the operator's decision is never silently overruled.

nodes.label: apply-tool-upgrade
nodes.rationale: It re-probes and requires the version to strictly advance so a command that exits 0 without upgrading is not mistaken for success, and unattended mode is gated per entry.

nodes.label: Path-scoped PR-lane gate with exclude list
nodes.norm_label: path-scoped pr-lane gate with exclude list
nodes.rationale: Blocking only matched files on main lets plugin-lane vault-content commits keep flowing, and the exclude keeps Obsidian auto-written files from wedging the gate.

nodes.label: Alibaba scoped monitoring key bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Deriving a scoped read-only key means polling scripts never hold account-level credentials.

nodes.label: Service mode
nodes.rationale: Running under systemd needs a persistent token file and no idle-out, with a refused symlink or non-600 file to protect the token.

nodes.label: digest= line on close
nodes.rationale: Closing a worker digests its session into failure-loop ledgers and prints one informational line that never changes the close's exit code.

nodes.label: One-line forms for operator commands
nodes.rationale: Operators receive a single literal line, never a chain or VAR= prefix, so commands match allow rules and no gate is skipped.

nodes.label: Waiter wraps workers
nodes.rationale: The waiter runs worker-event.sh on each WRAPPED/MERGED worker itself, so the chief is woken only when automation could not finish.

nodes.label: gen-briefs honours lane for model and effort
nodes.norm_label: gen-briefs honours lane for model and effort
nodes.rationale: HIMMEL-6063 added --lane but left model default and brief header native-only; operator says this should have been supported already, and decision 17 wants claudex legs at LEG_EFFORT high.

nodes.label: Choose your update route
nodes.rationale: The right commands depend on how himmel reached the machine (git, release channel, tarball, package) and on install scope.

nodes.label: Unquoted $ARGUMENTS convention
nodes.rationale: Quoting would collapse the argument list into one token and break flag parsing like 'both --dry-run'.

nodes.label: gh-pr-comments skill
nodes.rationale: Auto-triggers on review-thread intent for a PR and directs to normal.log for prefixes feeding reply/resolve.

nodes.label: gh-pr-reply skill
nodes.rationale: Requires /gh-pr-comments first so the prefix cache is populated.

nodes.label: gh-pr-resolve skill
nodes.rationale: Resolves a single thread by prefix and not the whole PR.

nodes.label: Forks registry credits
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the fork adapter registry and its roles so dormant and contribution-only forks are distinguished from runtime dependencies without inventing pins.

nodes.label: Inspired-by and borrowed passages
nodes.rationale: Separates vendored copies from himmel-authored text derived from ideas, and marks 'Not established' licences as granting no copy permission.

nodes.label: Plugins and skill families credits
nodes.rationale: One row per marketplace manifest entry credits the bundled skill family without claiming every skill is enabled.

nodes.label: Credits generation and check
nodes.rationale: Generating from checked-in sources and failing on missing rows or changed pins keeps the attribution index from drifting.

nodes.label: Credits metadata supplement
nodes.rationale: Supplies attribution fields the manifest and fork adapter registry do not carry, without becoming a second inventory, so credits.md can be generated.

nodes.label: Credits passages table (inspired-by / vendored attributions)
nodes.rationale: implied: credit upstream authors for ideas and vendored files used in specific himmel skills, commands and hooks.

nodes.label: Vendored plugin: domain-modeling (MIT, Matt Pocock)
nodes.rationale: Vendored from mattpocock/skills at a pinned commit, so its MIT text must be reproduced for attribution.

nodes.label: Vendored plugin: humanizer (MIT, Siqi Chen)
nodes.rationale: Vendored from blader/humanizer at a pinned commit, so its MIT text must be reproduced for attribution.

nodes.label: left-pad / WTFPL note
nodes.rationale: WTFPL is not a named compatible class but left-pad is only a never-installed, never-shipped T6 benchmark fixture, so it is called out and needs no action.

nodes.label: Methodology: locked versions from lockfiles
nodes.rationale: Lockfile versions are what a clean npm ci or bun install installs, whereas registry snapshots and local node_modules were found stale or drifted.

nodes.label: pele docs-site bundle (MIT, kepano)
nodes.rationale: Its code is bundled into the deployed site, so the MIT license text (and Lucide ISC notice) must be reproduced.

nodes.label: Vendored plugin: pstack (MIT, Lauren Tan)
nodes.rationale: Vendoring from cursor/plugins at a pinned commit (never the fork) requires reproducing the MIT license and recording pin and deviations in VENDORED.md.

nodes.label: Audit scope: direct dependencies only
nodes.rationale: The ticket's measured surface was direct deps, leaving the transitive tree unaudited, which is a real gap since a permissive direct dependency can pull in a copyleft transitive.

nodes.label: sharp prebuilt binaries (LGPL-3.0-or-later, accepted)
nodes.rationale: himmel neither modifies nor distributes the binaries and nothing lands in site/dist, so LGPL obligations are not triggered and a lockfile override is not worth it.

nodes.label: Vendored skill: technical-writing (MIT, Lauren Tan)
nodes.rationale: It shares pstack/LICENSE at the same pin as unslop, so the license is cited rather than repeated.

nodes.label: Vendored skill: unslop (MIT, Lauren Tan)
nodes.rationale: The MIT attribution requirement means the license text is reproduced for the vendored file.

nodes.label: Coexist with unslop, do not merge
nodes.norm_label: coexist with unslop, do not merge
nodes.rationale: Merging would break byte-identical vendoring and replacing unslop would lose rules 26 to 33.

nodes.label: Humanizer pilot verdict: ADOPT, opt-in
nodes.rationale: 46 pages showed 979 kept changes and em-dashes 1563 to 325, so the REJECT condition was not met and chief ruling closed the pilot early.

nodes.label: blast-radius POC and A/B result
nodes.rationale: It is the only skill with a defined slot, measurable outcome and cheap opt-in switch; the A/B caught 1 of 3 later defects and proved other real ones.

nodes.label: Formal verification boundary
nodes.rationale: All ten skills stay opt-in and off in worker profiles so no autonomous behavior is adopted without evidence.

nodes.label: Layer taxonomy A/B/C/D
nodes.rationale: Composing across layers is additive while competing within a layer is substitutive.

nodes.label: Registry status labels
nodes.rationale: Map rubric decision states to registry labels and add parked-idea and provisional for items outside the rubric states.

nodes.label: Enforcement strength — structural over instructional
nodes.rationale: Prose does not enforce; escalating on the second drift avoids waiting until the rule has lost authority and Claude rationalises bypasses.

nodes.label: Four converging rules (short, nested, state-not-prompt, first dollar)
nodes.norm_label: four converging rules (short, nested, state-not-prompt, first dollar)
nodes.rationale: Long always-loaded files get skimmed and ignored, eroding the authority of every rule in them.

nodes.label: Layer selection — lean-invoke vs default
nodes.rationale: Default-everything makes the root file grow until operator and Claude stop reading it, so lean-invoke keeps cost on the operator who knows when a rule applies.

nodes.label: Layering model (cheapest layer that still fires)
nodes.norm_label: layering model (cheapest layer that still fires)
nodes.rationale: The always-loaded root is the most expensive layer, so content goes to the cheapest layer that still fires when needed.

nodes.label: Memory as a map, not a backend
nodes.norm_label: memory as a map, not a backend
nodes.rationale: The index must stay one line per fact because an index that becomes the store defeats the lean-surface goal; directives must stay resident since nobody queries for a rule they do not know they violate.

nodes.label: The nesting trap
nodes.rationale: A subtree CLAUDE.md loads only inside that subtree, so cross-cutting operational rules placed there stop firing elsewhere.

nodes.label: Rule tags — [enforced: name] vs [prose]
nodes.rationale: Tagging each rule makes the [prose] rules a visible escalation backlog for the next drift.

nodes.label: No operational when-stuck rules in CLAUDE.md
nodes.norm_label: no operational when-stuck rules in claude.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is prunable under context pressure and may be gone exactly when stuck guidance is needed.

nodes.label: claudex effort ladder (default xhigh, decision 223)
nodes.rationale: The xhigh default spends codex usage budget on every worker, so mechanical chunks should step down to low explicitly per dispatch.

nodes.label: Ruling: effort-at-dispatch shipped on both paths
nodes.norm_label: ruling: effort-at-dispatch shipped on both paths
nodes.rationale: Re-verifying on main showed both Telegram and native-worker dispatch apply the lanes.json effort, closing the question as answered with no uncovered lane class.

nodes.label: Effort calibration
nodes.rationale: Effort names mean different thinking amounts across models, so Opus 5.5 moved to medium to avoid longer, costlier turns with no measured gain.

nodes.label: External Claude Code bounded worker (Telegram run.ts)
nodes.norm_label: external claude code bounded worker (telegram run.ts)
nodes.rationale: It is the concrete external Claude worker path read for the audit, so it stands in for the Claude row until another dispatcher is found.

nodes.label: Gap: no CLI actuator for pure-Claude bounded worker
nodes.norm_label: gap: no cli actuator for pure-claude bounded worker
nodes.rationale: run.ts exports runSession as a library with no CLI entry, so a hermes parent has nothing to call to spawn a Claude-lane worker.

nodes.label: Claude model pin for bounded runs
nodes.norm_label: claude model pin for bounded runs
nodes.rationale: Explicit model pinning stops bounded runs from inheriting the operator's default model whose time-limited quota is reserved for interactive work.

nodes.label: Group runs framed as untrusted third-party input
nodes.norm_label: group runs framed as untrusted third-party input
nodes.rationale: Group members are not the operator, so the prompt omits Jira sanction and forbids ticket changes or command execution; it is prompt framing, not a sandbox.

nodes.label: Prompt contract (inbox/outbox/context/no self-poll)
nodes.rationale: The poller owns Telegram delivery and polling, so the bounded run only reads files, appends replies and notes, and exits.

nodes.label: defaultVault blast radius
nodes.rationale: defaultVault applies vault cwd plus bypassPermissions to every unconfigured chat, so containment relies on that vault's own hooks and it should be set only for a trusted vault.

nodes.label: Group sessions are untrusted
nodes.rationale: Group sessions mix messages from every member, so they are framed as untrusted third-party input and omit Jira and command powers; a missing operator marker fails safe.

nodes.label: Jira sanction clause
nodes.rationale: The auto-mode classifier vetoes Jira writes when the workflow omits Jira, so the clause states ticket work is in scope, limited to non-destructive ops.

nodes.label: Per-chat session cwd and bypassPermissions
nodes.rationale: Spawning in the vault cwd loads the vault's own hooks (e.g. PHI-egress floor), and bypassPermissions avoids deadlock on unanswerable prompts since the himmel auto-approve hook isn't loaded.

nodes.label: Attachment to vault routing
nodes.rationale: Attachments sent to a vault-configured chat should be filed into the vault per its conventions rather than merely read.

nodes.label: Telegram Bridge README
nodes.rationale: Gives the operator and LLM sessions one guide to running, securing and configuring the bun Telegram bridge safely.

nodes.label: Cadence ledger and flow-run ledger
nodes.rationale: The ledger is the report, so a run that cannot record itself must never read as a quiet success, and the flow-run row keeps existing audit tooling from being blind to this step.

nodes.label: Tool-call decision funnel
nodes.rationale: Every tool call passes hooks, deny list, allow list, then mode so vetoes take precedence over allows; hook bypass env vars must be set in the launching shell.

nodes.label: Jira write-shape bounce (single sanctioned retry shape)
nodes.norm_label: jira write-shape bounce (single sanctioned retry shape)
nodes.rationale: Approval depends on command shape, so by the structural-over-instructional rule a deterministic bounce naming one retry shape replaces the opaque classifier denial and avoids tool-shopping across shapes.

nodes.label: Only provably unconditional writes are in scope for the Jira bounce
nodes.norm_label: only provably unconditional writes are in scope for the jira bounce
nodes.rationale: The retry guidance is unconditional, so it must never be handed to a command that might not write; every gap forfeits guidance only and never wrongly blocks.

nodes.label: Linux station (CachyOS) notes: plugins, arm-resume, Jira CLI, station traps
nodes.norm_label: linux station (cachyos) notes: plugins, arm-resume, jira cli, station traps
nodes.rationale: These lessons came from running himmel as the daily driver on an Arch-family station rather than from a fresh install.

nodes.label: Shadow verdict deterministic rule engine (allow/deny/abstain)
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot call a model, and re-implementing the production gate would drift so the ledger would end up measuring the drift.

nodes.label: Densify existing subject instead of duplicating
nodes.norm_label: densify existing subject instead of duplicating
nodes.rationale: Bounded normalised-name and alias matching appends evidence to existing subjects, avoiding duplicate pages without open-ended similarity guesses (LUNA-88).

nodes.label: Generation ledger and divergence guard
nodes.rationale: Reverting only byte-identical pages (by sha256) prevents deleting stubs the operator has since edited.

nodes.label: Anti-sprawl stub trigger
nodes.rationale: Requiring two canonical-URL-deduped contributors spanning two domains or authors means one article clipped twice yields no stub.

nodes.label: CR critic routes and proven invocation
nodes.norm_label: cr critic routes and proven invocation
nodes.rationale: Route selection from --implementer ensures the reviewer is a different model family than the author, and exits 2 rather than return a verdict that only looks cross-family.

nodes.label: Audit of headless call sites
nodes.rationale: The audit verifies each call site's mode fits its job shape, finding no misfits.

nodes.label: claude --bg mode
nodes.rationale: Long-lived workers needing SendMessage inbox and fleet visibility need a session, but the daemon env differs so settings must be compensated and launch confirmed.

nodes.label: claude -p mode
nodes.rationale: One-shot scripted calls exit on completion, leaving nothing to confirm or clean up, and routing through one chokepoint wrapper gives a single audit site.

nodes.label: Headed (konsole) mode
nodes.rationale: It is the only shape where a missing TTY is not a failure because a human is attached.

nodes.label: Lane seam: HIMMEL_CLAUDE_LANE
nodes.rationale: Launchers are not egress gates from scratch cwds, so each site classifies the reviewed repo and refuses non-native lanes unless the egress matrix allows it.

nodes.label: Run fixtures under a group deadline rule
nodes.norm_label: run fixtures under a group deadline rule
nodes.rationale: subprocess.run(timeout=) killed only the direct child and looping subshells ran for ~3h45m at 99.5% CPU.

nodes.label: Caching recommendation for graph pass
nodes.rationale: Measured cache-write versus cache-read tokens show the graph pass shares a long prefix, so batch plus 1-hour cached system block is cheapest.

nodes.label: API lane failure path
nodes.rationale: A failed call alerts once per hour and may rerun on the subscription, but never after a tool-granted call that may have half-done edits.

nodes.label: HIMMEL_API_FALLBACK switch
nodes.rationale: Lets a caller that must never spend the subscription turn the fallback off while still alerting.

nodes.label: Role map (roles.json)
nodes.rationale: Restricts which accounts auto routing may use per kind, so a broken map only removes widening and never refuses what the default allows.

nodes.label: Advisory repo security scan (HIMMEL-5816)
nodes.rationale: Advisory-only scanning via gh api, with no clone or execution, surfaces risks without gating anything.

nodes.label: Advisory-only scan contract (repo_scan field)
nodes.rationale: A scan that could not run or read every file is never written as clean, and trust_tier, safety_flag and the Phase 1.5 outcome are left unchanged so the scan cannot gate.

nodes.label: Three-stage follow-list scoring pipeline
nodes.rationale: Bounding the only non-deterministic step to the manual judge pass keeps evidence gathering and tier math deterministic and reproducible.

nodes.label: Deferred GitHub visibility flip
nodes.rationale: Making the repo public needs the owner's explicit go-ahead; choosing a license does not make it public.

nodes.label: MIT license decision
nodes.rationale: MIT is the most permissive widely recognised OSI license with attribution-only obligations, keeping adoption friction low for a harness meant to be copied.

nodes.label: Verify-before-critical rule
nodes.rationale: Hallucinated Critical findings (a fabricated >: typo, a nonexistent variable substitution) derail overnight fix batches, so Criticals must be grepped verbatim in the diff.

nodes.label: npm production dependency license allowlist
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are not redistributed, so an allowlist of permissive MIT-compatible licenses is enforced on every push to keep the shipping tree free of GPL/AGPL/LGPL/SSPL or unknown licenses.

nodes.label: C1-guardrail check
nodes.rationale: A baked node path that becomes unresolvable makes every tool call error and the guardrails fail OPEN.

nodes.label: C41-mcp-argv-key check
nodes.rationale: A key on the command line is readable by any local user via ps or /proc cmdline.

nodes.label: Silent vec-query hang detection (C40-qmd-vec)
nodes.rationale: A hung vector query is only seen as a client timeout and silently degrades to keyword-only search, so himmel probes it with a bounded vec query.

nodes.label: /himmel-doctor command
nodes.rationale: Surfaces field problems such as node-not-found guardrail hooks that otherwise fail open silently.

nodes.label: N44 fleet manifest key legs to workers
nodes.norm_label: n44 fleet manifest key legs to workers
nodes.rationale: The reader falls back to the old key while legacy names are on, and the removal rewrites the marked line to read m.workers only.

nodes.label: GET /api/agui/<run> SSE stream
nodes.rationale: The journal path must stay under its root's projects directory so symlinks cannot leak files outside the root.

nodes.label: Fleet view and cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: One row per live session with attention sections lets the operator see what needs them or the chief.

nodes.label: Journal roots and registerConfigRoot
nodes.rationale: Custom roots come only from the live census, never a request parameter, so a caller cannot make the server read arbitrary directories.

nodes.label: Agent run view (AG-UI)
nodes.rationale: Rendering an agent run as streamed AG-UI events shows who did what and where it failed.

nodes.label: Fail-closed on missing jq or bad payload
nodes.norm_label: fail-closed on missing jq or bad payload
nodes.rationale: implied: a guard that silently allows calls when its dependency is missing would give false safety, so it denies instead.

nodes.label: Observability-registry smoke-test trap
nodes.rationale: The registry path is scoped only by HIMMEL_OBSERVABILITY_CONFIG, so an unscoped smoke test registers a real expected task and pages on a scheduled-task-missing alert.

nodes.label: Compact tick line
nodes.rationale: Omitting healthy/default fields keeps the line short while absence still means the healthy default and unknown values stay visible.

nodes.label: Worker cost budget
nodes.rationale: Soft and hard cost limits scaled to new per-model prices cap runaway worker spend.

nodes.label: Per-worker lock status states (FRESH, STALE, WRAPPED, NOLIVE, FORKED, FREE, UNVERIFIED, NOTFOUND)
nodes.norm_label: per-worker lock status states (fresh, stale, wrapped, nolive, forked, free, unverified, notfound)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing these states prevents the chief from wrongly reclaiming a lock or mistaking a typo'd path for a released lock.

nodes.label: Tick-driven version drift repair
nodes.rationale: The tick repairs drift itself and only surfaces the held batch to avoid alert noise.

nodes.label: NOLIVE and FORKED worker states
nodes.rationale: A worker that never took its lock reads FREE forever and never wakes the waiter, so NOLIVE and FORKED surface it for message-or-relaunch action.

nodes.label: Red orphan is owed a worker (dispatch-owed)
nodes.norm_label: red orphan is owed a worker (dispatch-owed)
nodes.rationale: An open non-draft PR with failing checks and no live worker would otherwise stall, so a resume worker is launched to triage it.

nodes.label: Conversation alias match
nodes.rationale: implied: aliases and keywords let cross-cutting requests route to a repo when the cwd does not match.

nodes.label: CWD match via git-common-dir
nodes.rationale: --path-format=absolute is required because a plain checkout returns a relative .git, whose parent is not the repo root and silently breaks registry comparison.

nodes.label: Prompt fallback (never cached)
nodes.rationale: Cheap prompts beat sticky misroutes, so the choice is never cached and a repo is never silently picked.

nodes.label: Target repo resolution chain
nodes.rationale: No session cache is kept because routing errors are silent and expensive while a cheap re-resolve costs one git command and one JSON read.

nodes.label: Hermes dispatch immutable snapshot and audit ledger
nodes.norm_label: hermes dispatch immutable snapshot and audit ledger
nodes.rationale: Dispatching a private snapshot instead of the gated path prevents a swap or symlink retarget after the copy from changing what hermes reads.

nodes.label: Impostor
nodes.rationale: implied: a hook call not in the wirer's inventory could be an unreviewed enforcement change, so it is refused.

nodes.label: Wirer / inventory
nodes.rationale: Hand-kept ordered inventories make a wirer install missing entries and let unlisted hook calls be refused as impostors.

nodes.label: Text layer for detached and non-Linux launches
nodes.norm_label: text layer for detached and non-linux launches
nodes.rationale: The in-session seam guard only sees calls under a claude ancestor on Linux, so setsid, at, cron, systemd-run and non-Linux hosts need a parse-free deny-leaning scan of the raw command.

nodes.label: Subtitles-first transcripts (HIMMEL-4107)
nodes.rationale: Platform subtitles need no cookies and are cheaper than local whisper, so they are used first when coverage is sufficient.

nodes.label: X/Twitter media rung: /x-media-enrich (HIMMEL-1226)
nodes.rationale: X media is referenced by URL and never downloaded, so tweets whose substance is the media leave nothing searchable; this rung captures it.

nodes.label: GAP destr-clean-fd (open)
nodes.rationale: The guard regex needs f to end the flag word, so git clean -fd deleting untracked work slips through.

nodes.label: GAP secret-env-dump (fixed)
nodes.rationale: Hermes inherits the launching shell's environment, so an env dump would leak every token and HIMMEL_* variable.

nodes.label: GAP rows: Claude Code denies, hermes allows
nodes.norm_label: gap rows: claude code denies, hermes allows
nodes.rationale: The guard is a hand port, so ranked gaps show where hermes diverges and which to fix first by severity.

nodes.label: Dispatch coverage (matcher .*)
nodes.rationale: A hand-listed matcher left registry tools unjudged because hermes fullmatches pre_tool_call, so the matcher became .* with every tool classified and unclassified tools refused.

nodes.label: PHI / data-egress fence
nodes.rationale: Protects PHI paths on every engine of the cloud profile and is an extra fence beyond the six deny-guards, so not a parity GAP.

nodes.label: Native child guard parity (red-path probe)
nodes.rationale: A red-path probe showed a denied curl never reached a live listener, proving the network-CLI fence applies to delegate_task children.

nodes.label: hermes-agent (Nous) CR-critic + alpha main tier
nodes.rationale: Provides a cross-family reviewer in /pr-check and an alpha main tier on Codex without burning Max quota; prompts leave the machine, so a fail-closed local guard mitigates risk.

nodes.label: gh-init skill
nodes.rationale: Triggers on auth setup intent and defers to the slash command because the login flow is interactive.

nodes.label: Tests that can actually fail (unchecked setup shapes)
nodes.norm_label: tests that can actually fail (unchecked setup shapes)
nodes.rationale: 11% of agreed review findings were setup-fails-silently defects, mostly unguarded mktemp captures, so shape (a) was made a structural gate while (b) and (c) need reviewer judgment.

nodes.label: Symptom: outward-facing command denied with Stage 2 classifier error
nodes.norm_label: symptom: outward-facing command denied with stage 2 classifier error
nodes.rationale: An immediate identical retry is itself a signal the classifier weighs and can escalate, so exactly one delayed retry is allowed.

nodes.label: worker-pr-open
nodes.rationale: Ruling H2: the worker's command is always a fixed two-file-path literal so PR body text never reaches the auto-mode classifier.

nodes.label: Session-name suffix contract
nodes.rationale: Tooling reads roles back from session names, so renaming a suffix silently misclassifies burn data.

nodes.label: Autocompact A/B arm (200000 vs 400000)
nodes.rationale: A measured comparison against 400000 is opt-in and audited so the ceiling choice rests on evidence, and the arm is the manifest record only.

nodes.label: What counts as CI evidence
nodes.rationale: The Mergeable check lints only commit and title, and several common readings mislead, so only shell-unit and real statusCheckRollup count as evidence.

nodes.label: Superseded runs under a runner backlog
nodes.norm_label: superseded runs under a runner backlog
nodes.rationale: Rerunning a superseded run makes it the newest request in the concurrency group and cancels the PR's real head run, so reruns are restricted to the current head.

nodes.label: Exit-code to JSON-deny bridge
nodes.rationale: Codex blocks only on a JSON permissionDecision deny and ignores exit 2, so the adapter translates blocks while keeping guardrails single-sourced.

nodes.label: Adapter fix: wrapper, exit-2 to deny, swallow non-block outcomes
nodes.norm_label: adapter fix: wrapper, exit-2 to deny, swallow non-block outcomes
nodes.rationale: Codex renders nonzero non-deny hooks as failed banners and rejects allow envelopes, so only BLOCKs are forwarded and the adapter always exits 0.

nodes.label: Codex hooks: Claude-compatible engine with JSON deny
nodes.norm_label: codex hooks: claude-compatible engine with json deny
nodes.rationale: Codex blocks only on JSON permissionDecision deny and not exit 2, so guardrails would fire but never block without an adapter.

nodes.label: Mirroring plugin security guards into .codex/hooks.json
nodes.rationale: Codex injects CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for neither plugin nor project hooks, so plugin-delivered guards silently no-op'd until mirrored.

nodes.label: SessionEnd hooks wired to Codex Stop; telegram-session-end to SessionEnd
nodes.norm_label: sessionend hooks wired to codex stop; telegram-session-end to sessionend
nodes.rationale: Stop fires every turn so a per-turn Telegram relay would spam, while enqueue-and-exit fits SessionEnd's 1-3s cap.

nodes.label: Codex hook adapter translating exit-2 to JSON deny
nodes.norm_label: codex hook adapter translating exit-2 to json deny
nodes.rationale: Codex ignores a bare exit 2, so himmel's block must be translated into JSON permissionDecision deny for the guard to take effect.

nodes.label: Codex hook trust and sandbox behavior
nodes.norm_label: codex hook trust and sandbox behavior
nodes.rationale: New project hooks are trust-hashed on first use so untrusted hook sources are not run silently, and bypassing trust is a disarming flag to use only after vetting.

nodes.label: rc=2 fail-closed predicate contract (guard_call/pred_check)
nodes.rationale: The plain `if predicate` form merges rc=1 and rc=2 and fails open on errors, so helpers or explicit $? branching are required.

nodes.label: Guardrail predicates (is_on_main, is_dirty, is_merged_into_main...)
nodes.rationale: Shared predicates return 0/1/2 so guards can fail closed on internal errors (rc=2) instead of collapsing errors into the allow path.

nodes.label: Guardrails shared predicate library
nodes.rationale: One shared predicate library consumed by pre-commit, PreToolUse and slash commands means a new predicate lights up across all three layers at once.

nodes.label: Contributor Covenant 2.1
nodes.rationale: implied: adopting a widely used standard avoids writing a bespoke code of conduct.

nodes.label: Community Impact enforcement ladder
nodes.rationale: Escalating consequences (correction, warning, temporary ban, permanent ban) keep responses proportional to the harm.

nodes.label: Config feed (GET /api/feed)
nodes.rationale: One shared himmelctl report with progress, background loading and stale-while-revalidate hides a roughly two-minute doctor run from the operator.

nodes.label: Proposals-only contract
nodes.rationale: Creating tickets is an external write the operator controls and the auto-mode classifier gates.

nodes.label: Memory index line ceiling (MEMORY_LINE_CEIL)
nodes.rationale: The always-loaded MEMORY.md must stay O(themes) with one routing line per theme, and shrinking writes must pass so a bloated index can be worked down.

nodes.label: Topic-file cap (MEMORY_TOPIC_MAX)
nodes.rationale: Topic files that grow unbounded defeat lazy loading, so growth past the cap is denied and the session is sent to memory-compound to split the theme.

nodes.label: Memory-capture audit
nodes.rationale: It is decoupled from the memory-compound cadence because compound runs weeks apart and a detector riding it would grow latency.

nodes.label: Access-gating delegated to telegram:access
nodes.rationale: A channel message asking to bypass the allowlist is the prompt-injection shape, so access is owned by telegram:access and the skill only records the sender as provenance.

nodes.label: Idempotency via telegram_msg_id
nodes.rationale: The message-id is the idempotency key so re-runs report skipped (already-filed) instead of writing duplicate clips.

nodes.label: NEVER headless: pure Node tool via Bash
nodes.norm_label: never headless: pure node tool via bash
nodes.rationale: The CLI holds all deterministic logic so no Anthropic API or claude -p call is needed.

nodes.label: G-3 body-identity invariant
nodes.rationale: Constraining writes to frontmatter or a single added section, with YAML parse-validate and revert-on-failure, keeps existing clip content byte-identical.

nodes.label: Chief/worker dispatch fence (guard-chief-dispatch.sh)
nodes.rationale: PR/ticket work dispatched from a chief must go to an armed detached session, because in-process subagents die with the parent, are not relaunchable and dump reports into parent context; the ruling drifted twice.

nodes.label: Chief foreground guard (guard-chief-foreground.sh)
nodes.rationale: A foreground run of a slow chief-kit script blocks the chief's turn for minutes and queues every worker's SendMessage behind it.

nodes.label: Lane-routing dispatcher guard (guard-implementor-dispatch.sh)
nodes.rationale: After two recorded prose drifts, workers were routed through Claude subagents and burned the scarce subscription budget, so a hard block replaces another warning.

nodes.label: Ticket shape: six headed sections
nodes.rationale: Plain Impact/What/Why plus Plan and DoD let anyone read a ticket without knowing the code and make results checkable.

nodes.label: Ticket title rules: system vs user-facing
nodes.norm_label: ticket title rules: system vs user-facing
nodes.rationale: Titles name their sector or read as a plain sentence, with no commit prefixes or internal names, so tickets are legible to non-code readers.

nodes.label: Real-escape corpus (HIMMEL-8427)
nodes.rationale: Real review escapes frozen from merged history test the panel on defects that actually slipped past review, not just synthetic ones.

nodes.label: Status marker
nodes.rationale: A fixed leading word on each Results bullet lets the tick read worker phase mechanically.

nodes.label: Tick
nodes.rationale: One batched snapshot line of the fleet saves the chief from polling each worker.

nodes.label: Consult partial sandbox envelope
nodes.rationale: Removing edit tools and pinning settings prevents user or project scopes from widening write roots, though it is stated as a partial guarantee.

nodes.label: Judge lifecycle: write verdict, release lock, end turn
nodes.norm_label: judge lifecycle: write verdict, release lock, end turn
nodes.rationale: A judge that does not end its turn holds a fleet slot the chief cannot reclaim without killing the window.

nodes.label: RM ruling protocol (intent, applied, receipted)
nodes.rationale: Each ruling names a verb, class, sector and ground and is read back after apply so it is auditable.

nodes.label: Wrap only with no live subagent or orphan
nodes.norm_label: wrap only with no live subagent or orphan
nodes.rationale: An in-process subagent dies with its parent session and takes its verdict with it, and a 'safe to exit' claim is not evidence, so liveness is checked by tooling.

nodes.label: Results marker bullet protocol
nodes.rationale: The chief reads only the newest marker-bearing bullet, so markers must start the bullet and be written by append-results.sh to land at true EOF.

nodes.label: Worker wrap-up and subtree cleanup
nodes.rationale: A worker must release its lock, stop all background tasks and leave a resume brief so the chief can close the window and nothing is orphaned.

nodes.label: Symptom: wrap-subtree-check.sh prints WITHHELD
nodes.rationale: Surviving harness MCP servers are not the worker's to stop and do not block WRAPPED.

nodes.label: The release manager
nodes.rationale: On-demand rulings, burn-down and tag readiness for a release without a session idling between batches.

nodes.label: Telegram promotion feedback (LUNA-91)
nodes.rationale: One batched reply per originating chat avoids spamming the operator with one message per promotion.

nodes.label: Morning review: one consolidated report
nodes.rationale: Human review is the serial fraction capping fanout speedup (Amdahl's Law), so the checkpoint is batched into a single entry point.

nodes.label: Map-reduce-and-manage default shape
nodes.rationale: Workers contribute intelligence not actions and writes stay single-threaded, because unstructured swarms distract rather than scale.

nodes.label: Calling contract for prov_begin/record/end
nodes.rationale: Recording after the writer's atomic write succeeds and before the success line keeps ledger rows truthful about what actually happened.

nodes.label: Fail-closed security floor vs fail-open hygiene guards
nodes.norm_label: fail-closed security floor vs fail-open hygiene guards
nodes.rationale: Security fences must block when they cannot evaluate, while hygiene and notice hooks must not block work whenever a dependency is missing.

nodes.label: Write-time hook-file parse guard rationale
nodes.rationale: A hook file is live the instant it is saved, so a stray apostrophe broke every command fleet-wide without ever reaching a commit gate.

nodes.label: Pre-commit enforcement stages
nodes.rationale: Mechanical gates catch classes of recurring defects (secrets, drift, unchecked mktemp, bad commit shape) before they land instead of relying on contributor discipline.

nodes.label: A/B hook replay (PATH with and without Git\bin)
nodes.norm_label: a/b hook replay (path with and without git\bin)
nodes.rationale: Replaying the same stdin on two PATH arms separated PATH-dependent timeouts from PATH-independent quoted-path failures.

nodes.label: Bare bash resolves to the System32 WSL launcher
nodes.norm_label: bare bash resolves to the system32 wsl launcher
nodes.rationale: Machine PATH lists System32 before Git dirs, so a wedged WSL blocks every bare-bash hook until Codex's 600s default timeout.

nodes.label: Claude to Codex hook alignment audit
nodes.norm_label: claude to codex hook alignment audit
nodes.rationale: The audit lists which Claude hooks lack Codex wiring and why, so gaps like telegram-session-end could be mirrored and runtime-impossible ones accepted.

nodes.label: Claude Code hook replay benchmark (75 hooks)
nodes.norm_label: claude code hook replay benchmark (75 hooks)
nodes.rationale: Claude runs hooks through Git Bash with env vars set, so neither pwsh trap applies and all replayed hooks were <=1.0s.

nodes.label: Empirical Codex event / tool-name matrix
nodes.rationale: Codex has no Read/Edit/Write/Grep tools (Bash and apply_patch only), so Edit|Write guards never fire and apply_patch guards fail open on empty file_path.

nodes.label: Hook-set prune and exit-code contract
nodes.rationale: Timeouts were load amplified by a five-process wrapper chain, and propagating a nonzero code made Codex show an error and fail open, so the wrapper emits a fail-closed deny and exits 0.

nodes.label: Positional hook trust trap
nodes.rationale: Codex keys trust state by position in config.toml, so editing hooks.json shifts indices causing re-prompts and misapplied enabled=false.

nodes.label: Port / guard / accept decisions table
nodes.rationale: Consolidates per-item decisions so each harness gap is classified as accept, port or soft-defer.

nodes.label: PreToolUse dispatcher (chained guardrails with + separator)
nodes.rationale: Codex launched a full process stack per hook entry, so chaining guardrails into one adapter launch cut Git Bash process counts while keeping guard order.

nodes.label: Command starting with a quoted path is a pwsh string expression
nodes.norm_label: command starting with a quoted path is a pwsh string expression
nodes.rationale: pwsh parses a leading quoted path as an expression and fails with ParserError rc=1; a leading `& ` or commandWindows avoids it.

nodes.label: Shell-surface guards mirrored to Codex
nodes.rationale: These four guards read tool_input.command which matches the Codex shell payload, so they could be wired with no script change, while the Edit/Write arm would be a silent no-op under apply_patch.

nodes.label: Windows hook runner = pwsh -Command (two traps)
nodes.rationale: A live Codex session stalled ~10 min per hook, so the runner's shell semantics had to be documented to avoid repeating the stall.

nodes.label: Merge-forward rule
nodes.rationale: Merge-forward may cure only a red inherited from a broken base, never one the worker's own change introduced, so it needs proof via base and latest main runs.

nodes.label: SKIP_LIST suite is uncovered, never 'CI verifies'
nodes.norm_label: skip_list suite is uncovered, never 'ci verifies'
nodes.rationale: CI does not run SKIP_LIST suites, so citing CI as evidence is citing nothing; coverage is looked up from the runner so it cannot drift.

nodes.label: fixtures/fail-open pre-fix reconstructions
nodes.rationale: Each detector is proven red against a committed reconstruction of the pre-fix code so the lint is shown to actually catch what it targets.

nodes.label: Fails-open-on-unknown lint and convention
nodes.rationale: Written after 5 confirmed instances of the same fail-open mistake in one worker, so the standing guard catches the next occurrence of the shape rather than only numbered instances.

nodes.label: Capturing bug fixes (FAILED/WORKED ledger)
nodes.rationale: The Fixes-tried ledger breaks circular debugging by stopping a later or post-compaction session from retrying a failed fix.

nodes.label: Capturing human feedback
nodes.rationale: Proactively recording operator feedback in reviewer-notes.md avoids losing it between sessions.

nodes.label: Handover command index (create, move, bugs, maintenance, setup)
nodes.norm_label: handover command index (create, move, bugs, maintenance, setup)
nodes.rationale: Each op maps to a reference slice loaded on demand to keep context small.

nodes.label: Shared substrate: target repo, bucket, worktree gate
nodes.norm_label: shared substrate: target repo, bucket, worktree gate
nodes.rationale: All mutation ops resolve repo and bucket and run in a worktree the same way, so the shared logic lives in one reference.

nodes.label: Google Health connector fixtures README
nodes.rationale: Synthetic PHI-free recorded-shape fixtures let connector tests run offline.

nodes.label: Detect auth gap via /v1/messages, not /v1/models
nodes.rationale: /v1/models is registry-backed and keeps returning 200 during an OAuth gap, so only a real completion reveals the failure.

nodes.label: Loopback-pinned config.yaml host
nodes.rationale: CLIProxyAPI's default empty host binds all interfaces, which would expose the OAuth-wrapped subscription endpoint on the LAN.

nodes.label: One CLIProxyAPI instance per host
nodes.rationale: The proxy is a host process on 127.0.0.1:8317 that serves every client on the machine, so installing it per launcher would be redundant.

nodes.label: claudex lane
nodes.rationale: Claude Code with a swapped backend fires every PreToolUse hook natively, so its guard posture equals the native column.

nodes.label: claude-codex launcher
nodes.rationale: It runs Claude Code over the codex subscription via a local proxy to keep the full himmel harness while spending the codex usage budget.

nodes.label: claudex effort mapping and operating rules
nodes.norm_label: claudex effort mapping and operating rules
nodes.rationale: Effort is forwarded verbatim so downgrades reach codex, ultra is unreachable and max is unverified, hence the default xhigh (decision 223) and ladder capped at xhigh.

nodes.label: CLIProxyAPI prerequisite and guard files
nodes.rationale: Binding to 127.0.0.1 avoids LAN-exposing the OAuth-wrapped endpoint and PHI-marked workspaces are refused to prevent sending data to OpenAI.

nodes.label: Lane plugin profiles
nodes.rationale: Injecting a complete enabledPlugins map per dispatch gives lane workers a lean plugin set (~5,058 fewer tokens/session) without mutating the operator's config.

nodes.label: spawn-claudex --model tier allowlist
nodes.rationale: A new interface can be strict without breaking existing contracts, while the launcher's own CODEX_MODEL knob stays unvalidated so direct cc-codex uses of other proxy models keep working.

nodes.label: Plugin profile floor
nodes.rationale: A lane that cannot dispatch, search or hand over is broken, so the floor is forced true last and nothing can drop it.

nodes.label: claudex Sonnet classifier default
nodes.rationale: The launcher never runs with no classifier, but seeded deny rules rather than the classifier stop destructive git because the classifier alone allowed a force push.

nodes.label: Refuse alias not owned by Claude OAuth provider (owned_by, fail closed)
nodes.norm_label: refuse alias not owned by claude oauth provider (owned_by, fail closed)
nodes.rationale: Enforcing the provider in code removes dependence on the operator picking the right alias; a missing owned_by must refuse (fail closed).

nodes.label: Shadow ledger
nodes.rationale: A passive hash-chained record of approval-shaped decisions gives an audit trail without any ability to deny.

nodes.label: Approval-interrupts per week (gate number)
nodes.rationale: Nobody knows this rate, and below roughly ten per week the small version is the end state so the graduated ladder should never be built.

nodes.label: Blind means written before the prompt is routed
nodes.norm_label: blind means written before the prompt is routed
nodes.rationale: If the operator could see the harness's guess, agreement would measure anchoring rather than competence, making the evidence invisibly worthless.

nodes.label: Coarse class and hash only; known-subcommand whitelist
nodes.norm_label: coarse class and hash only; known-subcommand whitelist
nodes.rationale: Unrecognised words are where secrets live, and a ledger holding transcripts becomes an unread lake, so only validated subcommands and hashes are stored.

nodes.label: Refusal to publish a rate over a damaged ledger
nodes.norm_label: refusal to publish a rate over a damaged ledger
nodes.rationale: Silently skipping a torn row and printing a confident number yields a plausible understated result with nothing to signal it.

nodes.label: Deferred: chain verification tooling and keyed signatures
nodes.norm_label: deferred: chain verification tooling and keyed signatures
nodes.rationale: The threat model is model drift and confusion rather than a filesystem adversary, and signing if added must be by the launcher/hook process, never the agent.

nodes.label: drops.jsonl and rate suppression on any recorded drop
nodes.norm_label: drops.jsonl and rate suppression on any recorded drop
nodes.rationale: The hash chain is blind to rows that never landed, and a clock cannot be trusted to expire a known loss, so any drop suppresses the rate with no acknowledgement path.

nodes.label: Ledger location ~/.claude/himmel/trust/ledger.jsonl
nodes.rationale: It lives outside the repo because it is machine-local measurement, not source.

nodes.label: Never emit ask; defer by emitting nothing
nodes.norm_label: never emit ask; defer by emitting nothing
nodes.rationale: An ask reintroduces the dialog auto mode removes and in armed sessions is unanswerable and unbounded (measured 902.5s).

nodes.label: Invoke node directly with quoted $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
nodes.rationale: Avoids Windows bash-resolution failures, and quoting prevents word-splitting on paths with spaces that would make the hook fail open and silently lose observations.

nodes.label: denied_auto_classifier verdict (auto-mode classifier denials only)
nodes.rationale: PermissionDenied only fires for auto-mode classifier denials, so naming it plain 'denied' would be a partial signal wearing a name that reads as complete coverage.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest events recorded alongside Notification-derived count
nodes.norm_label: permissionrequest events recorded alongside notification-derived count
nodes.rationale: The event fires even in unattended sessions, and running two independent estimators side by side lets evidence decide which is right instead of silently swapping in an unvalidated one.

nodes.label: R0 shadow ledger (append-only hash-chained record)
nodes.rationale: It only records and emits no permission decision, so adding or removing it cannot change how prompts flow.

nodes.label: Refusal to report a rate from a window under one day
nodes.norm_label: refusal to report a rate from a window under one day
nodes.rationale: A twenty-minute sample scaled up yields a confident but artefactual number on the one figure the programme is gated on.

nodes.label: timeout: 10 on every hook
nodes.rationale: A command hook defaults to 600 seconds, so a stall would hold tool calls for ten minutes and turn the recorder into a behaviour change.

nodes.label: Missing outcome row is unresolved, not a denial
nodes.norm_label: missing outcome row is unresolved, not a denial
nodes.rationale: A Pre/Post pair alone cannot distinguish denied from stranded from crashed.

nodes.label: Residual blind spot: drops.jsonl on same volume as ledger
nodes.norm_label: residual blind spot: drops.jsonl on same volume as ledger
nodes.rationale: A second file on the same disk cannot fully solve volume-wide failure, so it is documented and HIMMEL_TRUST_LEDGER_DIR lets operators point at a monitored volume.

nodes.label: Cache and freshness rules
nodes.rationale: Head-bracketing REST reads, atomic writes and a fail-closed lock prevent serving stale or racing snapshots, with TTL 0 for merge-time freshness.

nodes.label: Query cost and pagination
nodes.rationale: One aliased GraphQL query per batch cuts a settled ready-check from 7 calls to 2, while failing closed on incomplete pagination.

nodes.label: Injection re-screen (HIMMEL-256)
nodes.rationale: Newly fetched untrusted text is screened and fails closed so injected content cannot reach later judge or triage prompts.

nodes.label: Branch on context-fill exit status
nodes.rationale: A stale or unknown reading prints nothing and exits 3/4, so a bare numeric comparison would look the same as being below threshold.

nodes.label: CR ledger
nodes.rationale: One row per responding critic at a head gives gates a shared evidence record of review.

nodes.label: CR marker
nodes.rationale: An untracked file written at pre-push blocks PR creation until the review gate clears it.

nodes.label: Gate integrity
nodes.rationale: Fixed paths for a gate's collaborators prevent a contaminated environment from forging the evidence the gate reads.

nodes.label: Variant sweep
nodes.rationale: Requiring a SWEEP line naming every site of a finding's class ensures a fix covers all variants of the bug.

nodes.label: Chief-spawned worker AskUserQuestion deny (block-worker-askuserquestion.sh)
nodes.rationale: Headed workers run in a window nobody answers, and two workers parked on AskUserQuestion (one for 77 minutes), so a second prose drift became structural.

nodes.label: Chief-spawned worker ScheduleWakeup deny (guard-worker-wakeup.sh)
nodes.rationale: A self-scheduled polling wake re-reads the worker's full context just to find 'not yet', a cost-program finding, so workers must use one foreground blocking wait.

nodes.label: Family F8 leg to worker file rename (slice T)
nodes.norm_label: family f8 leg to worker file rename (slice t)
nodes.rationale: implied: unifies leg/console file names with worker/chief terminology, owned by HIMMEL-6644.

nodes.label: Forwarders and aliases at old paths (HIMMEL-6647)
nodes.norm_label: forwarders and aliases at old paths (himmel-6647)
nodes.rationale: Each forwarder is deleted by its family's leftover PR after the last caller moves, so the old paths stop working only once nobody uses them.

nodes.label: leg-burn: PR-body line kept (do-not-rename list)
nodes.rationale: The plan's do-not-rename list keeps the leg-burn: PR-body line unchanged.

nodes.label: N02 HIMMEL_LEG_* to HIMMEL_WORKER_SESSION_*
nodes.rationale: It must never become HIMMEL_WORKER_*, because that name is a live security marker.

nodes.label: N03 HIMMEL_LEAN_LEG to HIMMEL_LEAN_WORKER_SESSION
nodes.rationale: implied: part of the F2 leg to worker-session env rename, for consistency with the HIMMEL_LEG_* names.

nodes.label: N04 LEG_* to WORKER_SESSION_*
nodes.rationale: LEG_DIGEST_CHAIN_SLACK_MIN takes the registry's name, which leg-digest-step.sh already reads, to stay consistent.

nodes.label: N05 HEADED_ARM_LEG_* to HEADED_ARM_WORKER_*
nodes.rationale: implied: part of the F2 rename of the fleet-sense 'leg' to 'worker' in the headed arm env names.

nodes.label: N13 clear-cr-marker.sh and cr-*.sh to review-*/coderabbit-*
nodes.norm_label: n13 clear-cr-marker.sh and cr-*.sh to review-*/coderabbit-*
nodes.rationale: scripts/cr/cr-trigger-ledger.sh is the CI-release ledger, not the CodeRabbit one, so the registry's alias row does not apply to it.

nodes.label: N15 headed-arm-leg.sh to headed-arm-worker.sh
nodes.rationale: implied: the leg terminology is being replaced by worker, so the script and its test files need matching names across 140 files.

nodes.label: N40 handover section directories rename
nodes.rationale: Plan row 60 renames console-sections/ and leg-sections/ to chief-sections/ and worker-sections/ as part of the chief/worker vocabulary move; the new names are not live yet (0/2).

nodes.label: N42 other leg-*.sh scripts (needs a ruling)
nodes.norm_label: n42 other leg-*.sh scripts (needs a ruling)
nodes.rationale: These scripts are not in the approved rename table, so renaming them needs a ruling; the leg-burn: PR-body line is kept per the plan do-not-rename list.

nodes.label: PR 1c: review leftovers (N13, N14, N32)
nodes.rationale: It drops the cr forwarders and read-both names after the last callers have moved.

nodes.label: PR 2: worker env and ids (V4a-2)
nodes.rationale: It comes before the worker scripts so that renaming the env first keeps each PR's breakage to one kind.

nodes.label: PR 3: worker scripts (V4b)
nodes.rationale: implied: scripts read the env names, so they are renamed after the env rename.

nodes.label: PR 4: templates, prefaces and tick fields (T)
nodes.norm_label: pr 4: templates, prefaces and tick fields (t)
nodes.rationale: It follows the scripts that read the preface, and tick.sh and console-wait.sh change the tick fields in the same PR.

nodes.label: console-sections/leg-sections to chief-sections/worker-sections
nodes.rationale: Directory names follow the chief/worker terminology adopted in the rename plan.

nodes.label: N20 leg-preface*.md to worker-preface*.md
nodes.rationale: Family F8 slice T renames leg-preface file names to worker-preface (owner HIMMEL-6644); new name is not live yet (0/5), so callers must be migrated first.

nodes.label: N21 console-template.md to chief-template.md
nodes.rationale: Family F8 file rename aligning the template name with the chief role; console-handoff-template.md is left alone because it has no ruled name.

nodes.label: N22 leg-brief-template.md to worker-brief-template.md
nodes.rationale: Family F8 slice T renames leg to worker in the brief template file name; new name not yet live (0/1).

nodes.label: N34 tick fields legs=, legset=, bank= to workers=, workerset=, usage=
nodes.norm_label: n34 tick fields legs=, legset=, bank= to workers=, workerset=, usage=
nodes.rationale: Ambiguous because the strings also match shell variables named bank or legs; tails= and parked= keep their names.

nodes.label: N35 hooks block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to worker names
nodes.norm_label: n35 hooks block-leg-askuserquestion.sh, guard-leg-wakeup.sh to worker names
nodes.rationale: Hook scripts are registered in .claude/settings.json so the switch needs an operator edit (HIMMEL-7139), then forwarders (HIMMEL-6647).

nodes.label: leak-classes home-path heuristics task
nodes.rationale: Two narrow follow-on gaps from the #664 panel were filed separately per CR-gate convention rather than widening that fix.

nodes.label: Windows jq CRLF chokepoint shim
nodes.rationale: Native Windows jq emits CRLF, which produced null lookups in the first shipped report; a single jq() wrapper piping through tr -d '\r' is used so the shim is not treated as optional and removed later.

nodes.label: Registry path-matching trap (Windows-only folding)
nodes.rationale: Case and drive-letter folding is gated to Windows because folding on case-sensitive Linux could route a report into another repo's bucket; failing closed on macOS is accepted over folding unconditionally.

nodes.label: Positive-control refusal (0 items vs nonzero last-seen)
nodes.norm_label: positive-control refusal (0 items vs nonzero last-seen)
nodes.rationale: Zero items against a nonzero last-seen count is treated as an instrument failure, so a broken search can never be read as 'everything closed'.

nodes.label: PR '## Release note' opt-in block
nodes.rationale: A PR opts into user-visible notes explicitly with kind-prefixed lines, so unmarked PRs count only in the Internal line.

nodes.label: User-visible versus internal changes
nodes.rationale: Only changes an adopter can see from outside the repo belong in user sections, with no ticket keys or PR numbers, which belong in git log.

nodes.label: Attestation trailers
nodes.rationale: Platform and security attestations are required only for sensitive or non-docs changes, and must be in the first commit rather than a reactive amend.

nodes.label: Platforms tested pre-push gate
nodes.rationale: Forces the operator to think about Linux-vs-macOS before push, where cross-platform bugs keep slipping through code review.

nodes.label: Symptom: pre-push gate fails on missing attestation trailer
nodes.norm_label: symptom: pre-push gate fails on missing attestation trailer
nodes.rationale: ready-check reads only the PR's first commit, so a late trailer clears the push gate but still blocks the chief's merge and the branch must be recut.

nodes.label: Relationship to other gates (gitleaks, code-review-before-push, platforms-tested)
nodes.norm_label: relationship to other gates (gitleaks, code-review-before-push, platforms-tested)
nodes.rationale: Each gate covers a different layer and none runs headless Claude, so together they enforce conscious decisions without budget cost.

nodes.label: When the security-reviewed gate fires
nodes.rationale: Docs-only diffs are skipped so the gate costs nothing where no code security surface exists.

nodes.label: Lean-invoke plus attestation gate (why not an upstream-action wrapper)
nodes.norm_label: lean-invoke plus attestation gate (why not an upstream-action wrapper)
nodes.rationale: A wrapper hook would fire a headless Claude call on every push against the same shared subscription budget (a 48-chunk run exhausted it in about 2.9 hours), so the operator runs review on demand and the gate only enforces the attestation.

nodes.label: Attestation trailers (Platforms tested, Security reviewed)
nodes.rationale: These gates ask the author to attest to things a machine cannot verify, and are opt-in for adopters via their own pre-commit config.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md Claude invocation billing rule
nodes.rationale: Governs how headless Claude calls draw on subscription budget, which is the constraint behind the lean-invoke design.

nodes.label: Docs remarks (remarks.tsv, docs-reviewer)
nodes.rationale: Operator's verbatim docs remarks form a learned bar for docs pages applied by judgement since no detector exists.

nodes.label: How the chief uses it (judge-side, decision 286)
nodes.norm_label: how the chief uses it (judge-side, decision 286)
nodes.rationale: Docs PRs do not wait on the operator, so the review runs once on the judge side and the operator reviews after the fact.

nodes.label: Code changes implied (three cases, decision 299)
nodes.rationale: Only three cases truly need a code change; otherwise a wrong page is a docs fix, so code work is not conflated with docs corrections.

nodes.label: Correctness pass
nodes.rationale: Every claim on a changed line is checked against code at the head because a false claim is a blocking defect and sampling would miss some.

nodes.label: Finding gate and severity (BLOCKING/SHOULD/NIT)
nodes.rationale: Gating each finding on an exact changed line, a cited source and a defensible severity keeps the review diff-scoped and avoids noise; a remark repeated more than once escalates to BLOCKING.

nodes.label: 3 KB output limit
nodes.rationale: implied: a bounded answer fits a judge/PR comment and is measured by the caller, not the model, so the limit holds deterministically.

nodes.label: Page verdict (keep/polish/restructure/generate-from-data/move-to-ADR/drop)
nodes.rationale: The verdict is first and never capped so that whole-page form problems are judged even when they rest on unchanged lines.

nodes.label: Remark pass
nodes.rationale: Each remark is applied by judgement, not pattern matching, and covers every instance of a kind of thing so the operator's intent is not narrowed to its quoted example.

nodes.label: Diátaxis modes (tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation)
nodes.rationale: One document should serve one mode, because mixing modes makes each worse.

nodes.label: Four layers: rhythm, Google style, STE, Global English
nodes.norm_label: four layers: rhythm, google style, ste, global english
nodes.rationale: Layered rules make each statement load one at a time and leave no sentence open to two readings.

nodes.label: Fork sync is upkeep, never a PR
nodes.norm_label: fork sync is upkeep, never a pr
nodes.rationale: Upstream code should not get a sync PR, judge or CodeRabbit review, so syncing is pushed straight to the himmel branch (HIMMEL-8334).

nodes.label: Himmel-only hooks (not in core)
nodes.rationale: These hooks check himmel's own files or style and have no meaning in a fork whose code is upstream's.

nodes.label: Fork adapter standard
nodes.rationale: Every fork needs a uniform registered standard so changes follow the himmel flow and the registry cannot be widened from a worktree.

nodes.label: Fork pre-commit core
nodes.rationale: Forks skip himmel's gates, so a small security-and-process core stops secrets and unticketed changes without imposing himmel's lint on upstream code.

nodes.label: Companion PR in same pass as issue
nodes.norm_label: companion pr in same pass as issue
nodes.rationale: An issue-only filing on a clean testable fix risks someone else taking the fix, and the operator wants credit for closing discovered bugs.

nodes.label: Dupe gate (step 1)
nodes.rationale: A competing PR burns tokens and maintainer goodwill, while the gate costs only two read-only searches, so it must run before any drafting or building.

nodes.label: Deterministic form decision (step 3)
nodes.rationale: Removing filer discretion makes the choice between advisory, PR, issue and skip repeatable, and keeps security disclosure channel selection with the operator.

nodes.label: Impact-first filing body (step 6)
nodes.rationale: A maintainer must understand what is wrong and why from the first two sentences or the filing gets closed as unclear.

nodes.label: Re-verify at upstream HEAD (step 2)
nodes.rationale: Findings from vendored, fork or built copies go stale, so every filing must cite the HEAD sha and file:line of the real source tree.

nodes.label: Verify and roster on tracking ticket (step 7)
nodes.norm_label: verify and roster on tracking ticket (step 7)
nodes.rationale: One idempotent roster row per finding keeps a re-run from duplicating dispositions on the tracking ticket.

nodes.label: VM concurrency rail
nodes.rationale: The old one-VM-at-a-time rule was Windows-era (shared ports and RAM) and blocked parallel linked clones, so it became one VM per port plus a RAM budget.

nodes.label: Hook-stack re-benchmark with outbound SKIP tripwire
nodes.norm_label: hook-stack re-benchmark with outbound skip tripwire
nodes.rationale: Replaying hooks that emit outbound irreversible effects would burn trigger slots or send real messages, so a source scan fails if such a hook is missing from SKIP.

nodes.label: Read-clamp PreToolUse hook (read-clamp.sh)
nodes.rationale: Repeated and whole-file reads were measured as the #2/#3 cost levers on a PR's token bill, and the instructional layer drifted, so it escalated to a structural hook.

nodes.label: Remote stations inventory (unreachable host is a WARN)
nodes.norm_label: remote stations inventory (unreachable host is a warn)
nodes.rationale: Memory is per-host and a silently skipped host is the multi-host bug recurring, so unreachable hosts warn; station specifics stay in the registry note so the skill text stays adopter-generic.

nodes.label: Shape triage (fact, directive, invocation)
nodes.rationale: A directive behind a qmd query is dead because the model never queries for a rule it does not know it is breaking, so shape decides where recall happens (D9, HIMMEL-570).

nodes.label: Branch caveat: qmd indexes primary checkouts only
nodes.norm_label: branch caveat: qmd indexes primary checkouts only
nodes.rationale: Content landed on a branch is not findable until merged, so the findability check and deletions run as a post-merge follow-up.

nodes.label: Scope qmd query with -c (singular) flag
nodes.rationale: An unscoped query dilutes hits on fresh notes and --collections is silently ignored, which would confirm a false pass.

nodes.label: Run in a dedicated session
nodes.rationale: A hurried inline trim loses recall hooks, and measured cache cost of editing MEMORY.md is small (14 kept, 1 compacted, 0 invalidated over 15 sessions).

nodes.label: Hub split for over-cap topic files
nodes.norm_label: hub split for over-cap topic files
nodes.rationale: A keyword match reads the whole topic file, so an over-8192-byte file becomes a hub plus sub-files via a pure move first.

nodes.label: Propagation review (operator-specific vs adopter-generic)
nodes.rationale: Auto-memory and the luna vault never reach other himmel users, so adopter-generic learnings must land in himmel docs.

nodes.label: qmd findability gate
nodes.rationale: A learning that does not surface in a search is not compounded, so no topic file is deleted until its content is confirmed findable.

nodes.label: Safety rails (land before trim, qmd gate before delete, snapshot first)
nodes.norm_label: safety rails (land before trim, qmd gate before delete, snapshot first)
nodes.rationale: The pass is zero-loss only if the order of landing, trimming and deleting is kept.

nodes.label: Read-many, write-once on a branch
nodes.rationale: Parallel writes at a shared note are avoided, and landing on a branch makes the pass trackable with an operator merge as the vault's review step.

nodes.label: Topic file as primary recall path
nodes.norm_label: topic file as primary recall path
nodes.rationale: A 2026-07-17 spike measured symptom-shaped qmd recall at 4/10 versus 3/3 deterministic for reading the named topic file, so folding to luna is a durability copy and not a reason to delete.

nodes.label: Four lead answers: shipped, waits on you, spent, runs next
nodes.norm_label: four lead answers: shipped, waits on you, spent, runs next
nodes.rationale: implied: leading with four answers lets the operator scan the day's state quickly, with missing inputs honestly marked 'not available'.

nodes.label: Opt-in doc-guard gate (.himmel-dev marker)
nodes.rationale: The catalog-sync gate guards contributors but must stay off for adopters using himmel only as a harness.

nodes.label: Warn-only doc-freshness detector
nodes.rationale: Double filtering by feat/fix changelog scoping and doc-presence suppression gives near-zero false positives for a drift nudge that must never stall a session.

nodes.label: Doc-guard gate (added-only, himmel-dev opt-in)
nodes.rationale: Adding a command or skill without a catalog entry is the primary gap, so only additions are gated and only contributor checkouts with a .himmel-dev marker are affected.

nodes.label: doc-guard pre-commit gate
nodes.rationale: Blocks adding a command or skill file without touching the commands catalog so docs do not drift, gated behind a .himmel-dev marker so adopters are unaffected.

nodes.label: Housekeeping digest
nodes.rationale: Batching board and informational changes into one 900 s window avoids a wake per minor change while urgent events stay immediate.

nodes.label: WAKE event taxonomy (telegram, tick, underfilled, doctor, cadence, review, pool-stale, ready, size, hold, worker-silent)
nodes.norm_label: wake event taxonomy (telegram, tick, underfilled, doctor, cadence, review, pool-stale, ready, size, hold, worker-silent)
nodes.rationale: Urgent events wake the chief once each with the evidence already gathered, while look-only changes are buffered so wakes stay cheap and non-repeating.

nodes.label: Prior art requirement
nodes.rationale: Chief, judge and consult sessions made no qmd lookups, so judges ruled without knowing related tickets; pointers only keeps the judge blind.

nodes.label: Core ticket builds only after a signed minerva spec
nodes.norm_label: core ticket builds only after a signed minerva spec
nodes.rationale: Core means the ship loop itself, and changes to it need an operator-signed spec enforced structurally (no flag, no free-text bypass) so in-flight or emergency work passes only via recorded bypasses.

nodes.label: Idle capacity is the chief's duty
nodes.norm_label: idle capacity is the chief's duty
nodes.rationale: When live workers sit below the cap with nothing launched, the chief pulls dispatchable work from the Jira backlog so capacity is not wasted.

nodes.label: Minerva design leg
nodes.rationale: A key with no spec needs a docs-only marker brief that writes just the spec, so the gate can be satisfied without lifting it for build briefs.

nodes.label: Prior art line (required)
nodes.rationale: Only 16 of 565 workers used retrieval before, so the chief runs the search once at dispatch and workers inherit it, avoiding re-derived or duplicated work.

nodes.label: handover-resume read path
nodes.rationale: The read path is fully mechanical, so it was moved into a script (HIMMEL-1038) and the command never loads the skill.

nodes.label: Hermes profiles: default and himmel_agent
nodes.rationale: An additive profile lets himmel add a main tier without touching the user's existing default setup, SOUL.md, config or .env.

nodes.label: on_session_finalize, never on_session_end
nodes.rationale: on_session_end is turn-scoped and would notify every turn, whereas finalize is the once-per-identity teardown.

nodes.label: Fleet CLIs auxiliary post-install items
nodes.rationale: Plain installers of claude, codex, hermes, copilot and grok leave one-time auth and config steps, calibrated on two stations.

nodes.label: Stale nudge from tech-debt.md
nodes.rationale: Surfacing the top three lingering or zombie items on resume prompts triage before the session continues.

nodes.label: Offline skip and pending-link skip
nodes.rationale: A network or token failure must never error out the parent command, so the item is skipped until the next successful run.

nodes.label: sync.log format
nodes.rationale: An append-only tab-separated log records every write, including mirrors, so syncs can be audited.

nodes.label: Legacy table-format bugs.md flag
nodes.rationale: A legacy table of open bugs counts as zero by headings, so it is flagged explicitly to keep it from vanishing from the metric unnoticed.

nodes.label: tech-debt.md generation
nodes.rationale: Lingering detection falls back to master-plan.md when plan.md is absent so a lingering epic is never silently skipped.

nodes.label: template_version mismatch behaviour
nodes.rationale: Warn-and-proceed keeps v1 items readable until the migration script runs.

nodes.label: Jira bidirectional last-modified-wins sync
nodes.rationale: Comparing file mtime to Jira updated lets whichever side was edited last win, with the skill winning ties as authoritative for the active session.

nodes.label: v2 frontmatter schema
nodes.rationale: A uniform frontmatter block (jira, bucket, priority, severity, timestamps, pending_jira_link) lets parsers and Jira sync treat every item alike.

nodes.label: Keeping docs/ui.md current (llms.txt and nav check)
nodes.norm_label: keeping docs/ui.md current (llms.txt and nav check)
nodes.rationale: A link test fails when a nav page id is missing from the page, which stops the entry pages from drifting.

nodes.label: GCP runner network
nodes.rationale: Runners have no external IP and egress only through an allowlisting squid proxy, limiting exposure to the listed GitHub and package hosts.

nodes.label: HANDOVER_DIR required (loud refusal)
nodes.rationale: Cron has no login shell so HANDOVER_DIR goes missing there, and proceeding would write the ledger into the git repo being published.

nodes.label: Pipeline lock (mkdir protocol, never take over stale lock)
nodes.norm_label: pipeline lock (mkdir protocol, never take over stale lock)
nodes.rationale: Two fires would reset --hard and clean the same worktree, and automatic stale-lock takeover produced a new race each time it was tried, so a dead holder is refused loudly instead.

nodes.label: Second corpus out of scope (--corpus-root refuses)
nodes.norm_label: second corpus out of scope (--corpus-root refuses)
nodes.rationale: A flag that looked like it worked but silently operated on the wrong repo was judged worse than a refusal.

nodes.label: Staleness measured by rev-list --count (not --merges)
nodes.rationale: himmel squash-merges every PR, so --merges always returns 0 while the true commit distance is the real number.

nodes.label: Threshold of 15 commits and its trade-off
nodes.norm_label: threshold of 15 commits and its trade-off
nodes.rationale: A threshold of 3 would cause constant PR churn, while 15 fires at the measured 36-commit gap and bounds staleness to about one busy day; it is not baked into the runner so changes apply next fire.

nodes.label: Why graph-cadence exists (stale graph, bare commits to main)
nodes.norm_label: why graph-cadence exists (stale graph, bare commits to main)
nodes.rationale: The graph silently rotted (36 commits behind) and hand refreshes were committed straight to main, bypassing the PR workflow, so an unattended PR-based runner removes the reason for that.

nodes.label: Sector opt-in custom field
nodes.rationale: The field id is config rather than code because it is a custom Jira field, and options come live from the field contexts.

nodes.label: create refusal rules (sections, home, placement)
nodes.rationale: create refuses tickets lacking detail sections, an epic or standalone home, or a version placement so every ticket is filed with context and a release.

nodes.label: transition Done fixVersion stamping
nodes.rationale: Done stamps the earliest unreleased fixVersion unless the key was deferred in a frozen version, which then closes unstamped with exit 3.

nodes.label: Clip pipeline chain (harvest to roadmap)
nodes.rationale: Chaining harvest, enrich, triage, synthesize and archive lets Clippings act as an inbox that drains as clips complete the chain.

nodes.label: Cookie-backed media paths removed (HIMMEL-4709)
nodes.rationale: Removing cookie paths and the HIMMEL_MEDIA_COOKIES switch means every media fetch is Scrapling and no cookie is sent anywhere.

nodes.label: Daily fetch health (HIMMEL-1449)
nodes.rationale: A cheap daily probe per integration classifies failures before harvest so broken fetch paths are visible rather than silent.

nodes.label: Daily timeline and daily report (LUNA-90, HIMMEL-4182)
nodes.norm_label: daily timeline and daily report (luna-90, himmel-4182)
nodes.rationale: A state recount makes the section idempotent so reruns update rather than double-count, and the report turns intake into decisions.

nodes.label: Instagram media rung /ig-media-enrich (HIMMEL-770)
nodes.rationale: The download and local-whisper path is expensive, so it is a lean-invoke escalation that holds thin clips and releases them only on verified success or permanent failure.

nodes.label: Proposals-only contract
nodes.rationale: Synthesis and roadmap output only proposes restructuring or tickets so the vault and Jira are never changed without a human.

nodes.label: Whisper GPU routing (HIMMEL-7680)
nodes.rationale: CUDA with a turbo model and Hebrew routing transcribes much faster and more accurately, falling back to CPU base when CUDA is unusable.

nodes.label: Default posture: optional lanes OFF
nodes.rationale: Every optional lane is off until configured and delegation rules skip absent lanes, so users enable only what they want.

nodes.label: The fleet: chief, workers, judge, GO
nodes.norm_label: the fleet: chief, workers, judge, go
nodes.rationale: A worker merges only on the chief's signed GO after a cheapest-tier judge ruling, so merging is gated and cost-controlled.

nodes.label: Jarvis (command layer)
nodes.rationale: The chief plans, workers implement in worktrees, a judge rules and the chief merges, so the fleet runs as one software factory steered from a single point.

nodes.label: The surface (himmel UI and other views)
nodes.norm_label: the surface (himmel ui and other views)
nodes.rationale: Views are read-only so that all steering goes through messaging the chief, keeping a single command channel.

nodes.label: Unattended runs (driver)
nodes.rationale: Arming, cap relaunch, AFK shifts, initiative and lessons let the fleet keep working with nobody at the keyboard, each turned on separately.

nodes.label: Checkable context-fill wrap check
nodes.rationale: A measured fill number replaces estimates and was needed because fill was routinely conflated with the token spend budget.

nodes.label: The five hang classes
nodes.rationale: Each controllable hang class resolves to either fallback or park so no armed run stalls undefined.

nodes.label: A zero needs a positive control
nodes.norm_label: a zero needs a positive control
nodes.rationale: A wrong slug, mangled path or wrong input can render as a clean 0 indistinguishable from a real pass.

nodes.label: Safety-classifier reroute is not a failure
nodes.norm_label: safety-classifier reroute is not a failure
nodes.rationale: Nothing is blocked on a reroute to Opus, so halting or escalating would waste an unattended run.

nodes.label: CR scripts (/pr-check sub-steps)
nodes.rationale: Splitting /pr-check into shell sub-steps keeps review mechanics deterministic and testable.

nodes.label: Report every finding, filter in a separate pass
nodes.norm_label: report every finding, filter in a separate pass
nodes.rationale: Suppressed findings are destroyed before the pass that would triage them, so the prompt asks for everything and lets /pr-check gate on Critical and Important only (HIMMEL-480).

nodes.label: Claude-only floor (not a bypass)
nodes.rationale: When external critics are absent a real review by Claude still happened, unlike SKIP_CR which is no review at all.

nodes.label: Panel heading format coupling
