nodes.rationale: Two producers and the filer parse the same headings, so a format change must be updated in lockstep.

nodes.label: MEDIUM findings excluded from filing
nodes.rationale: MEDIUM findings warrant attention before merge and filing them would let them drift into a backlog.

nodes.label: Polish is printed, not filed
nodes.rationale: Decisions 746 and 762 chose that polish items go into the PR body instead of creating tickets nobody works.

nodes.label: cr-scores agreed% fixed task
nodes.rationale: Fixed findings were accepted and acted on, so counting them as disagreement wrongly flags nearly 100%-accepted critics for dropping.

nodes.label: himmel rubric overrides
nodes.rationale: The upstream rubric rewards directory listings and repetition, which Claude 5 context-engineering guidance reverses, and the plugin cache cannot be edited without being discarded on update.

nodes.label: prose-audit three rules
nodes.rationale: Judgment and rationale must survive the audit, because deleting the why is how rules get re-derived wrong and shrinking by cutting explanation is a failed audit.

nodes.label: Context pointers
nodes.rationale: The wording of a pointer, not its target, decides when and how reliably the agent reaches material, so weak wording is a variance bug.

nodes.label: Information hierarchy and progressive disclosure
nodes.rationale: Pushing reference down the ladder keeps the top legible and protects steps from being buried, balancing hidden-material against bloat.

nodes.label: Leading words
nodes.rationale: A compact pretrained concept recruits existing model priors, anchoring behaviour in the fewest tokens.

nodes.label: Pruning discipline
nodes.rationale: Without pruning, stale layers settle as sediment because adding feels safe and removing feels risky.

nodes.label: /no-comments and comment-sicko
nodes.rationale: Vendored from pstack to prune comments outside a short keep list, and it runs only when typed because model invocation is disabled.

nodes.label: Project skills and agents
nodes.rationale: Profiles can only select plugins, so skills a profile must enable move into a plugin while project-scoped ones load only in this repo.

nodes.label: writing-for-agents skill
nodes.rationale: Documents an agent consumes need levers that make the agent's process predictable across runs, and the skill is user-invoked to cost zero listing tokens.

nodes.label: Per-suite timeout cap
nodes.rationale: Escalating TERM, grace, KILL across the whole process group means descendants die with the suite instead of being orphaned.

nodes.label: Cadence registry drives install wizard
nodes.rationale: The wizard menu is read from a JSON registry with a staleness lint so the menu cannot drift from the scripts that exist; the JSON wins when docs disagree.

nodes.label: Draft shape (six sections plus agent detail)
nodes.norm_label: draft shape (six sections plus agent detail)
nodes.rationale: Plain-language impact first and required Plan, DoD and Proof make tickets reviewable by humans and workable by agents.

nodes.label: Deterministic humanizer normalization
nodes.rationale: A deterministic punctuation pass with protected-literal checks avoids model rewrites that could alter facts or code.

nodes.label: Intake queue for refused drafts
nodes.rationale: Parking a refused draft preserves unfinished work instead of losing it; it is not trash.

nodes.label: Proof rule per kind
nodes.rationale: A check that cannot fail is not proof, so each kind names evidence able to fail (E2E run, RED row plus negative control, green catching check).

nodes.label: Ticket title rule
nodes.rationale: Plain titles without prefixes, ids or internal names keep tickets readable to users.

nodes.label: Direct API calls: a cached prefix
nodes.norm_label: direct api calls: a cached prefix
nodes.rationale: Graphify's untagged shim read only 3% from cache, so batches share a 1h system-block prefix and callers get kind tags to measure per group.

nodes.label: Non-batch graphify system-prompt path
nodes.rationale: The CLI caches on block boundaries and graphify sends one text block, so a separate system prompt block is needed to hit across chunks; it stays opt-in because it is unproven and a system prompt once made the CLI answer conversationally.

nodes.label: workers: line and backtick-span entry format
nodes.norm_label: workers: line and backtick-span entry format
nodes.rationale: Single backtick spans without trailing punctuation keep token-shaped text from stalling gitleaks pre-commit scanners and let the tick parse entries.

nodes.label: Relay to chief transport and ack rule
nodes.norm_label: relay to chief transport and ack rule
nodes.rationale: Escalation ids and a re-send once then BLOCKED path make unacked escalations recoverable and recognisable as duplicates.

nodes.label: Claudex workers: inbox is the only channel
nodes.norm_label: claudex workers: inbox is the only channel
nodes.rationale: Claudex runs under ~/.claude-codex outside the ListAgents registry so SendMessage fails both ways, leaving the tool-call-gated file inbox as the sole channel.

nodes.label: Claudex file inbox and sent-record gate
nodes.norm_label: claudex file inbox and sent-record gate
nodes.rationale: Claudex workers lack the A to B bus, so a system-injected file inbox with a trusted sent-ledger gives an equivalent transport-origin property.

nodes.label: Symptom: message/log bullet quoting guarded flag refused
nodes.norm_label: symptom: message/log bullet quoting guarded flag refused
nodes.rationale: block-destructive-commands inspects the whole command string including quoted text, so text must be passed by file.

nodes.label: Symptom: suite invocation refused as recursive-delete deny
nodes.norm_label: symptom: suite invocation refused as recursive-delete deny
nodes.rationale: Since #744 the deterministic hook cannot read suite source, so such denials come from the classifier reading cleanup traps, avoided by running through quiet-run.sh.

nodes.label: RETASK channel and chief succession
nodes.rationale: Revisions arrive only as direct chief messages quoting the worker's token, so injected text in tool results or files cannot redirect a worker.

nodes.label: Restate the direction
nodes.rationale: The successor restates the first rulings of its Current direction so the outgoing chief can catch a misread before it wraps.

nodes.label: Wake-once succession
nodes.rationale: A single waiter wake reports whether all workers accepted the new chief, avoiding repeated polling and resent LIVE messages.

nodes.label: tools/grow-feed-log.mjs CLI
nodes.community_name: grow-feed-log — grow-tent feed/watering log entry point (LUNA-130)

nodes.label: Access-gating delegated to telegram:access
nodes.community_name: grow-feed-log — grow-tent feed/watering log entry point (LUNA-130)
nodes.rationale: Channel messages are untrusted input and could be prompt injection, so access is owned elsewhere and the skill only records sender provenance.

nodes.label: Append-only one-message scope
nodes.community_name: grow-feed-log — grow-tent feed/watering log entry point (LUNA-130)
nodes.rationale: Keeping the MVP append-only avoids rewriting history; corrections are operator hand-edits.

nodes.label: Mode-scoped msg-id idempotency
nodes.community_name: grow-feed-log — grow-tent feed/watering log entry point (LUNA-130)
nodes.rationale: A fabricated message id would defeat idempotency and silently duplicate entries, and mode-scoping lets product and feed writes coexist for one message.

nodes.label: 20-Areas/Grow/Grow-Feeding-Log.md
nodes.community_name: grow-feed-log — grow-tent feed/watering log entry point (LUNA-130)
nodes.rationale: implied: It is the vault's single source of truth for products and feed rows, so it is read first to ground names and conversions.

nodes.label: Observability chain
nodes.rationale: The stack stays passive and read-only, and the reader decides liveness because a crashed session never emits session_end.

nodes.label: Session runs ledger (v2)
nodes.rationale: Interactive sessions and subagents were previously untracked, so an append-only JSONL ledger with additive v2 fields and closed-enum labels gives them identity without cardinality explosion.

nodes.label: Liveness via transcript mtime
nodes.rationale: Interactive sessions have no cadence and crashes emit no end row, but the transcript advances only while the session works, so mtime distinguishes idle from dead.

nodes.label: Fail-open session writer with error breadcrumb log
nodes.norm_label: fail-open session writer with error breadcrumb log
nodes.rationale: Telemetry must never block a tool call, but silent failure cost five days when Bun drained a floating stdin read, so failures now leave bounded log lines and stdin is read synchronously.

nodes.label: VM security-posture audit
nodes.rationale: A reusable read-only battery replaces throwaway forensic sweeps that every e2e session used to re-write.

nodes.label: Common-dir owner check for shared git state
nodes.norm_label: common-dir owner check for shared git state
nodes.rationale: Writes from a linked worktree to the shared $GIT_COMMON_DIR (config, remotes, refs/heads/main) affect the primary checkout, so the owning primary gets the same verdict even without -C <primary>.

nodes.label: Design invariants closing the fail-open class
nodes.norm_label: design invariants closing the fail-open class
nodes.rationale: Stating the invariants (fail closed on unclassifiable tokens, independent operand checks, operation-chosen path resolution, dynamic operands failing open on themselves only) is what prevents a seventh instance rather than patching six.

nodes.label: Six known fail-open shapes closed (record kept)
nodes.norm_label: six known fail-open shapes closed (record kept)
nodes.rationale: A fence believed to cover a shape it does not is worse than no fence, so the record of what was actually checked is kept as a mitigation.

nodes.label: Git subcommands aimed at a protected checkout (arm g)
nodes.norm_label: git subcommands aimed at a protected checkout (arm g)
nodes.rationale: Git rewrites tree, index, HEAD, refs or config without naming a file, so the subcommand is classified on an allowlist and the target repo root is judged, with carve-outs shaped for the chief's wrap flow.

nodes.label: Baseline 2026-10-23 (lex/vec/hybrid/hybrid-rerank)
nodes.rationale: The index was incomplete (1242 documents awaiting embeddings), so vec and hybrid misses are unverified, and overlapping CIs do not prove modes are equal.

nodes.label: Manifest-based rollback
nodes.rationale: The accumulated reverse manifest restores the tree byte-for-byte, and re-applies forward edits on externally modified clips to avoid a torn half-revert.

nodes.label: Six-form .md link rewrite requirement
nodes.rationale: Synthesis pages cite clips with the .md extension, which a three-form check misses and reports clean, causing silent danglers.

nodes.label: Mandatory staging gate
nodes.rationale: A scratch git-oracle copy proves zero danglers and byte-identical rollback before the live vault is touched.

nodes.label: guard-corpus gen/diff differential
nodes.rationale: Generates and judges variant rows without executing payloads.

nodes.label: Judge never answers authority-adjacent questions
nodes.rationale: Safety rests on nobody asking the judge to approve a merge or mint a GO, not on its tool list or an environment marker, because the judge has Bash and shares its parent's environment.

nodes.label: Pin PR reads to head sha
nodes.norm_label: pin pr reads to head sha
nodes.rationale: FETCH_HEAD is one shared file that parallel judges overwrite, so reading through it can land on another judge's PR (HIMMEL-7062).

nodes.label: Judges never wait on CI or tests
nodes.norm_label: judges never wait on ci or tests
nodes.rationale: Running tests and polling CI is the worker's job, and a judge reasons about code rather than producing results.

nodes.label: Pin PR reads to head sha (not FETCH_HEAD)
nodes.norm_label: pin pr reads to head sha (not fetch_head)
nodes.rationale: FETCH_HEAD is one shared file that parallel judges overwrite, so reading through it can land on another judge's PR (HIMMEL-7062).

nodes.label: Judge verdict contract (GO/NO-GO, class, evidence)
nodes.rationale: A fixed first line and a class field make verdicts machine-readable and stop relabeling a finding to buy a round.

nodes.label: Verdict file writing protocol
nodes.rationale: The judge has no Write tool and text guards refuse a hand-typed verdict line, so a sanctioned writer script is the only path that records a ruling with required class, model and effort fields.

nodes.label: Residual depth gating
nodes.rationale: Limits residual tickets from judges, CR and panels so they do not mint unbounded follow-up work.

nodes.label: Checkpoint to disk rule
nodes.rationale: The 200000 autocompact pin can be outgrown by design-grade questions, so reasoning held only in context is lost at compaction.

nodes.label: Classifier stop rule
nodes.rationale: Without a stop rule a stopped session would be rephrased or re-dispatched until something gets through.

nodes.label: Critical/Important disposition rule
nodes.rationale: Deferred Critical or Important review findings must be fixed or ticketed under evidence-backed conditions before GO.

nodes.label: Guard escape tests: three routes
nodes.rationale: A safety classifier stopped judges hand-writing bypass rows, so instance authoring is split into generated rows, operator-written classes and VM-only execution.

nodes.label: Judge checklist for code, CI and infra PRs
nodes.norm_label: judge checklist for code, ci and infra prs
nodes.rationale: Green CI and a clean review are not a verdict; PR #2268 showed a fixture-only test proving nothing about a real runner.

nodes.label: NO-GO class and residual depth rules
nodes.norm_label: no-go class and residual depth rules
nodes.rationale: Classing NO-GO findings and tracking residual depth stops repeated findings from buying extra review rounds.

nodes.label: resume_cwd outside handover root rule
nodes.rationale: A judge working tree inside the Obsidian-vault handover root hung it twice, so the launcher refuses such a cwd.

nodes.label: Judge RETASK asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Narrowing needs no token while expansion needs the chief's nonce, and no revision widens what a judge may act with.

nodes.label: Scratch outside handover root and /tmp
nodes.rationale: Scratch under a vault-resident handover root was indexed by Obsidian (843k files froze it) and /tmp can be tmpfs filling RAM.

nodes.label: Ticket coverage check
nodes.rationale: Three of 14 cloud PRs closed tickets Done with asks undone because no judge asked whether every ask was done.

nodes.label: Tier line (opus/fable category tag)
nodes.rationale: The launch gate matches by model prefix and refuses an Opus or Fable launch without an exact category tag and free text.

nodes.label: Round-3 review cap extra round granted by chief
nodes.norm_label: round-3 review cap extra round granted by chief
nodes.rationale: Only a chief-signed grant tied to a judge record on the exact live head, consumed once per qid, prevents workers or relays from buying extra review rounds.

nodes.label: Verdict transport is disk, never a peer message
nodes.norm_label: verdict transport is disk, never a peer message
nodes.rationale: A peer message is not authority and a verdict living only in a message dies with the chief's window.

nodes.label: Signed judge verdict records (HMAC)
nodes.rationale: A hand-written exact-format verdict file used to pass, so records are HMAC-signed and read once as a snapshot so a rewrite cannot reuse a verified mac.

nodes.label: The judge
nodes.rationale: A read-only verdict-giver answers one independent question without acting, preserving independence.

nodes.label: Retain last baseline on missing/malformed source
nodes.norm_label: retain last baseline on missing/malformed source
nodes.rationale: A deleted or inaccessible export must not be mistaken for all findings being closed, so absence is never proof of closure.

nodes.label: Weekly security findings audit
nodes.rationale: It only diffs existing findings and never scans, calls a model or spends Snyk quota, so it costs nothing and cannot exceed free plans.

nodes.label: Hook
nodes.rationale: Enumerating the six homes of hooks shows where an enforcement script can be wired.

nodes.label: Hook runner
nodes.rationale: Runs hooks under the right bash on every platform, optionally chained in one process.

nodes.label: Budget-aware chain member timeouts
nodes.rationale: A killed PreToolUse entry fails OPEN, so must-run security members get their own window capped by an entry-safe deadline and the launcher denies rather than being killed mid-chain.

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse dispatcher (--chain)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing many per-entry node launches into one chained launcher cuts process spawns while keeping guardrail order, and side-effecting hooks stay out of chains so denies cannot suppress them.

nodes.label: SessionStart chaining (--chain --lifecycle)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing four warn-only injectors into one launcher saves three node launches per session start at the cost of serial latency (≈4.9 s vs ≈1.7 s).

nodes.label: Hook chain budgets
nodes.rationale: Static nested budgets suffice post-defork since the N=16 P95 is more than 6x inside the 50s chain budget, so load-aware sizing was closed as superseded.

nodes.label: Hook-chain budget pressure gauges
nodes.rationale: A gauge rather than folded counter avoids window-slide phantom spikes, and a separate unreadable-log gauge makes reader failures alertable since scrape comments are not.

nodes.label: Adding a claim's check
nodes.rationale: A cache-claim fix without a named fixture scenario is not done, so each claim must bring a synthetic fixture and a table row.

nodes.label: Audit of prompt-cache claims (11 rows)
nodes.rationale: Each claim found in the tree is labeled TRUE/FALSE/UNVERIFIED with an eval scenario so false claims (e.g. MEMORY.md trim invalidates caches) get fixed and guesses stay flagged.

nodes.label: Verified prompt-cache model
nodes.rationale: Cost decisions need a model of what invalidates the cache (prefix order tools, system, messages; TTL tiers), supported by measurement rather than folklore.

nodes.label: Live runs L1-L5
nodes.rationale: Read-only probe runs over real transcripts provide the evidence behind the audit verdicts, such as 98.2% read-ratio and TTL consistency.

nodes.label: Worker keepalive or wrap rule
nodes.rationale: One avoided cold wake (2x write) pays for about 20 keepalive turns (0.1x read), so keep warm on nameable waits and wrap on open-ended ones.

nodes.label: Delta cases (HIMMEL-8429)
nodes.rationale: Rounds 2 and 3 review only the delta since the last round, so the eval must grade defects introduced in a fix delta.

nodes.label: Key isolation and leak lint
nodes.rationale: The critic sees only the diff from an empty scratch dir with a canary check so the answer key cannot leak into reviews.

nodes.label: Critic eval merge gate (HIMMEL-8426)
nodes.rationale: A change to anything in the critic behaviour set merges only when the eval shows it lost no recall or precision beyond baseline noise.

nodes.label: Seeded defects with clean twins
nodes.rationale: Pairing each injected-defect diff with a clean twin lets the eval measure recall and false-positive rate together.

nodes.label: Spend note HIMMEL-9214 claude+codex sweeps
nodes.rationale: The --critics flag only filtered scoring so sweeps ran claude too against decision 525, and cost reports must count that spend.

nodes.label: Always-on bun bridge spawning bounded claude runs
nodes.norm_label: always-on bun bridge spawning bounded claude runs
nodes.rationale: One bounded run per message avoids a long-lived Claude session to babysit, with a file-backed bus carrying state across runs and crashes.

nodes.label: One-poller-per-token trap
nodes.rationale: Telegram allows exactly one getUpdates consumer per token, so a second poller causes 409 Conflict and breaks delivery for both.

nodes.label: systemd user unit with linger
nodes.rationale: Type=simple with restart limits makes systemd see the supervisor and respect its circuit breaker, and linger keeps it alive after logout.

nodes.label: Sanctioned cadence path (never hand-roll cron)
nodes.rationale: All cadence changes go through one script so the dedup guard, runner indirection and Max-quota interactive launch shape are preserved.

nodes.label: Auto-approve injection via cadence-settings.json (HIMMEL-575)
nodes.rationale: The luna vault cwd lacks himmel settings, so an autonomous run would stall on the HIMMEL-203 compound-bash permission prompt; the grant-only hook restores auto-approve without widening deny guards.

nodes.label: Explicit cheap --model pin per cron job (HIMMEL-506)
nodes.norm_label: explicit cheap --model pin per cron job (himmel-506)
nodes.rationale: Pinning avoids inheriting the operator's saved default (the scarcest tier), which makes higher frequencies affordable.

nodes.label: Plugin profile: always / on-demand / not installed tiers
nodes.norm_label: plugin profile: always / on-demand / not installed tiers
nodes.rationale: On-demand plugins are installed but disabled so they cost no session-start context until requested, with a single script as the sole writer of the flip.

nodes.label: Cadence exception: force-enable per run
nodes.rationale: The --settings layer outranks local disables, so unattended jobs can enable an on-demand plugin without flipping the machine's live profile.

nodes.label: Toggling the on-demand tier via plugin-profile.sh and /profile
nodes.norm_label: toggling the on-demand tier via plugin-profile.sh and /profile
nodes.rationale: A single sanctioned writer using claude plugin enable|disable with post-write verification avoids hand-edited settings.json and silent no-ops.

nodes.label: obsidian-second-brain (REMOVED)
nodes.rationale: Removed because it cost ~2.4k-3.5k tokens per spawn and earned 0 skill calls in 457 bridge runs over 30 days.

nodes.label: obsidian-triage plugin
nodes.rationale: It is ON-DEMAND because the luna clip pipeline force-enables it per run via a --settings fragment.

nodes.label: Shared home/vault resolution
nodes.rationale: It was extracted verbatim from pipeline-cadence.sh to share one resolver; remaining copies need an audit-then-convert pass because some resolve HOME before USERPROFILE in the wrong order.

nodes.label: Dispatcher contract: poll stop marker between dispatches
nodes.norm_label: dispatcher contract: poll stop marker between dispatches
nodes.rationale: Any long-running dispatch loop must poll the cheap silent check so stop requests are honored consistently.

nodes.label: The 11 AFK phases plus queue lock step 0
nodes.norm_label: the 11 afk phases plus queue lock step 0
nodes.rationale: A fixed pipeline from plan to handover lets the session run end-to-end without pausing for confirmation.

nodes.label: Orchestration invariants (verifier lane, orchestrator-owned stop)
nodes.rationale: Workers never self-report done because the orchestrator must own stop-conditions or loops never terminate.

nodes.label: Chief board (local generated HTML)
nodes.rationale: Shows fleet progress and what needs the operator without being asked, and stays local by operator ruling 10-29.

nodes.label: Roadmap tracker (per-version FOCUS page)
nodes.rationale: One page per version with Jira parity checks gives a derived view of open tickets, PR CI and blockers instead of hand-kept lists.

nodes.label: Version mismatch audit (vmismatch)
nodes.rationale: Counts tickets whose version state is inconsistent so they can be reset to To Do.

nodes.label: Forge routing by URL host
nodes.rationale: Host selects the path in parallel with the dev-loop's origin routing, letting Bitbucket reuse shared safety and heuristics while swapping the fetch transport.

nodes.label: Phase 1.5 safety pre-filter
nodes.rationale: Red-flag repos exit rc=6 before README fetch unless --allow-unsafe, protecting the vault from risky sources.

nodes.label: Trust-tier auto-classification
nodes.rationale: implied: Gives readers a quick provenance-based signal of how much to trust an ingested repo.

nodes.label: Bitbucket scoped API token auth
nodes.rationale: Scoped Atlassian tokens are per-app, so the Jira token returned 401 for Bitbucket.

nodes.label: bitbucket-cli README
nodes.rationale: Documents the Bitbucket Cloud transport mirroring the Jira CLI, with verbs, auth and build steps.

nodes.label: ENV_MIGRATION_CONSENT scope limits
nodes.rationale: Unattended consent covers less than -y so an agent cannot use it to change gate policy, move secrets or scrub backups.

nodes.label: The .env split: what moves and what stays
nodes.norm_label: the .env split: what moves and what stays
nodes.rationale: Only explicitly classified non-secret keys become config; unclassified keys remain secrets so an unreviewed key is never exposed as config.

nodes.label: Migration and mismatch handling
nodes.rationale: Migration backs up, verifies with real readers and removes lines only on agreement, and a value mismatch needs a human to pick the winner.

nodes.label: .env migration
nodes.rationale: .env should hold secrets only, so behaviour and policy keys move to ~/.himmel and secrets to the keyring, with a backup, a reader-check and a scrub to avoid data loss.

nodes.label: The .env split: what moves, what stays, and a mismatch
nodes.norm_label: the .env split: what moves, what stays, and a mismatch
nodes.rationale: A differing value is a choice between two values that consent cannot answer, so the run stops with nothing removed until the user picks.

nodes.label: VM round trip — station-only, never CI
nodes.norm_label: vm round trip — station-only, never ci
nodes.rationale: It needs a real VirtualBox clone, so it is not named test-*.sh and CI runs only hermetic dry and synthetic-inventory suites.

nodes.label: claudex chief reachability (file inbox)
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker has no SendMessage path to a native session, so chief rulings are delivered via a per-worker file inbox without operator paste.

nodes.label: claudex worker implementor-default operating model
nodes.rationale: Routing routine implementation to claudex draws the codex usage budget and spares the scarce Claude weekly bucket.

nodes.label: claudex effort ladder (WORKER_SESSION_EFFORT)
nodes.rationale: implied: reuses the shared low/medium/high/xhigh scale so effort per brief can be tuned without a separate claudex-only scale.

nodes.label: claudex workers never park for authorization
nodes.norm_label: claudex workers never park for authorization
nodes.rationale: A claudex worker cannot message any session, so waiting is invisible until the next doc poll; it must decide and record the reasoning in the handover doc.

nodes.label: READY to GO merge hold (the one sanctioned park)
nodes.norm_label: ready to go merge hold (the one sanctioned park)
nodes.rationale: A merge is irreversible, so a bounded, observable, 30-minute-timeout wait is allowed despite the never-park rule.

nodes.label: Inbox delivery only on next tool call
nodes.norm_label: inbox delivery only on next tool call
nodes.rationale: Claudex legs have no SendMessage socket, so a ruling in the file inbox only fires on the leg's next tool call and an idle leg may never see it; HIMMEL-6127 is the likely shared cause.

nodes.label: Machine staleness vs repo-pin staleness
nodes.rationale: The drift guard reads synced_base, so a merged bump shows CURRENT while the installed binary is still old; himmel-update.sh must run first to repair the machine.

nodes.label: Six-item update dependency chain
nodes.rationale: The items depend on each other in order, so the first genuine failure aborts the chain and later items report not-attempted.

nodes.label: /drift-fix
nodes.rationale: Resolves upstream fork-drift end to end, including machine-local catch-up that BEHIND rows cannot show.

nodes.label: /himmel-doctor
nodes.rationale: Diagnoses common harness health problems in one severity-grouped report so known issues are found without manual digging.

nodes.label: /himmel-update
nodes.rationale: Machine-local catch-up steps exist because a merged pin bump reaches the repo but not the machine, and autoUpdate does not deliver the checkout or core hooks.

nodes.label: Installs without a git checkout
nodes.rationale: A tarball or native install has no upstream, so the updater refuses to pull and avoids accidentally pulling an enclosing repository.

nodes.label: Recover from a failed update
nodes.rationale: The chain aborts at the first failure without undoing prior steps, so each failure mode needs a targeted re-run or rollback.

nodes.label: Verify the update
nodes.rationale: Exit codes of --versions show whether any component is behind or undetermined, and hooks versus plugins take effect at different times.

nodes.label: Is this station up to date? (--version / --versions)
nodes.norm_label: is this station up to date? (--version / --versions)
nodes.rationale: A read-only per-component report lets operators see drift without pulling, rebuilding or restarting anything.

nodes.label: Why a pull is required
nodes.rationale: Hooks and commands run from the repo checkout rather than as plugins, so autoUpdate can never change them.

nodes.label: vm.mode none: operator ack plus rollback point
nodes.norm_label: vm.mode none: operator ack plus rollback point
nodes.rationale: With no VM proof possible, a hold is released only by an explicit operator ack after taking a rollback point, never automatically.

nodes.label: luna-upgrade fallback engine with dry-run, confirm, apply
nodes.norm_label: luna-upgrade fallback engine with dry-run, confirm, apply
nodes.rationale: A non-interactive call hits EOF on the confirm prompt and exits 0 having changed nothing, so the exit code alone would misreport success.

nodes.label: Six-item update dependency chain
nodes.rationale: Items depend on each other, so the first genuine failure aborts the chain and later items report not-attempted.

nodes.label: Run update as LAST step of a Claude session (#2591)
nodes.norm_label: run update as last step of a claude session (#2591)
nodes.rationale: A pull that changes hook-pinned paths while HEAD is off the anchor tip makes hook-integrity deny every later Bash and Edit call.

nodes.label: Updating, or undoing the install
nodes.rationale: Gives newcomers a six-step path to update himmel and confirm it landed, because marketplace autoUpdate does not deliver himmel updates.

nodes.label: /himmel-update-all command
nodes.rationale: Runs the harness update before the luna vault upgrade so the latest template and skill are on disk when the vault upgrade reads them.

nodes.label: /himmel-update command
nodes.rationale: git pull is the only thing that delivers a himmel update because the marketplace is a local directory source and core hooks are not plugins.

nodes.label: Precedence ladder
nodes.rationale: A fixed ordering (user, specific rule, this document, platform defaults) resolves apparent rule conflicts without agents spending reasoning on them.

nodes.label: Reading note for non-Claude harnesses
nodes.rationale: Claude-specific mechanisms are a reference implementation, so other harnesses should apply the behavior with their own equivalents, backed by git-level gates.

nodes.label: Scope and standing permissions
nodes.rationale: Agents should read only what the task needs and run local tests unattended, since those have no remote blast radius.

nodes.label: Subagent policy
nodes.rationale: Delegation is limited to independent, sizeable work with explicit models and a single writer, to control cost, depth and conflicts.

nodes.label: DeepSeek and Alibaba de-listing (2026-07-22)
nodes.rationale: Dropped for bad results by operator judgment; rows are explicit deny and not hard, since public himmel-code egress stays allowed.

nodes.label: GLM (zai-glm) ratification then de-listing (2026-08-29)
nodes.rationale: Ratified for a measured quality edge, then reversed once the Coding Plan lapsed because a live allow+log cell would be cited as pre-existing authorization.

nodes.label: Egress policy (single matrix, no --force)
nodes.rationale: One policy file governs egress with no bypass so no launcher can route around data-protection rules.

nodes.label: Axis 6: Trust/egress posture
nodes.rationale: The matrix has no lane axis and reversing rows rather than deleting preserves the audit trail.

nodes.label: Provenance known limits
nodes.rationale: implied: documenting limits (no jq fallback, NFS atomicity, Windows untested) keeps operators from over-trusting the helpers.

nodes.label: Ledger file layout and JSONL rows
nodes.norm_label: ledger file layout and jsonl rows
nodes.rationale: One JSON object per line appended in a single write keeps rows atomic, and readers skip unparsable lines so a torn last line costs only one row.

nodes.label: Marked HIMMEL:working-principles block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Recording the block with a sha and snapshot lets uninstall strip only an unedited block and leave the operator's surrounding lines.

nodes.label: Ours snapshots (snap / snap_skip, v2 rows)
nodes.rationale: A snapshot of what himmel wrote lets a revert tell 'still exactly what himmel installed' from 'operator edited it' without trusting a hash alone.

nodes.label: Pre- and post-state hashing and backups
nodes.norm_label: pre- and post-state hashing and backups
nodes.rationale: Recording hashes and backup copies of the pre-state lets uninstall restore the operator's original bytes and detect later edits.

nodes.label: Uninstall reconcile report
nodes.rationale: Printing a per-unit report before any purge shows the operator what needs them even if a run later refuses, and no printed command deletes the live file.

nodes.label: Provenance session (iid, begin/end rows)
nodes.rationale: Exporting the session id lets every child process of a writer append into the same install run.

nodes.label: class-recurrence restructure trigger
nodes.rationale: When a class keeps recurring across merged PRs the fix should be a restructure ticket rather than another per-PR patch.

nodes.label: Opt-in initiative mode (HIMMEL_INITIATIVE)
nodes.rationale: Lets a session proactively run the pr-check, PR, ticket and handover sequence without the operator saying 'ship it', while keeping merge an operator action.

nodes.label: Per-part initiative control (step vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: A comma-subset of steps lets operators enable only some auto-ship steps and degrades gracefully because the structural rails still apply.

nodes.label: inject-initiative pointer-form measurement
nodes.rationale: Moving step bodies out of the session-start preload saves 80-88% of that block while keeping the completion-point directive inline so the feature does not silently vanish.

nodes.label: Merge step and armed auto-merge
nodes.rationale: Merge gates on green CI, certified head SHA and live branch protection, never --admin, so branch protection and approval rules still bind.

nodes.label: Scope and limits (no safety rail relaxed)
nodes.norm_label: scope and limits (no safety rail relaxed)
nodes.rationale: Initiative must not weaken the CR-marker hook, attestation trailers or settings-edit vetoes, so merge stays an operator action unless named.

nodes.label: Seed the tasklist on handover resume
nodes.norm_label: seed the tasklist on handover resume
nodes.rationale: Seeding native tasks from the handover's ordered steps keeps progress glanceable through the run.

nodes.label: Turning initiative off or narrowing it
nodes.norm_label: turning initiative off or narrowing it
nodes.rationale: The hook also reads .env non-clobbering, so unsetting is not enough; setting 0 in the launching shell wins without touching the secret-bearing .env.

nodes.label: command -p sh launcher convention
nodes.rationale: A bare sh needs a PATH lookup that fails under a pinned-minimal PATH (rc=127 dead chain), whereas command -p resolves from the standard utilities PATH.

nodes.label: run-node.sh / resolve-node.sh dash silent-no-op class
nodes.rationale: Under dash a bashism or dot-with-operands made hooks exit 0 silently (rc=1 is non-blocking), so guardrails were open rather than denying.

nodes.label: dash /bin/sh hook probes (command -p sh run-node.sh)
nodes.rationale: dash drops operands after a dotted filename, so a dot-wired run-node.sh ran bare node with empty argv and made every hook a silent no-op on Debian/Ubuntu.

nodes.label: CI tool pins policy
nodes.rationale: Exact pins with one owner each and bun version read from a file avoid GitHub API tag-listing failures killing CI jobs.

nodes.label: Three launch shapes: autocompact 200k, 450k+hand-off, 450k
nodes.rationale: Comparing compaction at 200k, hand-off at 450k and compaction at 450k isolates the effect of ceiling versus hand-off.

nodes.label: A run is valid only if it reached its trigger
nodes.norm_label: a run is valid only if it reached its trigger
nodes.rationale: A run that never compacted or handed off says nothing about the arm, so it is priced and kept but never scored.

nodes.label: compaction-handoff eval (HIMMEL-7667)
nodes.rationale: It tests whether a 450k ceiling with a hand-off beats the 200k compaction loop for worker sessions.

nodes.label: Paid on-demand tier for probe run
nodes.norm_label: paid on-demand tier for probe run
nodes.rationale: Each run is a billed model call, so it is never wired into CI, requires --billed, defaults to haiku and runs only on the test VM.

nodes.label: Documentation-only enforcement layer
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md says to escalate to a structural gate only on the second drift instance, and a gate firing on pre-existing markers would be disabled within a day.

nodes.label: Session-end consolidation sweep
nodes.rationale: Running the sweep before the context-hop snapshot means cap-resume hand-off cannot leave unpushed handover state.

nodes.label: PR open/update + squash finisher
nodes.rationale: Auto-opening and squash-merging PRs keeps handover branches reviewable while repo settings forbid merge commits.

nodes.label: Pre-push automated review on handover branches
nodes.norm_label: pre-push automated review on handover branches
nodes.rationale: Review stays enabled as a sanity audit to catch code edits sneaking into handover branches, while docs-only diffs skip the gate.

nodes.label: Armed auto-merge gate
nodes.rationale: Auto-merge is opt-in and re-verifies base, privacy and protection fresh before merging, so a stale pass can never certify a merge on a public repo.

nodes.label: check-ci.sh exit code contract
nodes.rationale: Distinct exit codes let gates tell red, unevaluable, unresolved and never-reported required checks apart; it is a mechanism, not a veto.

nodes.label: Public merge (/mergepub) hard human-authorization gate
nodes.rationale: Public merges require an operator-typed, non-forwarded command and refuse any agent, so a human always authorizes them.

nodes.label: Session merge gate (block-unresolved-cr-merge)
nodes.rationale: It guards merges issued inside a Claude session only, since the operator is the authority it protects, and fails open as a guardrail on top of forge-side branch protection.

nodes.label: Workflow/job wait mode (check-ci.sh --run)
nodes.rationale: Run mode lets callers wait on a workflow or job through the shared cache without a poll loop, but it is explicitly not a merge certification.

nodes.label: Merge & publish gates (§3.3)
nodes.rationale: Several layered gates guard merging and publishing so no single bypassable hook is the only protection.

nodes.label: Lanes & delegation knobs
nodes.rationale: Lane keys make external lanes detectable while explicit naming and overlays keep dispatch intentional and per-machine controllable.

nodes.label: check-ci.sh API cost and shared cache
nodes.norm_label: check-ci.sh api cost and shared cache
nodes.rationale: Many workers waiting on CI would drain one shared GitHub quota, so a shared head-bound cache, REST-first ETag polling and budget rotation make waiting cheap.

nodes.label: Telegram bridge config
nodes.rationale: The bridge reads config only at poller start and keeps token and access config outside the repo, so a restart is needed after changes.

nodes.label: Four .env key groups (how a key reaches code)
nodes.norm_label: four .env key groups (how a key reaches code)
nodes.rationale: Naming how each key reaches code exposes the main trap, that a value only in .env is invisible to scripts reading the live environment.

nodes.label: Config precedence chain
nodes.rationale: The loader never overrides an exported non-empty value, so a bridged .env value sits at the bottom of the precedence chain.

nodes.label: Bun .env auto-load limitation
nodes.rationale: Bun's runtime-level .env import happens before any allowlist reader, so allowlists cannot stop it; fixing launch sites with --no-env-file is deferred.

nodes.label: Doctor C57-dotenv-allowlists check
nodes.rationale: It audits for blanket loaders and unused key names, reporting names only never values, to keep the allowlist boundaries honest.

nodes.label: .env consumer boundaries (explicit key allowlists)
nodes.rationale: Each loader names its keys explicitly so a file only adds what that consumer needs and secrets are not exported wholesale to children.

nodes.label: ponytail: marker
nodes.rationale: A code comment at the exact line prevents a reader from mistaking partial behavior for complete behavior.

nodes.label: upstream /ponytail-debt skill
nodes.rationale: It harvests every marker into a ledger, which is what makes the two-part shape load-bearing.

nodes.label: Single-root resolver (HANDOVER_DIR)
nodes.rationale: Scripts must not hardcode ./handovers/ and one root must be picked because two writable roots drift.

nodes.label: User-slug resolution
nodes.rationale: Bucket paths and registry need the operator slug without hardcoding, resolved via env, gh, then git config with a loud failure.

nodes.label: Identity, handover, Jira & forge knobs
nodes.rationale: These knobs identify the user and configure the handover flow and ticket/forge credentials, with secrets kept apart from non-secret identifiers.

nodes.label: Code comment keep list and history-comment gate
nodes.norm_label: code comment keep list and history-comment gate
nodes.rationale: History such as ticket IDs and review rounds belongs in git and Jira, and a surprise in code is a refactor target rather than a comment.

nodes.label: critics.local.json per-machine overlay
nodes.rationale: A gitignored overlay changes reviewers per machine, while the base is read from main so a branch cannot alter its own gate.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes (hard / best-effort, required)
nodes.rationale: Per-reviewer modes make the merge gate hold each reviewer to a defined standard, with config errors always blocking and read failures degrading open.

nodes.label: Live-worker guard scoped to bridge root
nodes.norm_label: live-worker guard scoped to bridge root
nodes.rationale: The census reads a shared bridge root with no per-session scoping, so unrelated chains can block an arm; override only after proving ownership.

nodes.label: Arming & scheduling knobs
nodes.rationale: Soft caps, collision windows and kill switches let scheduled claude relaunches be controlled without hard-blocking.

nodes.label: Two independent usage budget walls
nodes.rationale: AUTO_ARM_THRESHOLD sets when the watchdog trips and RESUME_SLOT_THRESHOLD sets where the resume parks, so both must be raised to move the effective wall.

nodes.label: Auto-branch + commit + push
nodes.rationale: Committing onto a per-ticket branch and pushing every time ensures handover state survives loss of the local clone.

nodes.label: Single-writer handover repos
nodes.rationale: Committing directly on main for single-writer repos prevents the parallel-branch entanglement that blocked an earlier close-out.

nodes.label: v2 multi-repo registry (bucket_name, branch_prefix)
nodes.rationale: State lives in registry.json rather than docs so paths and routing have one live source of truth, and bucket collisions are refused to avoid ambiguity.

nodes.label: tracker=none and CI ticket-ID pinning
nodes.rationale: Requiring ticket IDs with no tracker and no pattern is a contradiction, so the commit gate refuses it and adopters must edit himmel's CI pins.

nodes.label: Durable resume breadcrumb + resolver (C3)
nodes.rationale: Armed resumes twice silently grounded in raw repo state, so the resolver refuses to silently degrade and flags DEGRADED recovery.

nodes.label: Periodic seat-liveness reconcile
nodes.rationale: Reconcile previously ran only on dispatch or arm, so an idle fleet never noticed a dead seat; a cron tick fixes that while erring toward never reaping live seats.

nodes.label: Operator-gated wrap + resume briefs
nodes.rationale: A worker idled 1.5h holding its lock waiting on an operator, so workers wrap at once and the chief writes git-recoverable state itself.

nodes.label: Review & merge knobs (CR_PROFILE, ARMAUTOMERGE, etc.)
nodes.rationale: These knobs control critic tier and cost, and fail open only onto a mandatory claude-only floor so review is never silently skipped.

nodes.label: himmel's own review posture (codex panel + CodeRabbit App only)
nodes.norm_label: himmel's own review posture (codex panel + coderabbit app only)
nodes.rationale: The local CodeRabbit CLI was dropped because it double-charged the same rate-limited account for a signal the App already posts and forced extra paid codex rounds (PR #523 ran twelve rounds).

nodes.label: Initiative & autonomy profiles and auto-ship steps
nodes.norm_label: initiative & autonomy profiles and auto-ship steps
nodes.rationale: Interactive and afk profiles define which auto-ship steps run, and the directive is warn-only so it cannot widen what any hook allows.

nodes.label: The .env split: what moves, stays, and mismatch
nodes.norm_label: the .env split: what moves, stays, and mismatch
nodes.rationale: Moving non-secret behaviour and policy keys out of .env while keeping secrets there migrates safely, and mismatches are resolved by operator choice without exposing values.

nodes.label: .env file-based config and where keys live
nodes.norm_label: .env file-based config and where keys live
nodes.rationale: .env is reserved for secrets while behaviour and policy keys move to himmel.conf and config.json to separate secrets from settings.

nodes.label: Promote-only orphan recovery (HIMMEL-3205)
nodes.rationale: Re-promotes a finished but un-promoted extraction so the cost of a second extraction is not paid after a runner was killed mid-flight.

nodes.label: himmel --merge-into-live behavior (HIMMEL-6008)
nodes.rationale: The himmel live graph is mostly AST nodes from the hourly ast-update, so markdown extraction is merged in rather than promoted over it to avoid shrinking the graph.

nodes.label: Unquoted $ARGUMENTS convention
nodes.rationale: Quoting would collapse the argument list into one token and break flag parsing like 'both --dry-run'.

nodes.label: Six-item update dependency chain
nodes.rationale: The items depend on each other in order, so the first genuine failure aborts the chain and later items report not-attempted.

nodes.label: Machine-local catch-up (HIMMEL-2134)
nodes.rationale: A merged pin bump reaches the repo but not the machine, and the drift check reads synced_base rather than the installed artifact, so the staleness is otherwise invisible.

nodes.label: Gap-audit offer (HIMMEL-5836)
nodes.rationale: Surfaces non-green read-only checks with remedies without running anything until the operator agrees.

nodes.label: Reheal mode (--reheal)
nodes.rationale: Recovers husk notes in place when their transcripts later become salvageable, without any auto-delete.

nodes.label: Recrystallize mode (--recrystallize)
nodes.rationale: Reheal skips content-bearing uncrystallized notes, so this mode closes the gap with a bounded one-run-per-note LLM pass.

nodes.label: Per-session multi-vault routing
nodes.rationale: Each session is routed to the vault its own repo configures so a single --all pass does not cross-contaminate vaults.

nodes.label: Token-usage warning
nodes.rationale: Backfilling many notes at once makes downstream pipeline stages cost tokens proportional to the session count.

nodes.label: Ledger file layout and JSONL rows
nodes.rationale: One JSON object per line appended in a single write keeps rows atomic, and readers skip unparsable lines so a torn last line costs only one row.

nodes.label: Provenance session (iid, begin/end rows)
nodes.rationale: Exporting the session id lets every child process of a writer append into the same install run.

nodes.label: Pre- and post-state hashing and backups
nodes.rationale: Recording hashes and backup copies of the pre-state lets uninstall restore the operator's original bytes and detect later edits.

nodes.label: Ours snapshots (snap / snap_skip, v2 rows)
nodes.rationale: A snapshot of what himmel wrote lets a revert tell 'still exactly what himmel installed' from 'operator edited it' without trusting a hash alone.

nodes.label: Calling contract for prov_begin/record/end
nodes.rationale: Recording after the writer's atomic write succeeds and before the success line keeps ledger rows truthful about what actually happened.

nodes.label: Reading verdicts and backup retention
nodes.rationale: A single resolved predicate governs when backups and snapshots may be deleted so a held backup is never lost.

nodes.label: --purge-state --keep-backups retain-move
nodes.rationale: Moving ledger and backups together into one retained directory avoids a permanent orphaned backups dir and loses nothing.

nodes.label: TTY [r]estore/[d]elete saves live file first
nodes.rationale: Restore or delete would overwrite or destroy the operator's current bytes, so a sidecar copy is saved first and the action is skipped if the save fails.

nodes.label: Marked HIMMEL:working-principles block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Recording the block with a sha and snapshot lets uninstall strip only an unedited block and leave the operator's surrounding lines.

nodes.label: Uninstall reconcile report
nodes.rationale: Printing a per-unit report before any purge shows the operator what needs them even if a run later refuses, and no printed command deletes the live file.

nodes.label: Provenance known limits
nodes.rationale: implied: documenting limits (no jq fallback, NFS atomicity, Windows untested) keeps operators from over-trusting the helpers.

nodes.label: --dry-run hard gate
nodes.rationale: Dry-run must never write, so the agent aborts with a contract-violation error if it does.

nodes.label: G-8 harvest-completion gate (HIMMEL-1137)
nodes.rationale: A hard-killed harvest leaves partial state, and synthesizing over it would produce patterns from corrupted evidence.

nodes.label: Four pattern-detection lenses
nodes.rationale: Concept clusters, author convergence, tag overpopulation and folder pressure each surface a distinct kind of vault restructuring signal.

nodes.label: Confidence floor
nodes.rationale: Single-source or same-window evidence is noise; Pattern 2 is exempt from the domain rule because authors are inherently single-platform (HIMMEL-242).

nodes.label: Substantive-content gate (LUNA-43)
nodes.rationale: 8 of 20 synthesis pages were template-only boilerplate, which is dead weight at scale.

nodes.label: 14-day dedup window and deterministic slugs
nodes.rationale: Same pattern and subject yield the same slug so reruns do not duplicate proposals.

nodes.label: Counting invariant (LUNA-43)
nodes.rationale: Write emits the file in one shot, so the evidence count must be computed from the finalised list before writing to avoid mismatched headers.

nodes.label: Date extraction by category (daily/sample/interval)
nodes.rationale: Each data category stores its civil date at a different path, and sleep may lack civilEndTime, so a fallback from endTime plus endUtcOffset is needed.

nodes.label: Per-type mapping table (dataTypeId to field, unit, aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Multiple same-day points must collapse to one series value, and many numeric values arrive as JSON strings that need coercion.

nodes.label: Sleep metric migration note
nodes.rationale: sleep_hours used to mean time-in-bed, and because writeSeries only overlays emitted rows, old CSV values are not auto-reconciled and need a one-time repair.

nodes.label: Degraded sleep stage data handling
nodes.rationale: Unparseable stage timestamps would make the remaining valid stages under-count sleep, so sleep_hours is omitted while in-bed hours (from the session interval) still emit.

nodes.label: Durable artifact warnings field
nodes.rationale: Stderr warnings are lost, so recording them additively in the artifact keeps clean pulls byte-identical while preserving derivation-time loss; warning text embeds the dataPoint index so merge's exact-text dedup means the same event.

nodes.label: writeSeries overlay and merge-warning limitations
nodes.rationale: Overlay-only writes are intentional, so metrics absent from artifact rows are never rewritten and the operator must repair stale series manually.

nodes.label: Derived rhr_bpm from heart-rate samples
nodes.rationale: The Fitbit daily resting-HR aggregate stopped in 2024-09, so a 5th-percentile estimate from the live Samsung HR feed substitutes for it.

nodes.label: Categorical/no-data/rollup-only types excluded from series
nodes.rationale: Config enums, bulky waveforms, food definitions and multi-nutrient arrays are not simple vitals, and some types have no data or list 400s.

nodes.label: Tiebreak rules (last aggregate, main sleep session)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic stable picks (greatest source string, first session in API order) keep output reproducible without secondary sort keys.

nodes.label: Five enforcement layers
nodes.rationale: Each stage sees something the others cannot, so invariants are checked where cheapest and the important ones twice.

nodes.label: Handover system
nodes.rationale: One worker is one file so a resuming session cannot read half the picture, and the queue lock is structural because prose coordination failed three ways in one night.

nodes.label: Fleet: chief and workers
nodes.rationale: The fleet model fixes who may write what and who may spawn whom, with a single writer per artifact and the chief owning approval and merge.

nodes.label: Jira / backend seam
nodes.rationale: An MCP server costs context every session while a CLI costs nothing until called, so a hook routes to the CLI and keeps MCP for ops without a CLI verb.

nodes.label: Observability chain
nodes.rationale: The stack stays passive and read-only, and the reader decides liveness because a crashed session never emits session_end.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_AUTO_ACTIONS privileged-op gating
nodes.rationale: Privileged bridge ops are default OFF and enabled one by one, and aliases enable only arm-resume and restart, so merge-public must always be named explicitly.

nodes.label: Autonomy ladder (initiative to AFK)
nodes.rationale: Autonomy is ordered from least to most autonomous with an off switch on every rung, and all rungs are opt-in except the cap watchdogs, so an operator can bound what acts without them.

nodes.label: Layer-level off-switches
nodes.rationale: Operators need one table to turn each layer off entirely, while a few gates (leak-class, egress hard-deny, human-only public merge) are deliberately not switchable and fail closed.

nodes.label: Plugin profile: always / on-demand / not installed tiers
nodes.rationale: On-demand plugins are installed but disabled so they cost no session-start context until requested, with a single script as the sole writer of the flip.

nodes.label: Lanes registry and probes
nodes.rationale: Each lane declares a probe and quota so /lanes can report what is actually available on this machine, and a pre-commit guard keeps the volatile inventory out of CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Project permission model (allow list + deny backstop)
nodes.rationale: A literal-command allow list plus a deny backstop where denies always win keeps destructive operations blocked even inside worktrees.

nodes.label: User vs project hook scopes
nodes.rationale: The universal hook set must follow the operator outside the repo while the himmel-dev guardrail stack stays checked in at project scope; inject-initiative is wired at both with session-id dedup.

nodes.label: Branch + PR workflow
nodes.rationale: Never editing on main, worktree per ticket, ticketed conventional commits and squash merges keep main clean and changes traceable.

nodes.label: Guard changes: one structural round
nodes.rationale: Guard churn was the costliest pattern in the 30-day self-review (28 merges on the write fence alone), so later bypasses go into one residual ticket instead of new PRs.

nodes.label: Cleanups in capped batches
nodes.rationale: The 20-file cap comes from the history-comment prune data (median merge touched 21 files), preventing open-ended cleanup PRs.

nodes.label: Monthly self-review
nodes.rationale: A baseline of merges, fix share, guard churn and red-main merges lets each new 30-day window be compared to detect sprawl.

nodes.label: Opt-in doc-guard gate (.himmel-dev marker)
nodes.rationale: The catalog-sync gate guards contributors but must stay off for adopters using himmel only as a harness.

nodes.label: Adopter route (seven short steps)
nodes.rationale: An adopted repo only has worktree scripts, commit-msg/pre-push hooks, edit guard and merge gate, so it needs a shorter script-driven loop.

nodes.label: Contributor walkthrough (full loop)
nodes.rationale: Using a docs-only toy change keeps attestation simple while still exercising the full gate sequence.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker flow
nodes.rationale: The marker is advisory at push but a hard block at PR creation, so review is never skipped and reviewable docs are never zero-CR.

nodes.label: Reviewer modes (hard vs best-effort)
nodes.rationale: Holding hard reviewers while relaxing best-effort ones means an unavailable CodeRabbit never makes the operator wait.

nodes.label: CI release: heavy CI after review (planned)
nodes.rationale: Starting heavy jobs only after the review gate passes avoids burning runner hours on a head a reviewer is about to send back.

nodes.label: Four merge gates
nodes.rationale: Gates 3 and 4 fail closed while gates 1 and 2 fail open on API error, balancing safety with availability.

nodes.label: Attestation trailers
nodes.rationale: Platform and security attestations are required only for sensitive or non-docs changes, and must be in the first commit rather than a reactive amend.

nodes.label: Per-ticket usage record
nodes.rationale: It joins session token counts with review-ledger data once so a ticket's cost and review rounds are answered from one record.

nodes.label: Ticket join keys and pseudo-tickets (_chief, _unattributed)
nodes.rationale: Chief sessions are pooled under _chief with no allocation because an allocation rule would change every ticket's record whenever the range changes.

nodes.label: Phase-cost rows
nodes.rationale: One cumulative row per (day, session, phase) gives the cost view a single record to read, and unpriced models never borrow another model's price.

nodes.label: PR/CI join (opt-in, fail closed)
nodes.rationale: An unknown fact is never stored, so any gh failure aborts the whole run before anything is appended, keeping previous versions untouched.

nodes.label: Idempotency and append-only digest
nodes.rationale: With no compute timestamp the same inputs give the same bytes, so a ticket's record is appended only when its digest changes.

nodes.label: CI minutes (billed beside wall)
nodes.rationale: Billed minutes are stored as 'unknown', never 0, when billing is absent so a missing answer is not mistaken for free; reruns replace the row to keep the run id unique.

nodes.label: Commit the install before branching
nodes.rationale: A worktree is cut from committed history, so an uncommitted install leaves worktrees with no hooks and no protection.

nodes.label: Starter refuses edit tools, not shell writes
nodes.rationale: The starter hooks gate Edit/Write tools and git commits/pushes only, so a shell redirect to a file and other paths remain open.

nodes.label: Trust paths list
nodes.rationale: A change to a file that guards safety checks could disable them, so the agent that wrote it may not approve it.

nodes.label: Three meanings of profile
nodes.rationale: Install profile, saved profile file and plugin profile are independent choices that are easily conflated, so they are named once.

nodes.label: Opt-in axes: scope, install profile, channel, plugin profile
nodes.rationale: Nothing is a package deal and each choice has a cost, so adopters are shown what each lands and costs before picking.

nodes.label: .single-writer opt-out
nodes.rationale: A personal repo edited in place does not fit the review-gated worktree rule, so a per-checkout local opt-out lifts only the edit-tool hook.

nodes.label: EDIT_ON_MAIN_OK launching-shell switch
nodes.rationale: The hook runs in a process that never sees a per-call prefix, so the off switch must be set in the shell that launches Claude Code.

nodes.label: Ticket ID in commit messages
nodes.rationale: himmel's conventions assume Jira-style or #number references, so adopters can override with TICKET_ID_PATTERN or disable with TICKET_ID_REQUIRED=0.

nodes.label: Attestation trailers (Platforms tested, Security reviewed)
nodes.rationale: These gates ask the author to attest to things a machine cannot verify, and are opt-in for adopters via their own pre-commit config.

nodes.label: Which guards to disable and which to keep
nodes.rationale: Secret-read and destructive-command guards fail closed around irreversible harm at no cost, while ticket, attestation and similar gates are convention-specific.

nodes.label: One owner per guard hook
nodes.rationale: A hook wired from two settings layers runs twice per call, costing two bash startups and duplicate log rows.

nodes.label: Manual install recovery appendix
nodes.rationale: Exists only for when the installer cannot run and the portable core is still needed; it is not a supported second path.

nodes.label: blast-radius POC and A/B result
nodes.rationale: It is the only skill with a defined slot, measurable outcome and cheap opt-in switch; the A/B caught 1 of 3 later defects and proved other real ones.

nodes.label: Formal verification boundary
nodes.rationale: All ten skills stay opt-in and off in worker profiles so no autonomous behavior is adopted without evidence.

nodes.label: Layer taxonomy A/B/C/D
nodes.rationale: Composing across layers is additive while competing within a layer is substitutive.

nodes.label: Registry status labels
nodes.rationale: Map rubric decision states to registry labels and add parked-idea and provisional for items outside the rubric states.

nodes.label: Results marker bullet protocol
nodes.rationale: The chief reads only the newest marker-bearing bullet, so markers must start the bullet and be written by append-results.sh to land at true EOF.

nodes.label: RETASK channel and chief succession
nodes.rationale: Revisions arrive only as direct chief messages quoting the worker's token, so injected text in tool results or files cannot redirect a worker.

nodes.label: Merge only on chief GO quoting token
nodes.rationale: Merging is gated on an explicit chief GO that quotes the worker token so a worker cannot self-authorise a merge.

nodes.label: Ship order: commit, push, pr-check, open PR
nodes.rationale: One push per review round and a fixed order keep CI cost down and keep review rounds clean.

nodes.label: Worker wrap-up and subtree cleanup
nodes.rationale: A worker must release its lock, stop all background tasks and leave a resume brief so the chief can close the window and nothing is orphaned.

nodes.label: Waiter wraps workers
nodes.rationale: The waiter runs worker-event.sh on each WRAPPED/MERGED worker itself, so the chief is woken only when automation could not finish.

nodes.label: digest= line on close
nodes.rationale: Closing a worker digests its session into failure-loop ledgers and prints one informational line that never changes the close's exit code.

nodes.label: One-line forms for operator commands
nodes.rationale: Operators receive a single literal line, never a chain or VAR= prefix, so commands match allow rules and no gate is skipped.

nodes.label: The run kind
nodes.rationale: The run kind freezes one argv, shows it to the operator and runs exactly that once, so approval is for a specific command.

nodes.label: RUN_KIND_SHIPPED compiled switch
nodes.rationale: Being a compiled constant, a config edit cannot turn the run kind on; only a release plus re-install can.

nodes.label: Notice bot and request nonce
nodes.rationale: A session could write any text into the bridge bot's chat, so facts come from a second root-only bot and a nonce binds each code to one request root described.

nodes.label: Mode switch allowlist/all
nodes.rationale: Allowlist mode limits runs to argv a class names, while all mode permits any argv as operator or root, trading safety for flexibility.

nodes.label: Frozen request record
nodes.rationale: Freezing argv, file hashes, inode identity and cwd at request time lets exec detect any change after the operator approved.

nodes.label: open_regular and descriptor-held exec
nodes.rationale: Opening via O_PATH, fstat and fstatfs and exec from the held descriptor stops path swaps and device/FIFO side effects from changing what runs.

nodes.label: Executor re-check order
nodes.rationale: Re-checking hash, identity, config and floor at exec time ensures nothing changed between approval and run, and the code is spent regardless.

nodes.label: Never-remote floor
nodes.rationale: A root-owned word-set check is a seatbelt that config cannot remove, refusing requests naming disk wipe, secrets, main history, approval system or guards-off targets, though it is not a full policy.

nodes.label: Pre-commit gates and their CI copy
nodes.rationale: Contributors without hooks or using --no-verify skip every pre-commit gate, so each gate is mirrored in CI from its BASE copy (a PR cannot weaken the gate that judges it) or declared local by nature.

nodes.label: Pre-push gate delivery: push from the branch's own worktree
nodes.rationale: Pre-push hooks lint the pusher's cwd tree, not the pushed commits, so pushing from the primary checkout lints main's files and fails OPEN; comparing the SHA to the worktree HEAD closes it.

nodes.label: Main-branch reference-transaction guard
nodes.rationale: reference-transaction is not disabled by --no-verify and server-side branch protection returns HTTP 403 on this private repo, so a git hook is the only way to refuse unpublished commits on main.

nodes.label: Ask git for hook location instead of re-deriving it
nodes.rationale: Five review rounds found hand-derived hook paths wrong in new ways (core.hooksPath, relative paths, worktrees), so git's own `--git-path hooks` resolution is used.

nodes.label: Shim target stored in git config, shim is static
nodes.rationale: Embedding the target path in the hook file was exploitable or broken by newlines; git config round-trips arbitrary bytes exactly and nothing is parsed from hook file content.

nodes.label: Deliberate fail-open decisions of the ref-transaction guard
nodes.rationale: The hook fires on every ref update, so failing closed on an unresolved origin/main or a broken shim target would brick fetch, stash and tags repo-wide.

nodes.label: Portable export via .pre-commit-hooks.yaml
nodes.rationale: Worktree isolation was only structurally enforced in himmel while other repos like luna relied on prose, so two gates are exported for opt-in.

nodes.label: Prompt-stage hooks (wired in neither lane)
nodes.rationale: No UserPromptSubmit or UserPromptExpansion hook is wired because .claude/settings.json is operator-only, and the Codex lane has no prompt-stage event.

nodes.label: Anchor block-pr-check-args on HIMMEL_REPO not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
nodes.rationale: In a foreign-repo review CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the reviewed repo, so a guard located through it could be forged or never fire; a guard must not be located by the thing it guards against.

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse hooks
nodes.rationale: Guardrail scripts fire before tool calls so risky operations are blocked structurally rather than by instruction; some are shipped via the plugin to avoid a settings self-mod veto.

nodes.label: Session-sticky bypass convention
nodes.rationale: Claude cannot inject env vars into hook processes, so bypass vars must be set in the shell that launched Claude Code.

nodes.label: Hook timeout policy and latency SLO
nodes.rationale: An unset timeout inherits 600 s and a timed-out PreToolUse hook fails OPEN, so explicit measured 15 s / 60 s tiers bound hangs without firing under normal load.

nodes.label: Claude PreToolUse dispatcher (--chain)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing many per-entry node launches into one chained launcher cuts process spawns while keeping guardrail order, and side-effecting hooks stay out of chains so denies cannot suppress them.

nodes.label: Budget-aware chain member timeouts
nodes.rationale: A killed PreToolUse entry fails OPEN, so must-run security members get their own window capped by an entry-safe deadline and the launcher denies rather than being killed mid-chain.

nodes.label: SLO p95 < 1 s per hook
nodes.rationale: Measured ~7x load spread on Windows process start justifies the 15 s bound rather than a tight multiple of p95.

nodes.label: Per-tool spawn inventory and graphify hook pricing
nodes.rationale: Counting processes per tool call shows where graphify's stock hook entries add cost on high-frequency tools like Read and Glob, so pricing targets those.

nodes.label: Hook-stack re-benchmark with outbound SKIP tripwire
nodes.rationale: Replaying hooks that emit outbound irreversible effects would burn trigger slots or send real messages, so a source scan fails if such a hook is missing from SKIP.

nodes.label: run-node.sh / resolve-node.sh dash silent-no-op class
nodes.rationale: Under dash a bashism or dot-with-operands made hooks exit 0 silently (rc=1 is non-blocking), so guardrails were open rather than denying.

nodes.label: command -p sh launcher convention
nodes.rationale: A bare sh needs a PATH lookup that fails under a pinned-minimal PATH (rc=127 dead chain), whereas command -p resolves from the standard utilities PATH.

nodes.label: SessionStart chaining (--chain --lifecycle)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing four warn-only injectors into one launcher saves three node launches per session start at the cost of serial latency (≈4.9 s vs ≈1.7 s).

nodes.label: auto-approve-safe-bash pre-Bash gateway
nodes.rationale: Claude's native matcher refuses commands with simple expansion and denies silently in headless mode, so a hook that reads the literal command and only ever grants allow is the structural fix.

nodes.label: queue-lock.sh lock verb allow exception
nodes.rationale: The shape fell through to the auto-mode classifier which wrongly denied release as a merge without review, so a tightly guarded whole-command grant was added.

nodes.label: impacted-suites.sh literal allow exception
nodes.rationale: This required /pr-check gate step was sometimes denied by the classifier as Out-of-Place Publication and parked the worker, so it is granted only when bytes match the anchor's.

nodes.label: Review-owed marker pre-PR-create guard
nodes.rationale: Blocking gh pr create while a review-owed marker exists enforces review before PR; cwd-first repo resolution fixes foreign clones being un-gated and same-named branches false-blocking.
